contenido: The creation of the world and the fall of the ombre
1 In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
2 The earth was formless and empty, darkness covered the deep, and the breath of God hovered over the waters.
3 Then God said, "Let there be light." And the light existed.
4 God saw that the light was good, and separated the light from the darkness;
5 and called the light Day and the darkness Night. Thus there was an afternoon and a morning: this was the first day.
6 God said, "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, to establish a separation between them." And so it happened.
7 God made the firmament, and it separated the waters that are under it from those that are above it;
8 and God called the firmament Heaven. Thus there was an afternoon and a morning: this was the second day.
9 God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, and let solid ground appear.” And so it happened.
10 God called the solid ground Earth and all the waters Sea. And God saw that this was good.
11 Then he said, "Let the earth produce vegetables, herbs that bear seed, and fruit trees, that bear on the earth fruits of the same kind with their seed inside." And so it happened.
12 The earth brought forth vegetables, herbs that yield seed according to their kind, and trees that bear fruit of the same kind with their seed inside. And God saw that this was good.
13 Thus there was an evening and a morning: this was the third day.
14 God said, “Let there be stars in the firmament of heaven to distinguish day from night; May they mark the holidays, the days and the years,
15 and let them be like lamps in the firmament of heaven to illuminate the earth. And so it happened.
16 God made two great stars – the larger star to preside over the day and the smaller one to preside over the night – and he also made the stars.
17 And he placed them in the firmament of heaven to illuminate the earth,
18 to preside over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that this was good.
19 Thus there was an evening and a morning: this was the fourth day.
20 God said, "Let the waters be filled with a multitude of living creatures and let birds fly over the earth, through the firmament of heaven."

21 God created the great sea monsters, the various kinds of living beings that fill the waters by gliding in them, and all species of animals with wings. And God saw that
this was good.
22 Then he blessed them, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply; fill the waters of the seas and let the birds multiply on the earth.
23 Thus there was an evening and a morning: this was the fifth day.
24 God said, “Let the earth produce all kinds of living creatures: cattle, reptiles, and wild animals of every kind.” And so it happened.
25 God made the various kinds of animals of the field, the various kinds of livestock, and all the creeping things of the earth, whatever their kind. And God saw that this was good.

26 God said, “Let us make man in our image, according to our likeness; and that the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, the cattle, the wild beasts of the earth, and all
"animals that crawl on the ground."
27 And God created man in his image; He created him in the image of God, he created them male and female.

28 And he blessed them, saying, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth and subdue it; dominate the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky and all living things that move on
the land."
29 And he continued saying: “I give you all the plants that produce seed on the earth, and all the trees that bear fruit with seed: they will be your food.
30 And to all the wild animals of the earth, to all the birds of the sky, and to all the living things that crawl on the ground, I give green grass as food. And so it happened.
31 God looked at everything he had made, and saw that it was very good. Thus there was an evening and a morning: this was the sixth day.
1 Thus were heaven and earth finished, and all the creatures in them.
2 On the seventh day, God finished the work he had done, and ceased from doing the work he had undertaken.
3 God blessed the seventh day and consecrated it, because on it he ceased to do the work that he had created.
4 This was the origin of heaven and earth when they were created.
5 There was not yet any bush of the field on the earth, nor had any grass sprung up, because the Lord God had not caused rain to fall on the earth. Nor was there any man to cultivate the soil,
6 But a spring came out of the earth and watered the entire surface of the ground.
7 Then the Lord God fashioned the man out of clay from the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life. Thus man became a living being.
8 The Lord God planted a garden in Eden in the east, and there he placed the man whom he had formed.
9 And the Lord God caused all kinds of trees to grow out of the ground, which were attractive to the eye and appetizing to eat; He made the tree of the knowledge of good and evil sprout.
10 A river rises from Eden and waters the garden, and from there it divides into four branches.
11 The first is called Pishon: he is the one who runs through the entire region of Javilah, where there is gold.
12 The gold of that region is excellent, and there is also bdellium and lapis lazuli.
13 The second river is called Gihon: it is the one that runs through the entire land of Cush.
14 The third is called Tigris: it is the one that passes east of Asshur. The fourth is the Euphrates.
15 The Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to cultivate it and care for it.
16 And he gave him this command: "You may eat from all the trees in the garden,
17 excepting only the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. You must not eat of it, because the day you do so you will be subject to death.
18 Then the Lord God said, “It is not fitting for the man to be alone. "I'm going to give him proper help."

19 Then the Lord God fashioned all the animals of the field and all the birds of the air out of clay from the ground, and presented them to the man to see what name he would give them. Because every living being
It had to have the name that the man gave it.
20 The man gave a name to all the domestic animals, to all the birds of the air and to all the animals of the field; but among them he did not find adequate help.
21 Then the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall on the man, and when he fell asleep, he took one of his ribs and closed the empty place with flesh.
22 Then the Lord God formed the rib that he had taken from the man into a woman and presented her to the man.
23 The man exclaimed, “This is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh! She will be called Woman, because she was taken from man.
24 Therefore a man leaves his father and mother and cleaves to his wife, and the two become one flesh.
25 Both the man and the woman were naked, but they were not ashamed.
1 The serpent was
2 The woman answered him, “We can eat the fruits of all the trees in the garden.
3 But regarding the tree that is in the middle of the garden, God has told us: "Do not eat from it or touch it, otherwise you will be subject to death."
4 The serpent said to the woman, “No, they will not die.
5 God knows very well that when you eat from that tree, your eyes will be opened and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil.

6 When the woman saw that the tree was appetizing for food, pleasing to the eye, and desirable for acquiring discernment, she took some of its fruit and ate; then she gave it to her husband, who
He was with her, and he also ate.
7 Then the eyes of both of them were opened and they found that they were naked. That's why they made loincloths, weaving together fig leaves.
8 When they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden at the time when the breeze was blowing, they hid themselves from him among the trees of the garden.
9 But the Lord God called to the man and said to him, “Where are you?”
10 “I heard your footsteps in the garden,” he replied, “and I was afraid because I was naked. "That's why I hid."
11 He replied, “And who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I forbade you?
12 The man answered, "The woman whom you placed at my side gave me the fruit, and I ate of it."
13 The Lord God said to the woman, “How did you do such a thing?” The woman replied, "The serpent seduced me and I ate."

14 And the Lord God said to the serpent, “Because you have done this, curse you above all domestic animals and above all the animals of the field. You will crawl on your belly, and
you will eat dust all the days of your life.
15 I will put enmity between you and the woman, between your lineage and hers. "He will crush your head and you will lie in wait for his heel."

16 And the Lord God said to the woman, “I will multiply the sufferings of your pregnancies; You will give birth to your children in pain. You will feel attraction for your husband, and he will dominate you.

17 And he said to the man, “Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree that I forbade you, cursed be the ground because of you. With fatigue you will draw your food from it all the days of your life.
18 He will produce you thistles and thorns and you will eat the grass of the field.
19 You will earn your bread by the sweat of your brow, until you return to the land from which you were taken. Because you are dust and to dust you will return!
20 The man gave his wife the name Eve, because she was the mother of all living things.
21 The Lord God made the man and his wife coats of skin and clothed them.

22 Then the Lord God said, “The man has become like one of us in the knowledge of good and evil. Lest he now stretch out his hand, take also from the tree of life, eat
and live forever."
23 Then he expelled the man from the garden of Eden, to work the land from which he had been taken.
24 And after he had expelled the man, he placed the cherubim and the flame of the zigzagging sword to the east of the garden of Eden, to guard the access to the tree of life.
1 The man joined his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. Then he said: "I have conceived a man, with the help of the Lord."
2 Later she gave birth to Abel, Cain's brother, Abel was a shepherd and Cain a farmer.
3 After a while, Cain presented some fruit from the ground as an offering to the Lord,
4 while Abel offered him the firstfruits and the best of his flock. The Lord looked with favor on Abel and his offering,
5 but he did not look at Cain or his offering. Cain looked very resentful and hung his head.
6 The Lord said to him, “Why are you resentful and keep your head down?
7 If you do well you will be able to keep it upright; If you do wrong, sin is lurking at the door and stalking you, but you must master it.
8 Cain said to his brother Abel, "Let's go outside." And when they were in the field, he fell upon his brother and killed him.
9 Then the Lord asked Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” "I don't know," replied Cain. "Am I my brother's keeper?"
10 But the Lord replied, “What have you done? Listen! Your brother's blood screams towards me from the ground.
11 Therefore curse you from the ground that opened its jaws to receive your brother's blood shed for you.
12 When you cultivate it, it will no longer give you its fruit, and you will wander the earth as a wanderer and a vagabond.
13 Cain answered the Lord, “My punishment is too great for me to bear.
14 Today you throw me away from the fertile ground; I will have to hide from your presence and walk through the earth a wanderer and vagabond, and the first one who comes across me will kill me.
15 "If so, the Lord said to him, whoever kills Cain must pay sevenfold." And the Lord put a mark on Cain, so that when they met him, no one would dare to kill him.
16 Then Cain left the presence of the Lord and went to live in the region of Nod, east of Eden.
17 Cain joined his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Cain was the founder of a city, which he named after his son Enoch.
18 To Enoch was born Irad. Irad was the father of Mehuiah; Mehuiah was the father of Methushahel, and Methushahel was the father of Lamech.
19 Lamech had two wives: one was called Adah, and the other was Shilah.
20 Adam was the mother of Iabal, the ancestor of those who live in camps and raise livestock.
21 His brother's name was Iubal, the ancestor of those who play the lyre and the flute.
22 Shilah, for her part, was the mother of Tubal Cain, the ancestor of the bronze smiths and blacksmiths. Naamah was the sister of Tubal Cain.
23 Lamech said to his wives, “Ada and Silah, listen to my voice: women of Lamech, listen to my word! I killed a man with a wound, and a boy with a bruise.
24 For Cain will be avenged seven times, but Lamech will be avenged seventy-seven.
25 Adam joined his wife, and she had a son, whom she named Seth, saying, "God gave me another descendant in place of Abel, because Cain killed him."
26 Seth also had a son, whom he named Enos. It was then that the name of the Lord began to be invoked.
1 The list of Adam's descendants is as follows: When God created man, he made him like himself.
2 And when he created them, he made them male and female, blessed them and called them Man.
3 Adam was one hundred and thirty years old when he begat a son like himself, according to his image, and he named him Seth.
4 After Seth was born, Adam lived eight hundred years and had sons and daughters.
5 Adam lived a total of nine hundred and thirty years, and at the end of them he died.
6 Seth was one hundred and five years old when he became the father of Enos.
7 After Enos was born, Seth lived eight hundred and seven years and had sons and daughters.
8 Seth lived a total of nine hundred and twelve years, and at the end of them he died.
9 Enos was ninety years old when he became the father of Kenan.
10 After Kenan was born, Enos lived eight hundred and fifteen years and had sons and daughters.
11 Enos lived a total of nine hundred and five years, and at the end of them he died.
12 Kenan was seventy years old when he became the father of Mahalalel.
13 After Mahalalel was born, Quenan lived eight hundred and forty years and had sons and daughters.
14 Chenan lived a total of nine hundred and ten years, and at the end of them he died.
15 Mahalalel was seventy-five years old when he became the father of Jered.
16 After Iered was born, Mahalalel lived eight hundred and thirty years and had sons and daughters.
17 Mahalalel lived eight hundred and ninety-five years, and at the end of them he died.
18 Iered was one hundred and sixty-two years old when he became the father of Enoch.
19 After Enoch was born, Iered lived eight hundred years and had sons and daughters.
20 Iered lived a total of nine hundred and sixty-two years, and at the end of them he died.
21 Enoch was sixty-five years old when he became the father of Methuselah.
22 Enoch followed the ways of God. After Methuselah was born, Enoch lived three hundred years and had sons and daughters.
23 Enoch lived a total of three hundred and sixty-five years.
24 He always followed the ways of God, and then he disappeared because God took him away.
25 Methuselah was one hundred and eighty-seven years old when he became the father of Lamech.
26 After Lamech was born, Methuselah lived seven hundred and eighty-two years and had sons and daughters.
27 Methuselah lived a total of nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and at the end of them he died.
28 Lamech was one hundred and eighty-two years old when he became the father of a son,
29 whom he called Noah, saying, "This one will give us relief in our work and in the fatigue of our hands, a relief from the ground that the Lord cursed."
30 After Noah was born, Lamech lived five hundred and ninety-five years and had sons and daughters.
31 Lamech lived a total of seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and at the end of them he died.
32 Noah was five hundred years old when he became the father of Shem, Ham and Japheth.
1 When men began to multiply on the earth and daughters were born to them,
2 The sons of God saw that these were beautiful, and they took as wives as many as they wanted.
3 Then the Lord said, “My spirit will not remain active in man forever, for he is nothing but flesh; That is why he will not live more than one hundred and twenty years.

4 In those days – and even after – when the sons of God united with the daughters of men and they had children, there were giants on the earth: these were the heroes
famous from ancient times.
5 When the Lord saw how great was man's wickedness on earth and how all the designs he formed in his mind constantly tended toward evil,
6 he repented that he had made man on earth, and his heart was heavy.

7 Therefore the Lord said: "I am going to wipe out from the surface of the ground the men whom I have created - and along with them the beasts, the creeping things and the birds of the sky - because I repent
having done them.
8 But Noah was pleasing in the sight of the Lord.
9 This is the story of Noah. Noah was a just man, blameless among his contemporaries, and always followed the ways of God.
10 He had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.
11 But the earth was perverted in the sight of God and had become filled with violence.
12 Seeing that the land had become perverted, because all men had depraved conduct.
13 God said to Noah, “I have decided to destroy all mortals, because the earth has been filled with violence because of them. That's why I'm going to destroy them along with the earth.
14 Build yourself an ark of resinous wood, divide it into compartments, and cover it with bitumen inside and out.
15 You must make it like this: the ark will be one hundred and fifty meters long, thirty wide, and fifteen high.
16 You will also make a skylight for it and finish it two feet from the top. You will put the door on the side of the ark and make a first, a second and a third floor.
17 I am going to send the waters of the Flood to the earth, to completely destroy all beings that have the breath of life: everything that is on earth will perish.
18 But I will establish my covenant with you: you will enter the ark with your sons, your wife, and your sons' wives.
19 You will also bring into the ark a pair of every kind of living creature, of all flesh, so that they may survive with you; They must be a male and a female.
20 A pair of each species of birds, livestock and reptiles will go with you, so that they may survive.
21 Also, gather provisions of all kinds and store them up, so that they may be food for you and for them.
22 This is what Noah did, fulfilling exactly everything that God had commanded him.
1 Then the Lord said to Noah, “Enter the ark with all your family, for I have seen that you are the only truly righteous one among this generation.
2 Bring seven pairs of all kinds of pure animals and one pair of impure ones, the males with their females.
3 – also seven pairs of all kinds of birds – to perpetuate their species on the earth.
4 For in seven days I will make it rain for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe out from the surface of the earth all the creatures that I have made.
5 And Noah fulfilled the command that God gave him.
6 When the waters of the Flood fell on the earth, Noah was six hundred years old.
7 Then he entered the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives, to be saved from the waters of the Flood.
8 And the pure animals, the unclean animals, the birds, and all the creatures that crawl on the ground,
9 they went in pairs with him into the ark, as God had commanded them.
10 After seven days, the waters of the Flood fell on the earth.
11 Noah was six hundred years old, and it was the seventeenth day of the second month. That day, the fountains of the great ocean overflowed and the cataracts of heaven opened.
12 And a heavy rain fell on the land for forty days and forty nights.
13 That same day, Noah, his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, his wife, and his sons' three wives, had entered the ark;
14 and along with them, animals of all kinds: wild animals, cattle, creeping things, birds and all other winged animals.
15 All kinds of beings that are animated by a breath of life entered with Noah into the ark; and they did it in pairs,
16 males and females, as God had commanded. Then the Lord closed the ark behind Noah.
17 The Flood raged on the earth for forty days. As the waters rose, they carried the ark upward, and it rose above the earth.
18 The waters rose and rose above the earth, while the ark floated on the surface.
19 So they continued to rise higher and higher, until the mountains everywhere, even the highest ones, were submerged.
20 The water level rose more than seven meters above the mountains.
21 Then all the creatures that moved on the earth perished: the birds, the cattle, the wild beasts, all the animals that crawl on the ground, and also the men.
22 Everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died, everything that was on solid ground.
23 So all the creatures that were on the earth were eliminated, from man to cattle. the reptiles and the birds of the sky. Only Noah and those who were with him in the ark remained.
24 And the waters flooded the earth for one hundred and fifty days.
1 Then God remembered Noah and all the wild and domestic animals that were with him in the ark. He caused a wind to blow over the land, and the waters began to subside.
2 The fountains of the ocean and the floodgates of heaven were closed, and the heavy rain that fell from heaven ceased.
3 Little by little the waters receded from the land; and after one hundred and fifty days they had already decreased so much,
4 that on the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark stopped on the mountains of Ararat.
5 Thus they continued to gradually decrease until the tenth month; and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains appeared.
6 After forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark,
7 And he released a raven, which flew about, coming and going until the ground was dry.
8 Then he released a dove to see if the waters had gone down.
9 But the dove could not find a place to rest, and returned to the ark because the water still covered the entire earth. Noah stretched out his hand, took her, and brought her into the ark with him.
10 Then he waited seven more days, and again released the dove out of the ark.
11 It returned at dusk, carrying a green olive branch in its beak. This is how Noah knew that the waters had finished going down.
12 He waited another seven days and released her again. But this time the dove did not return.
13 The land began to dry out in the six hundred and first year of Noah's life, on the first day of the month. Noah removed the roof of the ark, and saw that the earth was drying out.
14 And on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the land was dry.
15 Then God said to Noah:
16 “Leave the ark with your wife, your sons, and your sons' wives.

17 Also bring out all the living creatures that are with you – birds, livestock, or any kind of animals that crawl on the ground – so that they fill the earth, be fruitful, and be fruitful.
multiply",
18 Noah went out accompanied by his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives.
19 Everything that moves on the ground; all the beasts, all the creeping things, and all the birds came out of the ark, one group after another.
20 Then Noah built an altar to the Lord, and taking pure animals and pure birds of all kinds, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.

21 When the Lord inhaled the pleasant aroma, he said to himself, "Never again will I curse the ground because of man, because the intentions of the human heart are evil from the beginning."
youth; nor will I punish all living beings again, as I ended up
to do it.
22 From now on, as long as the earth lasts, sowing and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, will not cease.
1 Then God blessed Noah and his sons, saying, “Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth.

2 Before you will be afraid of all the animals of the earth and all the birds of the sky, everything that moves on the ground, and all the fish of the sea: they have been put into your hands.
of you.
3 Everything that moves and has life will serve as food for them; I give them all that like before I gave them the vegetables.
4 They will only abstain from eating meat with their life, that is, with their blood.
5 And I will ask an account for the blood of each one of you: I will ask an account for it from all the animals, and I will also ask a man to account for the life of his neighbor.
6 Another man will shed the blood of him who sheds human blood, because man was created in the image of God.
7 You, for your part, be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and dominate it.
8 And God continued saying to Noah and his sons:
9 "Furthermore, I establish my alliance with you, with your descendants,

10 and with all the living creatures that are with you: with the birds, the cattle, and the wild beasts; with all the animals that came out of the ark, in a word, with all
the living beings that are on earth.
11 I will establish my alliance with you: mortals will no longer be destroyed by the waters of the Flood, nor will there be another Flood to devastate the earth.
12 God added: “This will be the sign of the covenant that I establish with you, and with all living beings that accompany you, for all future times:
13 I place my bow in the clouds, as a sign of my alliance with the earth.
14 When I cover the earth with clouds and my bow appears between them,
15 I will remember my covenant with you and with all living creatures, and the waters of the Flood will no longer rush in to destroy mortals.
16 When my bow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember my eternal covenant with all living creatures that are on the earth.
17 This, God said to Noah, is the sign of the covenant that I established with all mortals.
18 The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham and Japheth. Ham is the father of Canaan.
19 From these three sons of Noah, the whole earth was peopled.
20 Noah dedicated himself to agriculture and was the first to plant a vineyard.
21 But when he drank wine, he became drunk and lay completely naked in the middle of his tent.
22 Ham, the father of Canaan, seeing his father naked, went to tell his brothers, who were outside.

23 Then Shem and Japheth took a cloak, both of them put it on their backs, and walking backwards, they covered their father's nakedness. As their faces were looking in the opposite direction, they did not see
to his naked father.
24 When Noah woke up from his drunkenness and learned what his youngest son had done,
25 said, “Cursed be Canaan! "He will be the last of the slaves for his brothers."
26 And he added: “Blessed be the Lord, God of Shem, and may Canaan be his slave.
27 May God make a way for Japheth to live among the camps of Shem; and let Canaan be his slave.
28 After the Flood, Noah lived three hundred and fifty years,
29 and in all, he lived nine hundred and fifty years. After them, he died.
1 The descendants of Noah's three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth – who had children after the Flood – were as follows:
2 The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.
3 The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
4 The sons of Javan were Elisha, Tarshish, the Chitim, and the Rodanim.

5 These were the sons of Japheth, and from them, the maritime nations expanded throughout their respective territories, each with its language, its clans and its
nationalities.
6 The sons of Ham were Cush, Misraim, Put and Canaan.
7 The sons of Cush were Sheba, Javilah, Sabta, Ramah and Sabteca. The sons of Ramah were Sheba and Dedan.
8 Cush was the father of Nimrod, who became the first warrior on earth.
9 He was a mighty hunter before the Lord. That is why it is said: "A brave hunter before the Lord like Nimrod."
10 Babylon, Erech and Akkad – all of which are in the region of Shinar – were the initial nucleus of his kingdom.
11 From that region he went out to Ashur, and built Nineveh, with its town squares, Calach,
12 and Resen, between Nineveh and Calach. The latter was the capital.
13 Misraim was the father of the people of Lud, Anam, Lehab, Naftuj,
14 Patros and Casluj, and also of the inhabitants of Caphtor, from where the Philistines came.
15 Canaan was the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and of Heth;
16 also of the Jebusites, of the Amorites, of the Girgashites,
17 of the Hivites, of the Archites, of the Sinites,
18 of the Arvadites, the Semarites and the Jamathites. Later the Canaanite clans expanded,
19 and its borders extended from Sidon to Gaza by the way of Gerar; and as far as Lesa, going towards Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Sheboim.
20 These were the sons of Ham, according to their clans and their languages, with their respective territories and nationalities.
21 Sons were also born to Shem, the father of all the sons of Eber and the elder brother of Japheth.
22 The sons of Shem were Elam, Ashur, Arpaxad, Lud and Aram.
23 The sons of Aram were Us, Hul, Gether, and Mas.
24 Arpaxad was the father of Shelah, and he was the father of Eber.
25 Eber had two sons: the name of the first was Peleg, because in his time the land was divided. His brother was called Ioctan.
26 Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerach,
27 Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
28 Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
29 Ophir, Javilah and Iobab. All these were sons of Ioctan.
30 The places where they lived extended from Mesha, towards Sephar, to the mountain of the East.
31 These were the sons of Shem, according to their clans and their languages, with their respective territories and nationalities.
32 These were the clans of the sons of Noah, according to their origins and nationalities. From them, the nations expanded over the earth after the Flood.
1 Everyone spoke the same language and used the same words.
2 And when men migrated from the East, they found a plain in the region of Senaar and settled there.
3 Then they said to each other, “Let's go! "Let's make bricks and bake them over the fire." And they used bricks instead of stone, and asphalt served as a mixture.
4 Then they said, "Let us build a city, and also a tower whose top will reach to heaven, so that we may perpetuate our name and not be scattered throughout the earth."
5 But the Lord came down to see the city and the tower that the men were building,
6 and said, "If this is the first work you do, nothing you propose to do will be impossible for you, as long as you are one people and all speak the same language.
7 Let us go down then, and once there, let us confuse their language, so that they will no longer understand each other.
8 So the Lord scattered them from that place, scattering them throughout the land, and they stopped building the city.
9 That is why it was called Babel there; in fact, the Lord confused the language of men and scattered them throughout the whole earth.
10 This is the offspring of Shem; Shem was one hundred years old when he fathered Arpaxad, two years after the Flood.
11 After Arpaxad, Shem, was born, he lived five hundred years and had sons and daughters.
12 At thirty-five years old, Arpaxad became the father of Shelach.
13 After Shelah was born, Arpaxad lived four hundred and three years, and had sons and daughters.
14 At thirty-four years old, Eber became the father of Peleg.

1 Jacob resumed his march and went to the country of the Easterners.

2 There he saw a well in the middle of the field, next to which three flocks of sheep were lying, because they were watering the cattle at that well. The stone that covered the mouth of the well was very large.

5 He added, "Do you know Laban son of Nahor?" "Yes," they said.
6 He asked them again, "Are you well?" "Very good," they replied. "Precisely, there comes his daughter Rachel with the flock."

9 While he was still speaking with them, Rachel, who was a shepherdess, arrived with her father's flock.

1 Meanwhile, Jacob was settled in the territory where his father had resided as a foreigner, in the land of Canaan.
2 This is the story of Jacob.
3 Israel loved Joseph more than any other of his sons, because he was the son of old age, and he ordered him to make a long-sleeved tunic.
4 But his brothers, seeing that he loved him more than them, hated him so much that they could not even greet him.
5 Once Joseph had a dream and told it to his brothers.
6 “Listen to the dream I had,” he said to them.
7 “We were in the field tying sheaves. Suddenly my sheaf rose and stood erect, while yours formed a circle around mine and bowed before it.
8 His brothers asked him, "Do you intend to reign over us and have us under your dominion?" And they hated him even more for what he said about his dreams.
9 Then he had another dream, and he also told it to his brothers. «I had another dream, he told them. The sun, the moon and eleven stars prostrated themselves before me.
10 But when he told his father, he rebuked him, saying, “What does that dream you had mean? Will I, your mother, and your brothers come and bow down to the ground before you?
11 And his brothers were envious of him, but his father reflected on all these things.
12 One day his brothers had gone to Shechem to feed their father's flock.
13 Then Israel said to Joseph, “Your brothers are with the flock of Shechem. "I want you to go see them." "Okay," he replied.
14 His father added, “Go see how your brothers and the flock are doing, and bring me news.” And he sent him from the valley of Hebron. When Joseph arrived at Shechem,
15 A man found him walking around the field and asked him, "What are you looking for?"
16 He answered him, “I am looking for my brothers. Can you tell me where they are grazing the flock?
17 "They have left here," the man replied, "because I heard them say, 'Let's go to Dothan.'" Joseph then went in search of his brothers, and found them in Dothan.
18 They saw him from afar, and before he approached, they had already conspired to kill him.
19 “Here comes that dreamer,” they said to each other.
20 “Why don't we kill him and throw him into one of those cisterns? Later we will say that a beast devoured him. We'll see then how his dreams end!
21 But Reuben, when he heard this, tried to save him, saying, "Let us not make any attempt on his life."

22 And he added: “Do not shed blood. Throw him into that cistern out there in the desert, but don't lay your hands on him. In reality, his intention was to free it from their hands and return it to
his father safe and sound.
23 As soon as Joseph arrived at the place where his brothers were, they stripped him of his tunic—the long-sleeved tunic that he was wearing.
24 They took him and threw him into the cistern, which was completely empty.
25 Then they sat down to eat.
26 Then Judah said to his brothers, “What do we gain by murdering our brother and hiding his blood?
27 Instead of attacking his life, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, because he is our brother, our own flesh. And his brothers agreed.

28 But in the meantime, some Midianite merchants passed by and took Joseph out of the cistern. Then they sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of land, and Joseph was
taken to Egypt.
29 When Reuben returned to the cistern and realized that Joseph was missing, he tore his clothes,
30 And returning to his brothers, he said, “The boy has disappeared. Where will I go now?
31 Then they took Joseph's tunic, killed a goat, and soaked the tunic with blood.
32 Then they sent the long-sleeved tunic to their father, along with this message: “We have found this. Look carefully if it is your son's tunic or not.
33 When he recognized it, he exclaimed, “It is my son's tunic! A wild animal has devoured him. Joseph has been a prey to wild beasts!
34 Jacob tore his clothes, dressed in mourning, and mourned for his son for a long time.
35 His sons and daughters came to comfort him, but he refused all comfort, saying, “No. "I am going down in mourning to where my son is, to the abode of the dead." And he continued to lament.
36 But in the meantime, in Egypt, the Midianites had sold him to Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, captain of the guards.
1 At that time, Judah left his brothers and became friends with a man from Adullam named Hirah.
2 There he met the daughter of a Canaanite named Shuah, and after taking her as his wife, he married her.
3 She conceived and gave birth to a son, and he named him Er.
4 Then she conceived again and had another son, whom she named Onan.
5 Then she had another son again, and she named him Shelah. When she gave birth, she was in Quezib.
6 Later Judah married Er, his eldest son, to a woman named Tamar.
7 Er displeased the Lord, and the Lord put him to death.
8 Judah then said to Onan, "Join yourself to the widow of Er, to fulfill your duties as a brother-in-law and ensure a seed for your brother."
9 But Onan, knowing that the offspring would not belong to him, every time he married her, he spilled the semen on the ground to prevent his brother from having offspring.
10 His behavior displeased the Lord, and he also put him to death.

11 Then Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar, "Live like a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah grows up," because he feared that he would suffer the same fate as his brothers. That's why Tamar left
to live in his father's house.

12 A long time later Judah's wife, Shuah's daughter, died. Once the duel was over, Judah headed towards Timna in the company of his friend Hirah, the Adullamite, because they were shearing their sheep there.
13 Tamar was informed that her father-in-law was on his way to Timnah, where his flock was being sheared.

14 And when she saw that Shelah was already grown up, and yet had not been given to her as a husband, she took off her widow's clothing, covered herself with a veil so as not to be recognized, and sat at the entrance to Enaim, on the
road to Timna.
15 Because her face was covered, Judah saw her and thought she was a prostitute.
16 Then he left the road and went to her to say, "Let me lie with you," not knowing that it was his daughter-in-law. She replied: "What will you give me for sleeping with me?"
17 "I will send you a goat from my flock," he assured him. "Okay, she continued, as long as you leave me something as a pledge until you send it to me."
18 He asked him, “What should I leave you?” "Your seal with its cord and the staff you carry in your hand," he replied. He gave them to her and slept with her, leaving her pregnant.
19 Immediately she withdrew, took off the veil that covered her, and put on her widow's clothing again.
20 When Judah sent him the goat through his friend, the Adullamite, to rescue the garment that had been left in the woman's hands, he could not find it.
21 Then he asked the people of the place, "Where is that prostitute who sat at Enaim, by the roadside?" They answered him: "There was never a prostitute there."
22 He returned and said to Judah, “I couldn't find her. Furthermore, the local people assured me that there was never a prostitute there.
23 Judah replied, “Let him keep everything, otherwise we will make ourselves ridiculous. I complied by sending her the kid, and you couldn't find her.

24 About three months later, Judah was notified: “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has become a prostitute, and in one of her wanderings she became pregnant.” Then Judah exclaimed, "Take her outside and burn her alive."
25 But when they were going to take her out, she sent word to her father-in-law, “These things belong to the man who impregnated me. Find out who is the owner of this seal, this cord and that staff.
26 Recognizing them, Judah declared, "She is more righteous than I, because I did not give her Shelah to my son." And he did not have relations with her again.
27 When the time of delivery arrived, it turned out that there were twins in her womb.
28 While she was giving birth, one of them stretched out her hand, and the midwife tied a scarlet thread to it, saying, "This was the first to come out."
29 But then he withdrew his hand, and the other went out first. Then she said, “How you have made a breach!” That's why he was called Peres.
30 Then his brother came out, wearing the scarlet thread, and therefore they called him Zerah.
1 When Joseph was taken to Egypt, Potiphar – an Egyptian who was an official of Pharaoh, captain of the guards – bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him there.
2 But since the Lord was with Joseph, luck favored him, and he stayed in the house of his boss, the Egyptian.
3 Seeing that the Lord was with him and making all his works prosper,
4 His boss looked favorably on him and appointed him his steward, putting him in charge of his house and entrusting him with the administration of all his property.

5 From the moment he entrusted him with the care of his house and all his possessions, the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house, in honor of Joseph. The blessing of the Lord extended to
all your possessions, inside and outside the house.
6 That is why he left everything he owned in charge of Joseph, and he no longer worried about anything except the food he ate.
7 After a while, his master's wife fixed her eyes on him and said to him, "Lie with me."
8 But he refused and answered the woman: “Having me, my master no longer thinks about the affairs of his house, because he has entrusted me with everything he owns.

9 He himself exercises no more authority than I do in this house, and he has not imposed any restrictions on me, apart from the respect that is due to you, since you are his wife. How then can I commit such a serious crime?
and to sin against God?
10 And no matter how much she instigated him day after day, he did not agree to sleep with her and be her lover.
11 But one day, Joseph entered the house to fulfill his duties, at the precise moment when all the service personnel were absent.
12 Then she grabbed him by his clothes and said, "Lie down with me." But he fled, leaving his cloak in the woman's hands, and went away from there.
13 When she saw that Joseph had left the cloak in his hands and had run away,

14 He called his servants and said to them, “Look! My husband brought us a Hebrew, just to make him laugh at us. He tried to sleep with me, but I screamed as loud as I could.
I could.
15 And when he heard me shout for help, he left his cloak next to me and ran away.
16 She kept Joseph's cloak until her husband returned,
17 and then he told him the same story: “The Hebrew slave you brought to us mocked me and tried to rape me.
18 But when I cried out for help, he left his cloak at my side and ran away.
19 When his wife heard his wife's words, "Your slave did this and this to me," his master was furious.
20 He had Joseph arrested and put him in prison where the king's prisoners were held. That's how he ended up in jail.
21 But the Lord was with Joseph and showed him kindness, winning the favor of the chief jailer.
22 He entrusted all the prisoners in the prison to Joseph, and he directed everything that was done there.
23 The chief jailer did not supervise anything that he had entrusted to Joseph, because the Lord was with him and made everything he did prosper.
1 After these events, the king of Egypt's cupbearer and baker offended their master.
2 Pharaoh was angry with his two officials, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
3 and he had them placed under guard in the house of the captain of the guards, in the same prison where Joseph was imprisoned.
4 The captain of the guards commissioned Joseph to serve them, and they were detained for a time.
5 Once, while they were imprisoned in prison, the king of Egypt's cupbearer and baker had a dream during the same night, each dream having its own meaning.
6 The next morning, when Joseph went to see them, he found them depressed.
7 "Why are you looking sad today?" he asked Pharaoh's officials who were arrested with him in his master's house.
8 They answered him, "We have had a dream, and there is no one here to interpret it." Joseph said to them: “Interpretation is the work of God; But anyway, tell me what you dreamed.
9 The cupbearer told his dream to Joseph. «I dreamed, I told him that in front of me there was a vine,
10 and in it, three branches. As soon as the vine budded, its flowers came out and the grapes ripened in the clusters.
11 Pharaoh's cup was in my hand: I took the grapes, squeezed them into that cup, and put it in Pharaoh's hand.
12 Joseph said to him, "The interpretation is this: the three clusters represent three days,
13 Within three days, Pharaoh will pardon you, restore you to your charge, and you will put the cup in his hand, as you used to do before, when you were his cupbearer.
14 And when your luck improves, if you still remember that I was here with you, do not stop doing me this favor: tell Pharaoh about me, and try to get me out of this place.
15 For I was brought by force from the country of the Hebrews, and here I did nothing to be put in prison.
16 The chief baker, seeing how correctly he had interpreted the dream, said to Joseph: “I, for my part, dreamed that I had three wicker baskets on my head.
17 In the highest basket, there was all the baked goods that Pharaoh eats, and the birds ate from that basket that was above my head.
18 Joseph replied, “The interpretation is this: the three baskets represent three days.
19 In three days Pharaoh will have you beheaded, he will hang you on a post, and the birds will eat your flesh.

20 Indeed, on the third day Pharaoh's birthday was celebrated, and he entertained all his servants with a banquet. Then he reconsidered the causes of the chief cupbearer and the baker
greater among his servants,
21 And he restored the chief cupbearer to his post, so that he put the cup back into Pharaoh's hand;
22 Instead, he ordered the chief baker to be hanged, according to the interpretation that Joseph had given them.
23 However, the chief cupbearer no longer thought about Joseph, but forgot about him.
1 Two years later, Pharaoh had a dream: he was standing by the Nile,
2 when suddenly seven beautiful and robust cows came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.
3 Behind her came up seven other ugly and emaciated cows, which stood next to the first;
4 and the ugly and scrawny cows ate the seven beautiful and strong cows. Immediately Pharaoh woke up.
5 Then he fell asleep again and had another dream: seven large, lush ears came out of the same stalk.
6 But immediately afterwards seven more ears sprouted, thin and scorched by the east wind;
7 and the thin ears devoured the seven large ears loaded with grain. When he woke up, Pharaoh realized that he had been dreaming.
8 The next morning, Pharaoh felt very worried and sent for all the magicians and wise men of Egypt to tell them his dreams. But no one could interpret them.
9 Then the chief cupbearer went to Pharaoh and said, “Now I recognize my negligence.
10 Once Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and he put me and the chief baker in custody in the house of the captain of the guards.
11 He and I had a dream during the same night, each dream with its own meaning.
12 With us was a young Hebrew, a servant of the captain of the guards; We told him our dreams, and he interpreted them, giving each one his explanation.
13 And everything happened as he had interpreted it: I was restored to my position, while the other was hanged.
14 Pharaoh sent for Joseph, who was quickly taken out of prison. He shaved, changed his clothes and appeared before the Pharaoh.
15 Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have had a dream that no one can interpret. But I have been informed that it is enough for you to hear a dream to interpret it.
16 Joseph answered Pharaoh, "It is not I, but God, who will give Pharaoh the appropriate answer."
17 Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I dreamed that I was standing on the bank of the Nile,
18 And suddenly seven strong and beautiful cows came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.
19 Behind them came up seven other cows, emaciated, horrible-looking and skeletal, such as I had never seen in all the territory of Egypt.
20 And the scrawny and ugly cows devoured the other seven strong cows.
21 But once they had eaten them, no one would have said that they had them in their wombs, because they were still as horrible as before. I woke up immediately.
22 In the other dream, I saw seven beautiful ears, loaded with grains, sprouting from the same stem.
23 After them seven more ears sprouted, withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind,
24 who devoured the seven beautiful ears of wheat. I have told all this to the fortune tellers, but none of them have given me an explanation.
25 Joseph said to Pharaoh, “Pharaoh has dreamed of one thing, and so God has announced to him what he is about to accomplish.
26 The seven beautiful cows and the seven lush ears represent seven years. Both dreams are about the same thing.

27 And the seven scrawny and ugly cows that came up after them are seven years old, the same as the seven ears of grain without grain and scorched by the east wind. These will be seven years of famine.
28 It is as I just told Pharaoh: God wanted to show him what he is about to do.
29 In the next seven years there will be great abundance throughout Egypt.
30 But immediately afterward, there will be seven years of famine, during which not even the memory of that abundance will remain in Egypt, because famine will devastate the country.
31 Then no one will know what abundance is, because the famine will be very intense.
32 The fact that Pharaoh had the same dream twice means that this matter has already been resolved by God and that he is going to execute it immediately.
33 Therefore, it is necessary for Pharaoh to find a prudent and wise man, and put him in charge of all Egypt.
34 In addition, Pharaoh must establish inspectors throughout the country and demand from the Egyptians a fifth of the crops during the seven years of plenty.
35 They will gather the provisions that will be harvested in these next seven years of prosperity, and they will store the grain under the supervision of Pharaoh, to keep it stored in the cities.
36 Thus the country will have a reserve of food for the seven years of famine that will come upon Egypt, and it will not die of starvation.
37 The answer pleased Pharaoh and all his servants.
38 Therefore Pharaoh said to them, "Can we find another man who has the same measure of the spirit of God?"
39 And turning to Joseph, he said, “Since God has made you aware of all these things, there is no one who is as prudent and wise as you.
40 Therefore you will be in charge of my palace, and all my people will have to obey your orders. Only by the royal throne will I be superior to you.
41 And Pharaoh continued saying to Joseph, "I am now putting you in charge of all the territory of Egypt."
42 Immediately he took the ring off his hand and put it on Joseph's hand; He made him dress in fine linen clothing and hung a gold chain around his neck.
43 Then he made him get into the best chariot after his own, and they shouted before him, "Attention!" Thus he gave him authority over all of Egypt.
44 Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh, but no one will be able to move a hand or a foot in all the land of Egypt unless you approve."
45 Then he gave Joseph the name Saphnath Paneach, and gave him to wife Asnath, the daughter of Potipherah, priest of the city of On. And Joseph went to travel through the country of Egypt.
46 When Joseph entered the service of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, he was thirty years old. Joseph left the presence of Pharaoh and toured the entire territory of Egypt.
47 During the seven years of plenty, the land produced abundantly,
48 And he gathered all the provisions collected in those seven years and stored them in the cities, depositing in each of the crops from the neighboring fields.
49 In this way, Joseph accumulated an enormous amount of grain, as much as the sand of the sea, to such an extent that he stopped keeping track, because it surpassed all measurements.
50 Before the years of famine began, Joseph had two sons, whom Asnath, the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of On, bore him.
51 He called the first Manasseh, because he said, "God has made me completely forget my sorrows and my father's house."
52 And he named the second Ephraim, saying, "God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction."
53 Then ended the years of Egypt's abundance,
54 and the seven years of famine began, as Joseph had anticipated. In all countries there was hunger, but in Egypt there was food.
55 When the Egyptians and the people were also hungry, and the people cried out to Pharaoh to give them something to eat, he answered, "Go to Joseph and do what he tells you."
56 As the famine had spread throughout the land, Joseph opened the granaries and distributed rations to the Egyptians, since the famine was becoming more and more intense.
57 And from all sides they went to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, because famine devastated the entire land.
1 When Jacob heard that they were selling grain in Egypt, he asked his sons, "Why do you stand there, looking at each other?"

3 Then ten of Joseph's brothers went down to Egypt to stock up on grain;
4 But Jacob did not let Benjamin, Joseph's brother, go with them, for fear that misfortune would befall him.
5 So the children of Israel arrived among other people who were also going to get food, because there was hunger in Canaan.

8 And when he recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him,

10 “No, sir,” they answered. «It is true that your servants have come to buy groceries.

13 They continued saying, “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, sons of a man who resides in Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and another is no longer alive.

There will be no doubt that you are spies.

26 They loaded their donkeys with provisions and set out.
27 When they camped for the night, one of them opened the bag to feed his donkey, and found the money next to the opening of the bag.

28 Then he said to his brothers, “The money has been returned to me. It's here, in my bag. They were astonished, and trembling, they asked one another: "Why would God have given us

1 For the construction of the Dwelling you will use ten curtains of fine reinforced linen, violet purple, red purple and crimson, with artistically designed figures of cherubim.
2 Each curtain will be fourteen meters long and two meters wide. They will all be of the same dimensions,
3 and they will be joined together in two groups of five curtains each.
4 Furthermore, on the edge of the last curtain of the first series, you will put some violet purple loops, and you will do the same on the edge of the one at the end of the second series.
5 You will put fifty loops in one and fifty in another, so that the loops correspond to each other.
6 Then you will make fifty golden hooks, and with them you will join the curtains together, so that the Dwelling will form a whole.
7 You will also make eleven awnings of goats' hair to cover the Dwelling, like a tent.
8 Each of these awnings will measure fifteen meters long and two meters wide: they will all have the same dimensions.
9 Then you will join together five of these awnings separately on one side and six on the other, and you will fold the sixth awning over the front of the tent.
10 Then you will put fifty loops on the edge of the awning that closes the first set, and another fifty on the edge of the one that closes the second set.
11 In addition, you will make fifty bronze hooks and insert them into the loops, so you will join the tent together, so that it forms a whole.
12 As for the remaining part of the awnings, half will hang at the back of the Dwelling;
13 and the fifty centimeters that remain along each side will hang on both sides to cover it.
14 Furthermore, you will have to make for the Dwelling an awning of rams' skins dyed red, and on top of it another awning of fine leather.
15 You will also make racks of acacia wood for the Dwelling, arranged vertically.
16 Each frame will measure five meters long and seventy-five centimeters wide,
17 and will have two breakwaters joined together. This is how you will assemble all the frames of the Dwelling.
18 You will make twenty of these frames for the south side, which faces the Negeb,
19 and forty silver bases to support them, that is, two bases under each frame, one for each breakwater.
20 For the other side of the Dwelling, the part that faces north, you will also make twenty racks
21 with its forty bases of silver;
22 and for the back of the Dwelling, towards the west, you will make six frames,
23 plus another two for the angles of the back,
24 that will be joined, from bottom to top, up to the height of the first ring. This will be done with the two frames intended for the two angles.
25 There will then be eight frames with their sixteen silver bases, two under each frame.
26 In addition, you will make five crossbars of acacia wood to keep the frames on one side of the Dwelling in line,
27 five crossbars for the frames on the other side, and another five for those on the back, which faces west.
28 The central crossbar must pass halfway up the frames, from one end to the other.
29 Then you will overlay the frames with gold, you will forge gold rings to put the crossbars through them, and you will also overlay the latter with gold.
30 For the construction of the Abode you will keep in mind all the rules that were given to you on the Mountain.
31 You shall also make a veil of purple, violet, and scarlet, of crimson, and of fine reinforced linen, with artistically designed figures of cherubim.
32 You will hang it on four pillars of acacia wood covered with gold, which will be provided with hooks of the same metal and supported by four silver bases.
33 You will put the veil under the hooks, and behind it you will place the Ark of the Testimony. Thus the veil will mark the division between the Holy One and the Holy of Holies.
34 You will also place the lid on the Ark of the Testimony, in the Holy of Holies.
35 Outside the veil, you will set the table, and in front of it, on the south side of the Coin, the candelabrum. Thus the table will be located on the north side.
36 For the entrance of the tent you will make a curtain of purple, violet, and scarlet, of crimson, and of fine reinforced linen, all of this artistically embroidered.
37 And to support the curtain you will make five pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold; Their hooks will also be of gold, and you will rest them on bases of molten bronze.
1 Then you will make the altar of acacia wood; It will measure two and a half meters long by two and a half meters wide – that is, it will be square – and it will be one and a half meters high.

16 A curtain ten meters long, made of violet and scarlet purple, crimson and fine reinforced linen, artistically embroidered, will serve as a door. This curtain will hang from

17 All the pillars that surround the court will be joined together by silver rods; Its hooks will be silver and its bases bronze.

Israelites.

1 This is what you will do to consecrate them to serve my priesthood: take a bull and two rams without blemish,
2 and prepare unleavened bread, unleavened cakes kneaded with oil, and unleavened biscuits spread with oil with the best quality flour.
3 You will put all this in a basket and present it together with the bulls and the two rams.
4 Then you will order Aaron and his sons to come to the door of the Tent of Meeting and you will wash them with water.
5 Then you shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the mantle of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastplate, and you shall gird him with the belt of the ephod.
6 You will also place the turban on his head and the sign of his consecration on top of the turban.
7 Then you will take the anointing oil and pour it on his head and anoint him with it.
8 Immediately you will order his sons to come near; you will dress them in tunics,
9 You will gird them with a belt and adjust mitres for them. Thus the priesthood will belong to them by an irrevocable decree. In this way you will invest Aaron and his sons.
10 You will bring the bull up to the Tent of Meeting. Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on his head,
11 and you will sacrifice him before the Lord, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
12 You will take a little of its blood, anoint the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour out all the rest of the blood on the base of it.
13 Then you will take the fat that covers the entrails, the protuberance of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, and you will burn them on the altar.
14 But the meat, the hide, and the dung, you shall burn outside the camp. This is a sacrifice for sin.
15 Then you will take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons will lay hands on its head.
16 Once you have slain him, you will collect his blood and sprinkle it around the altar.
17 You will divide the animal into pieces, wash its entrails and its legs, and place them on the remaining parts and on its head.
18 Then you will let the whole ram burn on the altar. This is a burnt offering to the Lord, an offering that is burned with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
19 Then you will take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.

20 After you have slain him, you shall collect some of his blood and anoint with it the lobe of Aaron's right ear and the lobe of the right ear of his sons, the thumb of his right hand and the
thumb of his right foot. Then you will sprinkle this blood around
from the altar

right, because it is a ram offered for the investiture of priests.

36 On each of those days you shall offer a bull as a sin offering; you will offer it on the altar to atone for it and you will anoint it to consecrate it.

38 Every day you will offer two one-year-old lambs on the altar, and this permanently.

grandchildren, up to the third and fourth generation.

1 The Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
2 Speak to the Israelites in these terms: You may eat any land animal
3 that has split hooves – that is, divided into two halves – and that chews the cud.
4 But you must abstain from eating the following animals, even though they have split hoofs or are ruminants: the camel,
5 the hyrax
6 and the hare, because they chew the cud, but do not have divided hooves;
7 and also the pig, because it has cloven hooves, but does not chew the cud: this one must be considered unclean.
8 You must not eat the meat of these animals or touch their carcasses, but you must consider them unclean.
9 Among the animals that live in water, whether in the sea or rivers, you may eat those that have fins and scales.

10 But any animal that lacks fins and scales must be considered unclean, among the creatures that move through the water and among the living things that are in the water,
whether in the sea or in the rivers.
11 They will not eat their flesh and will be repulsed by their carcasses.
12 Everything that lives in water and does not have fins or scales will be unclean to you.
13 They must also consider the following birds unclean – and therefore cannot eat them: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the sea eagle,
14 the kite, the various species of falcon,
15 all varieties of crows,
16 the ostrich, the swallow, the seagull,
17 the owl, the hock, the owl,
18 the ibis, the pelican, the vulture,
19 the stork, the various species of heron, the hoopoe and the bat.
20 Furthermore, you must consider all winged insects that walk on four legs unclean.
21 But among the animals of this class, all those whose hind legs are longer, and therefore can jump on the ground, may eat,
22 that is, all varieties of locusts and crickets.
23 Any other winged insect that has four legs will be unclean to you.
24 Because of these animals, you may become unclean. Whoever touches their corpses will be unclean until the evening.
25 Whoever picks up the corpse of one of them must wash his clothes and will be unclean until the evening.
26 Likewise, all animals that do not have cloven hooves and that do not chew the cud will be unclean for you. Whoever touches them will be unclean.
27 All four-legged animals that walk on the soles of their feet will be unclean to you. Whoever touches their corpses will be unclean until the evening,
28 and whoever lifts up the corpse of one of them must wash his clothes and will be unclean until the evening. You must consider them impure.
29 Among the small animals that crawl on the ground, the following will be unclean for you: the mole, the mouse, and the various species of lizards;
30 the different kinds of lizards, the salamander and the chameleon.
31 You must consider all these small animals unclean. Whoever touches their corpses will be unclean until the evening.

32 The object on which the dead body of any of them falls will also be unclean, whether it is a wooden object, a garment, leather, a bag, or
anything else that is useful. These objects must be
immersed in water and will be unclean until evening; then they will be pure.
33 If one of these corpses falls into a clay pot, everything inside it will be unclean and the pot must be broken.
34 Any food that comes into contact with the water contained in that vessel will be unclean, and any drink will become unclean because of that vessel.
35 The object on which any of those corpses falls will be unclean. If it is an oven or a hearth, they will have to be torn down: they are impure, and you will have to consider them as such.
36 However, the fountain or the cistern where the water is collected will remain pure, but whoever touches one of those corpses will be unclean.
37 And if a corpse falls on the seed to be sown, it will be pure.
38 On the other hand, if water is thrown on the seed and some of those corpses fall on it, you must consider it unclean.
39 If an animal dies that you can eat, whoever touches the carcass will be unclean until the evening.
40 Whoever eats meat from that carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until the evening; and whoever lifts up the corpse must wash his clothes and will be unclean until the evening.
41 All animals that crawl on the ground are an unclean thing: it is not permitted to eat them.

42 Therefore you shall not eat any creeping thing that crawls on its belly, any insect that walks on four legs or has many legs, and any other animal that crawls on the ground,
because they are something unclean.
43 Do not defile yourselves because of these animals. Do not incur impurity because of them, so as not to be contaminated.
44 For I am the Lord your God, and you must sanctify yourselves and be holy, because I am holy. Do not incur impurity because of those animals that crawl on the ground.
45 For I am the Lord, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. You will be holy, because I am holy.
46 These are the instructions regarding animals, birds, all living creatures that move in the water, and all other animals that crawl on the ground.
47 Thus a distinction will be established between the pure and the impure, and between the living beings that are permitted to be eaten and those that cannot be eaten.

1 The Lord said to Moses and Aaron:

2 When a swelling, a rash, or a shiny spot appears on a person's skin, suggesting a case of leprosy, the person shall be brought to Aaron the priest or one of his sons,
priests,

3 which will examine the condition. If the hair in the affected area has turned white, and it appears more sunken than the rest of the skin, it is a case of leprosy. The priest, after having
observed, he must declare that person impure.

4 If the shiny spot is whitish but does not appear deeper than the skin and the hair that covers it has not turned white, the priest will keep the affected person isolated for seven
days.
5 On the seventh day he will examine her again and if he finds that the condition remains stationary and has not spread through the skin, the priest will keep her isolated for seven more days.

6 On the seventh day he will examine again, and if the disease has subsided and has not spread to the skin, he will declare the sick person clean; It is nothing more than an eruption. The sick person will wash his clothes and be pure.
7 But if after he has presented himself to the priest and has been declared pure, the rash continues to spread on the skin, he must be presented again to the priest.
8 And if he sees that the rash has spread, he must declare him unclean, because it is leprosy.
9 When symptoms of leprosy appear in a person, he or she will be taken to the priest.
10 If he discovers a whitish swelling on the skin, which has turned the hair white, and if an ulcer has formed on the swollen part,
11 then it is chronic leprosy. The priest must declare the sick person impure, without needing to isolate him, because he is certainly impure.
12 But if the leprosy spreads until it completely covers the skin of the affected person, from head to toe, as far as the priest can see,
13 and if, upon examination, he finds that the leprosy covers the entire body, then he must declare the affected person pure. It is pure, because it has become totally white.
14 However, as soon as an ulcer appears, it is unclean.
15 When the priest sees the ulcer, he will declare it unclean: the ulcer is unclean because it is leprosy.
16 But if the ulcer turns white again, the sick person will go to the priest again,
17 and he will examine it. If the condition has returned to white, the priest will have to declare the affected person pure, because he or she is pure.
18 If inflammation appears on a person's skin and then heals,
19 But in the place where the inflammation was, a whitish swelling or a pale reddish spot forms, the sick person must present himself to the priest.

20 If the priest sees that the affected area is deeper than the skin, and that the hair has turned white, he must declare it unclean: it is a case of leprosy that has proliferated in the inflammation.
21 But if he notices that there was no whitening of the hair or sinking of the epidermis, but that the condition subsided, he will keep the sick person isolated for seven days,
22 and if the inflammation continues to spread through the skin, you must declare it unclean: it is a real illness.
23 On the other hand, if the spot remains stationary and does not spread, it is the scar of inflammation, and therefore, the priest must declare the affected person pure.
24 If a person is burned with fire and a shiny pale reddish or whitish spot forms on the burn,

25 the priest will examine her. If the hair on the shiny spot has turned white and the affected part appears more sunken than the rest of the skin, it is leprosy that has proliferated in the burn.
The priest must declare the sick person unclean, because he is leprosy.
26 But if the priest finds that there is no whitening of the hair or sinking of the epidermis, and that the stain has been receding, he will keep the sick person isolated for seven days.
27 On the seventh day he will examine him, and if the disease has spread to the skin, the priest must declare him unclean: it is a case of leprosy.

28 But if the stain remains stationary, without spreading across the skin, and loses intensity, it is simply the effect of the burn. The priest will have to declare it pure, because it is nothing more than the
burn scar.
29 If a man or woman has a condition in the head or chin,

30 the priest will examine the affected part. If this appears more sunken than the rest of the skin, and the hair has become yellowish and weak, the priest will have to declare the sick person impure:
It is ringworm, that is, leprosy of the head and chin.

31 But if the priest verifies that the area affected by ringworm does not appear more sunken than the rest of the skin, and that there is no black hair in it, he will keep the patient isolated for seven days.
32 On the seventh day he will examine the condition, and if the ringworm has not spread and there is no yellowish hair, and the affected area does not appear more sunken than the rest of the skin,
33 The sick person will shave, excluding the affected part, and the priest will keep him isolated for seven more days.

34 On the seventh day he will undergo a new examination, and if the ringworm has not spread through the skin and the affected area does not appear more sunken, the priest will have to declare him pure.
35 If after being declared pure, the ringworm spreads on the skin,
36 The priest will examine him, and if the ringworm has spread, he will not need to check for yellowish hair: the sick person is unclean.

37 On the other hand, if you notice that the ringworm remains stationary and that black hair has grown in the affected area, the ringworm is cured. The person is pure, and the priest must declare him as such.
38 If a man or woman has shiny white spots on their skin,
39 and the priest sees that the spots are a faint white, it is an eczema that has broken out on the skin: that person is pure.
40 If a man's hair falls out and he becomes bald, he is pure.
41 If he loses his hair on the front of his head and becomes bald on his forehead, he is also pure.
42 But if on the bald part, whether on the forehead or on the back of the head, a pale reddish condition appears, it is leprosy that has proliferated on the bald part.
43 The priest will examine him, and if the swelling in the affected area is pale reddish in color and looks like leprosy on the skin of the body,
44 is about a leper. That person is impure, and the priest must declare him as such: he has leprosy on his head.
45 The person affected by leprosy will have torn clothes and loose hair; He will cover up to his mouth and shout: “Unclean, unclean!”
46 He will be unclean as long as his illness lasts. Because he is impure, he will live apart and his dwelling will be outside the camp.
47 When a leprous spot appears on a woolen or linen garment
48 – in the woof or warp of wool or linen – or in leather, or in something made of leather,
49 If the spot is yellowish or reddish, it is a leprosy spot and should therefore be shown to the priest.
50 He will examine it and keep the affected object isolated for seven days.

51 On the seventh day he will examine the stain again, and if it has spread on the garment - in the woof or warp - or on the leather - whatever the use for which it is intended - it is
malignant leprosy: that object is impure
52 and it will be burned. Since it is malignant leprosy, it must be consumed by fire.
53 But if the priest finds that the stain has not spread,
54 will order the object containing it to be washed and will keep it isolated for seven more days.

55 The priest will examine the stain after it has been washed: if it has not changed its appearance, even if it has not spread, the object is impure and you must burn it: it is corrosion, whether in the

56 But if the priest finds that the stain has diminished after being washed, he will remove it from the clothing or the leather, the woof or the warp.
57 And if it appears again, it is a contagious outbreak: the object must be consumed by fire.
58 But if the stain disappears from the clothing - from the woof or from the warp - or from the leather item that has been washed, it will be washed again, and then it will be pure.
