17 Clothes or leather on which semen has been spilled must be washed with water and will be unclean until evening.
18 And if a man has sexual relations with his wife, both of them shall bathe with water and be unclean until the evening.
19 When a woman has her period, she will be unclean for seven days, and whoever touches her will be unclean until the evening.
20 Whatever object she lies on or sits on while she remains unclean will be unclean.
21 Whoever touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and will be unclean until the evening.
22 Whoever touches any piece of furniture on which she sat must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and will be unclean until the evening.
23 If anyone touches an object that is on the bed or on the furniture where she sits, he will be unclean until the evening.
24 If a man lies with her, the woman's impurity is transmitted to him; He will be unclean for seven days, and whatever bed he lies on will be unclean.

25 When a woman has a discharge of blood for several days, outside the menstrual period, or when her menstruation lasts longer than it should, she will be unclean as long as the discharge lasts, as is
during menstruation.
26 Every bed you lie on and every piece of furniture you sit on will be unclean, just as during your menstrual period.
27 Whoever touches them will be unclean: he must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until the evening.
28 Once the discharge stops, the woman will count seven days, and then she will be pure.
29 On the eighth day, he will get two doves or two young pigeons, and present them to the priests at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

30 The priest will offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way, he will practice the rite of atonement before the Lord, in favor of that woman, because of the
impurity of its flow.
31 You must warn the Israelites about their impurities, so that they do not die because of them, because they have defiled my Dwelling, which is among them.
32 This is the ritual concerning the person who suffers from discharge: the one who has an ejaculation and therefore incurs impurity;
33 to the woman indisposed due to her menstruation; to the man or woman who suffers from discharge; and the man who sleeps with an impure woman.
1 The Lord spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron's two sons, who died when they stood before the Lord.

2 He said to him: Command your brother Aaron not to enter at any time into that part of the Sanctuary that is behind the veil, opposite the lid that covers the Ark. Otherwise he will die, because I
I appear in the cloud, on the lid of the Ark. Otherwise he will die, because I
I appear in the cloud, on the lid of the Ark.
3 He must enter the sanctuary only in this way: with a bull for a sin offering and with a ram for a burnt offering.

4 Furthermore, he must be dressed in the sacred linen tunic and covered with linen pants; He will gird himself with the linen sash and wear the linen turban. These are
sacred garments, which he will put on after having bathed with water.
5 Aaron will receive from the community of the Israelites two goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
6 He will offer his own bull as a sin offering, and will make a sin offering, and will make atonement for himself and for his family.
7 Then he will take the two goats and present them before the Lord, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
8 Then he will cast lots for the two goats: one lot for the Lord and the other for Azazel.
9 He will present the goat that lot has destined to the Lord, and offer it as a sacrifice for sin.
10 As for the goat destined by lot for Azazel, it will be placed alive before the Lord, to be sent into the wilderness for Azazel.
11 Aaron will offer his own bull as a sin offering and make atonement for himself and his family. He will immolate him,
12 And then he will take a censer full of coals taken from the altar that is before the Lord, and two handfuls of pulverized fragrant incense. He will carry all this behind the veil,
13 and he will put the incense on the fire before the Lord, so that the cloud of incense surrounds the lid that is on top of the Ark of the Testimony. That way he won't die.
14 Then he will take the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the lid, toward the east; and in front of the lid, he will make seven sprinklings of blood with his finger.

15 Immediately he will sacrifice the goat as a sacrifice for the sin of the people and carry its blood behind the veil. There he will do with it the same thing that he did with the blood of the bull: he will do the sprinkling
on the lid and in front of it.

16 Thus he will perform the rite of atonement for the Sanctuary, to purify it from the impurities and transgressions of the Israelites, whatever their sins, And he will do the same with the Tent of the
Encounter, who dwells with them in the midst of their impurities.

17 When Aaron enters the Sanctuary to perform the rite of atonement there, no one must be in the Tent of Meeting until he comes out. After practicing the rite of atonement for himself
himself, for his family and for the entire assembly of Israel,

18 Aaron will go out to the altar that is before the Lord to perform the rite of atonement on that altar: he will take blood from the bull and the goat, and put it on each of the horns of the
altar;
19 Then he will make seven sprinkles of blood with his finger on the altar, and thus he will purify it from the impurities of the Israelites, and he will sanctify it
20 When he has finished performing the rite of atonement in the sanctuary, in the Tent of Meeting, and in the altar, he will present the goat that is still alive,

21 Aaron will lay his two hands on the head of the animal and confess over it all the iniquities and transgressions of the Israelites, whatever sins they have committed,
carrying them on the goat's head. Then he will send him to the desert
means of a man designated for it.
22 The goat will carry upon itself, to an inaccessible region, all the iniquities that they have committed; and the animal will be released into the wilderness.
23 Aaron will enter the Tent of Meeting, take off the linen garments he had put on when he entered the sanctuary, and leave them there.

24 Then he will wash with water in the sacred area and put on his clothes again. Immediately he will go out to offer his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and to perform the rite of atonement
for himself and for the people.
25 He will make the fatty parts of the victim of the sin offering on the altar.
26 The man in charge of releasing the goat for Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe with water; then you can enter the camp again.

27 The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the sanctuary for the rite of atonement, will be brought outside the camp, and their
leather, its flesh and its excrement will be consumed by fire.
28 The person who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe with water; then you can enter the camp again.

29 This will be a decree for you forever: On the tenth day of the seventh month you will fast and abstain from doing any kind of work, whether the native or the foreigner who resides.
between you.
30 For on that day the ritual of atonement will be performed for you, to purify you from all your sins. Thus they will remain pure before the Lord.
31 That will be a day of complete rest for you, on which you must fast. This is a decree valid forever.

32 The priest who has been consecrated by anointing and invested to exercise the priesthood as successor to his father shall perform the rite of atonement; He will put on the linen garments
sacred vestments

33 and he will perform the rite of atonement for the most holy part of the Sanctuary, for the Tent of Meeting and for the altar. He will do the same for the priests and for all the members of the assembly.

34 This will be a decree for you forever: once a year the ritual of atonement will be performed for the Israelites for all their sins. And Moses did what the Lord
I had ordered him.
1 The Lord said to Moses:
2 Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites, and say to them, The Lord has given this command:
3 If a man of the house of Israel sacrifices an ox, a sheep, or a goat within the camp or outside it,

4 and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to the Lord, before his Dwelling, he will be considered guilty of blood: he has shed blood, and for this reason he will be excluded from
his town.

5 Thus it is commanded, so that the Israelites bring the victims that they usually sacrifice in the open field, and present them to the Lord, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, handing them over
to the priest so that they may be offered to the Lord as a sacrifice of communion.
6 Then the priest will sprinkle that blood on the altar of the Lord, at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and will burn the fatty parts as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

7 In this way, the Israelites will stop offering sacrifices to the satyrs, behind whom they are prostituting themselves. This will be a valid decree for them
always, throughout the generations.
8 Tell them further: If a man of the house of Israel or one of the foreigners who reside among you offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
9 and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to offer it to the Lord, he will be excluded from his people.
10 If a man of the house of Israel or any of the foreigners residing among you, like any kind of blood, I will turn my face against that person and exclude him from his people.

11 For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I myself have laid the blood on the altar for you, to be an atonement for you, since it is the blood that makes atonement, in
virtue of the life that is in it.
12 That is why I said to the Israelites, "None of you will eat blood, nor will the foreigner who resides among you."
13 And any Israelite or any of the foreigners residing among you, hunts an animal or a bird of those that it is permitted to eat, will shed its blood and cover it with earth.
14 For the life of all flesh is its blood. That is why I said to the Israelites: "Do not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood. "Whoever eats it will be cut off."
15 Anyone, whether native or foreign, who eats an animal killed or torn by wild animals, must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and will be unclean until the evening. Afterwards it will be pure.
16 And if he does not wash his clothes or bathe, he will bear his iniquity,
1 The Lord said to Moses:
2 Speak to the Israelites: I am the Lord your God.
3 You will not imitate the customs of Egypt, that country where you lived, nor those of Canaan, that land where I will make you enter. They will not follow his precepts,
4 but they will keep my laws and observe my precepts, acting in accordance with them. I am the Lord, your God.
5 You will keep my precepts and my laws, because the man who keeps them will live thanks to them. I am the Lord.
6 None of you will approach a woman of your own blood to have relations with her. I am the Lord.
7 You shall not have relations with your mother, your father's wife: she is your mother, and you must not have relations with her.
8 You shall not have relations with your father's wife: she is the very flesh of your father.
9 You shall not have relations with your sister, whether she is the daughter of your father or your mother, whether she was born in the house or outside it.
10 You will not have relations with your granddaughter, whether from your son or your daughter, because she is your own flesh.
11 You shall not have relations with the daughter of your father's wife: she is your father's descendant, your sister, and you must not have relations with her.
12 You shall not have relations with your father's sister: she is the same flesh as your father.
13 You shall not have relations with your mother's sister, because she is the same flesh as your mother.
14 You shall not have relations with your father's brother's wife: you shall not approach her, who is your aunt.
15 You shall not have relations with your daughter-in-law: she is your son's wife, and therefore you must not have relations with her.
16 You shall not have relations with your brother's wife: she is the same flesh as your brother.

17 You shall not have relations with a woman and her daughter at the same time, nor shall you marry her granddaughter, whether by her son or by her daughter: they are of the same flesh as that woman, and have relations with
them is depravity.
18 You shall not marry your wife's sister or have relations with her while your wife lives, provoking her rivalry.
19 You shall not approach a woman to have intercourse with her during the period of her menstrual impurity.
20 You shall not have relations with your neighbor's wife, making yourself unclean with her.
21 You shall not hand over any of your descendants to be sacrificed to Molech, and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the Lord.
22 You shall not lie with a man as if he were a woman: it is an abomination.
23 You shall not have sexual intercourse with a beast, making yourself unclean with it; and no woman will offer herself to an animal to unite with him: it is a perversion.
24 You will not become unclean in any of these ways, because the nations that I am going to drive out before you did so,
25 and that is why the country was desecrated. I have asked them to account for their iniquity, and the country has vomited out its inhabitants.
26 But you will observe my precepts and my laws, and you will not commit any of these abominations, whether the native or the foreigner who resides among you.
27 For all these abominations were committed by the men who inhabited the land before you, and therefore the land has been desecrated.
28 May the earth not also vomit you out because of your impurities, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
29 For everyone who commits one of these abominations will be excluded from his people.
30 Therefore, fulfill my commands and do not do any of the abominable things that were done before, so that you will not become unclean because of them. I am the Lord, your God.
1 The Lord said to Moses:
2 Speak these words to the entire community of Israel: You will be holy, because I, the Lord your God, am holy.
3 They will respect their mother and father, and observe my Sabbaths. I am the Lord, your God.
4 They will not turn to idols nor make gods of molten metal. I am the Lord, your God.
5 When you offer a sacrifice of communion to the Lord, you will do so in such a way that it will be accepted.
6 The victim must be eaten on the same day that the sacrifice is offered, or on the next day, and what remains on the third day will be burned.
7 And if anyone eats something on the third day, the victim will not be accepted, because it has become something harmful.
8 Whoever eats it will bear his guilt, because he has profaned what is consecrated to the Lord: that person will be excluded from his people.
9 At the time of harvesting, you shall not reap the entire field to its edges, nor shall you return to look for the ears that remain.
10 You will not pluck out the last cluster of your vineyard or gather the fallen fruit, but you will leave it for the poor and the foreigner. I am the Lord, your God.
11 You will not steal, lie, or deceive one another.
12 They will not swear falsely by my Name, for they would profane the name of their God. I am the Lord.
13 You shall not oppress your neighbor or despoil him; and you shall not withhold the hireling's wages until the next morning.
14 You shall not insult a blind man, but you shall fear your God. I am the Lord.
15 You will not do any injustice in judgments. You will not arbitrarily favor the poor nor be complacent with the rich: you will judge your neighbor with justice.
16 You shall not slander your countrymen, nor endanger the life of your neighbor. I am the lord.
17 You shall not hate your brother in your heart: you must rebuke him appropriately, so as not to bear a sin because of him.
18 You will not be vengeful toward your countrymen or hold a grudge against them. You will love your neighbor as yourself. I am the Lord.

19 You will observe my precepts. You will not cross your livestock with animals of another species. You will not sow two different kinds of seed in your field. You will not wear clothes
made with various materials.

20 If a man has sexual relations with a slave girl reserved for another man, but who has not been rescued or set free, compensation will be paid: they will not be punished with the penalty of
death, because the woman is not free.
21 The man will bring a ram to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, as a sacrifice of reparation to the Lord.
22 The priest will make atonement with the ram for that man before the Lord for the sin he committed, and the sin will be forgiven.

23 When you enter the land and plant fruit trees of all kinds, you must consider their fruits as something forbidden: for three years they will be left uncircumcised, and they cannot be
eat.
24 In the fourth year, all its fruits will be consecrated in a festival of praise to the Lord.
25 And only in the fifth year will you be able to eat the fruits and store the produce for yourselves. I am the Lord, your God.
26 You shall not eat anything that has blood in it. They will not practice magic or divination.
27 You shall not cut off the edge of your hair in a circle, nor cut off the edge of your beard.
28 No incisions will be made in the flesh for the dead, nor will tattoos be made. I am the Lord.
29 You shall not defile your daughter by prostituting her, lest the earth also become a prostitute and be filled with depravity.
30 They will observe my Sabbaths and respect my Sanctuary. I am the Lord.
31 They will not go to the spirits of the dead nor consult other spirits, becoming unclean because of them. I am the Lord, your God.
32 You will stand before the elder, and be respectful to the elderly. Thus you will fear your God. I am the Lord.
33 When a foreigner resides with you in your land, you shall not disturb him.
34 He will be to you as one of your countrymen and you will love him as yourself, because you were strangers in Egypt. I am the Lord, your God.
35 They shall not do any injustice in judgment, nor falsify measurements of length, weight, or capacity.
36 You must have a fair scale, a fair weight and a fair measure. I am the Lord, your God, who brought you out of Egypt.
37 Faithfully observe all my precepts and all my laws. I am the Lord.
1 And the Lord said to Moses:

2 You will say to the Israelites: Any man among you, or among the foreigners residing in Israel, who hands over any of his descendants to Molech, will be punished.
with death: the people of the country will stone him to death.
3 I will turn my face against that man and will cut him off from his people, because he gave one of his descendants to Molech, and thus defiled my Sanctuary and profaned my holy Name.
4 And if the people of the land close their eyes to that man, when he gives one of his descendants to Molech, and does not kill him,
5 I myself will turn my face against that man and his family, and I will cut him off from his people, along with all those who follow him, prostituting themselves after Molech.
6 And if a person consults the spirits of the dead or other spirits, and prostitutes himself after them, I will turn my face against that person and will cut him off from his people.
7 You will sanctify yourselves and be holy, because I am the Lord your God.
8 They will faithfully observe my precepts, I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
9 If anyone insults his father or mother, he will be punished with death, he has insulted his father and mother, and therefore his own blood will fall on him.
10 If a man commits adultery with his neighbor's wife, both of them will be punished with death.
11 If a man sleeps with his father's wife, it is as if he had relations with his own father; Therefore both will be punished with death, and their blood will fall on them.
12 If a man sleeps with his daughter-in-law, both of them will be punished with death; They have committed incest, and that is why their blood will fall on them.
13 If a man lies with another man as if he were a woman, both of them commit an abominable thing; For this reason they will be punished with death and their blood will fall on them.
14 If a man marries a woman and her mother, what he does is depravity: both he and they will be burned, so that there will be no such depravity among you.
15 If a man has sexual intercourse with a beast, he will be punished with death, and the beast will also be killed.
16 If a woman approaches a beast to join herself with it, both the woman and the beast will be killed: both will be punished with death and their blood will fall on them.

17 If anyone marries his sister, whether he is his father's or his mother's daughter, in such a way that he sees her nakedness and she sees his, they commit an ignominy: both will be cut off in the sight of their
compatriots. For having had relations with his sister, he must bear
his fault.

18 If a man lies with a woman during her menstrual period and has intercourse with her, both of them will be cut off from his people, because he has exposed the source of the woman's discharge and she
has discovered it.
19 You shall not have relations with your mother's sister or with your father's sister, because that would be like having relations with yourself: those who do so will bear their guilt.
20 If a man sleeps with his paternal uncle's wife, it is as if he had relations with the latter: those who do so will bear the guilt and die without having children.
21 If a man marries his brother's wife, what he does is indecent, because it is as if he had relations with his brother: those who do so will not have children.
22 Observe all my precepts and my laws, and put them into practice: then I will not vomit you out of the land where I will make you enter to live there.
23 Do not follow the precepts of the nation that I will drive out before you. Precisely because they did all these things, I repulsed them.
24 and I assured you that you would possess your land, that land flowing with milk and honey, the land that I will give you as a possession.

25 Therefore you must separate the clean animals from the impure ones, and the impure birds from the pure ones. Do not become abominable because of an animal, a bird or any other
vermin that crawl on the ground, because I separated them so that you
They consider them impure.
26 You will be holy, because I, the Lord, am holy, and I separated you from other people, so that you may belong to me.
27 The man or woman who consults the dead or other spirits will be punished with death: they will be stoned to death, and their blood will fall on them.
1 The Lord said to Moses: Speak these words to the priests, the sons of Aaron: No one shall incur impurity because of the corpse of one of his people,
2 unless it is a very close patient: your mother, your father, your son, your daughter or your brother;
3 or by the corpse of a virgin sister, who was very close to him, because she had not yet married.
4 But no one may incur impurity or profane himself because of a married woman in his family.
5 The priests shall not shave their heads, nor cut the edges of their beards, nor make incisions on their bodies.

6 They will be consecrated to their God and will not profane the name of their God; because they are the ones who present the offerings that are burned for the Lord – the food of their God – and that is why they must be holy.
7 Neither shall they marry a woman defiled by prostitution, nor a woman divorced from her husband, because the priest is consecrated to his God.
8 You must consider him holy, because he offers the food of your God. It will be holy to you, because I, the Lord who sanctifies you, am holy.
9 If a priest's daughter defiles herself by prostitution, she defiles her own father, and for this she will be burned.

10 The priest who has the preeminence among his brothers, the one on whose head the anointing oil was poured and who received the investiture to wear the vestments, shall not wear his hair.
loose nor tear their garments;
11 He will not enter where there is a dead body nor incur impurity, even if it is because of his father or his mother.
12 Nor will he depart from the Sanctuary of God, so as not to profane it, because he has upon him the consecration conferred with the anointing oil of his god. I am the Lord.
13 The priest must take a virgin as his wife.
14 He shall not marry a widow, nor a divorced woman, nor a woman defiled by prostitution. He will only do it with a virgin from his own people,
15 so as not to profane his descendants among his people, for I am the Lord who sanctifies him.
16 The Lord continued saying to Moses:
17 Speak to Aaron: None of your descendants who have a physical defect will come forward to offer the food of their God throughout the generations.
18 No one may approach who has a bodily defect: no one who is blind, lame, disfigured or deformed;
19 who has a broken leg or arm;
20 who is hunchbacked or stunted; that has a spot in the eyes; who is sick with scabies or ringworm, or who is castrated.
21 No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a defect shall present the burnt offerings to the Lord; Because he has a defect, he will not approach to present the food of his God.
22 Instead, he will be able to eat the food of his god, both the most holy things and holy waves.
23 But he will not enter behind the veil nor approach the altar; He has a bodily defect and should not desecrate those places that are consecrated to me, because I am the Lord, who sanctifies them.
24 Thus spoke Moses to Aaron and his sons, and to all the Israelites.
1 The Lord said to Moses:
2 Instruct Aaron and his sons to be very careful with the sacred gifts that the Israelites consecrate to me, lest they profane my holy Name. I am the Lord.

3 Therefore tell them this: If any of their descendants, in any generation, participate in a state of impurity in the sacred gifts that the Israelites consecrate to the Lord, it will be
excluded from my presence. I am the Lord.

4 No descendant of Aaron who is a leper or suffers from gonorrhea may eat of the sacred gifts until he is purified. If someone touches what has become impure because
of a corpse, or if he has an ejaculation,
5 or if he touches an animal or a human being that makes him unclean – whatever the kind of uncleanness may be –
6 If anyone touches any of it, he will be unclean until the evening and will not eat of the sacred things without first washing with water.
7 When the sun sets he will be pure, and then he will be able to eat the sacred things, because they are his food.
8 He shall not eat any animal killed or torn to pieces by wild beasts, otherwise he would incur impurity. I am the Lord.
9 Let them observe my prescriptions, lest they bear a sin because of the food, and die because they have defiled it. I am the Lord, who sanctifies you.
10 No stranger may eat of the sacred things, nor may a guest or a priest's servant do so.
11 But if a priest buys a slave with his money, he may eat of the sacred things; and also the slaves born in his house may eat his bread.
12 If a priest's daughter marries someone who is not a priest, she will not be able to eat the sacred offerings.
13 But if a priest's daughter is widowed or divorced and, having no children, returns to her father's house as in her youth, she may eat her father's bread. No stranger will eat of it;
14 And if anyone inadvertently eats a sacred offering, he must restore it to the priest, adding also a fifth of its value.
15 The priests will not allow the Israelites to desecrate the sacred gifts that they reserve for the Lord,
16 or that they bear a sin that requires reparation, for eating those sacred gifts. For I am the Lord, who sanctifies you.
17 The Lord said to Moses:

18 Speak these words to Aaron and to his sons and to all the Israelites: If a man of the house of Israel, or any of the foreigners residing in Israel, presents his offering to the Lord for a
holocaust – whether in fulfillment of a vow or as a voluntary offering –
19 for that offering to be accepted, it will have to be an ox, sheep or goat, male and without defect.
20 Do not offer anything that has any defect, because it will not be accepted.

21 And if anyone - whether in fulfillment of a special vow or as a voluntary offering - presents to the Lord as a communion sacrifice an animal of the larger or smaller livestock, so that this offering may be
accepted, it will have to be without defect: there will be no imperfection in it.
22 You must not offer or present as a burnt offering to the Lord any animal that is blind, damaged or mutilated, ulcerated, mangy or festering.
23 Instead, they may offer as a freewill offering an ox or a sheep with a limb that is too long or too short; but it will not be accepted from them in fulfillment of a vow.
24 Nor shall they offer animals with their testicles crushed, destroyed, torn off or cut off. They will not do any of this in their land,
25 Nor will they accept these animals from foreigners to offer them as food to their God, because there is a deformity in them and they have a defect. That is why they will not be accepted.
26 The Lord said to Moses:
27 When a calf, a lamb, or a goat is born, it will be with its mother for seven days, and from the eighth it will be accepted as a burnt offering to the Lord.
28 But they shall not sacrifice any livestock, large or small, together with their young, on the same day.
29 When you offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the Lord, do so in such a way that it will be accepted by you.
30 It will be eaten that same day; They will not leave anything for the next day. I am the Lord.
31 Faithfully observe my commandments. I am the Lord.
32 Do not profane my holy name, so that I may be sanctified among the Israelites. I am the Lord, who sanctifies you,
33 the one who brought them out of Egypt to be their God. I am the lord.
1 The Lord said to Moses:
2 Speak to the Israelites in these terms: These are my festivals, the festivals of the Lord in which you will call the liturgical assemblies:

3 For six days you will work, but the seventh will be a day of rest, of liturgical assembly, in which you will not do any work. It will be a Sabbath consecrated to the Lord, whatever the day.
place where they live.
4 The feasts of the Lord, the liturgical assemblies that you will convene in due time, are as follows:
5 In the first month, on the fourteenth day, at sunset, the Lord's Passover will be celebrated,
6 and on the fifteenth of that same month the festival of unleavened bread will take place in honor of the Lord. For seven days they will eat unleavened bread.
7 On the first day they will have a liturgical assembly and will not do any menial work.
8 For seven days they will offer a burnt offering to the Lord. On the seventh day there will be a liturgical assembly and you will not do any menial work.
9 The Lord said to Moses:
10 Speak these words to the Israelites: When you enter the land that I am giving you and when you gather the harvest, you will give the first sheaf to the priest.
11 On the day after the Sabbath, he will offer it to the Lord with the gesture of presentation, so that it may be accepted for them;
12 And on that same day you will sacrifice as a burnt offering to the Lord a lamb that is one year old and without blemish.

13 Together with it, they shall present, as an offering that is burned with a pleasing aroma to the Lord, an oblation consisting of two tenths of the best quality flour mixed with oil; and they will add as
libation one and a half liters of wine.

14 Before that day, that is, before giving the offering to their God, they will not eat bread, roasted grain, or young ears of grain. This is a decree valid forever, throughout the generations, whoever
be the place where they live.
15 They will also count seven weeks, from the day on which they deliver the sheaf offered with the gesture of presentation, that is, from the day after the Sabbath. The weeks must be complete.
16 Therefore you will have to count until the day after the seventh Sabbath: fifty days in all. Then they will offer to the Lord an offering of new grain.

17 You will bring two loaves from your homes, to be offered with the gesture of presentation. Each bread must be prepared with two tenths of the best quality flour and cooked
after fermenting: they are the first fruits to the Lord.

18 Along with the bread, seven lambs of one year old and without blemish, one bull and two rams, with their corresponding oblations and libations, shall be offered as a burnt offering to the Lord, as an offering to be
It burns with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
19 They shall also offer one goat as a sin offering, and two one-year-old lambs as a fellowship offering.

20 The priest will offer them to the Lord with the gesture of presentation, together with the bread of the first fruits and two lambs. All this is a thing consecrated to the Lord and will belong to the priest.

21 That same day they will make a call: you will have a liturgical assembly and no menial work can be done. This is a decree valid forever, throughout the generations,
whatever place they live,

22 When you gather the harvest of your land, you will not reap the entire field to its edges, nor will you return to look for the fallen ears: you will leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the Lord, you
God.
23 The Lord said to Moses:
24 Speak to the Israelites: The first day of the seventh month will be a day of rest for you, a commemoration announced by the sound of trumpets, and there will be a liturgical assembly.
25 You will not do any menial work and you will present an offering that is burned in honor of the Lord.
26 The Lord said to Moses:
27 Furthermore, the tenth day of that seventh month will be the day of Atonement. There will be a liturgical assembly, they will observe the fast and present a burnt offering to the Lord.
28 Throughout that day you will not do any work, because it is the Day of Atonement, when the ritual of atonement will be performed for you before the Lord your God.
29 Whoever does not observe fasting throughout that day will be excluded from his people.
30 And I will destroy from his people anyone who does any kind of work.
31 You will not do any work. It is a decree valid forever, throughout generations, wherever they live.
32 This will be a day of rest for you, on which you will observe fasting, On the ninth day of the month in the evening, from that afternoon until the next, you will observe this rest.
33 The Lord said to Moses:
34 Speak to the Israelites in these terms: Furthermore, on the fifteenth day of this seventh month the Feast of Huts will be celebrated in honor of the Lord, for seven days.
35 On the first day there will be a liturgical assembly, and you will not do any menial work.

36 For seven days they will present a burnt offering to the Lord. On the eighth day, they will celebrate a liturgical assembly and present an offering that is burned to the Lord: it is a solemn assembly and
you will not do any work.

37 These are the festivals of the Lord, in which you will convene liturgical assemblies and present burnt offerings to the Lord - burnt offerings, oblations, sacrifices and libations, according to
corresponds to each day–
38 in addition to the Sabbaths of the Lord, and the gifts, the votive offerings and the voluntary offerings that you offer to the Lord.
39 On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when they have harvested the produce of the land, they will celebrate the Feast of the Lord for seven days. The first and eighth days will be rest.
40 On the first day you will take fruit from the best leafy trees and willows in the river, and you will rejoice in the presence of the Lord your God for seven days.
41 Thus they will celebrate the Feast of the Lord for seven days every year, in the seventh month. This is a decree valid forever, throughout generations.
42 For seven days they will live in huts. This is how all the natives of Israel will have to do it,
43 so that future generations may know that I made the Israelites live in huts when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord, your God.
44 In this way, Moses declared to the Israelites what the festivals of the Lord were.
1 The Lord said to Moses:
2 Command the Israelites to bring pure ground olive oil for the lampstand, so that a lamp can be kept burning permanently.

3 Aaron must prepare it in the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil that is before the Ark of the Testimony, so that it burns regularly before the Lord throughout the night. This is a decree
valid forever, throughout generations.
4 He will arrange the lamps before the Lord, on the pure gold lampstand, so that they burn regularly.
5 Also prepare twelve cakes of the best quality flour, using two-tenths of a measure for each one.
6 Then you will place them in the presence of the Lord, in two rows of six, on the table of pure gold;
7 and on each row you will put pure incense, as a memorial of bread, as an offering that is burned to the Lord.
8 This will be arranged every Sabbath before the Lord: it is a permanent obligation for the Israelites.

9 The loaves will be for Aaron and his sons, and they must eat them in the sacred area, because it is a most holy thing. It is a right that Aaron will always have over the
offerings that are burned for the Lord.
10 Among the Israelites a man appeared, whose mother was an Israelite and his father was an Egyptian. When a fight broke out between the latter and an Israelite,
11 The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed against the Name, uttering a curse. Then they brought him to Moses—his mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, and she was of the tribe of Dan.
12 And the man was taken into custody, until a decision could be made by an oracle from the Lord.
13 The Lord said to Moses:
14 “Bring the blasphemer out of the camp; Let all who heard him put their hands on his head, and let the whole community stone him to death.
15 Then say to the Israelites: Any man who curses his God will bear his sin.

16 Whoever utters a blasphemy against the name of the Lord will be punished with death: the entire community must stone him to death. Whether foreigner or native, if he utters a blasphemy against
Name, will be punished with death.
17 Whoever mortally wounds any man will be punished with death.
18 Whoever mortally wounds an animal will pay the corresponding compensation: life for life.
19 If anyone harms his neighbor, the same thing that he did will be done to him:
20 fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; The same injury will be done to him that he has caused to the other.
21 Whoever kills a man will be punished with death.
22 There will be only one right for you, valid for both the foreigner and the native. For I am the Lord, your God.
23 Thus spoke Moses to the Israelites. Then they took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him to death. In this way they executed the order that the Lord had given to Moses.
1 The Lord said to Moses on Mount Sinai:
2 Speak to the Israelites: When you enter the land that I am giving you, the land will observe a Sabbath in honor of the Lord.
3 For six years you will sow your field, prune your vineyard, and harvest its produce.
4 But in the seventh year the land will have a Sabbath of rest, a Sabbath in honor of the Lord: you shall not sow its field nor prune your vineyard;
5 You will not reap the new growth of the last harvest nor gather the grapes of your vineyard that is left unpruned: it will be a year of rest for the land.
6 However, you, your male and female slave, and your hired servant, as well as the guest who resides with you, may eat whatever the land produces during its rest;
7 and also the cattle and animals that are on the land may eat all its products.
8 You must count seven weeks of years – seven times seven years – so that the period of the seven weeks of years adds up to a total of forty-nine years.
9 Then you will blow a loud trumpet blast: on the tenth day of the seventh month – the Day of Atonement – you will blow the trumpet throughout the entire land.

10 Thus they will sanctify the fiftieth year, and proclaim a deliverance for all the inhabitants of the land. This will be a jubilee for you: each one will recover his property and return to his
family.
11 This fiftieth year will be a jubilee for you: you will not sow or reap what grows again from the last harvest, nor will you harvest the vineyard that is left unpruned;
12 because it is a jubilee, it will be sacred to you. They will only be able to eat what the field produces by itself.
13 In this jubilee year each of you will return to your property.
14 When you sell or buy something from your fellow countrymen, do not defraud one another.
15 When purchasing, you will take into account the number of years that have passed since the jubilee; and when selling, your compatriot will take into account the number of productive years:
16 The greater the number of years, the greater the price you will pay; and the fewer the number of years, the lower that price will be, because what he sells you is a certain number of crops.
17 Do not defraud one another, and fear your God, for I am the Lord your God.
18 Observe my precepts and faithfully fulfill my laws; so they will live safely on this earth.
19 The land will bear its fruits, you will eat until you are satisfied and you will live safely in it.
20 But perhaps you are wondering, "What will we eat in the seventh year, if we cannot sow or gather our produce?"
21 I will send you my blessing in the sixth year, and it will produce a harvest sufficient for three more years.
22 Thus, when you sow in the eighth year, you will still be eating the grain of that harvest; and they will continue to eat it until the ninth, until the harvest arrives.
23 The land cannot be sold permanently, because the land is mine, and you are to me as foreigners and guests.
24 In any land you own, you will grant the right of redemption over the land.
25 If your brother is left destitute and is forced to sell part of his property, his closest relative will come to exercise the right of redemption over what his brother has sold.
26 If he has no one who can exercise this right, but he acquires for himself what is necessary for the ransom,
27 will calculate the years that have passed since the sale, return the difference to the buyer, and thus you can return to your property.

28 If he lacks sufficient means to recover it, what has been sold will remain in the possession of the buyer until the year of jubilee, but in the year of jubilee it will be released, and the seller will return to his
property.
29 If someone sells a house in a walled city, his right to redeem it will last until the year of its sale is completed; the remaining period will last a whole year.
30 If it has not been redeemed before the end of that year, the house will definitely pass to the buyer and his descendants, and will not be redeemed at the jubilee.
31 But the houses of the towns that do not have walls will be considered as the open field: they can be rescued, and in the year of jubilee they will be free.
32 As for the cities of the Levites, they will always have the right of ransom over the houses that are in the cities that they own.

33 And if any of the Levites does not redeem it, the house that he sold - and which is his property - will be free in the jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are his property
among the Israelites.
34 But the fields surrounding their cities cannot be sold, because they are their property forever.
35 If your brother is left destitute and has nothing to pay you, you will support him as if he were a stranger or a guest, and he will live with you.
36 Do not demand any kind of interest from him: fear your God and let him live with you as a brother.
37 Do not lend him money at interest, nor give him food to profit.
38 I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
39 If your brother is left destitute and is forced to sell himself to you, do not impose slave labor on him.
40 He will be at your service as an employee or as a guest, and will work for you only until the jubilee year.
41 Then he will be free with his children, return to his family, and return to his parents' property.
42 For they are my servants: I brought them out of Egypt, and therefore they must not be sold as slaves,
43 You shall not exercise despotic power over your brother, but you shall fear your God.
44 The male and female slaves that you have will come from neighboring nations: only from them will you be able to acquire them.
45 You may also acquire them among the children and relatives of foreigners residing among you, among those who were born in Israel. They will be your property,

46 and they may leave them as an inheritance to their children, so that they may possess them as perpetual property. They may have these as slaves; but no one can exercise despotic power over his brothers
Israelites.
47 If a foreigner living with you becomes prosperous, and your brother, on the other hand, remains destitute and has to sell himself to that foreigner or to a descendant of a foreigner's family,
48 Your brother will have the right to ransom, even after he has been sold. One of his brothers will be able to rescue him,
49 your uncle, your cousin, or some other close relative; and if he has the resources, he will be able to rescue himself.

50 Together with him who bought it, he will calculate the total number of years from the time it was sold until the year of jubilee; and the sale price will depend on the number of years, also computing the time in
who worked for him, as if he were a salaried employee.
51 If there are still many years left, you must return a sum proportionate to the sale price for its ransom;
52 and if there are a few years left until the jubilee year, the calculation for the payment of the ransom will be made according to the remaining years.
53 In any case, your brother will serve the buyer year after year, as if he were a hired servant; and do not allow him to treat him despotically before your very eyes.
54 If he is not rescued during those years, he will be free in the jubilee year, along with his children.
55 For it is me whom the Israelites must serve: they are my servants, whom I brought out of Egypt. I am the Lord, your God.
1 Do not make idols or erect images or commemorative stones; Do not place engraved stones in your land to bow down before them, for I am the Lord your God.
2 Observe my Sabbaths and respect my Sanctuary. I am the Lord.
3 If you live according to my precepts and faithfully observe my commandments,
4 I will send the rains in due time, so that the earth will give its products and the plants of the field their fruits.
5 Then the time of threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the vintage, until the sowing. They will eat bread until they are satisfied and will live safely in their land.
6 I will ensure peace in the land and you will rest without anyone disturbing you: I will drive away harmful animals from the land and no sword will devastate the land
7 You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall to the sword before you.
8 Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred will chase ten thousand; and your enemies will fall to the sword before you.
9 I will look kindly on you, make you fruitful and numerous, and keep my alliance with you.
10 They will eat old grain that has been stored for a long time, and they will have to throw away the old grain to make room for the new.
11 I will put my Dwelling in your midst and will not dislike you;
12 I will always be present among you: you will be my People and I will be your God.
13 I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt so that you would no longer be your slaves. I broke the bars of their yoke and made them walk with their heads held high.
14 But if you do not obey me and do not keep all these commandments;
15 if they despise my precepts and show aversion to my laws; If you stop practicing my commandments and break my covenant,

16 I, in turn, will treat them in the same way: I will cause terror to dominate them – the weakness and fever that consume the eyes and waste away the life. They will plant their seeds in vain, because
their enemies will eat them.
17 I will turn my face against you and you will be defeated by your enemies; They will be subjected to their adversaries and will flee even if no one pursues them.
18 And if they do not obey me despite this, I will continue to correct them seven times more because of their sins.
19 I will humble that enormous pride, making the sky to you like iron and the earth like bronze.
20 Then they will exhaust their strength in vain, because the earth will not produce its products nor the plants of the field their fruits.
21 And if you continue to displease me and refuse to obey me, I will punish you again seven times more because of your sins.
22 I will send the wild beasts against you to snatch your children and destroy your livestock. They will decimate them, and your roads will be deserted.
23 And if despite this they do not correct themselves and continue to annoy me,
24 I will also turn against you and punish you seven times more because of your sins.

25 I will draw against you a sword that will avenge the transgression of the covenant. Then they will seek refuge in their cities, but I will send them the plague and they will fall into the power of the enemy.
26 When I deprive you of daily sustenance, ten women will bake your bread in their oven, and will distribute it so well measured that you will eat but not be satisfied.
27 And if you still do not obey me and continue to contradict me,
28 I will treat them with indignation and will severely rebuke them seven times more because of their sins.
29 They will eat the flesh of their sons and their daughters,
30 And I will destroy your high places, I will tear down the altars where you offer incense, and I will throw your carcasses on your lifeless idols. I will dislike them,
31 I will turn their cities into ruins, I will desolate their sanctuaries, and I will no longer inhale the aroma of their sacrifices.
32 I will devastate the land, to such an extent that its enemies will be terrified when they come to occupy it.
33 I will scatter you among the nations and draw the sword behind you. Thus the country will become a desert and its cities, ruins.
34 And during all the time that it will be desolate, while you live in the country of your enemies, the land will pay the sabbatical years it owes.
35 In all the time of desolation, she will finally observe the rest that she did not observe in her sabbatical years, when you lived in her.

36 I will fill the survivors with panic in the land of their enemies: the sound of a falling leaf will drive them away: they will flee as one flees from the sword, and they will fall even though
no one chases them.
37 Without being pursued, they will trample each other as if they had a sword before them. You will not be able to stand before your adversaries,
38 But they will perish among the nations and be swallowed up by the land of their enemies.
39 And those who still survive will perish in the land of their enemies, because of their own faults, and also because of the faults of their fathers.
40 Then they will confess the sins that they and their parents committed for having been unfaithful to me, and above all, for having turned against me.
41 But I will also turn against them and bring them into the country of their enemies. Thus their uncircumcised heart will be humbled and they will pay for their sins.
42 I will remember my covenant with Jacob, with Isaac, and with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

43 But first, the land will be abandoned and will pay the sabbatical years it owes, while it is desolate due to their absence; and they will also pay for their guilt, since
They despised my laws and abhorred my precepts.

44 But even then, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or dislike them to the point of annihilating them and annulling my alliance with them: because
I am the Lord, your God.
45 I will remember for them the covenant that I established with their ancestors, with whom I brought out of Egypt in the sight of the nations to be their God. I, the Lord.
46 These are the precepts, the laws and the instructions that the Lord established between him and the Israelites on Mount Sinai, through Moses.
1 The Lord said to Moses:
2 Speak to the Israelites in these terms: If anyone offers as a vow to the Lord the sum equivalent to one person,
3 the following assessment will be applied: If it is a male from twenty to sixty years old, the sum will be fifty shekels of silver, in shekels of the Sanctuary;
4 and if it is a woman, the sum will be thirty shekels.
5 If the age is from five to twenty years, the sum will be twenty shekels for a male and ten for a female.
6 If the age is from one month to five years, the sum will be five shekels of silver for a male and three for a female.
7 If the age is sixty years or older, the sum will be fifteen shekels for a man and ten shekels for a woman.
8 But if the offerer is too poor to pay the established sum, he will present himself to the priest, who will set an equivalent proportionate to the resources of the one making the vow.
9 If someone gives an animal that can be presented to the Lord as an offering, the animal offered will be a sacred thing.

10 It is not allowed to change it or replace it with another, whether good for bad or bad for good. If someone substitutes one animal for another, both the animal offered and its substitute will be one thing.
sacred.
11 If it is an unclean animal, which cannot be presented as an offering to the Lord, it must be presented before the priest,
12 which will value it. Whether high or low, the appraisal set by the priest will be accepted;
13 and if someone wants to rescue the animal, they will have to add one fifth more to the established sum.
14 If a man consecrates his house to the Lord, the priest must value it. Whether high or low, the appraisal set by the priest will be accepted.
15 And if he who consecrated his house wishes to redeem it, he must add a fifth to the sum at which it has been valued, and thus it will be his again.

16 If a man consecrates any piece of land that he owns to the Lord, it will be valued according to the amount of seed that can be sown on it: fifty shekels of silver for every four hundred kilos of
barley seed
17 If he consecrates it in the year of the jubilee itself, this assessment will be maintained.
18 But if he consecrates his field after the jubilee, the priest must calculate the price according to the years remaining until the jubilee, and the corresponding discount will be made.
19 If the one who consecrated his field wants to redeem it, he will have to add a fifth to the sum at which it has been valued, and thus it will be his again.
20 But if he does not redeem his field and it is sold to another, it will no longer be redeemable:
21 When it is free in the jubilee year, it will be consecrated to the Lord as if it were interdicted land, and it will become the property of the priest.
22 If someone consecrates to the Lord a field that he bought, but it is not his own land,
23 must calculate the amount of its value until the year of jubilee, and the person will pay that same day the sum in which it has been valued, as a consecrated offering to the Lord.
24 In the jubilee year the field will return to the one who sold it, that is, to the true owner of the land.
25 All assessments will be made in sanctuary shekels; Each shekel is equivalent to twenty gueras.
26 However, no one may consecrate a firstborn of his livestock, since, because it is a firstborn, it belongs to the Lord: whether it is a calf or a lamb, it belongs to the Lord.

27 But if they are unclean animals, they may be redeemed for the sum at which they have been valued, adding one fifth of their value. If not rescued, the animal will be sold by the
established sum.

28 None of the property belonging to a person – be it a man, an animal, or a field owned by him – may be sold or redeemed if it has been consecrated to the Lord by total extermination:
All these things are exclusively consecrated to the Lord.
29 Nor can any person who must be exterminated be released, but must be put to death.
30 The tenth part of what the earth produces – both the planted fields and the fruit trees – belongs to the Lord: it is a thing consecrated to the Lord.
31 If a man wants to redeem any part of his tithes, he must add a fifth of its value.
32 A tenth of the livestock, large or small, that is, one in ten of all the animals that pass under the shepherd's staff, will be consecrated to the Lord.
33 No one should select between good and bad, or substitute one for the other. If he makes the substitute, they will be a sacred thing, and they will not be able to be rescued.
34 These are the commandments that the Lord gave to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.

13 having relations with another man, and her husband does not find out, because she secretly dishonored herself, and there are no witnesses nor was she caught in the act;
14 if the man has a fit of jealousy and is jealous of his wife, who has really dishonored herself; or, if a man feels jealous of a woman, even though she is innocent:

15 In such cases, the man must present his wife to the priest and give as an offering for her a tenth of a measure of barley flour. But he shall not pour oil on that offering nor
will add incense, because it is an oblation motivated by jealousy, of
a commemorative oblation, which should commemorate a crime.

priest, for his part, will have in his hands the bitter waters, bearers of
damn.

don't do you any harm.

swelling your belly.

The woman will remain an example of a curse among her people.

ritual.

corpse. That same day he will consecrate his head again:

1 In the first month of the second year after the departure from Egypt, the Lord said to Moses in the desert of Sinai:

about the Abode.

They broke camp.

1 Once the people complained bitterly before the Lord. When the Lord heard them, he was filled with indignation. The fire of the Lord was kindled against them and devoured the edge of the camp.

5 How we remember the fish we ate for free in Egypt, and the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic!
6 Now our throats are dry! We are deprived of everything, and our eyes see nothing but manna!
7 The manna looked like coriander seed and its color was like that of bdellium.

parents?

alone.

Egypt!", the Lord will give them meat to eat.

They began to speak in ecstasy; but then they didn't do it again.

They scattered them around the entire camp.

that you advance before them, by day in the pillar of cloud, and by night in the
column of fire

grandchildren to the fourth generation.

37 and said to him, “I sent for you urgently. Why didn't you want to come? Do I not have the means to shower you with honors?

40 Balak sacrificed cows and sheep and sent them to Balaam and made him go up to Bamot Baal, from where he could see a part of the people.

2 If among you, in one of the cities that the Lord your God will give you, there is a man or a woman who does what is evil in the sight of the Lord your God and breaks his covenant.
3 because you are going to serve others and bow down before them – before the sun, the moon or the entire Army of heaven – contrary to what I have commanded you.
4 and the fact comes to your knowledge, carry out a thorough investigation. And if it is true that the thing is like this, that such an abomination has been committed in Israel.
5 Bring the man or woman who has committed this crime to the gates of your city and stone them to death.
6 For someone to be sentenced to death, the testimony of two or more witnesses is required. No one will be sentenced to death based on the testimony of just one.
7 The witnesses will be the first to raise their hands against him to put him to death, and then all the people will do the same. Thus you will make evil disappear from among you.

8 If it is too difficult for you to judge a lawsuit for homicide, for claiming rights, for injuries. or any other cause that has arisen in your city, you will rise
to the place that the Lord your God chooses,
9 and you shall present yourself to the Levitical priests and to the sitting judge. You will present the case to them, and they will let you know the sentence.
10 You must comply with what they tell you in the place chosen by the Lord your God, proceeding in everything according to their instructions.
11 Coming in accordance with the decision they make and the sentence they pronounce, without deviating from what they indicate to you either to the right or to the left.
12 He who opens presumptuously, ignoring the priest who is there to serve the Lord your God, or the judge, that man will die. Thus you will make the evil of Israel disappear.
13 And when the people find out, they will be afraid and will stop acting presumptuously.

14 When you enter the country that the Lord your God will give you, when you take possession of it and live in it, if you ever say, "I am going to appoint a king to rule over me, like all the nations around me."
around me",

way."

19 He will keep it at his side and read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, observing all the words of this Law and putting these precepts into practice.

5 For the Lord your God chose the priest and his sons out of all your tribes, so that he would always be in his presence and minister in the name of the Lord.
6 If a Levite residing in any part of Israel moves of his own free will from one of your cities to the place chosen by the Lord his God,

13 You will be blameless in your dealings with the Lord your God.

15 The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me; You will make him arise from among you, from among your brothers, and it is to him that you will listen.

16 This is precisely what you asked the Lord. Your God, on Horeb, on the day of the assembly, when you said: "I no longer want to listen to the voice of the Lord my God, nor will I look at this great fire any longer,
because otherwise I will die.

21 You may be wondering, “How will we know that such a word has not been spoken by the Lord?”

1 When the Lord your God has destroyed the nations whose territory he gives you, and when you have dispossessed them and live in their cities and in their houses,

homicide.

life.

three.

your God.

is with you.

release.

delivery.

1 If you see your brother's ox or sheep lost, do not neglect them and go and return them to him as soon as possible.

24 Be a man of your word, and fulfill the vow you make spontaneously to the Lord your God, expressing it with your own lips.

2 Once he is away from home, if the woman marries another

in all your companies.

22 Always remember that you were a slave in Egypt, so I command you to act in this way.
1 If a dispute arises between two men and they go to court, they will be judged, and the innocent will be acquitted and the guilty will be condemned.

3 You may inflict up to forty blows on him, but no more, lest by punishing him more than necessary, the punishment will be excessive and your brother will be debased in your eyes.
4 You shall not muzzle the ox that threshes.

29 Then they asked themselves, "Who did this?" After finding out, they learned that it was Gideon, Joash's son.
30 Immediately they said to Joash, “Bring your son here. He must die, because he has torn down the altar of Baal and cut down the sacred pole that was next to it!

31 But Joash answered those standing before him, “Is it your business to defend Baal? Are you the ones who have to save him? If Baal is God, let him defend himself, since
Gideon tore down his altar. Whoever attempts to defend it will die before
"dawn."
32 Therefore, from that time on, Gideon was called Ierubaal, because they said, “Let Baal defend himself against him, since he broke down his altar!”
33 All Midian, Amalek, and the Easterners gathered together, crossed the Jordan, and camped in the plain of Izreel.
34 Then the spirit of the Lord came upon Gideon: he blew the trumpet, and the men of Abiezer gathered behind him.
35 He sent messengers throughout the territory of Manasseh, and they also joined him. He did the same in Asher, in Zebulun, and in Naphtali, and they all came to meet him.
36 Gideon said to God, “If you are really going to save Israel through me, as you have promised, grant me this:
37 I am going to spread a woolen fleece over the threshing floor; If dew falls only on the fleece, and all the rest remains dry, I will know that you will save Israel through me, as you have said.
38 This is how it happened: Gideon got up early in the morning, squeezed the dew out of the fleece, and filled a cup of water with it.

39 Then he said to God, “Do not be angry with me if I dare to speak to you again. I would like to do another test with the fleece: Let only the fleece remain dry and the entire ground be covered with dew.
40 This is what God did that night: only the fleece remained dry, while the ground was covered with dew.

1 The next morning, Jerubaal – that is, Gideon – got up early with the people who were with him, and they camped at En Jarod. Midian you had camped further north, at the foot of the hill
of Moré, over the valley.

"saved."
3 Therefore, proclaim in the ears of the people: "Whoever is afraid or trembles, let him return." So Gideon tested them, and twenty-two thousand men returned, leaving only ten thousand.

4 Then the Lord said to Gideon, “There are still too many people; Order them to go down to the edge of the water, and there I will test them. Only those I indicate will go with you;
the others will not accompany you.

5 Gideon brought the people down to the water, and the Lord said to him, “All those who drink with their tongues, as dogs lick, you will put aside; and to all who kneel
to drink, you will put them on the other.
6 Those who licked the water and put it in their mouths were three hundred; The rest of the troops, however, knelt to drink.
7 The Lord said to Gideon, “I will save them with these three hundred men and will put Midian into your hands. Let the bulk of the troops return, each one to his home.

8 The three hundred men gathered up the pitchers of all the troops, and also their trumpets, while Gideon sent away the other Israelites, leaving only those three hundred. The camp of

10 If you are afraid to attack, go down first with your servant Purá
11 and listen to what they say. "This way you will have courage and attack the camp." Gideon went down accompanied by Purah, his servant, to the end of the camp, where the guard posts were.

13 When Gideon arrived, he heard a man telling his companion a dream. «I had a dream, I told him; I saw a barley cracker coming rolling through the camp of Midian. Upon reaching a
tent, collided with it and overturned it, so that the tent fell to the ground.
14 His companion answered him, “This means nothing other than the sword of Gideon, the son of Joash, the man of Israel. "God has put Midian and all its camp into his hands."

15 When Gideon heard the story of the dream and its interpretation, he fell down to worship. Then he returned to the camp of Israel and said, “Up! The Lord has put the camp of
Midian.

17 Then he said, “Look closely at what I do, and do the same. When you get to the end of the camp, do the same as me.
18 I and all my companions will blow the trumpets; Then you too will blow the trumpets around the camp and shout: For the Lord and for Gideon!

19 Gideon and the hundred men who accompanied him arrived at the edge of the camp at the beginning of the midnight watch. When the replacement of the
sentinels, they blew the trumpets and broke the pitchers they were carrying
in the hand.

21 Each one remained still in his respective place, around the camp. Then the whole camp woke up, and they fled, screaming.

22 While the three hundred men were blowing the trumpets, the Lord caused the entire camp to turn their swords against each other. The troops fled to Bet Sitá, towards Sartan, to the shore of
Abel Mejolá, in front of Tabat.
23 Then the men of Israel gathered together from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh, and pursued Midian.

24 Gideon sent messengers throughout the mountain of Ephraim, saying, "Go down to meet Midian and take the fords to Beth Barah and the Jordan before them." The men of
Ephraim gathered together and occupied the fords as far as Beth Barah and the Jordan.

1 The people of Ephraim said to Gideon, “What have you done to us? Why didn't you call us when you went to fight against Midian? And they violently reproached him for it.
2 But he answered them, “What have I done compared to what you have done? A single bunch of Ephraim is worth more than the entire vintage of Abiezzer.
3 God gave you the leaders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. Compared to this, what have I managed to do? After he said these words to them, their animosity against him subsided.

5 Then he said to the people of Sukkot, "Please bring some bread for the troops that are with me, because they are exhausted with fatigue, and I am pursuing Zebah and Shalmunah, kings."
of Midian.

9 Then Gideon said to those of Penuel, “When I return victorious, I will tear down this tower.”

of sword.

13 After the battle, Gideon son of Joash returned up the slope of Jaresh.
14 Then he detained a young man from Sukkot, questioned him, and he gave him in writing the names of the leaders and elders of Sukkot. There were seventy-seven men.

15 Then he appeared before the men of Sukkot and said to them, "Here are Zebah and Shalmunah, the men for whom you mocked me, saying, 'Do you already have Zebah and Shalmunah in your power?'
Salmunah so that we can give bread to your hungry troops?
16 Then he took the elders of the city, gathered thorns and thistles from the desert, and smote the men of Sukkot with them.

19 Gideon answered them, "They were my brothers, my mothers' sons. I swear by the life of the Lord, if you had spared their lives, I would not kill them now!"
20 Then he said to Iether, his eldest son, "Kill them right here." But the boy was afraid to draw his sword, because he was still very young.

21 Zebah and Shalmunah said, "You kill us, for a man is measured by his courage." Gideon arose, killed Zebah and Shalmunah, and kept the ornaments that his camels were carrying in the
neck.
22 The men of Israel said to Gideon, "You rule us, and let your son and your grandson rule us after you, because you saved us from the power of Midian."
23 But Gideon answered them, “Neither will I rule over them nor will my son; only the Lord will govern them.
24 Then he added: "I am going to ask you one thing: that each of you give me a ring from what you have received as loot." Because the defeated were Ishmaelites, and that is why they had gold rings.
25 “We will gladly give them to you,” they replied. Then he spread out his cloak, and each Israelite placed on it a ring from his spoils.

26 The weight of the rings that he took was one thousand seven hundred shekels of gold, not counting the pins, the earrings, and the purple garments worn by the kings of Midian, and not counting
nor the camel collars.
27 With all this, Gideon made an ephod and installed it in his city, Ophrah. All Israel went to prostitute themselves there, in front of the ephod, which became a trap for Gideon and his family.

29 Ierubaal, son of Joash, left and remained in his house.
30 Gideon had seventy sons of his own, because he had many wives.
31 The concubine he had in Shechem also bore him a son, whom he named Abimelech.

35 And they did not thank the house of Jerubaal Gideon for all the good that he had done to Israel.

12 The trees said to the vine, "Come and reign over us."

28 Then Gaal son of Ebed exclaimed, “What authority does Abimelech have over Shechem that we are subject to him? Have not the son of Ierubaal, and of Zebul, his lieutenant, been subjected to
the people of Hamor, the father of Shechem? Why do we have to be subjected to
them?
29 If this people were put into my hands, I would drive out Abimelech, challenging him to strengthen his army and go out to fight!

37 But Gaal insisted: "They are people who come down the slope of the Navel of the Earth, and another group comes along the path of the Oak of the Diviners."

38 Then Zebul said to him, "Weren't you the one who became bold and said, 'Who is Abimelech that we should be subject to him?' There are the people you despised! Go now to

40 Abimelech pursued him: Gaal retreated, and many fell dead before reaching the city gate.
41 Abimelech returned to Arumah, and Zebul expelled Gaal and his brothers from Shechem, preventing them from living there.
42 The next day, the people of Shechem set out on the campaign trail. When Abimelech received the news,

They were in the field and they defeated them.

47 When Abimelech received the news that all the lords of Migdal Shechem were in one place,

"I."

Migdal Shechem, about a thousand men and women.

53 But a woman threw a millstone on his head and broke his skull.

1 After Abimelech, Tolah, son of Puah, son of Dodo, arose to save Israel. He was from Issachar, but he lived in Samir, on the mountain of Ephraim.

Gilead.

they settled there.

4 David added, “What has happened? Tell me everything. Then he said: “The troops fled from the battlefield and many of the people fell in the battle; Saul and his son Jonathan also died.

6 The young man answered, “I happened to be on Mount Gelboah, and suddenly I saw Saul leaning on his spear, while the chariots and horses were pursuing him closely.
7 When he turned around, he saw me and called to me. "Here I am," I told him.

19 He set out in pursuit of Abner, turning neither to the right nor to the left.

of his brother Asahel.

bite before sunset!

1 When Saul's son heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he was greatly discouraged, and all Israel was terrified.

1 All the tribes of Israel came to David in Hebron and said, “We are of your blood!

15 Ibjar, Elishua, Nepheg, Iafiah,

1 David again gathered together the choicest of Israel—thirty thousand men—

about the cherubs.

5 Meanwhile, David and the entire house of Israel made great celebrations in honor of the Lord, singing to the sound of zithers, harps, drums, cymbals, and cymbals.

7 Then the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah, and God struck him right there for that mistake. Thus he died next to the Ark of God.
8 David was moved, because the Lord had attacked Uzzah, and that place was called Peres Uzzah – which means "Breach of Uzzah" – to this day.

19 Then he distributed to all the people, to all the multitude of Israel, men and women, a loaf of bread, a cake of dates, and a cake of raisins per person. Then all the people left, each
one to his house.

his servants, as any useless person would undress!

1 When David settled in his house and the Lord gave him peace, freeing him from all his enemies around him,

8 And now this is what you will say to my servant David: Thus says the Lord of hosts: I brought you out of the pasture field, from behind the flock, to be the leader of my people Israel.

11 from the day that I appointed Judges over my people Israel. I have given you peace, freeing you from all your enemies. And the Lord has announced to you that he himself will make you a house.

12 Yes, when you have reached the end of your days and go to rest with your fathers, I will raise up after you one of your descendants, one who will come from your loins, and I will establish his kingship.

18 Then King David sat before the Lord and exclaimed, "Who am I, Lord, and what is my house that you have brought me here?"
19 And since this seemed too little to you, you have also made a promise to your servant's house, for a distant future. Is this what you usually do with men, Lord?
20 And what more could David say to you, if you, Lord, know your servant well?
21 Because of your word and according to your plan, you have done this great work, making it known to your servant.
22 That is why you are great Lord, there is no one like you, nor is there a God apart from you, because of everything we have heard with our own ears.

23 And who is like your people, like Israel, the only nation on earth whom God went to rescue to make them his people and give them a name? You have done things for him
great and terrible, driving out the nations and their gods before the
people you rescued from Egypt.
