1 Word that came to Jeremiah for all the Jews who lived in Egypt, those who lived in Migdol, in Tafnis, in Nof and in the district of Patrós:

2 Thus speaks the Lord of the armies, the God of Israel: You have seen all the evil that I brought upon Jerusalem and all the cities of Judah: today they are in ruins and without
inhabitants,
3 because of the evil that committed to wrong me, going to burn incense in honor of other gods that you didn't know them, nor you, nor their parents.
4 I sent them tirelessly to all my servants the prophets, to say to them: Do not do these things abominable things that I detest.
5 But they have not listened nor have they inclined his ear, so that he might turn from his wickedness, ceasing to burn incense to other gods.
6 Then my anger was poured out and my fury, and burned up the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, They have turned into ruin and desolation, as is happening today.

7 And now, thus speaks the Lord, God of hosts, the God of Israel: Why do they do such great evil to each other? yourselves? Why are men and women exterminated from the midst of Judah?
women, children and little ones, without leaving even a remnant for you?

8 This is what they get, wronging me with the works of his hands and burning incense to other gods in the country of Egypt, where they have entered to reside there, in order to become
exterminate and become a curse and ignominy among all the nations of
the land.

9 Have they forgotten the evil of their fathers, the wickedness of the kings of Judah and their princes, the wickedness of yourselves and your wives, committed in the country of Judah and in the streets
from Jerusalem?
10 To this day, they they have not felt compassion or fear and have not walked according to my Law and my precepts, which I set before you and your fathers.
11 Therefore thus speaks the Lord of the armies, the God of Israel: I turn my face against you for your evil, to exterminate all Judah

12 I will take the rest of Judah who insisted on enter Egypt to reside there, and everyone will completely disappear in the country of Egypt: they will fall under the sword, they will completely disappear by the
famine from the smallest to the greatest, they will die by sword and famine, and
They will become imprecation, devastation, curse and ignominy.
13 I will ask how much of those who live in the country Egypt as I asked Jerusalem by means of the sword, famine and the plague

14 There will be no fugitive or survivor for the rest of Judah, for those who entered the country of Egypt in order to reside there. As for returning to the country of Judah, where they long to return, no, they will not return,
except for some fugitives.

15 All the men who knew that their women burned incense to other gods, as did women present – a great assembly – and all the people who lived in the country of
Egypt, in Patros, answered Jeremiah:
16 "Concerning the word that we You have led in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to you.

17 On the contrary, we will carry out the promise that has come out of our mouth: we will burn incense to the Queen of the heavens and we will make libations to him, as we and our fathers did,
our kings and our princes, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of
Jerusalem. Then we were full of bread, we were happy and not
We saw the misfortune.
18 But since we stopped burn incense to the Queen of heaven and pour out libations to her, we lack of everything and we will disappear completely by sword and hunger.

19 And the women added: «When we burn incense to the Queen of heaven and pour out to her libations, do we make cakes with his figure and pour out libations to him without
the consent of our husbands?
20 Jeremiah then said to all the people, the men, the women and all the people who had given him that answer:

21 "Did not the Lord remember and remember present that incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, you and your fathers, your kings and your princes, and also
the people of the country?

22 And since the Lord could no longer bear the evil deeds and abominations that you committed, your country has become turned into a desert, a devastation and a curse, and has been left
depopulated, like today.

23 Because you burned incense and sinned against the Lord, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord nor walk according to their Law, their precepts and their testimonies, that is why this misfortune has befallen them,
like today."
24 Jeremiah said to all men and women women: "Listen to the word of the Lord, all you people of Judah, who They are in the country of Egypt:

25 Thus says the Lord of hosts, God of Israel: You women have declared this with your mouth, and with your hands have carried it out: "We will fulfill our vows to burn incense to

theirs.

1 Word that the prophet Jeremiah spoke to Baruch, son of Neriah, when he, under the dictation of Jeremiah, wrote these words on a scroll, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah:
2 “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says about you, Baruch:
3 You say: “Woe to me, for the Lord adds affliction to my pain! I am tired of moaning, and I cannot find rest!
4 This is what you will say to Baruch: Thus says the Lord: What I had built, I will demolish; What I had planted, I am going to uproot.

5 You seek great things for yourself! Do not look for them anymore, because I will bring disaster upon every living being - oracle of the Lord - but I will not make you keep your life as a booty.
wherever you go."
1 This is the word of the Lord that came to the prophet Jeremiah concerning the nations.

2 For Egypt, concerning the army of Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt, who was by the river Euphrates, at Carchemish, and whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, defeated in the fourth year
of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
3 Prepare your shield and buckler, and advance to battle!
4 Saddle the horses and let the riders ride! Form up with your helmets on, polish your spears, put on your breastplates!

5 But what do I see? They are terrified, they retreat! His warriors are defeated, they flee in disarray, without looking back. Terror spreads everywhere! –oracle
of the Lord.
6 The most agile cannot flee nor the bravest escape: to the north, on the banks of the Euphrates, they stumble and fall.
7 Who is this that rises like the Nile and whose waters surge like rivers?
8 It is Egypt that rises like the Nile and whose waters surge like rivers. He said: “I will go up, I will cover the earth, I will destroy the city and its inhabitants.
9 Charge, steeds, let the chariots advance in fury, let the mighty men come out, people of Cush and Put who wield the shield, and Lydians who draw the bow!

10 But that day is for the Lord of hosts a day of vengeance to take revenge on his adversaries. The sword devours and is satisfied, it is watered by its blood. For the Lord of hosts has a
sacrifice in the northern country, next to the Euphrates river.
11 Go up to Gilead, gather balm, virgin, daughter of Egypt! You multiply the remedies in vain, your wound does not heal.
12 The nations have known your ignominy, the earth is full of your cries, because one brave man stumbles against another and they both fall together.
13 Word that the Lord spoke to the prophet Jeremiah, when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to attack the country of Egypt.
14 Announce it in Egypt, proclaim it in Nigdol, make it heard in Nof and Taphnis! Say: Stand up, prepare yourself, for the sword devours all around you!
15 Why does Apis flee, why has your Bull not resisted? The Lord has run over him!
16 Your crowd stumbles and falls, and they say to each other: "Up, let us return to our people, to our native land, far from the destroying sword!"
17 Give this name to Pharaoh, king of Egypt: "Pure commotion, but at the wrong time."
18 I swear on my life, oracle of the King whose name is Lord of hosts, that someone will come, like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel above the sea!
19 Prepare your luggage for exile, daughter who lives in Egypt, because Nof will be a devastation, burned, depopulated.
20 Egypt was a magnificent calf, a horsefly from the North attacks her.

21 Even her mercenaries in her midst were like fattened lambs; but they also retreat, they flee all together, they do not resist. Because the day of their ruin is coming, the time when
They will have to account.
22 Listen! They are like a hissing snake, because they advance with impetus, they reach it with axes as if they were lumberjacks;
23 they cut down their forest – oracle of the Lord – although it was impenetrable. Because they are more numerous than locusts and cannot be counted.
24 The daughter of Egypt is ashamed, she is handed over to the people of the North!
25 The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, has said: “I am going to punish Ammon of Noah, Pharaoh and Egypt, all their gods and their kings, Pharaoh and those who trust in him.

26 I will deliver them into the hands of those who threaten their lives, into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and into the hands of his servants. But after this, Egypt will be inhabited as in
ancient times –oracle of the Lord–».

27 And do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, do not be afraid, Israel! For I will save you from a far country, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and live in peace,
calm and without anyone disturbing him.

28 Do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, declares the Lord, for I am with you. Yes, I will annihilate all the nations to which I myself expelled you, but I will not annihilate you:
I will correct with equity, although I will not leave you unpunished.
1 Word of the Lord, concerning the Philistines, which came to the prophet Jeremiah before Pharaoh defeated Gaza.

2 Thus says the Lord: Look! The waters rise from the North, they become an overflowing torrent; They flood the earth and what it contains, the city and its inhabitants. They shout
men, all the inhabitants of the country groan.
3 At the noise of their horses, at the roar of their chariots, at the tumult of their wheels, parents ignore their children, because their hands fail.
4 It is because of the day that comes to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off all help from Tire and Sidon. Because the Lord destroys the Philistines, the rest of the island of Caphtor.
5 Gaza shaved his head, Ashkelon is lost. Ashdod, rest of the Anakites, how long will you make incisions?
6 Ah, sword of the Lord! How long will you not rest? Go back to your pod, stay calm and calm down!
7 How can you rest, when the Lord gives you an order? Towards Ashkelon and towards the coast of the sea, there he has appointed him.
1 For Moab. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Woe to Nebo, for she is devastated! Kiriathaim has been taken, the citadel is humiliated and destroyed!
2 The glory of Moab is no more! In Heshbon they plot evil against her: "Come, let us extirpate her as a nation!" You too, Madmen, will be reduced to silence, the sword advances behind you.
3 Hear the cry of Joronaim: utter devastation and disaster!
4 Moab has been destroyed, the cries are heard all the way to Zoar!
5 Yes, people go up the hill of Luchit crying; yes, on the slope of Horonaim a cry is heard: "Disaster!"
6 Flee, every man for himself, like a bush in the desert!
7 Because you trusted in your works and your treasures, you too will be captured. Chemosh will go into exile, with his priests and his princes.
8 The destroyer will occupy every city, not a single one will escape, the valley will perish and the plateau will be laid waste, as the Lord has said.
9 Bring salt to Moab, for it will be completely destroyed; Their cities will be a desolation, where no one lives.
10 Cursed is he who negligently performs the work of the Lord! Cursed is he who turns away his sword from blood!

11 Moab lived peacefully from his youth, he rested on his dregs; They did not transfer it from vessel to vessel – it had not gone into exile. This way its flavor was preserved and its aroma was not altered.
12 Therefore, the days will come, declares the Lord, when I will send decanters to decant it; they will empty their vessels and break their jars.
13 And Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, in whom they trusted.
14 How can they say, “We are warriors, men of valor for battle”?
15 The destroyer of Moab came up against him, the best of his young men brought down the slaughterhouse - oracle of the King whose name is Lord of hosts.
16 The ruin of Moab is imminent, its misfortune is hastening.
17 Grieve for him, all of you, your neighbors, all who know his name. Say: “How the mighty scepter is broken, the staff full of glory!”
18 Come down from glory, sit down in the dung, daughter who lives in Dibon! For the destroyer of Moab has come up against you, he has destroyed your strongholds.
19 Stand in the way, lie in wait, inhabitant of Aroer; Ask the fugitive and the fugitive, say: "What happened?"
20 Moab is defeated! Yes, it has been undone! Let out shouts and screams! Announce on the Arnon: Moab is devastated!
21 A judgment is coming to the land of the plateau, to Holon and Iahsah, against Mephaat,
22 against Dibon, against Nebo, against Beth Diblataim,
23 against Kiriathaim, against Beth Gamul, against Beth Meon,
24 against Kerioth, against Bozrah, and against all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
25 The power of Moab is broken, and its arm is broken! –oracle of the Lord–.
26 Make him drunk, because he has defied the Lord! May Moab wallow in his vomit and become a source of laughter himself.
27 Did you not laugh at Israel? Has he been caught among thieves, so that whenever you talk about him you shake your head?
28 Leave the cities and live on the rocks, you inhabitants of Moab! Be like the dove that puts its nest on the slopes of a ravine!
29 We have heard the pride of Moab, the very proud: what haughtiness, what pride, what arrogance, what haughtiness in his heart!
30 I know their petulance, declares the Lord, their vain gossip, their inconsistent works.
31 Therefore I groan for Moab, I cry out throughout all Moab, I sigh for the people of Kir Hareseth.
32 I weep for you as for Iazer, vineyard of Sibma; Your branches surpassed the sea, they reached Iazer. But a devastating thing has broken into your harvest and your vintage.

33 Joy and gladness have departed from the gardens of the land of Moab. I dried the wine in the vats, the crusher does not tread the grapes, the scream of the crusher is no longer the cry of the grape harvest.
34 The cry of Heshbon reaches Elealeh; They raise their voice to Yahas, from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath Selisiah. For even the waters of Nimrim are a desolation.
35 I will destroy from Moab, declares the Lord, him who climbs to high places and burns incense to his gods.
36 Therefore my heart wails for Moab like a flute; My heart cries like a flute for the people of Kir Hareseth. That is why the profits they had obtained have been lost.
37 For all the heads are shaved and all the beards are shaved; There are incisions on all their hands and they all wear a hair shirt.
38 On the roofs of Moab and in its streets there is nothing but lamentation; For I have destroyed Moab like a vessel that no one wants, declares the Lord.
39 How it has been undone! They moan! With what shame Moab has turned its back! Moab has become the laughter and horror of its neighbors.
40 For thus says the Lord: Look! He soars like an eagle, spreading his wings toward Moab.
41 The cities are taken, the strongholds conquered. The heart of the mighty men of Moab, on that day, is like the heart of a woman in labor.
42 Moab has been annihilated as a people, for having defied the Lord.
43 Panic, pit and net upon you, inhabitant of Moab! –oracle of the Lord–.
44 He who escapes from panic will fall into the pit; He who comes up from the pit will be caught in the net. For I will bring this upon Moab, in the year in which they will give an account.

45 In the shadow of Heshbon the exhausted fugitives stop, but a fire comes out of Heshbon and a flame from the city of Sihon; she devours the temples of Moab and the skull of the
turbulent.
46 Woe to you, Moab! The people of Quemós have perished! For your sons are taken prisoners, and your daughters are taken into captivity.
47 But I will change the fortunes of Moab in the days to come, declares the Lord. So much for the judgment of Moab.
1 For the Ammonites. Thus says the Lord: Has Israel no children, no heir? Why has Milcom inherited Gad and his people settled in its cities?

2 Therefore the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make Rabbah of the Ammonites hear the war cry: she will be a desolate hill, her cities will be burned, and Israel will inherit her heirs,
says the Lord.

3 Groan, Heshbon, for Ai has been devastated, cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Put on a hair shirt, lament, and go from here to there through the fences, because Milcom is going into captivity, with his
priests and their princes!
4 Why do you boast of the valleys, of your fertile valley, apostate daughter, you who trust in your treasures and say: "Who will attack me?"
5 I will bring panic upon you, says the Lord of hosts, from all around you: you will be driven out, each one on his own, and no one will gather the fugitives.
6 After this, I will change the fate of the Ammonites, declares the Lord.
7 For Edom. Thus says the Lord of hosts: Is there no more wisdom in Teman? Are the intelligent lacking in counsel or is their wisdom worn out?
8 Flee, turn your back, hide under the ground, inhabitants of Dedan, because I bring ruin upon Esau, it is time to give account!
9 If grape harvesters come to you, they will not leave a single cluster; If they are night thieves, they will destroy as they please.
10 Yes, I myself have stripped Esau naked, I have exposed his hiding places, and he cannot be hidden. His race and his brothers have been devastated, his neighbors no longer exist.
11 Leave your orphans, I will make them live, and let your widows trust in me!

12 For thus says the Lord: Those who were not condemned to drink the cup had to drink it. And you, are you going to go unpunished? No, you are not going to go unpunished, but you are going to drink it!
13 Yes, I swear by myself, declares the Lord, Bozrah will become a desolation, a reproach, a wilderness, and a curse, and all its cities will become eternal ruins.
14 I have heard a message from the Lord, a herald has been sent to the nations: “Gather together! To assault the city! Stand up for combat!
15 For I make you small among the nations, contemptible among men.

16 Your self-sufficiency, the pride of your heart, has deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock, who occupy the height of a hill. Even if you raise your nest like the eagle, from there you will
I will precipitate - oracle of the Lord -.
17 Edom will become a devastation; Everyone who passes by her will be amazed, and will hiss in amazement when they see all her plagues.
18 As in the catastrophe of Sodom and Gomorrah, and its neighboring cities – says the Lord – no man will dwell there anymore, no human being will reside.

19 As a lion comes up from the depths of the Jordan to an evergreen pasture, so I will make them flee from there in an instant, and there I will establish my chosen one. Because who is like me? Who me
Will he be summoned to court? Who is the pastor who will oppose me?
20 Therefore, hear the plan of the Lord for Edom, his plans for the inhabitants of Teman: Yes, even the smallest sheep will be carried away, his pasture will be amazed because of them.
21 At the sound of his fall the earth trembles, and the echo resounds to the Red Sea.
22 Look! He ascends, soars like the eagle, spreads his wings over Bozrah; The heart of the warriors of Edom, on that day, will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
23 To Damascus. Jamat and Arpad are ashamed, because they have heard bad news; His heart breaks with anxiety, he cannot calm down.
24 Damascus faints, takes flight, terror attacks her, she is prey to anguish and pain like a woman in labor.
25 How the glorious city, the city of joy, is abandoned!
26 Therefore their young men will fall in their squares and all the men of war will perish on that day, declares the Lord of hosts.
27 I will set fire to the fortress of Damascus, and he will devour the palaces of Ben Hadad.
28 To Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, defeated by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. Thus speaks the Lord: Stand up! To the assault of Quedar! Devastate the children of the East!
29 Take your tents and your flocks, your awnings and your luggage; Take away their camels and shout against them: "Terror everywhere!"

30 Flee, flee quickly, hide yourself under the ground, inhabitants of Hazor, declares the Lord, for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has plotted a plan against you, he has plotted a plot against you.
project.
31 Stand up! Advance against a carefree nation, which feels secure – oracle of the Lord – which has no doors or locks, and lives apart!

32 His camels will be the plunder, and his many flocks will be the prey. I will scatter to the four winds the "Shaved Temples", from all sides I will attract their ruin - oracle of the
Sir–.
33 Hazor will be a den of jackals, a desolation forever; No man will live there, no human being will reside there.
34 The word that the Lord spoke to the prophet Jeremiah concerning Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
35 Thus says the Lord of hosts: I will break the bow of Elam, the beginning of its strength.
36 I will bring four winds against Elam from the four corners of the sky. I will scatter them to the four winds, and there will not be a single nation where those expelled from Elam will not come.

37 I will terrify Elam before his enemies and before those who threaten his life; I will bring disaster upon them, the fierceness of my anger, declares the Lord. I will send the sword after them,
until they have been exterminated.
38 For I will set my throne in Elam, and I will destroy the king and the princes from there, declares the Lord.
39 But in the days to come, I will change the fortunes of Elam, declares the Lord.
1 The word that the Lord spoke to Babylon, to the land of the Chaldeans, through the prophet Jeremiah:

2 Announce it among the nations, proclaim it, do not hide it! Say: Bel has covered himself with shame! Marduc has been destroyed! Their statues have been humiliated, their
idols!
3 For a nation rises up against her from the North: it will leave her land devastated and there will be no more inhabitants; both men and animals have emigrated, they have left.
4 In those days and at that time, declares the Lord, the children of Israel will come, along with the children of Judah; They will cry as they walk and seek the Lord, their God.
5 They will ask the way to Zion, with their faces turned towards her: "Come, let us join the Lord in an eternal, unforgettable alliance!"
6 Lost sheep, that was my people: their shepherds led them astray, making them roam the mountains; They went from mountain to hill, forgetting their sheepfold.
7 Whoever found them devoured them, their adversaries said: "We are not guilty, because they sinned against the Lord, the habitation of righteousness, the hope of their fathers."
8 Emigrate from the midst of Babel, leave the country of the Chaldeans! Be like the goats at the head of the flock.

9 For I raise up and raise up against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the North, who will range themselves against her, and so she will be conquered. His arrows are like those of a skilled warrior who
He never returns empty-handed.
10 Chaldea will be plundered, and all its plunderers will be satisfied, declares the Lord.
11 Yes, rejoice, have fun, you plunderers like a calf in the pasture, neigh like stallions!
12 Your mother has been humiliated, she who gave birth to you is confused. now it is the last of the nations, a desert, a wasteland, a steppe.
13 Because of the Lord's anger, it will no longer be inhabited; it will be a desolation. Whoever passes through Babylon will be astonished and will hiss in stupor when he sees all its wounds.
14 Form line around Babylon, all you who bend the bow; shoot at her, do not spare the arrows, because she has sinned against the Lord!
15 Let out howls around you! She surrenders, her bastions fall, her walls collapse. This is the vengeance of the Lord! Get revenge on her, do to her what she did
16 Cut out from Babylon the sower, and him who wields the sickle at the time of harvest. Before the destroying sword, each one turns to his people, each one flees to his country.
17 Israel was a lost sheep, driven away by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured her, and now, lately, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, broke her bones.
18 Therefore this is what the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am going to call the king of Babylon and his country to account, just as I called the king of Assyria to account.
19 I will bring Israel back to their pasture, so that they may graze in Carmel and in Bashan and be satisfied in the mountains of Ephraim and Gilead.
20 In those days and at that time, declares the Lord, the iniquity of Israel will be sought, and the sins of Judah will be gone, and will not be found, for I will forgive those whom I leave alive.

21 Go up to the country of Merataim, go up against him and against the inhabitants of Pecod! Massacre and consecrate to extermination what remains of it – oracle of the Lord – and do as I ordered you!
22 There is noise of war in the country and a total disaster!
23 How the hammer of the whole earth was brought down and broken into pieces! How Babylon has become desolate among the nations!
24 I set a trap for you and you were trapped, without realizing it, Babylon. You have been surprised and taken, because you had provoked the Lord.
25 The Lord opened his arsenal and brought out the weapons of his fury, for the Lord of hosts has a task in the land of the Chaldeans.
26 Come here, all of you, without exception, open your barns, pile it up like sheaves, consecrate it to extermination: let nothing remain!
27 Slaughter all their oxen, let them go down to the slaughterhouse. Woe to them, because their day has come, their time to give an account!
28 Hey! Fugitives and fugitives from Babel come to announce in Zion the vengeance of the Lord, our God, the vengeance of his Temple.

29 Call the archers against Babel, all those who draw the bow; camp against it, around it, so that not a single one escapes. Reward her according to her works, treat her according to what you
she did, because she has been arrogant towards the Lord, towards the Holy One of Israel!
30 Therefore their young men will fall in the streets and all their men of war will perish on that day, declares the Lord.
31 Here I am against you, Arrogant, - oracle of the Lord of hosts - because your day has come, the time when you will have to give an account.
32 Then the Arrogant One will stumble and fall, and no one will make her stand up. I will set fire to their cities and they will devour all around them.
33 Thus says the Lord of hosts: The children of Israel are oppressed along with the children of Judah; Their jailers hold them and refuse to release them.
34 But its redeemer is strong, his name is Lord of hosts: he will defend his cause to give tranquility to the earth and make the inhabitants of Babel tremble.

planted.

16 He does not oppress anyone, he does not retain a pledge or take things by force; He gives his bread to the hungry, clothes the naked

sin.

desert.

provocative offerings, they deposited there their pleasant-smelling perfumes and

They made the object of their love abominable.

rebels

commemorative.

us!".

6 –The Lord is the God of hosts: “the Lord” is his name!–.

1 Word of the Lord, which was addressed to Joel, son of Petuel.

4 What the caterpillar left, the locust devoured, what the locust left, the aphid devoured, what the aphid left, the rodent devoured.

8 She groans, like a virgin dressed in mourning for the husband of her youth.

13 Dress in mourning and mourn, priests! Groan, servants of the altar! Come, spend the night dressed in penance, ministers of my God! Because it has been deprived of
House of your God of offering and libation.

1 Blow the trumpet in Zion, sound the alarm on my holy Mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the country tremble, because the Day of the Lord is coming, because it is near!

2 Day of darkness and darkness, cloudy day and gloomy clouds! Like the dawn that spreads over the mountains, a people advances, numerous and strong, such as never existed before,
nor will there be one after him, even in the most distant generations.
3 Before him the fire devours, behind him the flame consumes. The country is like a garden of Eden before it, behind it a desolate desert. Nothing escapes you!
4 Their appearance is like that of horses, they rush like steeds:
5 like a noise of war chariots leaping over the tops of the mountains; like the crackling of the burning flame that devours the leaf litter; like a strong people in battle array.
6 Before him, the people tremble, all faces contort.
7 They rush forward like mighty men, like warriors they scale the walls. Each one moves forward and their paths do not intersect.
8 They do not trample each other, each one follows his own line; They attack in the middle of the arrows, without breaking formation.
9 They rush into the city, they rush over the walls, they climb into the houses, they enter through the windows like a thief.

15 Blow the trumpet in Zion, prescribe a fast, call a solemn meeting,
16 Gather the people, call the assembly, gather the elders, gather the little ones and the infants! Let the newlywed come out of his bedroom and the newlywed from her wedding bed!

17 Between the vestibule and the altar, let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep and say: “Lord, forgive your people, do not give your inheritance to shame, and do not let the nations mock it! Why should it be said among the people: Where is your God?
18 The Lord was filled with jealousy for his land and had compassion on his people.

19 The Lord answered and said to his people, “Now I am sending you the wheat, the new wine, and the oil, and you will be satisfied with these. Never again will I give you up to disgrace among the nations.

survivors will be those whom the Lord calls.

false gods, whom their fathers had followed,

4 Does the lion roar in the jungle without having prey? Does the cub raise his voice from his den without having hunted anything?
5 Does the bird fall to the ground on a trap if there is no bait? Does the trap jump off the ground without having caught anything?
6 Does the trumpet sound in a city without the people being alarmed? Does a misfortune happen in the city without the Lord causing it?

13 Hear and bear witness against the house of Jacob, oracle of the Lord of hosts:
14 On the day that I punish Israel for their crimes, I will punish the altars of Bethel; The corners of the altar will be demolished and fall to the ground.

13 For he who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who reveals to man what his plans are, who makes the dawn and darkness, who walks on the heights of the
earth, is called "Lord, God of hosts."
1 Listen to this word that I speak, tell it to you, it is a funeral song, house of Israel:
2 The virgin of Israel has fallen and will not rise again; She lies prostrate on the ground and no one lifts her up.

5 Do not seek Bethel, do not go to Gilgal, do not go to Beersheba, for Gilgal will go into captivity and Bethel will be reduced to nothing.
6 Seek the Lord and you will live, lest he fall like fire on the house of Joseph and devour Bethel, without anyone quenching it.

8 He who makes the Pleiades and Orion, he who changes darkness into dawn and daylight into darkness, he who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out on the earth, is called "the
Lord."

10 Woe to those who hate him who reproaches at the Gate and detest him who speaks with integrity!

11 Therefore, because you have despoiled the weak by demanding a tribute of grain, you will not inhabit those houses of carved stones that you built, from those choice vineyards that you
they planted, they will not drink the wine.
12 For I know the multitude of your crimes and the enormity of your sins, oppressors of the righteous, who demand ransom and trample the poor at the Gate!
13 Therefore, the sensible man remains silent at this time, because it is a time of misfortune.
14 Seek good and not evil, so that you may have life, and so the Lord, God of hosts, will be with you, as you say.

16 Therefore, thus says the Lord, God of hosts: There will be lamentations in all the squares and groaning in all the streets. They will summon the peasants to mourn and the mourners
for the lamentations.

18 Woe to those who long for the Day of the Lord! What will the Day of the Lord be for you? It will be darkness and not light!
19 As when someone flees from a lion and encounters a bear; or upon entering his house, he puts his hand against the wall and a snake bites him...
20 The Day of the Lord will be darkness and not light, it will be dark, without any light!
21 I hate, I despise their festivals, and their assemblies disgust me.
22 When you offer me burnt offerings, I take no pleasure in your offerings nor do I look at your sacrifices of fatted calves.

2 If you do not listen and make up your mind to give glory to my Name, says the Lord of hosts, I will send the curse upon you and curse your blessings; I have already cursed you, because you do not
They decide to do that.
3 I will break your arm, I will throw dung in your faces – the dung of your festivals – and you will be swept away with it.
4 Then you will know that I gave you this warning, so that my alliance with Levi may continue, says the Lord of hosts.
5 My alliance with him was life and peace, and I granted them to him; It was fear, and he feared me and revered my Name.
6 The true doctrine was in his mouth and there was no evil on his lips; He walked with me in peace and righteousness, and turned many away from evil.
7 For the lips of the priest preserve knowledge and from his mouth one seeks instruction, because he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.
8 But you have gone astray, you have caused many to stumble with your doctrine, you have perverted the alliance with Levi, says the Lord of hosts.
9 That is why I have made you despicable and vile to all the people, because you do not follow my ways and show partiality in applying the Law.
10 Don't we all have one Father? Has not only one God created us? Why do we betray each other, thus desecrating the alliance of our fathers?

11 Judah has betrayed, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem. For Judah has profaned what is consecrated to the Lord, what he loves, by marrying the daughter of a god
foreigner.
12 The man who does this, may the Lord remove from the camps of Jacob the witness, the guarantor, and even the one who presents the offering to the Lord of hosts.
13 You do another thing: you cover the altar of the Lord with tears, cries and groans, because he no longer turns to the offering, nor accepts it from your hands.
14 And you say, "Why?" For the Lord has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you betrayed, although she was your companion and the woman of your covenant.

15 Has he not made one being, having flesh and spirit? And what is this unique being looking for? An offspring given by God. Be careful, then, of your spirit and that no one betrays the wife of his
youth.
16 For if anyone disowns out of hatred, he covers his garment of violence, says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel. Be careful, then, of your spirit and do not betray.

17 You weary the Lord with your words, and you say, "How do we weary him?" When you say: "Everyone who does evil is well regarded by the Lord, and he takes pleasure in it" or
also: "Where is the God of justice?"

1 I send my messenger to prepare the way before me. And immediately the Lord whom you seek will enter his Temple; and the Angel of the covenant that you desire is coming, says the Lord of
the armies.
2 Who can endure the Day of His coming? Who will remain standing when he appears? For he is like the fire of the smelter and like the lye of the washermen.
3 He will sit to melt and purify: he will purify the sons of Levi and purify them like gold and silver; and they will be to the Lord those who present the offering according to righteousness.
4 The offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the Lord, as in the old days, as in the former years.

5 I will approach you for judgment and will firmly testify against soothsayers, adulterers and perjurers, against those who oppress the hireling, the widow and the orphan,
against those who violate the law of the stranger, and do not fear, says the Lord of
the armies.
6 For I, the Lord, have not changed, but you remain sons of Jacob!

7 From the time of your fathers, you have turned away from my precepts and observed us. Return to me and I will return to you! says the Lord of hosts. You say: "How
"Will we come back?"
8 Can a man disappoint God? However, you let me down! You say: "How have we disappointed you?" In the tithe and in taxes.
9 A curse is upon you, because you, the entire nation, have failed me.

10 Bring the full tithe to the treasury house, so that there may be food in my House. Put me to this test, says the Lord of hosts, and you will see if I will not open the floodgates of heaven for you and
I pour out blessings for you in abundance.
11 I will scare them away from the locusts, so that they do not destroy the fruits of the earth and the vineyard does not remain barren in the field, says the Lord of hosts.
12 All nations will proclaim you happy, because you will be a land of delight, says the Lord of hosts.
13 You speak harshly against me, says the Lord,
14 and they still ask, "What have we said against you?" You say: "It is useless to serve God, and what do we gain by observing his commandments or by walking in mourning before the Lord of hosts?
15 That is why we call the arrogant happy: those who do evil prosper; They defy God, and nothing happens to them!
16 Then those who fear the Lord spoke to each other. The Lord paid attention and listened: a memorial was written before him, in favor of those who fear the Lord and respect his Name.
17 They will be my exclusive property, says the Lord of hosts, on the Day that I prepare. I will have compassion on them, as a man has compassion on his son who serves him.
18 You will again see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between the one who serves God and the one who does not serve him.

19 For the Day is coming, burning like an oven. All the arrogant and evildoers will be like chaff; The Day that is coming will consume them, says the Lord of hosts, until it leaves them no root nor
branch.
20 But for you who fear my Name, the sun of righteousness will shine, bringing health in its rays, and you will leap forth like well-fed calves.
21 You will trample down the wicked, and they will be ashes under the soles of your feet, on the Day that I prepare, says the Lord of hosts.
22 Remember the Law of Moses my servant, to whom I prescribed, in Horeb, precepts and laws for all Israel.
23 I am going to send you Elijah, the prophet, before the great and terrible Day of the Lord comes.
24 He will turn the hearts of the fathers towards their children and the hearts of the children towards their fathers, so that I will not come to punish the country with total extermination.

13 Then they sat on the ground next to him for seven days and seven nights, without saying a single word, because they saw that his pain was very great.
1 After this, Job broke his silence and cursed the day of his birth.
2 He spoke and exclaimed:
3 May the day in which I was born and the night in which he said, "A man has been begotten" disappear!
4 May that day become darkness! May God take care of him from above and not even a ray of light shine on him.
5 May darkness and shadows claim him for themselves, may a dark cloud hang over him and an eclipse of the sun terrify him.
6 Yes, let a thick darkness take hold of him and not add him to the days of the year or include him in the calculation of the months!
7 May that night be barren and no shout of joy enter into it!
8 May those who curse the days, those skilled in stirring up Leviathan, curse her.
9 Let the stars of their dawn be darkened; May he wait in vain for the light and see us the flashes of dawn.
10 Because he did not close the doors of his mother's womb to me nor hide so much misery from my eyes.
11 Why didn't I die at birth? Why didn't I expire when I came out of the womb?
12 Why did two knees welcome me and two breasts nurse me?
13 Now he would lie quietly, he would be asleep and so he would rest,
14 together with the kings and counselors of the land who had mausoleums built,
15 or with the princes who possessed gold and filled their dwellings with silver.
16 Or it would not exist, like a buried abortion, like the children who never saw the light.
17 There the wicked cease to stir, there the weary rest.
18 The prisoners are also at peace, they do not have to hear the jailer's cries.
19 Small and great are there one and the same, and the slave is freed from his master.
20 Why give birth to the unfortunate and life to those who are full of bitterness,
21 to those who long for death in vain and seek it more than treasure,
22 to those who would rejoice to reach the grave and rejoice to find a tomb,
23 to the man whose path is closed and to whom God surrounds him on all sides?
24 Moaning has become my bread and my lamentations are poured out like water.
25 For what I feared most happened to me and something terrible happened to me.
26 I have no calm, no tranquility, no peace, only constant agitation!
1 Then Eliphaz of Teman spoke and said:
2 Would anyone dare to talk to you, when you are so depressed? But who can contain his words?
3 You have taught many people and strengthened weak hands;
4 Your words supported him who stumbled and you have strengthened the weak knees.
5 But now your turn comes, and you become depressed, it is your turn, and you are bewildered.
6 Does not your piety give you confidence and your upright life does not give you hope?
7 Remember this: who perished in innocence or where the righteous men were exterminated?
8 From what I have seen, those who cultivate evil and sow misery reap the same:
9 They perish under the breath of God, they disappear under the breath of his wrath.
10 The lions cease to roar and roar, and the teeth of their cubs are broken;
11 the lion perishes for lack of prey] and the lionesses' cubs are scattered.
12 A word came to me stealthily, its faint whisper captivating my ears.
13 Among the nightmares of night visions, when a deep drowsiness invades men.
14 A fear came over me, a chill, that shook all my bones:
15 a gust of wind blows across my face, making the hairs on my body stand up;
16 Someone is standing, but I don't recognize his face, it's just a shape before my eyes; There is silence, and then I hear a voice:
17 Can a mortal be righteous before God? Is a man pure before his Creator?
18 If he does not trust his own servants and even finds errors in his angels,

1 Call out, see if someone answers you! To which of the saints will you turn?
2 For exasperation kills the fool and passion kills the fool.
3 I have seen the fool take root, but immediately I cursed his dwelling.
4 Their children will be far from help, crushed at the Gate, with no one to rescue them.
5 What they reap will be eaten by the hungry, and the thirsty will sigh for their riches.
6 No, evil does not come from the ground nor does misery spring from the earth:
7 It is man who engenders misery, as eagles take flight upward.
8 I, for my part, would seek God, to him I would explain my cause.
9 He performs great and unsearchable works, wonders that cannot be numbered.
10 He pours rain on the earth and makes water flow through the fields.
11 He puts the humble on high and the afflicted reach salvation.
12 He makes the schemes of the crafty fail, so that the work of their hands does not prosper.
13 Surprise the wise in their own cunning, and the plan of the wicked is quickly undone.
14 In the middle of the day, they encounter darkness, and they grope at noon, as if it were night.
15 He saves the orphan from the sword, and the needy from the hand of the powerful.
16 Thus, the weak regain hope and the wicked close their mouths.
17 Happy is the man whom God rebukes and who does not disdain the lesson of the Almighty!
18 For he wounds, but binds up the wound; He hits, but heals with his hands.
19 Six times he will deliver you from trouble, and the seventh time, evil will not overtake you.

23 Yes, you will have an alliance with the stones of the field and the wild beasts will be at peace with you.
24 You will know that in your tent there is prosperity, and when you review your dwelling, nothing will be missing.
25 You will see that your descendants multiply and that your shoots are like the grass of the earth.

1 Job answered, saying:
2 Ah, if my pain could be weighed and all my misfortune put in the balance!

4 The arrows of the Almighty are stuck in me and my spirit absorbs their poison; The terrors of God are trained against me.
5 Does the wild donkey bray on the green grass or does the bull low over its fodder?
6 Do you eat a tasteless food without salt or does the egg white have flavor?
7 What I was reluctant to even touch is my food in illness.
8 If only my request were fulfilled and God granted me what I hope for!
9 If God decided to crush me, if he released his hand and broke me in two!
10 Then I would have something to console myself and I would jump for joy in my implacable torment, for not having renounced the words of the Saint.
11 What strength do I have to be able to wait? What is my end to endure with patience?
12 Do I have the resistance of stones or is my flesh bronze?
13 No, I do not find any help within myself and my resources have been exhausted.
14 The broken man who has lost the fear of God deserves the loyalty of his friend well.
15 But my brothers have betrayed me like a torrent, like the channel of passing torrents,
16 that run cloudy during the thaw, dragging the melted snow.
17 When summer comes, they evaporate; With the heat, they become extinct in their own bed.
18 The caravans turn aside, enter the desert and perish.
19 The caravans of Tema look towards them, the travelers of Sheba hope to find them.
20 But they are ashamed of having waited, they get there, and are disappointed.
21 This is what you are like to me now: you see something horrible, and you are filled with fear.
22 I never said to them: "Give me something, give me a part of your property,
23 Deliver me from the power of the enemy, rescue me from the hands of the violent.
24 Instruct me, and I will be silent; let me understand where is my mistake,
25 Are righteous words hurtful? But what is settled with your reproaches?
26 Or do you try to fix everything with reproaches, while you throw the words of a desperate man to the wind?
27 You would cast lots for an orphan and traffic with your own friend!
28 Make up your mind once and for all, turn to me! Am I going to lie to their faces?
29 Return, I pray you, and let there be no falsehood; Come back, my justice is at stake.
30 Is there falsehood in my tongue or does my palate not know how to discern misfortune?
1 Is not man's life on earth a bondage? Aren't your days those of a salaryman?
2 Like a slave who longs for the shadow, like a hireling who waits for his wages,
3 Thus empty months have been my inheritance, nights of pain have been assigned to me.
4 When I go to bed, I think: "When will I get up?" But the night becomes very long and I am prey to restlessness until dawn.
5 Worms and dusty scabs cover my flesh, my skin cracks and oozes.
6 My days ran faster than a shuttle: when the thread ran out, they came to an end.
7 Remember that my life is a breath and that my eyes will no longer see happiness.
8 The eye that now looks at me will see me no more; Your gaze will search for me, but I will no longer exist.
9 A cloud dissipates and disappears: so he who goes down into the Abyss goes up no more.
10 He does not return to his house nor does he see the place where he was again.
11 Therefore, I will not bridle my tongue: I will speak with all the anguish of my spirit, I will complain with bitterness in my soul.
12 Am I the Sea or the Sea Dragon that You set a guard against me?
13 When I think, "My bed will comfort me, my bed will share my groans,"
14 then you horrify me with dreams and startle me with visions.
15 It would be better for me to be strangled, I prefer death to these despicable bones!
16 I will not live forever: leave me alone, for my days are a breath.
17 What is man that you take him so seriously and fix your attention on him,
18 visiting it every morning and examining it every moment?
19 When will you stop looking at me? Won't you give me respite even to swallow saliva?
20 If I sinned, what harm did I do to you, guardian of men? Why have you targeted me and made me a burden to you?
21 Why don't you forgive my trespasses and overlook my faults? Look, very soon I will lie down in the dust, you will look for me, and I will no longer exist!
1 Bildad of Suach replied, saying:
2 How long will you speak in this way and will your words be a rushing wind?
3 Does God distort the law and the Almighty distort justice?
4 If your children sinned against him, he left them to their own crimes.
5 But if you turn to God and implore the Almighty,
6 If you remain pure and upright, surely he will soon watch over you and restore your abode as a righteous man.
7 Your beginnings will have been a small thing, compared to the greatness of your future.
8 Question, if not, past generations, consider what their parents experienced.
9 We are from yesterday and know nothing, our days on earth are a shadow.
10 They will instruct you and speak to you, they will draw out these words from their hearts.
11 Does papyrus sprout out of the swamps? Does reed grow where there is no water?
12 Still tender, and without anyone cutting it, it withers faster than any other herb.
13 Such is the fate of those who forget God, so the hope of the wicked perishes.
14 Your trust is just a thread, your security a spider's web.
15 He leans on his house, and it does not resist, he clings to it, and is not left standing.
16 There it is full of sap before the rays of the sun, its shoots spread over its garden;
17 Its roots intertwine in the stony ground, they cling to the rocky terrain.
18 But as soon as they remove it from its place, it denies it, saying, "I never saw you."
19 That is the good fortune that falls to him, while another springs from the dust!
20 No, God does not disdain the upright man, nor does he take the wicked by the hand.
21 He will again fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with joyful acclamations.
22 Those who hate you will be covered with shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.
1 Job answered, saying:
2 Yes, I know very well that it is so: how could a mortal be right against God?

5 He uproots the mountains without their knowledge and turns them over in his fury.
6 He moves the earth from its place and its pillars tremble.
7 He commands the sun to stop shining and sets a seal on the stars.
8 He alone stretches out the heavens and walks on the ridges of the sea.
9 He creates the Big Dipper and Orion, the Pleiades and the southern constellations.
10 He does great and unsearchable things, wonders that cannot be numbered.
11 He passes by me, and I do not see him; It goes by, and I don't notice it.
12 If he snatches prey, who will stop him or who will ask him what he is doing?
13 God does not restrain his fury: Rahab's followers lie prostrate at his feet.
14 How much less could I reply to him and present my arguments in front of him!
15 Even if I were right, I could not answer and I would have to implore the one who accuses me.
16 Even if I called him and he answered me, I don't think he would listen to me.
17 He crushes me for a trifle and multiplies my wounds without reason.
18 It does not give me respite even to take breath, but it satisfies me with bitterness.
19 If it is a question of strength, he is the strongest; If justice, who could summon him?
20 If I am right, he condemns me with my own mouth; If I am upright, he declares me perverse.
21 I am a man of integrity: I care nothing about myself and I feel contempt for my life!
22 Everything is the same! That is why I say: "He destroys the upright and the wicked."
23 If a scourge sows death suddenly, it laughs at the despair of the innocent.
24 If a country falls into the hands of a wicked man, he puts a veil over the faces of the judges: if not him, who else can it be?
25 My days pass faster than a runner, they flee without seeing happiness.
26 They glide like reed boats, like an eagle pounces on its prey.
27 If I think: "I'm going to forget about my complaints, I'm going to put on a good face and smile."
28 Terror attacks me for all my sorrows, knowing that you do not absolve me.
29 I will be judged guilty, so why should I labor in vain?
30 Even if I washed myself with snow and purified my hands with potash,
31 You would sink me in the mire and even my clothes would abhor me.
32 No, he is not a man like me, to answer him and appear together in a trial!
33 If there were at least one referee between us, who would put his hand on both of us,
34 so that God may remove his rod from me and his terror may not make me afraid!
35 Then I would speak to him without fear, because I am convinced that I am not like that.
1 My soul is disgusted with life, I want to give free rein to my complaint, I will express all my bitterness.
2 I will say to God: "Do not condemn me, let me know why you reproach me."
3 Is it a pleasure for you to oppress, to despise the work of your hands and to favor the plan of the wicked?
4 Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see things as men see them?
5 Are your days like those of a mortal and your years like the days of a man,
6 so that you may be on the lookout for my guilt and go in search of my sin,
7 even though I know that I am not guilty and that no one can deliver from your hand?
8 Your hands fashioned me and made me, and then, changing your mind, you destroy me.
9 Remember that you made me from clay and that you will return me to dust.
10 Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
11 You clothed me with skin and flesh and knit me together with bones and sinews.
12 You gave me life and treated me with love, and your care preserved my breath.
13 But you hid high in your heart, now I understand what you had in mind!
14 If I sin, you watch over me and do not absolve me of my guilt.
15 If I am guilty, woe is me! If I am innocent, I cannot raise my head either, saturated with ignominy, intoxicated with affliction.
16 If I rise up, you hunt me down like a lion and redouble your awesome power against me.
17 You raise up new witnesses against me, you increase your anger against me and you attack me with relief troops.
18 Why did you take me from my mother's womb? I would have expired without anyone seeing me,
19 it would be as if I had never existed, they would have taken me from the womb to the grave.
20 The days of my life last so little! Get away from me! So I can smile a little,
21 Before I go, so as not to return, to the region of darkness and shadows,
22 to the land of darkness and disorder, where the very light is darkness.
1 Sophar of Naamah answered, saying:
2 Will there not be an answer to so much talk? Will he who talks too much always be right?

5 But if God spoke and opened his lips against you;

7 Can you search the depths of God or glimpse the perfection of the Almighty?
8 She is higher than the sky: what can you do? It is deeper than the Abyss: what can you understand?
9 Because of its length, it is longer than the land and wider than the sea.
10 If God passes by and imprisons, and if he calls for judgment, who will stop him?
11 He knows false men, he sees evil, and will he not know how to discern it?

15 then you will lift up your spotless forehead, you will be firm and you will fear nothing.
16 Thus you will forget the sorrows, you will remember them as a passing current.
17 Life will rise brighter than noon, darkness will be like a dawn.
18 You will be safe, because there will be hope; You will look around you, and you will go to bed peacefully.

1 Job answered, saying:
2 Truly, you are the voice of the people and wisdom will die with you!

5 «To misfortune, contempt – so happy people think – one more blow for the one who staggers!
6 The tents of robbers are at peace; There is security for those who provoke God, for those who have God in their grasp.
7 But ask the beasts, and they will instruct you, the birds of the air, and they will inform you,
8 to the reptiles of the earth, and they will teach you.
9 Who among all of them does not know that all this was done by the hand of the Lord?
10 He holds in his hand the life of every living thing and the spirit of every human being.
11 Does not the ear discern words as the palate tastes food?
12 In white hair is wisdom and in advanced age, intelligence.
13 But with God are wisdom and power, to him belong counsel and understanding.
14 If he destroys, no one rebuilds; If it imprisons, no one can open.
15 If he withholds the waters, there is a drought; If you let them go, they flood the earth.
16 With him are strength and prudence, to him belong the one who errs and the one who causes error.
17 He makes counselors walk barefoot and deprives judges of sound judgment.
18 He unties the kings' belts and ties a rope around their waists.
19 He makes the priests go barefoot and overthrows those who are firmly established.
20 It leaves the safest speechless and deprives the elderly of reason.
21 Cover the nobles with contempt and loosen the belt of tyrants.
22 He strips the depths of their darkness and brings out the darkness into the light
23 He exalts nations and makes them disappear, he expands peoples and suppresses them.
24 He deprives the leaders of the earth of intelligence and makes them wander in a trackless desert:

1 Yes, I saw all this with my own eyes, I heard it with my ears and I understood it,
2 What you know, I know too: I am not below you.
3 But I want to speak to the Almighty, my desire is to argue with God.
4 You cover up everything with your lies, you are all useless doctors!
5 If you would shut up once and for all, you would prove your wisdom!
6 Listen, then, to my defense; Pay attention to my complaint.
7 Is it because of God that you speak falsely and to favor him you appeal to deception?
8 Are you partial to him and claim to be God's advocates?
9 Will that benefit you when he examines you? Will they play with him like one plays with a man?
10 No, he will be the first to accuse them if they sneakily take sides.
11 Will not his majesty terrify you, and will his terror not come upon you?
12 What you claim are sentences of ashes, your answers are of clay.
13 Stop talking to me, I'm the one who will talk, no matter what happens to me!
14 I will risk everything for everything and put my life in danger.
15 Let him kill me! I no longer have hope, I just want to defend my behavior before him.
16 And this same thing will be a triumph for me, because no wicked man can appear before him.
17 Hear, hear well my words, may my statements reach your ears.
18 I am prepared for the judgment, I know that the right will be on my side.
19 Is there anyone who can incriminate me? Then I would agree to remain silent and expire.
20 Grant me only two things, so that I will not hide from your presence:
21 take the palm of your hand away from me and let your terror not frighten me.
22 Then call me, and I will answer you, or I will speak, and you will answer me.
23 How many are my faults and my sins? Make my rebellion and my sin known.
24 Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?
25 Do you want to scare a leaf carried by the wind? Are you going to chase a dried straw?
26 You pronounce bitter sentences against me and impute to me the guilt of my youth,
27 You who put my feet in the stocks, you who watch all my paths and fence the soles of my feet!

1 Man, born of a woman, has a short life full of torments:
2 like a flower, it springs up and withers; He flees without stopping, like a shadow.
3 And you open your eyes about someone like that, face him with you in judgment!
4 But who will bring out the pure from the impure? Nobody, certainly.
5 Since its days are determined and you know the number of its months, since you have set an insurmountable limit,
6 Look away from him and leave him alone, so that he can enjoy his day like a hired hand!
7 For the tree there is hope: if it is cut down, it can still grow green and will not cease to have shoots.
8 Although its root is old in the ground and its trunk is dead in the dust,
9 As soon as it feels the water, it produces new shoots and puts out branches, like a young plant.
10 But when a man dies, he remains inert; The mortal who expires, where is he?
11 The water of the sea evaporates, a river runs out and dries up:
12 so a man lies down and does not get up; The heavens will disappear, before he wakes up, before he rises from his sleep.
13 Oh, if you would hide me in the Abyss, if you would hide me until your anger passes and set a time to remember me!

17 my crime would be sealed in a bag and you would cover my guilt with a cover.
18 But the mountain falls and crumbles, the rock is removed from its place;

1 Eliphaz of Teman replied, saying:
2 Does a wise man give answers in the air and fill his interior with wind?
3 Do you argue with useless words and speeches that are of no use?
4 Furthermore, you destroy piety, and make no reflection before God!
5 Because it is your fault that inspires your words and you choose the language of crafty people.
6 Your own mouth condemns you, not I; your own lips testify against you.
7 Are you the first man born? Were you born before the hills?
8 Have you had access to divine counsel and have you monopolized wisdom?
9 What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand more than us?
10 Here there are also old men with white hair, people older than your own father.
11 Is the comfort that God gives you and a word spoken gently not enough for you?
12 Why do you let yourself be carried away by your impulses? What do those sullen eyes mean?
13 when you turn your anger against God and utter insults from your mouth?
14 What is man that he be pure, and he that is born of a woman that he be righteous?
15 If God does not trust even his saints and heaven is not pure in his eyes.
16 How much less that abominable and corrupt being, man, who drinks iniquity like water!
17 I am going to explain to you, listen to me; Let me tell you something I saw.
18 This is what the wise men tell, what their fathers did not hide from them:
19 The land was given to them alone, and no stranger passed among them.
20 The wicked torments himself all the days of his life, very few years are reserved for the cruel man;
21 horrible voices echo in his ears, in complete peace, the devastating one attacks him.
22 He does not hope to escape from darkness and is destined for the sword.
23 He wanders like food for vultures and knows that his ruin is certain. The dark day
24 terrifies him, anguish and oppression attack him, like a king prepared for the attack.
25 Because he stretched out his hand against God and became bold against the Almighty:
26 attacked him with his neck outstretched, with the full thickness of his armored shields,
27 because he had anointed his face with fat and strengthened his loins.
28 Now he lives in destroyed cities, in houses where no one lives anymore, which threaten to turn into rubble.
29 He will not become rich, his fortune will not last, nor will his possessions spread throughout the land.
30 It will not escape the darkness, a flame will wither its shoots, its flower will be blown away by the wind.
31 Do not trust lies, because you are wrong, and your reward will be disappointment.
32 Its foliage will wither before its time and its branches will not maintain its greenness.
33 Like a vine, it will lose its still sour grapes, like an olive tree it will drop its flowers.

1 Job answered, saying:
2 I have already heard many similar speeches. You are all sad comforters!
3 Will the words in the air end once and for all? What is it that prompts you to reply like this?
4 I too would speak like you, if you were in my place. He would deafen them with words and make gestures of commiseration.
5 I would comfort them with my mouth and my lips would not stop moving.
6 But if I speak, my pain is not relieved; If I keep quiet, he doesn't leave me either.
7 For now, he has exhausted me and desolated me, all his fears
8 have me cornered; He rises up against me as a witness, my weakness accuses me to my face.
9 His anger tears me apart and harasses me, he gnashes his teeth against me. My adversary pierces me with his gaze;
10 They opened their jaws against me. They struck my cheeks with contempt, they all conspired against me.
11 God gives me over to the power of the unjust, he casts me into the hands of the wicked.
12 I was calm and he tore me apart, grabbed me by the neck and tore me to pieces. He made me a target before him,

14 Open one breach after another in me, attack me like a warrior.
15 I have a hair shirt sewn to my skin, my forehead is buried in the dust.
16 My face is red from crying and darkness envelops my pupils.
17 However, there is no violence in my hands and my prayer is pure.
18 Earth, do not cover my blood, may there be no resting place for my cry!
19 Even now, my witness is in heaven and my guarantor is on high.
20 My friends mock me, while my eyes shed tears before God.
21 Let him be an arbitrator between a man and God, as between a man and his neighbor!
22 Because my years are numbered and I am going to embark on the path of no return.
1 My breath is gone, my days are gone, only the tomb remains!
2 Am I not the target of ridicule and their provocations not revealed to me?
3 Deposit a bond with you in my favor: if not, who will shake my hand?
4 You closed his heart to discernment; Therefore, you will not let them succeed.
5 The distribution is announced to friends, while the children's eyes fail!
6 You have made me a mockery of the people, I am like someone who is spit in the face.
7 My eyes are weak with sadness, and all my members are like a shadow.
8 Righteous men are dismayed by this, and the innocent is indignant against the wicked.
9 But the righteous man establishes himself in his path and he who has pure hands redoubles his energy.
10 Come all of you, come again: I will not find a single wise man among you!
11 My days have passed, my plans and the aspirations of my heart have been undone.
12 They change night into day: "The light, they say, is near the darkness."
13 What can I expect? The Abyss is my dwelling, in darkness I spread my bed.
14 I shout to the Pit: "You are my father!", and to the worms: "My mother and my brothers!"

2 You see that I have opened my mouth, my tongue has begun to speak.
3 My heart overflows with wise words, my lips will speak the pure truth.
4 The breath of God made me, the breath of the Almighty gave me life.
5 Answer me, if you are able; Prepare yourself, and take your stand before me.
6 To God, I am just like you, I too was modeled from clay.
7 Therefore, the fear of me will not terrify you, nor will the weight of my hand overwhelm you.
8 Yes, you have said in my ears – I heard the sound of your words –:
9 “I am pure, I did not commit any fault; I am clean and free from guilt;
10 Yet he finds pretexts against me and considers me his enemy:
11 Put my feet in the stocks and watch all my steps.
12 But I answer you: In this they are not right, because God is greater than man.
13 Why do you try to argue with him as if he did not respond to any of your words?
14 In reality, God speaks once, and then again, without anyone paying attention.
15 In a dream, in a night vision, when a deep slumber comes over men and they are asleep in their beds,
16 then he reveals himself to mortals and terrifies them with appearances,
17 to turn man away from his evil deeds and to destroy the pride of mortals;
18 to preserve his soul from the Pit] and his life from the Underground Canal.
19 He also corrects him on his bed because of his suffering, when his bones tremble without ceasing:
20 Man feels nauseated by food and loses his taste for desirable delicacies;
21 His flesh disappears from view and his bones, which were not seen before, become transparent;
22 His soul approaches the Pit and his life approaches the waters of Death.
23 If there is an angel with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show the man his duty;
24 If he has compassion and says: "Save him from going down to the Pit, I have found a rescue."
25 then his flesh regains its youthful freshness and he returns to the days of his adolescence;
26 He calls on God, who shows favor to him, he contemplates his face with shouts of joy, he announces his salvation to others,
27 and sing among men this song: “I had sinned and perverted the law, but he did not treat me accordingly;
28 He saved my soul from passing through the Pit and my life contemplates the light!
29 All this is what God does, two and three times, for man,
30 to bring back his life from the Pit and illuminate him with the light of the living.
31 Listen, Job, listen to me; Shut up, and I'll talk.
32 If you have something to say, reply to me, speak, because I would like to agree with you.
33 Otherwise, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.
1 Elihu spoke and said:
2 Listen, wise men, to my words, and you experts, pay attention to me!
3 For the ear discerns words as the palate tastes food.
4 Let us decide among ourselves what is right, let us all recognize together what is good.
5 For Job declares: “I am right, but God has deprived me of my right.
6 He lies about my case; My wound is incurable, although I did not commit any fault.
7 Is there anyone like Job, who drinks sarcasm like water,
8 who goes in the company of evildoers and walks with wicked men?
9 For he says, “It does no good for a man to try to obtain favor from God.”
10 Therefore, listen to me, men of understanding: far from God is evil, and far from the Almighty is injustice!
11 For he rewards a man according to his works and treats each one according to his conduct.
12 No, it is not true that God does evil and that the Almighty distorts the right!
13 Who has entrusted him with the earth and who has entrusted him with the whole world?
14 If he withdrew his spirit and gathered up his breath of life,
15 all living would expire at the same time and men would return to dust.
16 If you have intelligence, listen to this, pay attention to the sound of my words.
17 Would I know how to govern the Just, the Powerful?
18 To him who calls “Useless!” to a king and "Wicked!" to the dignitaries,
19 who does not side with princes nor favor the rich to the detriment of the poor, because they are all the work of his hands!
20 They die in an instant, in the middle of the night; he wounds the nobles, and they disappear, he deposes the strong man without anyone's help.
21 For his eyes look upon the ways of man, and he observes his steps:
22 There is no darkness or darkness where those who do evil can hide.
23 For he does not set a date for man to stand trial before God:
24 He breaks down the great without prior examination and puts others in their place.
25 So, because he knows all their actions, he overthrows them in one night, and they are crushed.
26 He slaps them like evildoers in a place that is visible to everyone,
27 because they refused to follow him and did not understand all his ways,
28 making the cry of the poor reach him and making him hear the cry of the oppressed.
29 If he remains motionless, who will shake him? If you cover your face, who will see it? He watches, however, nations and individuals
30 so that no wicked man reigns, one of those who are a trap for the people.
31 You just have to say to God: “I was seduced, I will not do evil again;
32 instruct me, until I can see. "If I committed an injustice, I will not reoffend."
33 Will he repay according to your opinion, since you have despised his instruction? Since you're the one who decides, not me, tell him everything you know.
34 Wise men will say to me, and also every wise man who hears me:
35 "Job does not know what he is saying and his words are meaningless."
36 Let Job be examined to the end for having responded like a wicked man.
37 For he, to his sin, adds rebellion, applauds among us and multiplies his words against God.
1 Elihu spoke and said:
2 Do you think you are within your rights to say: "I am more righteous than God"?
3 Because you say, "What good is it to me, what do I gain by not sinning?"
4 But I will give you an answer, you and your friends with you.
5 Look up at the sky and contemplate, observe the clouds: they are higher than you!
6 If you sin, what harm do you cause? With your many rebellions, what can you do?
7 If you are righteous, what do you give him or what does he receive from your hand?
8 Your wickedness affects a man like you, and your justice affects a mere mortal!
9 They cry out under the weight of oppression, they ask for help against the arm of the powerful.
10 But no one says, "Where is God, my Creator, who makes songs resound in the night,
11 who instructs us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?
12 Then, no matter how much they shout, he does not answer, because of the pride of the wicked.
13 No, God does not listen to vain things, the Almighty does not take notice!
14 Even less when you say that you do not see him, that there is a judgment pending before him, and that you wait for it.
15 And now, because his anger does not punish and he does not pay much attention to rebellion,
16 Job has opened his mouth in vain, and it is through ignorance that he speaks too much.
1 Elihu spoke and said:
2 Bear with me a little, and I will instruct you: there is still something to be said in defense of God.
3 I will bring my knowledge from afar to justify my Creator
4 No, my words do not lie: it is a consummate master who is next to you.
5 God is great and does not retract, he is great for the firmness of his decisions.
6 He does not let the wicked live and gives justice to the oppressed
7 He does not take his eyes off the righteous, he seats them on the throne with kings and exalts them forever.
8 If they are sometimes bound with chains, or prisoners in the bonds of oppression,
9 is to denounce their actions and the rebellions they committed in their arrogance.
10 He opens their ears to correct themselves and exhorts them to turn from wickedness.
11 If they listen and submit, they end their days in prosperity and their years in delight;
12 But if they do not listen, they cross the Channel and perish because of their ignorance.
13 Those with wicked hearts, who accumulate resentment and do not ask for help when he chains them,
14 die in their youth, as those who lead a licentious life waste away.
15 Through oppression he saves the oppressed and opens his ear through affliction.
16 He also invites you to move from anguish to a spacious place without narrowness, where your table, well served, will be full of delicacies.
17 But if your measure is full for the condemning judgment, the judgment and the sentence will drag you down.
18 May not anger incite you to rebellion nor lead you astray from the magnitude of the atonement.
19 Will your riches and all your displays of strength be of value before God in danger?
20 Do not long for that night when the peoples will be uprooted from their place,
21 Beware of turning to evil, for that is why you were tried with misfortune!
22 Yes, God is sublime by power: who teaches like him?
23 Who inspects your conduct? Who can say to him: "You have done wrong"?
24 Remember rather to exalt his work, that other men celebrate with their songs.
25 Everyone contemplates it, man perceives it from afar.
26 Yes, God is so great that we cannot understand him, the number of his years is unfathomable.
27 He draws the drops of water upward and distills the rain that feeds the springs:
28 the rain that the clouds pour out and that falls in torrents on the ground.
29 Who will understand the movement of the clouds and the noise that comes from their dwelling?
30 He spreads his light around him and submerges the depths of the ocean.
31 Thus he sustains the people and gives them plenty of food.
32 He covers the palm of his hands with rays and points out a safe target.
33 His thunder announces his coming, and in his anger, he creates the tempest.
1 This is also why my heart trembles and jumps out of my chest.
2 Listen to the loudness of his voice and the noise that comes out of his mouth!
3 He casts his lightning under the heavens and his brilliance reaches to the ends of the earth.
4 Behind him, a voice roars: he thunders his majestic voice and does not hold back the lightning while his voice is heard.
5 God makes us contemplate wonders, he does great things that we cannot understand.
6 When he says to the snow, "Fall on the earth," and to the downpours, "Let it rain heavily,"
7 He suspends the activity of men, so that all may recognize his work;
8 wild animals go into their dens and take refuge in their holes.
9 The storm breaks from the southern constellation, and the cold from the northern winds.
10 At the breath of God ice is formed and the expanse of waters freezes.
11 He loads the cloud with moisture, and the thundercloud expands its lightning,
12 that revolves around you, according to your plans, to execute each of your commands throughout the entire surface of the earth:
13 whether he fulfills his will for a punishment or to dispense his benefits.
14 Pay attention to this, Job, stop and consider the wonders of God.
15 Do you know how God directs them and how his cloud makes lightning shine?
16 Do you know how the clouds sway, wonders of a master of wisdom?
17 You, who cannot bear the burning of your clothing, when the land is calm under the south wind,
18 Can you stretch out with it the vault of heaven, solid as a mirror of molten metal?
19 Teach us what we should say to him: we will argue no more, because of the darkness.
20 If I speak, will anyone tell him? Should he be informed of what a man says?
21 Until now the light was not seen: it was obscured by the clouds; but a wind passed and dissipated them.
22 A golden glow comes from the north; A terrible storm reigns around God!
23 He is the Almighty, and we cannot reach him! He is sublime for his strength and his equity, great for his justice and oppresses no one.
24 Therefore men fear him, and he does not regard even the wise.
1 The Lord answered Job out of the storm, saying:
2 Who is this who darkens my plan with meaningless words?
3 Fasten your belt like a warrior: I will ask you, and you will instruct me!
4 Where were you when I founded the earth? Indicate it, if you are able to understand.
5 Who set its measurements? Do you even know? Who stretched the measuring rope over it?
6 On what were its pillars sunk or who laid its cornerstone,
7 while the morning stars sang in chorus and all the children of God shouted?
