8 Who enclosed the sea with two doors, when it gushed forth from the mother's womb,
9 when I gave him a cloud for a garment and for swaddling clothes, dense clouds?
10 I drew a boundary around it, set bars and gates for it,
11 and I said to him, “You will come this far and you will not pass; here the pride of your waves will be broken.
12 Have you once in your life commanded the morning, indicated its position to the dawn,
13 that he may take the earth by its edges and shake off the wicked from it?
14 It takes shape like clay under the seal and is dyed like a garment:
15 then the wicked are deprived of their light, and their exalted arm is broken.
16 Have you penetrated to the sources of the sea and walked along the bottom of the ocean?
17 Have the Doors of Death opened to you and have you seen the Doors of Shadow?
18 Do you cover the extent of the earth with your intelligence? Tell me, if you know all this.
19 Where does one go to where the light dwells and where is the abode of darkness,
20 so that you can guide her to her domain and show her the way to her house?
21 Surely you know, because you were already born and the number of your days is very great!
22 Have you penetrated to the deposits of snow and seen the reserves of hail,
23 that I keep for times of trouble, for days of war and combat?
24 By what path does the light expand and the east wind spread over the earth?
25 Who has made a channel for the downpour and a way for the roar of thunder,
26 to send rain on a desolate land, on a desert where no man lives,
27 to water the desolate wastelands and make grass sprout in the steppe?
28 Does the rain have a father, and who has begotten the drops of dew?
29 From whose womb does ice come and who gives birth to the frost of heaven,
30 when the waters harden like stone and the surface of the ocean freezes?
31 Do you tie the bonds of the Pleiades or untie the ropes of Orion?
32 Do you bring out the Hyades in their time and guide the Bear and her cubs?
33 Do you know the laws of heaven? Do you regulate their dominion over the earth?
34 Can you raise your voice to the clouds so that a body of water covers you?
35 Do lightning strike when you send it and they say to you, "Here we are"?
36 Who put wisdom in the ibis or who gave intelligence to the rooster?
37 Who counts the clouds wisely and who tilts the skins of heaven,
38 when the powder melts into a mass and the clods stick together?
39 Do you hunt the prey for the lioness and satisfy the hunger of her cubs,
40 when they crouch in their dens and lie in wait in the thicket?
41 Who prepares provisions for the raven, when its young cry out to God and wander for want of food?
1 Do you know how mountain goats give birth? Do you observe the birth of the deer?
2 Do you count the months of her pregnancy and know the time of her delivery?
3 They crouch down, throw out their young and deposit their litters.
4 Their young become strong and grow, they go to the field and do not return again.
5 Who set the wild ass free and loosed the bonds of the onager?
6 I gave him the steppe as a house and as a dwelling, the salty land.
7 He laughs at the tumult of the city, he does not hear the mule driver shout.
8 He explores the mountains in search of grass, he goes after every green blade.
9 Will the wild bull agree to serve you and spend the night next to your stable?
10 Will you keep him in the furrow with a rein and thresh the valleys behind you?
11 Would you count on him because he is very strong or could you entrust your work to him?
12 Do you trust that he will return to gather the grain in your threshing floor?
13 The ostrich flaps its wings happily, but it does not have the plumage of the stork.
14 When she abandons her eggs in the ground and lets them warm in the dust,
15 forget that a foot can step on them and that a beast can crush them.
16 He is cruel to his children, as if they were not his own, and is not afraid that their labor will be in vain,
17 because God denied him wisdom and did not grant him understanding.
18 But as soon as he gets up and gains momentum, he laughs at the horse and its rider.
19 Do you give strength to the horse and cover its neck with mane?
20 Do you make him jump like a locust? His haughty neighing is terrible!
21 The joyful noise on the plain rushes forward with vigor to meet the weapons:
22 He laughs at fear and is not afraid of anything, he does not shrink from the sword.
23 Above him resounds the quiver, the flashing spear and the javelin.
24 Roaring with impatience, it devours the distance, it does not contain itself when the trumpet sounds.
25 He neighs at every trumpet call, from afar he smells the battle, the voices of command and the war cries.
26 Is it because of your intelligence that the falcon covers itself with feathers and spreads its wings towards the south?
27 At your command does the eagle take flight and make its nest on high?
28 The rock is his dwelling day and night, the steep rock is his fortress
29 From there he is on the lookout for his prey and his eyes look into the distance.
30 Their chicks are filled with blood; Where there are corpses, there she is.
1 The Lord turned to Job and said to him:
2 Will he who argues with the Almighty give in? Will he who reproaches God reply?
3 And Job answered the Lord:
4 I am so little! What can I answer you? I'll cover my mouth with my hand.
5 I spoke once, and I will not repeat it; There is a second time, and I will not insist.
6 The Lord answered Job out of the storm, saying:
7 Fasten your belt like a warrior: I will ask you, and you will instruct me!
8 Do you really want to annul my sentence and condemn me, to justify yourself?
9 Do you have an arm like God's and your voice thunders like his?
10 Then adorn yourself with magnificence and haughtiness, clothe yourself with splendor and majesty!
11 Give free rein to the overflows of your anger and humiliate the proud with your single glance.
12 With a look, subdue the arrogant, crush the wicked where they are.
13 Sink them all together into the dust, lock them up in the underground prison!
14 Then I myself will praise you for the victory won by your hand.
15 Look before you at Behemoth: he feeds on grass like an ox.
16 How much strength there is in his kidneys, what vigor in the muscles of his belly!
17 He straightens his tail like a cedar, the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit together.
18 His bones are tubes of bronze: his members are like bars of iron.
19 It is the first of God's works, which made him the champion of his companions,
20 because the mountains bring him a tribute, and so do the wild animals that frolic in them.
21 He lies down under the lotuses, in the recesses of the reed beds and swamps.
22 The lotuses cover it with their shadow, the willows of the torrent surround it.
23 If the river is angry, it is not disturbed; He is serene, even though a Jordan reaches his throat.
24 Who can take him by the eyes or pierce his nose with an awl?
25 And Leviathan, can you catch him with a hook and tie his tongue with a rope?
26 Will you stick a reed up his nose or pierce his jaws with a hook?
27 Will he make long supplications to you or speak tender words to you?
28 Will he make a covenant with you and take him as a slave forever?
29 Will you play with him like a bird and tie him for the entertainment of your daughters?
30 Will fishermen trade in it and merchants fight for it?
31 Will you shoot his skin with darts and his head with harpoon blows?
32 Try to put your hand on him, think about the fight and you will give up.
1 Your hope would be disappointed: just by looking at it you would be terrified.
2 Isn't it too fierce to excite you? Who could resist him?
3 Who faced him, and was safe and sound? No one under the heavens!
4 I will not fail to mention its members, I will speak of its incomparable strength.
5 Who tore the outside of his cloak or pierced his double breastplate?
6 Who forced open the doors of his jaws? Terror reigns around their fangs!
7 Its back is a row of shields, locked by a stone seal.
8 They press against each other, not a breeze passes between them.
9 They are attached to each other, they form a block and do not separate.
10 His sneeze casts rays of light, his eyes shine like the flashes of dawn.
11 Torches issue from their mouths, sparks of fire escape from them.
12 Smoke comes out of their nostrils like from a pot boiling on fire.
13 His breath lights the coals, a flame comes out of his mouth.
14 Strength resides in his neck and fear spreads before him.
15 His flesh is solid: they are attached to him and do not move.
16 His heart is hard as a rock, durable as a millstone.
17 When it rises, the waves tremble, the waves of the sea recede.
18 The sword touches it, but it does not stick, nor does the spear, the dart, or the javelin.
19 Iron is like straw to him, and bronze is like rotten wood.
20 The arrows do not make him flee, the stones of the sling become tow.
21 The club seems to him like a blade of grass and he laughs at the noise of the saber.
22 It has pointed tiles underneath, it drags like a rake over the mud.
23 He makes the deep waters boil like a pot, he turns the sea into a cauldron.
24 He leaves behind him a luminous trail: the ocean seems covered in white hair.
25 There is no one on earth like him, he was made not to fear anything.
26 Look at the highest ones in the face, he is the king of the fiercest beasts.
1 Job answered the Lord, saying:
2 I know that you can do everything and that no project is unrealizable for you.
3 Yes, I spoke without understanding, of wonders that surpass me and that I do not know.
4 «Listen, let me speak; I will question you and you will instruct me.
5 I knew you only by hearsay, but now my eyes have seen you.
6 Therefore I recant, and repent in dust and ashes.

7 After speaking these words to Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz of Teman: "My anger is kindled against you and against your two friends, because they have not told the truth about me, as my
servant Job.

8 Now get seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job. You will offer a burnt offering for yourselves, and my servant Job will intercede for you. And I, in regard to him, do not
I will inflict no humiliating punishment on them, for not having told the truth about
me, like my servant Job.
9 Then Eliphaz of Teman, Bildad of Suah, and Sophar of Naamah went to do what the Lord had told them, and the Lord had regard for Job.
10 Afterwards, the Lord changed Job's fortunes, because he had interceded on behalf of his friends, and doubled everything Job had.

11 All his brothers and sisters, as well as his former acquaintances, came to him and held a banquet with him in his house. They pitied and consoled him for all the misfortune that
the Lord had sent her. And each of them gave him a silver coin and
a gold ring
12 The Lord blessed Job's last years much more than his first. He owned fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand donkeys.
13 He also had seven sons and three daughters.
14 He called the first “Dove,” the second “Cinnamon,” and the third “Eyeshadow.”
15 In all the land there were no women as beautiful as Job's daughters. And their father gave them a share of inheritance among their brothers.
16 After this Job lived another hundred and forty years, and saw his children and his children's children, to the fourth generation.
17 Job died very old and full of days.
1 Proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel,
2 to know wisdom and instruction, to understand deep words,
3 to obtain careful instruction – justice, equity and rectitude –
4 to give insight to the unwary, and to the young, knowledge and reflection;
5 Let the wise man listen, and he will increase his knowledge, and the intelligent man will acquire the art of leading.
6 to understand proverbs and sharp sayings, the words of the wise and their enigmas.
7 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, fools despise wisdom and instruction.
8 Listen, my son, to your father's instruction and do not reject your mother's teaching,
9 for they are a diadem of grace for your head and a necklace for your neck.
10 My son, if sinners try to seduce you, do not accept.
11 If they say: “Come with us, let us lay a bloody ambush, let us lie in wait for the innocent;
12 Let us swallow them alive like the Abyss, all whole, like those who go down into the Pit;
13 We will find all kinds of precious goods, we will fill our houses with the spoils;
14 you will have your share just like us, we will all make a common purse.
15 my son, do not accompany them on the road, remove your feet from their paths,
16 because their feet run toward evil and are quick to shed blood.
17 But the net is spread in vain, if all the birds can see it:
18 They lay a bloody ambush against themselves, they lie in wait for their own lives.
19 Such is the fate of him who gains unjustly; They take the life of the one who owns them.
20 Wisdom cries out in the streets, makes her voice heard in the squares;
21 He knocks on the busiest corners, at the entrance to the city gates, and says his words:
22 «How long, you fools, will you love naivety? How long will the insolent take pleasure in their insolence and the fools hate science?
23 Consider my rebuke: I am going to open my heart to you and make my words known to you.
24 Because I call and you resist, I stretch out my hand and no one pays attention,
25 because you ignore all my advice and do not accept my rebuke,
26 I, in turn, will laugh at your ruin, I will mock when terror overtakes you,
27 when terror overtakes them like a storm and ruin comes upon them like a hurricane. when distress and tribulation come upon them:
28 then they will call to me, and I will not answer; they will search for me eagerly, and will not find me.
29 Because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord,
30 because they did not want my advice and despised all my reproaches,
31 They will taste the fruit of their own conduct, they will be satisfied with their advice.
32 Because the naive are killed by their own error, and laziness destroys the fools,
33 But whoever listens to me will live safely and be at ease, fearing no evil.”
1 My son, if you receive my words and keep my commandments with you,
2 giving ear to wisdom and inclining your heart to understanding;
3 if you call on intelligence and raise your voice to understanding,
4 If you search for it like silver and search for it like treasure,
5 then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God.
6 For the Lord gives wisdom, from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.
7 He reserves his help for upright men, he is a shield for those who walk uprightly;
8 He protects the paths of equity and guards the path of his faithful.
9 Then you will understand justice and equity, righteousness and all the paths of good.
10 For wisdom will penetrate your heart and knowledge will be the delight of your soul;
11 reflection will take care of you and intelligence will protect you,
12 to deliver you from the evil way, from the man who speaks wickedly;
13 of those who abandon the paths of righteousness, to take dark paths;
14 of those who enjoy doing evil and rejoice in the perversions of wickedness;
15 of those who walk by crooked paths and crooked paths.
16 Thus you will be free from the strange woman, from the strange one who uses seductive words,
17 who abandons the friend of his youth and forgets the covenant of his God.
18 His house sinks into death and his paths lead to the Shadows;
19 Those who enter it will not be able to turn back nor will they reach the paths of life.
20 So you will walk in the path of the good and follow the path of the righteous,
21 For the upright will inhabit the land and upright men will remain in it.
22 But the wicked will be cut off from the land and the traitors will be uprooted from it.
1 My son, do not forget my teaching, and let your heart observe my commandments,
2 because they will bring you long days, years of life and prosperity.
3 May good faith and loyalty never abandon you: tie them around your neck. write them on the table of your heart,
4 and you will find favor and approval in the eyes of God and man.
5 Trust in the Lord with all your heart and do not rely on your own understanding;
6 Acknowledge him in all his ways and he will make straight your paths.
7 Do not be wise in your own eyes, fear the Lord and depart from evil:
8 that will be a remedy for your flesh and sap for your bones.
9 Honor the Lord with your possessions and with the first fruits of all your earnings:
10 So your barns will be filled with wheat and your winepresses will overflow with new wine.
11 My son, do not despise the Lord's correction, nor be displeased when he rebukes you,
12 because the Lord rebukes those he loves like a father his dearly loved son.
13 Happy is the man who finds wisdom and the one who gains understanding,
14 because winning it is worth more than silver and it yields more than fine gold!
15 It is more precious than pearls and nothing desirable can be equal to it.
16 In his right hand is long life, and in his left is wealth and glory.
17 Her ways are pleasant ways and all her paths are peaceful.
18 It is a tree of life for those who hold on to it, and those who hold on to it are happy.
19 By wisdom the Lord founded the earth, by understanding he established the heavens;
20 By his knowledge the oceans sprung up and the clouds drop the dew.
21 Preserve, my son, prudence and reflection; May they not depart from your eyes.
22 They will be life to your soul and grace to your neck.
23 Then you will walk safely on the path and your foot will not stumble.
24 If you lie down, you will not tremble, and once you lie down, your sleep will be pleasant.
25 You will not fear any shock or the wicked who come like a storm.
26 For the Lord will be your security and will keep your foot from a trap.
27 Do not deny a benefit to someone who needs it, as long as it is in your power to do so.
28 Do not say to your neighbor, "Come back later, tomorrow I will give it to you," if you have the means to help him.
29 Do not plot evil against your neighbor, while he lives safely with you.
30 Do not argue with a man for no reason, if he has not caused you any harm.
31 Do not envy a violent man or choose any of his ways.
32 For the wicked man is abominable to the Lord, and he reserves his privacy for the upright.
33 The curse of the Lord is in the house of the wicked, but he blesses the dwelling of the righteous.
34 He mocks the insolent and favors the humble.
35 The wise will inherit glory, but the fools will bear ignominy.
1 Listen, children, to the instruction of a father, pay attention, so that you may understand:
2 What I give you is a sound doctrine, do not abandon my hope.
3 I was also a son to my father, tender and very dear in my mother's eyes.
4 He said to me to instruct me: Let your heart retain my words, observe my commandments and you will live.
5 Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding, do not forget the words of my mouth nor deviate from them.
6 Do not abandon her, and she will protect you, love her, and she will take care of you.
7 The beginning of wisdom is trying to acquire it; With everything you possess, acquire intelligence.
8 Appreciate her to the fullest, and she will exalt you; It will glorify you, if you embrace it.
9 He will put a diadem of grace on your head, he will give you a crown of glory.
10 Listen, my son, and receive my words. and your years of life will be multiplied.
11 I instruct you in the way of wisdom, I guide you along straight paths.
12 When you walk, your step will not be shortened, and if you run, you will not stumble.
13 Hold fast to the instruction, do not let go; Keep her well, because she is your life.
14 Do not enter the path of the wicked or advance in the path of the wicked.
15 Avoid it, do not pass by it, turn away from it, and pass by.
16 For they do not sleep unless they do evil; They lose sleep, if they don't make someone fall,
17 since they feed on the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
18 The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, increasing until it is full day.
19 But the path of the wicked is like a thick darkness: they do not know where they will stumble.
20 My son, pay attention to what I say to you, incline your ear to my words.
21 May they not depart from your eyes, keep them well within your heart,
22 because they are life to those who find them and health to every living thing.
23 Watch your heart carefully, for from it spring the fountains of life.
24 Remove perverse words from you and remove malice from your lips.
25 Let your eyes look straight ahead and your gaze go straight ahead.
26 Be careful where you put your feet and make sure all your ways are firm.
27 Do not turn to the right or to the left, turn your feet away from evil.
1 My son, listen to my wisdom, incline your ear to my understanding,
2 so that you maintain due discretion and your lips preserve knowledge.
3 For the lips of another woman's lips drip with honey, and her palate is smoother than oil,
4 But in the end, she is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a double-edged sword.
5 His feet descend to Death, his steps rush into the Abyss;
6 She does not take into account the path of life, she wanders without knowing where.
7 Therefore, children, listen to me and do not depart from the words of my mouth.
8 Keep your path far from her and do not approach the entrance to her house,
9 lest you give your honor and your years to others, to a cruel man;
10 May strangers be satisfied with your strength and your work end up in someone else's house,
11 and that at last you will have to groan, when your body and your flesh are consumed.
12 Then you will say, “How have I hated instruction and my heart despised warnings?
13 I did not listen to the voice of my teachers nor did I pay attention to those who taught me.
14 He was almost at the height of misfortune, in the midst of the assembly and the community.
15 Drink the water from your cistern and the water that flows from your own well.
16 May not your fountains be scattered outwards nor your streams of water into the streets.
17 May they be for you alone and may there be no strangers with you.
18 Blessed be your fountain, and find your joy in the wife of your youth,
19 kind deer, gracious gazelle! May their loves intoxicate you at all times and may you always be captivated by their affection.
20 My son, why will you allow yourself to be captivated by a stranger's woman and embrace the breasts of a stranger?
21 The ways of man are under the eye of the Lord and he considers all his paths.
22 The wicked will fall prey to their own faults and will be trapped in the bonds of their sin.
23 He will die for lack of instruction and will go astray because of his great foolishness.
1 My son, if you have made yourself a guarantor for your neighbor and have shaken your hand on behalf of another,
2 if you have become entangled in your words and have allowed yourself to be trapped by your own mouth,
3 then, my son, do work to save yourself, since you have fallen into the hands of your neighbor: go and throw yourself at his feet and bother him,
4 Do not give rest to your eyes or rest to your eyelids;
5 Deliver like a gazelle from a net and like a bird from the hand of the hunter.
6 Look at the ant, lazy one, observe its habits and learn to be wise:
7 she, who has no boss, no overseer, no owner.
8 provides himself with food in summer and gathers his food during the harvest.
9 How long will you lie down, lazy, when will you rise from your sleep?
10 “Sleep a little, snooze a little, rest a little with your arms crossed”:
11 Thus poverty will come upon you like a robber and misery like an armed man.
12 He is a vile man, a wicked man, who has a mouth full of perversity;
13 winks his eye, taps with his feet, makes a sign with his fingers:
14 In his depraved heart he plots evil, he is always sowing discord.
15 Therefore, his ruin will come suddenly, he will be destroyed suddenly and without remedy.
16 There are six things that the Lord hates, and seven that are an abomination to him;
17 haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood;
18 the heart that plots evil plans, the feet quick to run towards evil,
19 the false witness who utters lies, and the one who sows discord between brothers.
20 Observe, my son, your father's precept and do not reject your mother's teaching.
21 Bind them to your heart constantly, knot them around your neck.
22 May they guide you as you walk, watch over you when you lie down, and converse with you when you wake up.
23 For the commandment is a lamp, the teaching a light, and the rules of instruction a way of life,
24 to protect you from a bad woman and from the seductive tongue of a stranger.
25 Do not covet their beauty in your heart nor be captivated by their looks.
26 Because the price of a prostitute is a crust of bread, but a married woman is fishing for a luxurious life.
27 Can a man put fire on his chest without his clothes catching fire?
28 Can you walk on hot coals without burning your feet?
29 This is what happens to someone who sleeps with his neighbor's wife: whoever touches her will not go unpunished.
30 Is not a thief despised, even though he steals to satisfy his appetite when he is hungry?
31 Once discovered, he pays seven times and has to hand over all the goods in his house.
32 He who commits adultery is a fool; he who does so ruins himself:
33 What he will get are blows and ignominy, and his disgrace will never be erased.
34 For jealousy makes a man angry, and he will have no compassion on the day of vengeance;
35 will not accept any compensation, nor will he want to know anything even if you want to give him more.
1 My son, observe my words and treasure my commandments.
2 Observe my precepts, and you will live, keep my teaching as the pupil of your eyes.
3 Bind them to your fingers, write them on the tablet of your heart.
4 Say to Wisdom: “You are my sister,” and call Intelligence “Friend,”
5 to protect you from another woman, from the stranger who uses seductive words.
6 While I was at the window of my house, I looked through my grille,
7 And I saw among the unwary, I saw among the teenagers a young man lacking in judgment,
8 who was passing along the street, near the corner, and was going towards her house,
9 in the twilight, at dayfall, in the middle of the night and darkness.
10 Suddenly, that woman comes up to him, with the air of a prostitute and her heart full of cunning:
11 She is boisterous, ribald, her feet do not stop in her house;
12 sometimes in the streets, sometimes in the squares, he is lurking on every corner.
13 She grabs him, covers him with kisses, and says to him with all impudence:
14 «I had to offer sacrifices of communion, today I have fulfilled my vows;
15 That's why I went out to meet you, eager to see you, and found you.
16 I have covered my bed with blankets of multicolored cloth, of Egyptian thread;
17 I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, with aloes and cinnamon.
18 Come! Let us get drunk with love until morning, let us surrender to the delights of pleasure.
19 Because my husband is not at home, he has gone on a long journey,
20 took the money bag, he will not return until the full moon.
21 Thus she persuades him with her great ease, she drags him with her seductive lips.
22 Immediately he follows her, like an ox that is led to the slaughter, like a deer that falls into a snare,
23 until an arrow pierces his liver, like a bird that rushes into a trap, without realizing that its life is at stake.
24 And now, my son, listen to me, and pay attention to the words of my mouth:
25 May your heart not turn aside to its paths, may it not go astray in its paths,
26 because there are many victims that she caused to fall, and all those she killed were strong:
27 His house is the path of the Abyss, which goes down to the chambers of Death.
1 Is not Wisdom calling and Intelligence making its voice heard?
2 On the highest peaks that line the road, stationed at the crossroads of the paths,
3 by the gates, at the entrance to the city, in the places of entry, she says with a loud voice:
4 «I call you men, and my voice is addressed to human beings.
5 Understand, you fools, what insight is; Understand, fools, what common sense is.
6 Listen: what I am going to say is very important, my lips open to express what is right.
7 Yes, my mouth speaks truth, wickedness is an abomination to my lips.
8 All my words are according to justice, there is nothing twisted or devious in them;
9 all are exact for him who knows how to understand and right for those who have found science.
10 Acquire my instruction, not silver, and knowledge rather than refined gold.
11 For Wisdom is worth more than pearls, and nothing desirable can be equal to it.
12 I, Wisdom, dwell in prudence and possess the science of reflection.
13 The fear of the Lord is to detest evil: I detest arrogance, pride, evil conduct, and a perverse mouth.
14 To me belong counsel and skill, I am intelligence, mine is power.
15 By me kings reign and rulers decree justice;
16 Through me princes rule and nobles judge the earth.
17 I love those who love me and those who earnestly seek me will find me.
18 With me are riches and glory, lasting goods and righteousness.
19 My fruit is worth more than gold, than fine gold, and I yield more than refined silver.
20 I walk in the path of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of equity,
21 to distribute possessions to those who love me and to fill their treasures.
22 The Lord created me as the firstfruits of his ways, before his works, forever.
23 I was formed from eternity, from the beginning, before the origins of the earth.
24 I was born when the abysses did not exist, when there were no fountains of mighty waters.
25 Before the mountains were founded, before the hills, I was born,
26 when he had not yet made the earth or the spaces or the first elements of the world.
27 When he established heaven, I was there; When I traced the horizon over the ocean,
28 when he condensed the clouds on high, when he gave power to the fountains of the ocean,
29 when he set his boundary to the sea so that the waters would not transgress its borders, when he established the foundations of the earth,
30 I was at his side like a beloved son and delighted him day after day, enjoying myself before him at all times,
31 I enjoyed myself on the face of the earth, and my delight was to be with the sons of men.
32 And now, children, listen to me: happy are those who observe my ways!
33 Listen to the instruction and be wise: do not neglect it!
34 Happy is the man who listens to me, watching at my doors day after day and keeping watch at the entrance of my house!
35 For he who finds me has found life and has obtained favor from the Lord;
36 But whoever sins against me harms himself, and everyone who hates me loves death.
1 Wisdom built his house, carved its seven columns,
2 He sacrificed his victims, mixed his wine, and also prepared his table.
3 She sent her servants to proclaim on the highest places in the city:
4 "Whoever is foolish, let him come here." And to the one lacking understanding, he says:
5 “Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine that I have mixed.
6 Abandon naivety, and you will live, and go straight on the path of intelligence.
7 He who corrects an insolent person brings on himself disgrace, and he who rebukes a wicked person brings dishonor on himself,
8 Do not rebuke an insolent man, lest he hate you; rebuke a wise man, and he will love you,
9 Give to the wise and he will become even wiser; instruct the righteous and he will gain knowledge.
10 The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
11 For your days will be multiplied through me and years will be added to your life.
12 If you are wise, you are wise for yourself, if you are insolent, you alone will suffer.
13 Mrs. Foolishness is turbulent, she is stupid and she knows nothing.
14 She sits at the door of her house, on a chair, on the heights of the city,
15 to shout to passers-by who are going straight down the road:
16 "Whoever is foolish, let him come here." And to the one lacking understanding, he says:
17 “Stolen waters are sweet and bread taken in secret is delicious!”
18 But he does not know that there are the Shadows, and their guests, in the depths of the Abyss.
1 Proverbs of Solomon. A wise son is his father's joy, but a foolish son is his mother's affliction.
2 Ill-gotten treasures are of no use, but justice delivers from death.
3 The Lord does not let the righteous suffer hunger, but rejects the greed of the wicked.
4 The indolent hand impoverishes, but the laborious arm enriches.
5 He who gathers in the summer is a cautious man, he who sleeps in the harvest is contemptible.
6 Blessings come upon the righteous, the mouth of the wicked covers violence.
7 The memory of the righteous is blessed, but the name of the wicked will rot.
8 He who has a wise heart accepts the commandments, but he who has foolish lips goes to perdition.
9 He who walks with integrity walks safely, he who follows crooked paths will be discovered.
10 He who winks his eye causes suffering, he who rebukes frankly gives peace of mind.
11 The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked covers violence.
12 Hatred causes quarrels, but love covers all faults.
13 Wisdom is found on the lips of the intelligent, and the rod is on the back of the fool.
14 The wise treasure knowledge, but the mouth of a fool is imminent ruin.
15 The fortune of the rich is his stronghold, the poverty of the weak is his ruin.
16 The wages of the righteous lead to life, the income of the wicked leads to sin.
17 He who respects instruction walks towards life, but he who rejects rebuke goes astray.
18 He who conceals his hatred has lying lips, and he who raises a slander is a fool.
19 Where words abound, sin is never lacking; he who restrains his lips is a cautious man.
20 The tongue of the righteous is polished silver, the heart of the wicked is not worth much.
21 The lips of the righteous sustain many, but fools die for lack of sense.
22 The blessing of the Lord is what enriches, and our effort adds nothing to it.
23 Committing infamy is a diversion for a fool, and so is wisdom for an intelligent man.
24 What they fear will happen to the wicked, and to the righteous what they desire will be given.
25 The storm passes, and the wicked is no more, but the righteous has eternal foundations.
26 As vinegar is for the teeth and smoke for the eyes, so is the lazy person to whom he is given a task.
27 The fear of the Lord lengthens the days, but the years of the wicked will be shortened.
28 The hope of the righteous is joyful, but the hope of the wicked will fade away.
29 The way of the Lord is a refuge for the upright man and a ruin for those who do evil.
30 The righteous will never waver, but the wicked will not inhabit the earth.
31 Wisdom flows from the mouth of the righteous, but the perverse tongue will be cut off.
32 The lips of the righteous exude kindness, and the mouths of the wicked exude wickedness.
1 The Lord hates counterfeit scales, but he likes accurate weights.
2 With arrogance comes ignominy, but wisdom is with the humble.
3 Integrity guides upright men, but perversity ruins traitors.
4 Fortune is of no use in the day of wrath, but justice delivers from death.
5 The righteousness of an upright man makes his way straight, but the wicked fall because of their wickedness.
6 Justice frees upright men, but traitors are trapped by their greed.
7 When the wicked die, all hope vanishes and the trust placed in riches disappears.
8 The righteous are delivered from danger, and the wicked fall in their place.
9 The wicked ruins his neighbor with his mouth, but the righteous are saved by their experience.
10 When the righteous are happy, the city rejoices, when the wicked perish, shouts of joy are heard.
11 With the blessing of righteous men a city is built, the mouth of the wicked destroys it.
12 He who despises his neighbor is a fool, and an intelligent man knows how to keep silent.
13 The gossiper reveals secrets, but the faithful man keeps due reserve.
14 For lack of government a town sinks, but it is saved if there are many men of counsel.
15 He who bonds for another has a very bad time, he who avoids bonds is safe.
16 A graceful woman obtains glory, and the bold obtain wealth.
17 A faithful man does good to himself, but a cruel man torments his own flesh.
18 The wicked earn a deceitful reward, and he who sows righteousness a sure reward.
19 Just as justice leads to life, he who pursues evil walks towards death.
20 Crooked hearts are abominable to the Lord, but those who walk upright enjoy his favor.
21 Sooner or later, the wicked will not go unpunished, but the descendants of the righteous will be saved.
22 A golden ring in a pig's trunk is a woman who is beautiful but lacks judgment.
23 The righteous desire nothing but good, and the wicked can only hope for fury.
24 One gives generously and increases his wealth, another saves more than necessary and ends up destitute.
25 A generous man will prosper, and he who gives drink will have his thirst quenched.
26 The people curse the one who hoards the wheat, but they cover the one who sells it with blessings.
27 He who earnestly seeks good earns favor, but he who seeks evil, evil will overtake him.
28 He who trusts in his wealth withers, but the righteous will grow like foliage.
29 He who disturbs his own house will inherit the wind, and the fool will be a slave to the wise.
30 The fruit of righteousness is a tree of life, and the wise captivate hearts.
31 If the righteous is rewarded on earth, how much more is the wicked and the sinner!
1 He who loves correction loves knowledge, and he who hates rebuke becomes brutal.
2 The good man obtains favor from the Lord, but the Lord condemns the malicious.
3 No one is established through wickedness, but the root of the righteous will be unshaken.
4 A perfect woman is her husband's crown, a shameless woman is like cavities in his bones.
5 The plans of the righteous are right, the schemes of the wicked are nothing but deceit.
6 The words of the wicked are bloody ambushes, but their own mouths deliver the righteous.
7 As soon as the wicked are cast down, they are no more, but the house of the righteous stands.
8 A man is praised for his good judgment, but he who is false in heart falls into disgrace.
9 Better is a simple man who is self-sufficient than a boastful man who lacks bread.
10 The righteous provide for the needs of his livestock, but the bowels of the wicked are cruel.
11 He who cultivates his land will be satisfied with bread, but he who pursues chimeras is a fool.
12 The wicked covet the prey of the wicked, but the root of the righteous is well established.
13 In the sin of the lips there is a fatal trap, but the righteous escapes the danger.
14 Man is satisfied with the fruit of his words, and each receives the wages of his work.
15 A fool thinks his path is right, but a wise man listens to advice.
16 A fool immediately expresses his displeasure, but a prudent man hides an insult.
17 He who speaks the truth declares what is right, but a false witness is an impostor.
18 A charlatan cuts like a sword, but the tongue of the wise is a remedy.
19 True lips remain forever, but a lying tongue lasts only for a moment.
20 There is deceit in the hearts of those who plot evil, and joy in those who give healthy counsel.
21 Nothing bad will happen to the righteous, but the wicked are full of misfortunes.
22 Lying lips are abominable to the Lord, but those who do the truth enjoy his favor.
23 A wise man hides what he knows, but the hearts of fools proclaim their folly.
24 The laborious hand will rule, the lazy hand will pay tribute.
25 Restlessness depresses a man's heart, but a good word comforts him.
26 The righteous man excels others, but the wicked are led astray by their conduct.
27 A lazy man has no game to roast, and the most precious asset is a hard-working man.
28 In the path of righteousness is life, and the path it follows does not lead to death.
1 A wise son loves correction, but the insolent does not listen to rebuke.
2 A man will eat the fruit of his words, but traitors are eager for violence.
3 He who watches his mouth protects his life, he who opens his lips too much ends in ruin.
4 The lazy man covets and his desire is vain, but the desire of the industrious will be fulfilled.
5 The righteous hate lies, but the wicked cause shame and confusion.
6 Righteousness preserves him who walks uprightly, but wickedness ruins the sinner.
7 There are those who boast of being rich and have nothing, and there are those who pretend to be poor and have great assets.
8 Wealth is a guarantee for a man's life, but the poor do not listen to threats,
9 The light of the righteous shines, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.
10 A fool provokes discord with his presumption, and wisdom is with those who allow themselves to be advised.
11 Wealth acquired at once does not last, but he who accumulates little by little increases it.
12 Hope deferred makes the heart sick, desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
13 He who despises the word will be lost, but he who keeps the commandments will be rewarded.
14 The teaching of the wise is a source of life, to avoid the traps of death.
15 Good judgment wins favor, but traitors walk towards their ruin.
16 The prudent man knows well what he is doing, but the fool shows off his folly.
17 A bad emissary plunges into misfortune, but a faithful envoy restores health.
18 Misery and ignominy for him who rejects correction, he who heeds a warning will be honored.
19 A wish fulfilled is a delight to the soul, turning away from evil is an abomination to fools.
20 Go to the wise, and you will become wise, but he who associates with fools is ruined.
21 Evil pursues sinners, and good rewards the righteous.
22 A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children, but the sinner's fortune is reserved for the righteous.
23 The furrow of the poor yields food in abundance, but there are those who are lost for lack of justice.
24 He who stings the rod hates his son, he who loves him strives to correct him.
25 The righteous eat their fill, but the stomach of the wicked is empty.
1 Wisdom builds a house, but foolishness destroys it with its own hands.
2 He who walks uprightly fears the Lord, but he who walks in crooked ways despises him.
3 Pride springs from the mouth of a fool, the lips of the wise are his defense.
4 Where there are no oxen, the stable is clean, but the strength of a bull brings much profit.
5 A truthful witness does not deceive, but a false witness utters lies.
6 The insolent seeks wisdom and does not find it, but knowledge is easy for the intelligent.
7 Get away from the presence of a fool: you will not find knowledge on his lips.
8 The wisdom of the prudent is knowing how to discern his path, the folly of fools is pure deceit.
9 A fool mocks atoning sacrifices, but among upright men is the favor of God.
10 The heart knows its own bitterness and no stranger associates with its joy.
11 The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the righteous will flourish.
12 There are paths that seem straight, but in the end they are paths of death.
13 Even between laughter, the heart suffers, and at last joy ends in sorrow.
14 The erring man is satisfied with the fruits of his conduct, and the good man with his actions.
15 The unwary believe everything they are told, but the prudent watch their steps.
16 The wise man fears evil and turns away from it, the fool is reckless and feels secure.
17 The angry man commits crazy things, the thoughtful man knows how to endure.
18 The inheritance of the unwary is foolishness, the crown of the prudent is knowledge.
19 The wicked will bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
20 The poor man is hateful even to his neighbor, but the rich man has many friends.
21 He who despises his neighbor sins, but happy is he who has pity on the humble!
22 Do not those who plot evil live astray? But there is love and fidelity for those who dedicate themselves to good.
23 Every fatigue brings some benefit, but charlatanry only brings poverty.
24 The crown of the wise is prudence, the diadem of fools is folly.
25 A truthful witness saves lives, he who speaks lies is an impostor.
26 The fear of the Lord is a safe refuge, which serves as a defense for children.
27 The fear of the Lord is a source of life, which separates us from the bonds of death.
28 A numerous people is the glory of the king, the lack of subjects is the ruin of the sovereign.
29 He who is slow to anger shows great intelligence, he who is angry shows his foolishness.
30 A peaceful heart is the life of the body, but envy corrodes the bones.
31 He who oppresses the weak insults his Creator, he who takes pity on the needy honors him.
32 The wicked is destroyed by his own malice, the righteous finds refuge in his integrity.
33 Wisdom lies in the intelligent heart, but it is not known among fools.
34 Justice exalts a nation, but sin is the shame of the people.
35 The king's favor is for the prudent servant, and his anger is for the shameless.
1 A gentle response appeases anger, a hurtful word exacerbates fury.
2 The tongue of the wise makes knowledge lovely, but the mouth of fools overflows with folly.
3 The eyes of the Lord are everywhere, watching the bad and the good.
4 A gentle tongue is a tree of life, a perverse tongue wounds the most living things.
5 A fool despises his father's instruction, but he who accepts rebuke is prudent.
6 In the house of the righteous there is much wealth, in the earnings of the wicked there is trouble.
7 The lips of the wise sow knowledge, but not the hearts of fools.
8 The sacrifice of the wicked is abominable to the Lord, the prayer of righteous men obtains his favor.
9 The Lord abhors the conduct of the wicked, but loves him who pursues righteousness.
10 He who abandons the path will be punished, he who hates rebuke will die.
11 The Abyss and Perdition are before the Lord: how much more the hearts of men!
12 An insolent man does not like to be rebuked, nor does he go to where the wise are.
13 A happy heart gladdens the countenance, a grieving heart depresses the spirit.
14 An intelligent heart seeks knowledge, the mouth of fools feeds on foolishness.
15 For the unfortunate, every day is bad, but the happy heart is always celebrating.
16 Better is a little with fear of the Lord than a great treasure with anxiety.
17 Better a plate of vegetables with love than a fattened ox, but with hate.
18 An angry man provokes quarrels, but he who is slow to anger calms disputes.
19 The path of the sluggard is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the industrious is clear.
20 A wise son brings joy to his father, a foolish son despises his mother.
21 Foolishness is the joy of the foolish, but the intelligent goes straight on his way.
22 Due to lack of deliberation, plans fail, with many advisors, they are carried out.
23 It is a man's pleasure to give a good answer, and how good is a timely word!
24 The wise man ascends a path of life, and thus turns away from the deep Abyss.
25 The Lord tears down the house of the proud, but keeps the boundaries of the widow standing.
26 Evil intentions are abominable to the Lord, but pure words please him.
27 He who gains dishonestly disturbs his house, he who hates bribery will live.
28 The righteous meditate before responding, but the mouth of the wicked overflows with evil.
29 The Lord is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
30 A bright look gladdens the heart, good news strengthens the bones.
31 The ear attentive to a salutary warning will lodge among the wise.
32 He who rejects correction despises himself, he who hears a rebuke gains wisdom.
33 The fear of the Lord is a school of wisdom, and humility precedes glory.
1 Man makes plans in his heart, but the Lord puts the answer on his lips.
2 A man thinks that all his ways are pure, but the Lord weighs hearts.
3 Commit your works to the Lord, and your projects will be carried out.
4 The Lord made everything for a purpose, even the wicked, for the evil day.
5 The haughty heart is abominable to the Lord, sooner or later it will not go unpunished.
6 Through goodness and faithfulness faults are atoned for, and evil is avoided by the fear of the Lord.
7 When the Lord is pleased with a man's conduct, he reconciles him even to his enemies.
8 Better is a little with justice than abundant profits with injustice.
9 The heart of man sets a course for itself, but the Lord secures his steps.
10 There is an oracle on the king's lips: he makes no mistake when he pronounces sentence.
11 The scale and the right scales belong to the Lord, and all the weights in the bag are his work.
12 The king hates evil deeds, because a throne is established by righteousness.
13 Righteous lips enjoy the favor of the king: he loves him who speaks rightly.
14 The king's anger is a messenger of death, but a wise man appeases it.
15 When the rest of the king is radiant, there is life, and his favor is like spring rain.
16 To acquire wisdom is worth more than fine gold, to acquire intelligence is preferable to silver.
17 The path of upright men is to turn away from evil; he who watches his way preserves his life.
18 Before a catastrophe there is pride, and before a fall there is a haughty spirit.
19 It is better to be humble among the poor than to share the spoils with the proud.
20 He who pays attention to the word will find happiness, and happy is he who trusts in the Lord!
21 He who knows how to discern is known for being intelligent, and sweet words are more persuasive.
22 Good judgment is a source of life for those who possess it, but foolishness is the punishment of fools.
23 The heart of the wise gives wisdom to his mouth and makes his words more persuasive.
24 Kind words are a honeycomb, sweet to the taste and healthy to the body.
25 There are paths that seem straight, but in the end they are paths of death.
26 The hunger of the worker works for him, because his mouth stimulates him.
27 The infamous man digs misfortune, and on his lips there is like a devouring fire.
28 A wicked man sows discord, and a slanderer separates friends.
29 The violent man seduces his neighbor to lead him astray.
30 He who closes his eyes, devising evil things, and purses his lips, has already committed evil.
31 White hair is a crown of glory, and it is found in the path of righteousness.
32 He who is slow to anger is worth more than a hero, and the self-possessed one is worth more than a conqueror.
33 Lots are cast in the folds of the mantle, but the decision comes from the Lord.
1 Better a dry crust with peace than a house full of banquets with discord.
2 The wise servant will prevail over the shameless son and will share the inheritance with his brothers.
3 There is a crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but it is the Lord who tests hearts.
4 The evildoer pays attention to slander, the liar listens to the evil tongue.
5 He who mocks the poor insults his Creator, he who rejoices in a misfortune will not go unpunished.
6 Grandchildren are the crown of the elderly, and the glory of children is their parents.
7 Refined language is not good for a fool, much less a lie for nobles!
8 A gift is a talisman for the giver: wherever he goes, everything turns out well for him.
9 He who hides an offense cultivates friendship; returning to things separates him from a friend.
10 One rebuke to an intelligent man does more than a hundred blows to a fool.
11 The wicked only seek rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent to him.
12 It is better to meet a bear deprived of her cubs than a fool in his madness.
13 If anyone returns evil for good, misfortune will not depart from his house.
14 Starting an altercation is opening a floodgate: leave before the dispute breaks out.
15 Absolving the wicked and condemning the righteous are two things that the Lord hates.
16 What is money for in the hands of a fool? To acquire wisdom? If you don't have intelligence!
17 A friend loves on any occasion, and a brother is born to share adversity.
18 He is a fool who shakes hands to be surety for his neighbor.
19 He who loves quarrels loves sin, he who raises his door too high seeks ruin.
20 A perverse heart will not find happiness, and a crooked tongue will fall into misfortune.
21 He who fathers a fool is his woe, and there is no joy for the father of a fool.
22 A cheerful heart is the best remedy, but a depressed spirit dries up the bones.
23 The wicked accepts gifts secretly to distort the paths of justice.
24 Before the intelligent man is wisdom, but the fool looks anywhere.
25 A foolish son is the sadness of his father and the bitterness of her who begat him.
26 If it is wrong to fine a righteous man, hitting nobles is beyond measure.
27 He who measures his words is a man of knowledge, and he who keeps his cool is intelligent.
28 Even a fool, if he remains silent, can be considered wise, and intelligent if he closes his lips.
1 He who lives in isolation follows his whims and is irritated against all sound advice.
2 The fool does not wish to understand, but rather to reveal his own opinions.
3 With wickedness comes ignominy, and with the loss of honor comes contempt.
4 Deep waters are the words of a man, an overflowing torrent is the fountain of wisdom.
5 It is not right to rehabilitate the wicked, harming the righteous in judgment.
6 The lips of a fool promote disputes, and his mouth incites striking.
7 The mouth of a fool is his ruin, and his lips are a trap for his life.
8 The words of the detractor are like sweets that go down to the depths of the bowels.
9 He who lets himself be at work is the brother of him who destroys.
10 The name of the Lord is a fortified tower: the righteous run to it and are safe.
11 The rich man's fortune is his stronghold, he imagines it as an impregnable wall.
12 Before ruin a man becomes arrogant, but humility precedes glory.
13 He who answers before listening shows his foolishness and attracts disgrace.
14 A man's spirit sustains him in his illness, but who will lift up a broken spirit?
15 An intelligent heart acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
16 A rule makes way for the one who gives it and introduces him into the presence of the great.
17 The first to defend his cause is right, until the adverse party arrives and challenges him.
18 Lots put an end to disputes and decide between the powerful.
19 An offended brother is more irreducible than a stronghold, and disputes are like the bolts of a citadel.
20 A man fills his stomach with the fruit of his words: each one is satisfied with what comes from his lips.
21 Death and life depend on the tongue, and those who indulge it will eat its fruit.
22 He who found a woman found happiness and obtained favor from the Lord.
23 The poor man speaks pleadingly, but the rich man responds harshly.
24 There are companions who lead to ruin and there are friends who are more attached than a brother.
1 Better is a poor man who walks in integrity than a foolish man with crooked lips.
2 Without science, not even zeal is good, and he who is hasty fails in his attempt.
3 The foolishness of man perverts his way, and then his heart is provoked against the Lord.
4 Fortune multiplies friends, but the poor man is separated even from his friend.
5 The false witness will not go unpunished and the one who speaks lies will not escape.
6 There are many who flatter the nobleman and they are all friends of the one who gives gifts.
7 Even his brothers hate the poor man, how much more will his friends distance themselves from him!
8 He who acquires good judgment loves himself, and he who is reasonable will do well.
9 A false witness will not go unpunished, and he who speaks lies will perish.
10 A comfortable life does not suit the fool, much less does it suit a slave to rule over princes!
11 A man's good judgment appeases his anger, and his glory is to overlook an offense.
12 The king's fury is like the roar of a lion, and his favor is like dew on the grass.
13 A foolish son is a calamity to his father, and a woman's quarrels are a constant drain.
14 House and fortune are the inheritance of parents, but a prudent woman is a gift from the Lord.
15 Sloth makes one fall into lethargy, and the lazy person will go hungry.
16 He who keeps the precepts keeps himself, he who neglects his own conduct will die.
17 He who has mercy on the poor lends to the Lord, and he will return the good he has done.
18 Correct your son while there is hope, but do not go on until he dies.
19 The irascible man exposes himself to fines, if you try to help him, you make things worse.
20 Listen to advice and accept correction, and in the end you will become wise.
21 There are many plans in the heart of man, but only the Lord's plan is carried out.
22 What is expected of a man is fidelity and it is better to be poor than a liar.
23 The fear of the Lord leads to life, he who is satisfied with it spends the night without being visited by evil.
24 The lazy man sinks his hand into the plate and is not even able to put it in his mouth.
25 Strike the insolent, and the simple will become cautious, rebuke the intelligent, and he will understand.
26 He who mistreats his father and casts out his mother is a son who causes shame and dishonor.
27 If you fail, my son, to listen to instruction, you will stray far from the words of wisdom.
28 A vile witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity.
29 There are punishments established for the insolent and blows for the backs of fools.
1 Wine is exciting and drink is turbulent: he who becomes drunk will not become wise.
2 The king's fury is like the roar of a lion: he who puts him outside risks his life.
3 It is a man's honor to avoid disputes, but a fool causes them to break out.
4 The lazy man does not plow in the fall, but in the harvest he searches, and there is nothing.
5 Deep waters are the designs of the human heart: the intelligent man knows how to extract them.
6 Many boast of their fidelity, but who will find a sincere man?
7 The righteous walk with integrity, happy are his children after him!
8 A king sitting at the judgment seat discerns all evil with his eyes.
9 Who can say, “I have purified my heart, I am clean from my sin”?
10 Use two weights and two measures, both of which the Lord made.
11 By his way of acting, the child already shows whether his conduct will be pure and upright.
12 The ear that hears and the eye that sees: the Lord made both.
13 Do not love sleep, so as not to become impoverished, open your eyes wide and you will be satisfied with bread.
14 "Bad, bad!" says the buyer, but as soon as he leaves, he congratulates himself.
15 There is gold and many pearls, but nothing is more precious than a wise mouth.
16 Take his clothes, because he was a surety for another, take him as a pledge, because he gave his guarantee to strange people.
17 The bread of lies is pleasant to a man, but then his mouth is filled with pebbles.
18 Projects are strengthened with advice and war is waged with strategy.
19 The slanderer discovers secrets, have nothing to do with a charlatan.
20 He who curses his father and mother will have his lamp go out in complete darkness.
21 Fortune gained quickly at the beginning will not be blessed at the end.
22 Do not say, "I will repay evil with evil," wait on the Lord and he will save you.
23 The Lord abhors the use of two weights, falsified scales are no good.
24 The steps of man depend on the Lord: how can man understand his way?
25 It is a trap for a man to consecrate something lightly and reconsider after making a vow.
26 A wise king discerns the wicked and turns the wheel on them.
27 The spirit of man is a lamp of the Lord, which searches to the depths of his bowels.
28 Goodness and faithfulness guard the king, and he upholds his throne by justice.
29 The glory of the young is their strength, and the splendor of the old is their white hair.
30 The sores of a wound are a remedy for evil and blows heal to the depths of the bowels.
1 The king's heart is a stream of water in the hands of the Lord: he directs it where he wills.
2 It seems to a man that all his path is right, but the Lord weighs the hearts.
3 Practicing justice and law pleases the Lord more than sacrifices.
4 Haughty eyes, an arrogant heart, the light of the wicked: all this is sin.
5 The projects of the industrious man are pure gain, he who is hasty ends up in poverty.
6 Treasures acquired by deceit are the fleeting illusion of those who seek death.
7 The plunder of the wicked carries them away themselves, because they refuse to do what is right.
8 Crooked is the path of the criminal, but he who is pure works righteously.
9 It is better to live in a corner of the roof than to share the house with a quarrelsome woman.
10 The soul of the wicked desires evil, he has no pity on his neighbor.
11 The simple becomes wise when the insolent is punished, and assimilates knowledge when the wise is instructed.
12 The righteous man observes the house of the wicked, and casts the wicked into misfortune.
13 He who closes his ears to the cry of the weak will call and there will be no answer.
14 A secret gift appeases anger, and a secret gift appeases violent fury.
15 Doing justice is a joy for the righteous, but it is a calamity for evildoers.
16 He who strays from the path of prudence will rest in the Assembly of Shadows.
17 He who loves pleasure ends in poverty, he who loves wine and the good life will not become rich.
18 The wicked will be a ransom for the righteous, and the traitor for the upright.
19 It is better to live in a desert country than with a quarrelsome and ill-tempered woman.
20 In the dwelling of the wise there are precious treasures and perfume, but the fool devours them.
21 He who pursues justice and faithfulness will find life, justice and honor.
22 The wise man takes a city of mighty men by storm, and destroys the strength in which she trusted.
23 He who guards his mouth and his tongue guards his life from trouble.
24 Insolent is called the arrogant and haughty person who acts with excessive pride.
25 Desire kills the lazy, because his hands refuse to work.
26 The wicked covets all day long, but the righteous gives without ever refusing.
27 The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination, how much more so if it is offered in infamy!
28 The lying witness will perish, but the man who listens will always be able to speak.
29 The wicked is bold, but he who is upright establishes his way.
30 There is no wisdom, nor understanding, nor counsel before the Lord.
31 The horse is equipped for the day of battle, but victory belongs to the Lord.
1 A good name is worth more than great riches, and being esteemed is worth more than silver and gold.
2 The rich and the poor have this in common: the Lord made them both.
3 The cautious man sees evil and hides, the unwary go ahead and pay it.
4 The reward of humility is the fear of the Lord, wealth, honor and life.
5 There are thorns and snares in the path of a crooked man: he who takes care of himself turns away from them.
6 Start the child on the path he should follow, and even in his old age he will not depart from it.
7 The rich dominate the poor and the debtor is a slave to the creditor.
8 He who sows injustice will reap misfortunes and the rod of his fury will destroy him.
9 The generous man will be blessed, because he shares his bread with the poor.
10 Throw out the insolent and the fighting will cease: there will be no more discord or insults.
11 He who loves purity of heart and speaks with grace has the king as a friend.
12 The eyes of the Lord watch knowledge, and he confuses the words of the traitor.
13 The lazy man says: "There is a lion outside, I am going to be killed in the middle of the street."
14 A deep pit is the mouth of other men's wives: he who provokes the Lord will fall into it.
15 Foolishness clings to the heart of a young man: the rod of correction will remove it from him.
16 He who exploits the weak to magnify himself will have to give to the rich and will end up destitute.
17 Words of the wise. Incline your ear, listen to my words, and pay attention to my experience:
18 It will be a delight to keep them inside you and always have them ready on your lips.
19 So that you can put your trust in the Lord, today I am going to instruct you too.
20 Have I not written you thirty speeches, containing advice and instructions,
21 to make you know exactly the true words, so that you can respond faithfully to him who sent you?
22 Do not rob the weak because they are weak, nor trample the poor at the city gate,
23 for the Lord will defend his cause, and those who rob him, he will rob of life.
24 Do not associate with a hot-tempered man or go with an angry man,
25 lest you learn their customs and set a trap for yourself.
26 Do not be one of those who shake hands, of those who are sureties for a debt:
27 If you do not have the means to pay, they will take away the bed on which you lie.
28 Do not move the old boundaries, those that your fathers placed.
29 Do you see a man skilled in his craft? He will appear before kings and will not be at the service of mediocre people.
1 If you sit at the table with a man, pay close attention to what is in front of you;
2 stick a knife in your throat, if you have a big appetite.
3 Do not covet their delicacies, for they are deceitful food.
4 Don't strive to get rich, stop thinking about that.
5 Your eyes fly towards wealth, and there is nothing anymore, because it puts on wings and flies towards the sky like an eagle.
6 Do not eat the bread of a malicious man or covet his delicacies,
7 because he is really what he thinks within himself: “Eat and drink,” he tells you, but his heart is not with you.
8 The morsel you ate, you will vomit, and you will have wasted your beautiful words.
9 Do not speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the good sense of your words.
10 Do not move the ancient boundaries, nor go into the fields of the orphans,
11 For his Avenger is mighty and will defend his cause against you.
12 Open your heart to instruction and your ears to the words of knowledge.
13 Do not be mean to correct a child: if you hit him with the rod, he will not die.
14 You will strike him with the rod, and you will deliver his life from the Abyss.
15 My son, if your heart is wise, my heart also will be glad:
16 My heart will rejoice when your lips speak righteously.
17 May your heart not envy sinners, but always fear the Lord.
18 Thus, surely, you will have a future and your hope will not be disappointed.
19 Listen, my son, and you will become wise, and direct your heart on the right path.
20 Do not associate with drunkards or those who gorge on meat,
21 because the drunkard and the glutton become poor, and drowsiness makes them walk around dressed in rags.
22 Listen to your father, who begat you, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
23 Acquire the truth and do not sell it, as well as wisdom, instruction and understanding.
24 The father of a righteous man rejoices, he who has a wise son rejoices over him:
25 May your father and mother rejoice and she who gave birth to you be filled with joy!
26 My son, pay attention to me and accept my ways willingly.
27 For a prostitute is a deep pit, and a strange woman is a narrow pit:
28 She also lies in wait like a thief and multiplies betrayals among men.
29 For whom are the lamentations? Who are the moans for? Who are the complaints for? For whom are the sighs? For whom are the wounds for no reason? For whom the cloudy look?
30 For those who spend their time drinking and go in search of aromatized wine.
31 Don't look at the wine: how red it is! How it sparkles in the glass! How it flows smoothly!
32 But in the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.
33 Your eyes will see strange things, your heart will speak without rhyme or reason;
34 You will be like a man lying on the high seas, lying on the top of a mast.
35 “They hit me, but it didn't hurt me; They hit me, but I didn't realize it. When will I wake up? I will order even more!
1 Do not envy the wicked or desire to be with them,
2 because his heart only plots violence and his lips speak only of misdeeds.
3 With wisdom a house is built and with intelligence it stands firm;
4 with science the pantries are filled with all the precious and pleasant goods.
5 Better is a wise man than a strong man, and a learned man than a very vigorous one,
6 because war is won with strategy and victory is won with the number of advisors.
7 Wisdom is too high for a fool: at the gate of the city he does not open his mouth.
8 He who only thinks of doing evil is called a master of evil.
9 Foolishness devises nothing but sin, and the insolent becomes abominable to men.
10 If you falter in the day of adversity, how little strength you have!
11 Deliver those who are dragged to death, save those who go with faltering steps to punishment.
12 If you say, "This is not my concern!" will not he who weighs hearts take it into account? He who observes you will know it and will reward each one according to his works.
13 Eat honey, my son, because it is good; Honeycomb honey is sweet to your palate.
14 Keep in mind that this is wisdom for your soul: if you find it, you will have a future and your hope will not be disappointed.
15 O evildoer, do not lie in wait for the abode of the righteous nor despoil his dwelling,
16 For the righteous, though he falls seven times, will rise, while the wicked sink into misfortune.
17 If your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and if he stumbles, do not rejoice,
18 lest the Lord see it and take it amiss, and turn his indignation away from him.
19 Do not be angry with evildoers or be envious of evildoers,
20 because the wicked has no future and his lamp will be extinguished.
21 Fear the Lord, my son, and also the king, and do not mix with the seditionists,
22 For their calamity will arise suddenly, and who knows the ruin that these two will cause?
23 These are also the words of the wise. It is not right to be a respecter of persons in judgment.
24 He who says to a guilty man, "You are innocent," is cursed by the people and execrated by the nations;
25 Everything goes well for those who condemn it and they will be blessed with happiness.
26 He who gives a correct answer gives a kiss on the lips.
27 Arrange your work outside, prepare it in the field, and then you will build your house.
28 Do not testify against your neighbor without reason: do you intend to deceive with your lips?
29 Do not say, "I will do to him what he did to me; I will repay him according to his works."
30 I passed by the field of a lazy man and by the vineyard of one who lacks understanding,
31 And I saw that nettles had grown everywhere, thistles covered the surface, and its stone fence was demolished.
32 When I saw this, I began to reflect, I looked and learned the lesson:
33 "Sleep a little, snooze a little, and rest a little with your arms crossed":
34 Thus poverty will come upon you like a robber and misery like an armed man.
1 These are also proverbs of Solomon, collected by the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
2 It is the glory of God to keep a thing hidden, and the glory of kings to investigate it.
3 The sky is high, the earth is deep, and the hearts of kings are impenetrable.
4 Remove the dross from the silver, and a vessel will come out for the goldsmith;
5 Remove the wicked from the presence of the king, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
6 Do not give yourself importance in the presence of the king nor put yourself in the place of the great:
7 It is better to be told, "Come up here," than to see yourself humiliated before a nobleman. What your eyes have seen,
8 do not rush to take him to court; for what will you do in the end, when your neighbor covers you with confusion?
9 Plead your cause against your neighbor, but do not reveal another's secret,
10 lest he who hears it blame you and your infamy is irreparable.
11 Apples of gold with filigrees of silver is the word said opportunely.
12 A ring of gold and a necklace of fine gold is the wise man who rebukes the one who knows how to listen.
13 Like the freshness of snow in harvest time, he is a faithful messenger to him who sends him: he comforts the spirit of his master.
14 Clouds and wind, but no rain, is he who boasts of giving and gives nothing.
15 With much patience a magistrate is convinced, and a soft tongue breaks even a bone.
16 Have you found honey? Eat what you need, lest you get fed up and have to throw it up.
17 Seldom set foot in your neighbor's house, lest he become fed up with you and hate you.
18 Mace, sword and pointed arrow is he who testifies falsely against his neighbor.
19 Chopped tooth, faltering foot is trusting the traitor when adversity comes.
20 To remove the cloak on a cold day, to pour vinegar on a sore, is to sing songs to a troubled heart.
21 If your enemy is hungry, feed him; If he is thirsty, give him a drink:
22 so you heap burning coals on your head and the Lord will reward you.
23 The north wind breeds rain and a mocking tongue, an irritated face.
24 It is better to live in a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome woman.
25 Fresh water for a parched throat is good news that comes from a faraway country.
26 A troubled fountain and a polluted spring is the righteous who hesitates before the wicked.
27 It is not good to eat a lot of honey or seek excessive honors.
28 A city dismantled and without a wall is the man who does not control his genius.
1 Like snow in summer and rain in the harvest, glory is so bad for a fool.
2 As the bird flutters and the swallow flies, so a gratuitous curse does not reach.
3 The whip for the horse, the bridle for the donkey, and the rod for the back of the fool.
4 Do not respond to a fool according to his foolishness, lest you also become like him;
5 Respond to a fool according to his folly, lest he be considered wise in his own eyes.
6 He mutilates his feet, he drinks trouble, he who sends messages through a fool.
7 As the legs of a lame man falter, so is a proverb in the mouths of fools.
8 Like holding a stone in the sling, it is paying honor to a fool.
9 A thorn in the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouths of fools.
10 An archer who strikes everyone who passes by is the one who hires a fool or a drunk.
11 As a dog returns to his vomit, so the fool returns to his folly.
12 Have you seen a man who considers himself wise? You can expect more from a fool than from him.
13 The lazy man says, “There is a lion on the road! A lion in the squares!
14 The door turns on its hinges and the lazy man on his bed.
15 The lazy man sinks his hand into the plate and gets tired just bringing it to his mouth.
16 The lazy person considers himself wiser than seven people who answer correctly.
17 Like grabbing a loose dog by the ears, it is meddling in someone else's dispute.
18 Like a madman who throws deadly torches and arrows at random,
19 Such is the man who deceives his neighbor and then says to him, “It was just a joke!”
20 Without wood the fire goes out, and if there is no detractor the fight subsides.
21 Coal for the embers and wood for the fire is a quarrelsome man who stirs up a dispute.
22 The words of the detractor are like sweets that go down to the depths of the bowels.
23 Silver dross applied to a clay vessel are the honeyed lips with an evil heart.
24 He who hates pretends with his lips, but harbors deceit within himself:
25 If he adopts a kind tone, do not trust, because there are seven abominations in his heart;
26 Hatred can be hidden by cunning, but in the assembly its malice will be revealed.
27 He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who rolls a stone will fall into it.
28 A lying tongue hates its victims, and a flattering mouth causes ruin.
1 Do not boast about tomorrow, because you do not know what each day brings.
2 Let someone else praise you, not your mouth, let him be a stranger, not your own lips.
3 Heavy is the stone and so is the sand, but heavier still is the spite of a fool.
4 Fury is cruel, wrath overflows with water, but who can withstand jealousy?
5 Better an open rebuke than hidden affection.
6 Loyal is the wound that a friend inflicts, the kisses of the enemy are deceptive.
7 A satisfied man tramples a honeycomb, for the hungry, even bitter is sweet.
8 Like a bird that wanders far from its nest, so is a man who wanders far from his home.
9 Perfumed oil gladdens the heart, and the sweetness of a friend more than advice itself.
10 Do not abandon your friend or your father's friend, nor go to your brother in the day of misfortune: a neighbor near is better than a brother far away.
11 Be wise, my son, rejoice my heart, and I will be able to reply to him who denigrates me.
12 The cautious man sees evil and hides, the unwary go ahead and pay it.
13 Take his clothes, because he was a surety for another, take him as a pledge, because he gave his guarantee to strange people.
14 Greeting your neighbor loudly, early in the morning, is considered a curse.
15 Incessant dripping on a rainy day and a quarrelsome woman are alike:
16 wanting to stop it is like stopping the wind or collecting oil with your hand.
17 Iron sharpens iron, and man sharpens his neighbor.
18 He who tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who respects his master will receive honors.
19 As the face is reflected in water, so a man sees himself in others.
20 The Abyss and Perdition are insatiable, and the eyes of man are also insatiable.
21 There is a crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but a man is valued for his reputation.
22 Even if you crush a fool in a mortar, among the grains, with a tamper, his foolishness will not depart from him.
23 Know well the condition of your sheep, pay close attention to your flocks,
24 because wealth does not last forever nor a diadem indefinitely.
25 When the grass was cut, the shoots appeared, and the hay from the mountains was piled up,
26 have lambs to clothe you, goats to pay the price of a field,
27 and enough goat's milk to feed you, to support your family, and for your servants to live on.
1 The wicked flees without anyone pursuing him. but the righteous are safe as a lion's cub.
2 When there is rebellion in a country, its leaders are many; With an intelligent and expert man, stability reigns.
3 A poor man who exploits the weak is like torrential rain that leaves no bread.
4 Those who abandon the Law praise the wicked, those who observe it are indignant against him.
5 The wicked do not understand what is right, those who seek the Lord understand everything.
6 Better is a poor man who walks in integrity than a rich man whose path is crooked.
7 He who observes the Law is an intelligent man, but he who associates with libertines dishonors his father.
8 He who increases his fortune with usury and interest accumulates it for him who has compassion for the poor.
9 If anyone turns away his ear from hearing the Law, even his prayer is an abomination.
10 He who leads the upright astray will himself fall into his own pit, but upright men will inherit happiness.
11 The rich man considers himself wise, but the poor intelligent man knows him thoroughly.
12 When the righteous triumph, there is great celebration; When the evil ones prevail, everyone hides.
13 He who conceals his crimes will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy.
14 Happy is the man who always fears the Lord, but the stubborn will fall into misfortune.
15 Roaring lion and hungry bear is the evil one who dominates a weak people.
