16 A prince without intelligence multiplies extortions, but he who hates profit will prolong his days.
17 A man burdened with the blood of another will flee to the grave: let no one stop him!
18 He who walks with integrity will be saved, he who goes crookedly on two paths falls into one of them.
19 He who cultivates his soil will be satisfied with bread, he who pursues chimeras will be satisfied with poverty.
20 The sincere man will be filled with blessings, the one who wants to become rich suddenly will not go unpunished.
21 It is not right to be a respecter of persons, but a man becomes venal for a morsel of bread.
22 The malicious man runs after fortune, not knowing that poverty will come upon him.
23 He who rebukes another will ultimately be more esteemed than the man with a flattering tongue.
24 He who despoils his father and mother and says, "This is no fault," is a companion of the one who destroys.
25 An ambitious man sows discord, he who trusts in the Lord will have prosperity.
26 He who trusts in himself is a fool, he who acts wisely will be saved.
27 He who gives to the poor will not know poverty, but he who closes his eyes will be filled with curses.
28 When the wicked triumph, everyone hides; When they disappear, the righteous multiply.
1 The man who refuses to be rebuked will be destroyed suddenly and without remedy.
2 When the righteous rule, the people rejoice; When an evil man rules, the people groan.
3 He who loves wisdom is his father's joy, he who frequents prostitutes squanders his wealth.
4 With law, a king gives stability to the country, but he who overwhelms it with taxes ruins it.
5 The man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net under his feet.
6 In the crime of the wicked there is a snare, but the righteous run full of joy.
7 The righteous care for the cause of the poor, but the wicked are unable to understand.
8 The provocateurs stir up the city, but the wise calm the effervescence.
9 When a wise man enters into a dispute with a fool, whether he is angry or amused, it resolves nothing.
10 The bloodthirsty hate the upright man, but the upright seek his company.
11 The fool gives free rein to his bad mood, but the wise restrains it and appeases it.
12 If a leader is carried away by gossip, all his servants become evil.

those times,
7 In her father's place will arise a shoot from the same roots as her: he will attack the army and penetrate the stronghold of the king of the North, fight against them and win.
8 Even his gods, with their statues of molten metal and their objects of silver and gold, he will take captive to Egypt; and he, for some years, will keep away from the king of the North.
9 The latter will then enter the kingdom of the king of the South, and then return to his country.

10 The sons of the king of the North will resume hostilities and gather a great multitude of troops. One of them will burst forth like an overflowing river, flood and bring hostilities to his stronghold.
11 The king of the South will be angry and will go out to fight against the king of the North. He will raise a great multitude, but they will fall into the hands of the king of the South.
12 The multitude will be annihilated; then his heart will be proud and he will humble thousands of men, but he will no longer be the strongest.
13 The king of the North will again raise a larger crowd than the first and, after a few years, will break out with a large and well-equipped army.
14 In those times, many will rise up against the king of the South, and some violent men from your people will rise up to fulfill a vision, but they will fail.
15 The king of the North will come, build ramparts, and take a fortified city. The forces of the South will not resist, and not even its chosen troops will have the strength to resist.
16 The invader will do as he pleases and no one will oppose him; He will settle in the country of Beauty, and the entire country will fall into his hands.
17 Then he will prepare to subdue the entire southern kingdom, and will make an agreement with him: he will give him an exceptional woman to destroy him, but that will not last or give him results.
18 He will turn toward the coastal regions, and conquer a good number of them; but a magistrate will put an end to the outrage, without him being able to return the affront.
19 Then he will return to the strongholds of his country, but he will stumble and fall and will not be found again.
20 In his place will arise one who will make a tax collector pass through the most beautiful land in the kingdom, but in a few days he will be destroyed, although not from the front or in war.
21 In his place will arise a commoner, who will not be invested with royal dignity. He will arrive quietly and take over the royalty through intrigue.
22 The opposing forces will be swept away before him and will be destroyed, as will the prince of the Covenant.
23 He will use the pacts made with him to act maliciously: thus he will rise high and become strong with few people.

24 He will enter quietly into the most fertile regions of the province, and will do what neither his fathers nor his fathers' fathers had done: he will distribute spoils, plunder among his people.
and riches, and will plan against strongholds, but only for a time.

25 At the head of a great army, he will stir up his strength and courage against the king of the South, and he will go to war with a great army, extremely strong, but he will not resist, because they will collude.
against him.
26 The same ones who ate his delicacies will destroy him, his army will be swept away and many victims will fall.
27 The two kings, full of evil intentions, will tell each other lies while sitting at the same table; but nothing will be accomplished, because the appointed time is yet to come.
28 He will return to his country with great riches and full of aversion against the holy Covenant: he will act and then return to his country.
29 At the appointed time, he will return to the South, but this last time will not be like the first.

30 Ships from Chitim will come against him, and he will be discouraged; He will turn back and vent his fury against the Holy Alliance; upon his return, he will reach an understanding with those who leave the Alliance
holy
31 Forces sent by him will attack, desecrate the Sanctuary and the Citadel, abolish the perpetual sacrifice and install the Abomination of Desolation.
32 Through intrigue he will cause the transgressors of the Covenant to apostatize, but the people of those who know God will stand firm and take action.
33 Wise men of the people will instruct many, but they will be victims of sword and fire, captivity and plunder, for some days.
34 As they fall, they will receive a little help, and many will join them, but hypocritically.
35 Some of the wise men will fall, in order to be purified, tested and whitened, until the time of the End, because the deadline is set.

36 The king will act as he pleases, he will exalt himself and magnify himself above all gods, and he will say monstrous things against the God of gods. And he will succeed until the Wrath is exhausted, because what is
decreed will be executed.
37 He will not respect the gods of his fathers, nor the favorite god of women; He will not respect any divinity, because he will exalt himself above all.
38 In his place he will honor the god of fortresses: he will honor a god his fathers did not know, with gold, silver, precious stones and valuables.

39 He will use the people of a foreign god as defenders of the fortress; and he will shower everyone who recognizes him with honors, give him authority over many, and distribute plots of land to him.
land.

40 At the time of the End, the king of the South will attack him. The king of the North will attack him like a whirlwind, with war chariots, cavalry and numerous ships; will penetrate the countries like a river
overflowing and will flood them.
41 He will enter the land of Beauty, and thousands of men will fall, but Edom, Moab, and the rest of the Ammonites will be delivered from his hand.
42 He will stretch out his hand over the countries, and the land of Egypt will not escape.
43 He will take possession of the treasures of gold and silver, and all the precious objects of Egypt; The Libyans and the Cushites will march in his train.
44 But news from the East and the North will fill him with fear; then he will go out full of fury to destroy and exterminate many people.
45 He will plant the pavilions of his palace between the sea and the holy mountain of Beauty, and then he will come to an end, without anyone coming to his aid.

1 At that time, Michael, the great Prince, will arise, standing beside the children of your people. It will be a time of tribulation, such as has never existed since there was a nation.
until the present time. At that time, your people will be liberated: everyone who
is registered in the Book.
2 And many of those who sleep on the dusty ground will awaken, some to eternal life, and others to ignominy, to eternal horror.
3 The wise men will shine like the brightness of the firmament, and those who have taught many righteousness will shine like the stars, forever and ever.
4 As for you, Daniel, hide these words and seal the Book until the time of the end. Many will search here and there, and knowledge will increase.
5 I, Daniel, looked and saw that two other men were standing, one on one bank of the river and another on the opposite bank.
6 One of them said to the man dressed in linen who was standing on the waters of the river, "When will these wonders end?"

7 I heard the man dressed in linen standing on the waters of the river. He raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by him who lives forever: "A time will pass, two times and
half a time; and when the force of the
holy people, all these things will also end.
8 I heard, but I did not understand. Then I said, "My Lord, what will be the last of these things?"
9 He answered, “Go Daniel, for these words are hidden and sealed until the end time.
10 Many will be purified, whitened and refined; The wicked will do evil, and no wicked will be able to understand, but the wise will understand.
11 From the time when the perpetual sacrifice will be abolished and the Abomination of Desolation will be installed, one thousand two hundred and ninety days will pass.
12 Happy is he who knows how to wait and reaches one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days!
13 As for you, go to the end: you will rest and rise to receive your lot at the end of days.
1 Adam, Seth, Enos;
2 Quenan, Mahalalel, Iered;
3 Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech;
4 Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth.
5 The descendants of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Ivan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.
6 The descendants of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
7 The descendants of Iavan were Elisha, Tarshish, Chitim, and Rodanim.
8 The descendants of Ham were Cush, Misraim, Put and Canaan.
9 The descendants of Cush were Sheba, Javilah, Sabta, Raemah, and Sabteca. The descendants of Raemah were Sheba and Dedan.
10 Cush was the father of Nimrod, who was the first warrior on earth.
11 Misraim was the father of the Jews, of the Annamites, of the Iahabites, of the Naphtuhites,
12 of the Patrusites, the Casluhites and the Caphtorites, from which the Philistines come.
13 Canaan was the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and of Heth;
14 also of the Jebusites, of the Amorites, of the Girgashites,
15 of the Hivites, of the Archites, of the Sinites,
16 of the Arvadites, the Semarites and the Jamathites.
17 The descendants of Shem were Elam, Ashur, Arpaxad, Lud and Aram. The descendants of Aram were Us, Jul, Geter and Meshech.
18 Arpaxad was the father of Shelah, and he was the father of Eber.
19 Eber had two sons; The name of the first was Peleg, because it was in his time that the earth was divided. His brother was called Ioctan.
20 Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerach,
21 Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
22 Ebal, Abimael, Sheba,
23 Ophir, Javilah and Iobab. All of these were descendants of Ioctan.
24 Sem, Arpaxad, Shelach,
25 Pelech, Reu,
26 Serug, Nahor, Terah,
27 Abram, that is, Abraham.
28 Abraham's sons were Isaac and Ishmael.
29 These were their descendants: The firstborn of Ishmael was Nebaioth; then, Quedar, Abdeel, Mibsam,
30 Mismah, Dumah, Massah, Jadad, Temah,
31 Ietur, Nafis and Quedma. These are the sons of Ishmael.
32 Descendants of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: she gave birth to Zimran, Yochshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah. The sons of Jochshan were Sheba and Dedan.
33 The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Enoch, Abidah, and Eldaah. All of these are descendants of Quetura.
34 Abraham was the father of Isaac. Isaac's sons were Esau and Israel.
35 The descendants of Esau were Eliphaz, Reuel, Ieush, Iaelam, Korah.
36 The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Shephi, Gaetam, Kenaz, Timna and Amalek.
37 The sons of Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizah.
38 The descendants of Seir were Lotan, Shobal, Sibeon, Anah, Dishon, Eser and Dishan.
39 The sons of Lotan were Hori and Homam; and Lotan's sister was Timnah.
40 The sons of Shobal were Allian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi and Onam. The sons of Sibeon were Aiah and Anah.
41 The descendants of Anah were Dishon and his sons, namely, Hamram, Esban, Itram and Cheram.
42 The sons of Eser were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Yaakan. The sons of Dishan were Us and Aran.
43 The kings who reigned in Edom before the Israelites had a king are these: Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
44 When Bela died, Iobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah succeeded him.
45 When Iobab died, Husham of the land of the Temanites succeeded him.
46 When Husam died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the field of Moab, succeeded him; the name of their city was Avith.
47 When Hadad died, Samlah succeeded him, Samlah of Masrekah succeeded him.
48 When Samlah died, Saul of Rehoboth of the River succeeded him.
49 When Saul died, Baal Hanan son of Acbor succeeded him.
50 When Baal Hanan son of Acbor died, Hadad succeeded him; The name of his city was Pai, and the name of his wife was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, who in turn was the daughter of Mezahab.
51 Hadad died, and there were leaders in Edom: the leader Timnah, the leader Aliah, the leader Yeteth,
52 the leader Oholibamá, the leader Elá, the leader Pinón,
53 the leader Kenaz, the leader Teman, the leader Mibsar,
54 the leader Magdiel, the leader Iram. These were the leaders of Edom.
1 These are the children of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah, Issachar and Zebulun,
2 Dan, Joseph and Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

3 The descendants of Judah were Er, Onan and Shelah; All three were born to him by the daughter of Shuah, the Canaanite. Er, the firstborn of Judah, was evil in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord took away his
life.
4 Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, bore him Perez and Zerah. The sons of Judah were five in all.
5 The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
6 The sons of Zerah were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Chalcol and Dardah: five in all.
7 The son of Carmi was Achar, who troubled Israel by violating the anathema.
8 Ethan's son was Azariah.
9 The sons of Hezron were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
10 Ram was the father of Aminadab; Aminadab was the father of Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah.
11 Nahshon was the father of Salma; Salma was the father of Boaz.
12 Boaz was the father of Obed; Obed was the father of Jesse.
13 Jesse was the father of Eliab, his firstborn; of Abinadab, his second son; from Shimeah, the third;
14 of Nathanael, the fourth; of Radai, the fifth;
15 of Osem, the sixth; of David, the seventh.
16 His sisters were Seruiah and Abigail. The sons of Seruiah were Abishai, Joab and Asahel: three in all.
17 Abigail gave birth to Amasa, whose father was Iether the Ishmaelite.
18 Caleb son of Hezron had children with his wife Azubah and Jerioth. His sons were Ieser, Shobab and Ardon.
19 When Azubah died, Caleb took Ephrathah as his wife, and to her he was born Hur.
20 Hur was the father of Uri, and Uri was the father of Besalel.
21 Then Hezron married the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead. He was sixty years old when he took her as his wife, and to her Segub was born.
22 Segub was the father of Jair, who owned twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead,
23 But Geshur and Aram took from him the camps of Yair, and also Kenath and its towns: sixty cities in all. They were all descendants of Machir, father of Gilead.
24 When Hezron died, Caleb joined himself to Ephrathah, the wife of his father Hezron, and to her was born Ashhur the father of Tekoah.
25 The descendants of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron, were Ram, his firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Osem, and Ahijah.
26 Jerahmeel had another wife named Ataraah, who was the mother of Onam.
27 The sons of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, were Maash, Yamin, and Echer.
28 The sons of Onam were Shamai and Iadah; The sons of Samai were Nadab and Abisur.
29 The name of Abishur's wife was Abihail, and she gave birth to Ahban and Molid.
30 The sons of Nadab were Sheled and Apaim. Séled died without having children,
31 And the son of Apaim was Isei. The son of Isei was Sheshan, and the son of Sheshan was Ahlai.
32 The sons of Iadah, the brother of Samai, were Iether and Jonathan. Iether died without having children,
33 And the sons of Jonathan were Pelet and Zazah. These were the descendants of Ierachmeel.
34 Sheshan had no children. but daughters; He also had an Egyptian slave named Iarjá,
35 to whom he gave one of his daughters as a wife, and she became the mother of Atai.
36 Atai was the father of Nathan; Nathan was the father of Zabad;
37 Zabad was the father of Ephalal; Eflal was the father of Obed;
38 Obed was the father of Jehu; Jehu was the father of Azariah;
39 Azariah was the father of Jeles; Jelesah was the father of Elasah;
40 Elasah was the father of Shishmai; Shishmai was the father of Shallum;
41 Shallum was the father of Iecamiah, Iecamiah was the father of Elishama.
42 The descendants of Caleb, the brother of Jerahmeel, were: Mesha, his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Maresah, the father of Hebron.
43 The sons of Hebron were Korah, Tappuach, Rechem, and Shema.
44 Shema was the father of Rajam, the father of Jorkeam; Rechem was the father of Samai.
45 The son of Shammai was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth Sur.
46 Ephah, Caleb's concubine, gave birth to Harran, Mozah, and Gazez; Haran was the father of Gazez.
47 The sons of Jahdai were Regem, Jotham, Gesham, Peleth, Ephah and Saaf.
48 Maacah, Caleb's concubine, gave birth to Sheber and Tirchanah.
49 She also gave birth to Shaaph, the father of Madmanah, and Sheva, the father of Macbenah and Gibeah. Caleb's daughter was Achsha.
50 These were the sons of Caleb. The descendants of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, were Shobal, father of Kiriath Iearim;
51 Shalmah, father of Bethlehem; Haref, father of Beth Gader.
52 The descendants of Shobal, the father of Kiriath Iearim, were Haroeh, that is, half of the Manachathites.
53 and the clans of Kiriath Iearim, namely, the Itrites, the Putites, the Sumatites, and the Misraites. The Soratíes and those of Estaol come from them.
54 The descendants of Shalma were Bethlehem and the Netophathites, Atrot Bet Joab - the other half of the Manachatites - the Sorites,
55 the clans of the Sofries who lived in Iabés, the Tiratíes, the Simatíes and the Sukatíes. These are the Kenites, descendants of Hamath, father of the house of Rechab.
1 These are the sons who were born to David in Hebron: Amnon the son of Ahinoam of Izreel, his firstborn; Daniel, son of Abigail of Carmel, his second son;
2 Absalom, son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur, the third; Adonijah, son of Jagit, the fourth;
3 Shephatiah the son of Abital, the fifth; Itream, son of his wife Eglá, the sixth.
4 These six sons were born to David in Hebron, where he reigned seven years and six months. Furthermore, David reigned in Jerusalem thirty-three years,
5 And these are the sons who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimeah, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon, the four sons of Bathsheba, daughter of Ammiel.
6 Also Ibjar, Elishama, Eliphelet,
7 Nogah, Nepheg, Iafiah,
8 Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet, that is, nine.
9 These are all the sons of David, not counting the sons of his concubines. Their sister was Tamar.
10 Solomon's son was Rehoboam; Rehoboam's son, Abijah; Abijah's son Asa; Asa's son, Jehoshaphat;
11 Jehoshaphat's son Jehoram; Joram's son, Ahaziah; Ahaziah's son, Joash;
12 Joash's son Amaziah; Amaziah's son, Azariah; Azariah's son Jotham;
13 Jotham's son Ahaz; the son Ahaz, Hezekiah; Jotham's son Ahaz; Ahaz's son Hezekiah; Hezekiah's son, Manasseh;
14 Manasseh's son Ammon; the son of Ammon, Josiah.
15 The sons of Josiah were Yochanan, his firstborn; Joaquím his second son; Zedekiah, the third; and Shallum, the fourth.
16 The sons of Jehoiakim were Jeconiah and Zedekiah.
17 The descendants of Jeconiah the prisoner were Shealtiel,
18 Malkiram, Pedaiah, Shinesar, Iechamiah, Hosamah, and Nedabiah.
19 The sons of Pedaiah were Zerubbabel and Shimei; the sons of Zerubbabel, Meshullam, Hananiah, and Shelomith, their sister.
20 The sons of Meshullam, Jashubah, Ohel, Berekiah, Hashadiah, and Iushab Hesed: five in all.
21 The son of Hananiah was Pelatiah; Pelatias' son, Isaiah; Isaiah's son, Rephaiah, Arnan; Arnan's son, Obadiah; Obadiah's son, Shecaniah.
22 The sons of Shecaniah were Shemaiah, Jathus, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat: six in all.
23 The sons of Neariah were Elioenai, Hezekiah, Azricam: three in all.
24 The sons of Elioenai were Hodiaiah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akcub, Yochanan, Delaiah, and Anani: seven in all.
1 The descendants of Judah were Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur and Shobal.
2 Rheaiah the son of Shobal was the father of Jahat; Yajat was the father of Ajumai and Lahad. These are the families of the Soreatites.
3 The descendants of Etam were Izreel, Ishma and Ibdas. His sister was called Haslelponí.
4 Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer was the father of Husah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, father of Bethlehem.
5 Ashhur, father of Tekoa, had two wives: Jelah and Naarah.
6 Naarah gave birth to Ahuzam, Jepher, the Timnites, and the Ahastarites. These are the sons of Naara.
7 The sons of Jelah were Sereth, Sojar, and Ethnan.
8 Cos was the father of Anub, of Hasobebah, and of the families of Ajarhel, the son of Harum.
9 But Iabez was more famous than his brothers, and his mother gave him the name Iabez, saying, "I gave birth in pain."

10 Iabas called upon the God of Israel, exclaiming, "If you truly bless me, you will enlarge my borders, your hand will be with me, and you will drive away evil so that my affliction may disappear." And God
granted what he had asked for.
11 Chelub, Shuha's brother, was the father of Mechir, who was the father of Estón.
12 Estón was the father of Beth Rafah, of Paseah, and of Techinah, the father of Ir Nachas. These are the men of Rekah.
13 The sons of Kenaz were Othniel and Seraiah; the sons of Otniel, Jatat and Meonatai.
14 Meonatai was the father of Ophrah, and Seraiah was the father of Joab, founder of the Valley of the Blacksmiths, because they were blacksmiths.
15 The sons of Caleb the son of Jephuneh were Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah's son was Kenaz.
16 The sons of Jehalelel were Ziph, Zipha, Tiria and Asarel.
17 The sons of Ezra were Iether, Mered, Epher, and Ialon. Bithiah gave birth to Miriam, Samai, and Ishbaj, father of Estemoa.

18 The wife of Estemoa, the wife of Judah, gave birth to Iered, the father of Gedor, to Eber, the father of Soco, and to Iecutiel, the father of Zanoah. These are the sons of Bithia, Pharaoh's daughter, whom Mered
had taken as a wife.
19 The wife of Odias, the sister of Naham, the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Estemoah the Maacathite, also had children.
20 Simon's sons were Amnon, Rinah, Ben Hanan, and Tilon. The sons of Isei were Zójet and Ben Zójet.
21 The descendants of Shelah the son of Judah were Er the father of Lekah, Lada the father of Mareshah, and the families of the flax workers at Beth Ashbeah.
22 Iochim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, and Saraph were married in Moab, before returning to Bethlehem. These are very old facts.
23 They were potters and lived in Netaim and Gederah; They lived there with the king, working at his service.
24 The descendants of Simeon were Nemuel, Iamin, Iarib, Zerah and Saul.
25 Saul's son was Shallum; Shallum's son Mibsam; the son of Mibsam, Mishma;
26 the son of Mismah, Jamuel; Jamuel's son, Zacur; Zaccur's son, Shimei.
27 Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; But his brothers did not have many children, and all their clans were not as numerous as the descendants of Judah.
28 They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar Shual,
29 Bilhah, Esem, Tolad,
30 Bethuel, Jorma, Shekelag,
31 Bet Marcabot, Jasar Susim, Bet Biri and Saaraim. These were their cities until the reign of David.
32 Their towns were Etham, Ain, Rimmon, Token and Asan – five cities in all –
33 and all the towns that are around those cities, as far as Baalat. They lived there and were registered by groups.
34 Mesobab, Iamlech, Iosah, son of Amaziah;
35 Joel, Jehu, son of Iosibiah, son of Seraiah, son of Asiel;
36 Elioenai, Iaacoba, Iesojaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Ieshimiel and Benaiah;
37 Zizah, son of Siphi, son of Allon, son of Iedaiah, son of Shimri, son of Shemaiah:
38 All these who have been mentioned by name were leaders in their clans, and their families multiplied considerably.
39 They went to the entrance to Gerar, to the east of the valley, looking for pasture for their livestock.
40 And they found abundant and good pasture, and a spacious, quiet, and secure land, because the descendants of Ham had lived there before.

41 Those who were mentioned by name came in the time of Hezekiah king of Judah and destroyed the camps of the descendants of Ham and the shelters that were there,
consecrating them to total extermination until today. There they settled
instead of them, because there was pasture for their cattle.
42 Some of Simeon's sons, five hundred men, went to Mount Seir, their leaders being Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Isei;
43 And after they defeated the remnant of Amalek, who had fled, they lived there to this day.

1 Descendants of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. Reuben was the first to be born, but because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, to the son of Israel, and was not
inscribed in the genealogies as the firstborn.
2 Judah, in fact, prevailed among his brothers and from him comes the Prince; but the birthright belongs to Joseph.
3 The descendants of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, were Enoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
4 Joel's son was Shemaiah; Shemaiah's son, Gog; Gog's son Shimei;
5 Shimei's son Micah; Micah's son, Rheaiah; Rheaiah's son, Baal;
6 the son of Baal, Beerah, whom Tiglath Pileser, king of Assyria, carried away captive. This was leader of the Reubenites.
7 His brothers, grouped by families according to their genealogies, were Ieiel, the first, then Zechariah,
8 and Belah, son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel. These lived in Aroer and extended to Nebo and Baal Meon.
9 They also extended to the east, to the edge of the wilderness bordering the Euphrates River, because their livestock had multiplied in the land of Gilead.
10 In the time of Saul they fought against the Agarites, and they fell into their hands. Thus they occupied their camps throughout the eastern part of Gilead.
11 The children of Gad lived opposite them in the land of Bashan as far as Salkah.
12 Joel was the first to settle in Bashan; Sefán, the second; then Ianai and Safat did it.
13 His brothers, grouped by families, were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Iorai, Iacán, Zia and Eber: seven in all.
14 These are the sons of Abijail, the son of Huri, the son of Yaroah, the son of Gilad, the son of Michael, the son of Iesisai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz.
15 So the son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, was head of their families.
16 They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and in all the pastures of Sharon, to its borders.
17 All of them were recorded in the days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel,

18 The sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and half of the tribe of Manasseh were very brave; they carried shield and sword and wielded the bow. Those who were trained for war formed
an army of forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty men.
19 They fought against the Agarites, against Jetur, Naphis and Nodab,
20 And God helped them, so that the Agarites and all who were with them fell into their hands; In combat they invoked God and he was favorable to them, because they trusted in him.
21 Thus they managed to capture their livestock – fifty thousand camels, two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys – as well as one hundred thousand people.
22 Since it was God who fought on their behalf, they killed many enemies and took their place until the exile.

5 When Saul saw that he was dead, his armor bearer also fell on his sword and died.
6 So Saul and his three sons died; His entire house died at the same time.

Philistines and settled there.

9 Then they stripped Saul and took his head and his weapons. Then they sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to announce the good news to their idols and to the people.
10 They deposited Saul's weapons in the temple of God and hung his head in the temple of Dagon.
11 When all Iabas of Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,

12 All the brave men set out, removed Saul's body and the bodies of his sons, and took them to Iabas. There they buried his bones under the Terebinth
of Iabés and fasted seven days.
13 Thus Saul died, because he had rebelled against the Lord, not keeping his word, and because he had evoked and consulted the spirit of a dead man,
14 instead of consulting the Lord. That is why the Lord put him to death and transferred the kingship to David, son of Jesse.
1 All Israel gathered around David in Hebron and said to him, “We are of your blood!

4 The Hall in front, whose length covered the entire width of the House, was ten meters, and had a height of sixty meters. Furthermore, he covered it inside with pure gold.
5 He covered the central nave with cypress wood and then covered it with fine gold, on which he had palm trees and garlands represented.
6 He covered the ship with a decoration of precious stones, and the gold used was gold from Parvaim.
7 He also overlaid the posts, the thresholds, the walls, and the doors of the nave with gold, and had cherubim carved on the walls.

9 You saw the misery of our fathers in Egypt, you heard their cry by the Red Sea,

10 You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, against his servants and all the people of his country, because you knew with what arrogance they had treated them; Thus you acquired a reputation that lasts until
today.
11 You parted the sea for them, and they crossed it without getting their feet wet; But you plunged their pursuers into the abyss, like a stone into mighty waters.
12 You guided them by day with a pillar of cloud and by night with a pillar of fire, to illuminate the path they should travel.
13 You went down to Mount Sinai and spoke to them from heaven; You gave them just rules and trustworthy laws, excellent precepts and commandments.
14 You made known to them your holy Sabbath day and prescribed for them commandments, precepts and a Law, through Moses your servant.

15 You gave them bread from heaven to satisfy their hunger, you made water flow from the rock to quench their thirst, and you commanded them to go and take possession of the land that, with your hand raised, you had sworn to give them.
16 But our fathers were arrogant, stubborn, and disregarded your commandments.

17 They refused to obey, not remembering the wonders you had done for them; They were obstinate, insisting on returning to their servitude in Egypt. But you are the God of forgiveness, compassionate and
merciful, slow to anger and full of faithfulness; That's why you haven't
abandoned.
18 They made themselves a calf of molten metal, saying, "Here is your God, who brought you out of Egypt," and thus they committed a great outrage.

19 But even then, in your great mercy, you did not abandon them in the wilderness: the pillar of cloud did not depart from them by day to guide them on the way, not the pillar of fire during the
night, to illuminate the path they had to travel.
20 You gave them your good spirit, so that they would know how to discern; You did not take the manna from their mouths and gave them water to quench their thirst.
21 You sustained them for forty years in the desert and they never lacked anything: their clothes did not wear out nor did their feet swell.
22 You gave them kingdoms and peoples, and divided them as a border area: they took possession of the country of Sihon, king of Heshbon, and the country of Og, king of Bashan.
23 You multiplied their children like the stars of heaven, and brought them into the land that you had promised their fathers to possess.

24 The sons entered and took possession of the country, and you subdued the inhabitants of the country, the Canaanites, before them: you put them into their hands, as well as their kings and the people of the country, so that they
They will treat them at their discretion.

25 Thus they conquered strongholds and fertile soil; They took over houses full of all kinds of goods, dug cisterns, vineyards and olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. They ate until
They were satisfied and fat, and because of your great goodness, they lived in the midst of delights.
26 But afterwards they were unruly and rebelled against you: they threw your Law behind their backs, they killed the prophets who warned them to return to you, and they committed great outrages.

27 You delivered them into the hands of their oppressors, and they oppressed them. In the time of oppression, they cried out to you; you listened to them from heaven and, because of your great
mercy, you sent them saviors who saved them from their oppressors.

28 But as soon as they felt calm, they did evil again before you, and you abandoned them into the hands of their enemies, who oppressed them; They called on you again and you heard them from heaven:
How many times did you save them by your mercy!

29 You commanded them to return to your Law, but they were arrogant and did not obey your commands; They sinned against your standards, which man must fulfill to have life;
They turned their backs in rebellion, were obstinate and did not obey.
30 You were patient with them for many years; you warned them with your spirit, through your prophets; but they did not listen and you handed them over to other peoples.
31 However, in your great mercy you have not destroyed them or abandoned them, for you are a compassionate and merciful God.

32 And now, our God, great, powerful and fearsome God, who maintains the covenant and faithfulness, do not despise the tribulations that have befallen us, our kings and our kings.
our leaders, our priests and prophets, our fathers and all your
people, from the time of the kings of Assyria to the present day.
33 You have been righteous in everything that has happened to us, because you have acted faithfully and we have committed evil.
34 Yes, our kings, our leaders, our priests and our fathers did not practice the law, they did not heed your commandments or the warnings you had given them.
35 During their reign, in the midst of the great goods that You granted them, and in the spacious and fertile land that You gave them, they did not serve You nor did they turn from their evil deeds.
36 Look, today we are enslaved, yes, we are slaves here, in the country that you gave to our fathers, so that we could enjoy its fruits and its goods.

37 Their abundant products are for the kings whom you have imposed on us because of our sins, and they dispose of our people and our livestock at their discretion. In what oppression we have

king's cities

trumpets.

chosen.

1 In the one hundred and fifty-first year, Demetrius, son of Seleucus, left Rome and arrived with a few men at a maritime city, where he proclaimed himself king.

21 Alcimus fought to remain in the high priesthood,
22 And all those who were disturbing the people joined him: thus they became masters of Judah and caused tremendous damage to Israel.
23 Judas, seeing that Alcimus and his followers were doing more harm to the Israelites than to the pagans,
24 He went out to tour the entire territory of Judea to take revenge on the deserters and not let them circulate through the region.

28 «Let us not make war; "I will go to interview them in peace with a small escort."
29 When he appeared before Judas, they both greeted each other friendly, but the enemies were ready to kidnap Judas.

37 “You have chosen this House, which is called by your Name, to be a house of prayer and supplication for your people.
38 Give this man and his army what they deserve, and let them fall by the edge of the sword. Remember their blasphemies and do not give them respite.
39 Nicanor left Jerusalem and camped at Bethhoron, where he was joined by a contingent from Syria.
40 Judas, for his part, camped at Adasa with three thousand men, and prayed this:
41 "When the king's messengers blasphemed, your Angel appeared and destroyed one hundred and eighty-five thousand of them.
42 Likewise, destroy this army before us today, so that the rest may recognize that their leader blasphemed against your Sanctuary, and judge him according to his wickedness.
43 On the thirteenth day of the month Adar, the armies entered into battle and Nicanor's army was defeated. The first to fall was Nicanor himself,
44 And when the soldiers saw that he had fallen, they threw down their weapons and fled.
45 The Israelites pursued them for a whole day, from Adasa to the vicinity of Gazara, blowing alarm trumpets behind them.
46 People came out from all the surrounding Jewish towns and surrounded them, until they were forced to turn against each other.

47 So they all fell by the edge of the sword, and not one was left. The Jews seized the spoils and the booty, and cut off Nicanor's head and his right hand, which he had raised with
arrogance Then they took them and hung them at the entrance of
Jerusalem.
48 The people were filled with joy; everyone celebrated that day like a big party
49 And they determined to commemorate that day every year, the thirteenth of Adar.

to them; Above all, he learned that they were brave warriors.

the ends of the earth, had defeated them, completely crushing them,
while the rest paid tribute to them every year.

8 of their best provinces – the region of India, Media and Lydia – which they later handed over to King Eumenes.

They plundered their property, subdued the country, razed their fortresses, and
They imposed their dominance to this day.

21 The proposal pleased the Romans.
22 And this is the copy of the document that they engraved on bronze plates and sent to Jerusalem as a memorial of peace and covenant:
23 «May the Romans and the nation of the Jews have happiness at sea and on land forever! Far be it from them the sword and the enemy!
24 If war first threatens Rome, or any of its allies, in any part of its dominions,
25 The nation of the Jews will fight at your side with all their heart as circumstances demand.
26 The enemies will not receive wheat, nor weapons, nor money, nor ships. This is what Rome has established. They will observe their commitments without any compensation.
27 In the same way, if a war first threatens the nation of the Jews, the Romans will fight at their side, with all their soul as circumstances demand.
28 Their attackers will not receive wheat, weapons, money, or ships. This is what Rome has established. They will observe their commitments with loyalty.
29 These are the clauses that the Romans stipulated with the Jewish People.
30 "If later each of them decides to add or remove something, they will do so by common agreement, and what they add or remove will have binding force."

Canaan.

are not subject to any authority other than that of the High Priest.
39 I give the city of Ptolemais and its surroundings as a present to the Temple of Jerusalem, to cover the expenses of the Sanctuary.
40 For my part, I will give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver, which will be taken from the king's revenue in the appropriate places.
41 All the amount that the treasury agents have stopped paying, as was done in previous years, will be delivered from now on for the works of the Temple.
42 In addition, the five thousand shekels of silver that used to be collected each year from the income of the Sanctuary will be remitted for the benefit of the priests who practice worship.

43 All those who, due to a debt to the royal Treasury or for any other reason, take refuge in the Temple of Jerusalem or in any of its premises, will be absolved, they with the
possessions they have in my kingdom.
44 The expenses for the construction and repair works of the Sanctuary will be borne by the king.

45 The king will also be in charge of building the walls of Jerusalem and fortifying its enclosure, as well as rebuilding the walls in the cities of Jerusalem.
Judea.

46 When Jonathan and the people heard these words, they did not believe them or accept them, because they remembered the great damage that Demetrius had caused to Israel and the oppression
to which he had subjected them.
47 Then they decided on Alexander because, in their opinion, he made better peace proposals, and they were always his allies.
48 King Alexander gathered a large army and took a position against Demetrius.
49 Both kings engaged in battle, and Alexander's army retreated. Demetrius pursued them and prevailed over them.
50 And although he fought fiercely until sunset, Demetrius succumbed that day.
51 Alexander sent an embassy to Ptolemy, king of Egypt, with this message.
52 “I have returned to my kingdom, and have sat on the throne of my fathers, taking power. After defeating Demetrius, I have taken possession of my country,
53 For I fought with him, I defeated him and his army, and I occupied his royal throne.
54 Let us now establish bonds of friendship between us: give me your daughter as a wife, and I will be your son-in-law, and I will give you and her gifts worthy of you.
55 King Ptolemy answered in these terms: “Happy the day when you returned to the country of your fathers, to sit on its royal throne!
56 I am going to fulfill right now what you have written. Come to Ptolemaida so we can meet, and I will be your father-in-law as you have said.
57 Ptolemy left Egypt with his daughter Cleopatra and arrived at Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.
58 King Alexander went to meet him, and Ptolemy gave him his daughter Cleopatra, the wedding being celebrated in Ptolemais with the magnificence typical of kings.
59 Then Alexander wrote to Jonathan to come and see him.

60 He went to Ptolemais with great pomp; There he met with the two kings and presented them with silver and gold, also offering numerous gifts to his Friends. In this way he gained the favor of
them.
61 Then a group of transgressors, the most undesirable people of Israel, conspired against him and accused him before the king. But this one, instead of paying attention to them,
62 He ordered that Jonathan be stripped of the clothes he was wearing and dressed in purple. So they did it.
63 The king made him sit next to him and said to his dignitaries: "Go around the city with him and proclaim that no one dares to bring any accusation against him or bother him for any reason."
64 As soon as his detractors saw the honors paid to him, the terms of the proclamation and the purple with which he was clothed, they fled.
65 The king honored him by enrolling him among his chief Friends, and made him general and governor.
66 So Jonathan returned to Jerusalem in peace and full of joy.
67 In the one hundred and sixty-fifth year, Demetrius, son of Demetrius, came to the country of his fathers from Crete,
68 and Alexander, very upset by this news, returned to Antioch.
69 Demetrius appointed Apollonius, the governor of Coele-Syria, general, and he raised a large army and camped in Iamnia, sending to the High Priest Jonathan to say:
70 “You are the only one who rebels against us, and because of you, I am mocked and despised. Why do you use your authority against us in the mountains?
71 If you really trust your troops, go down now to face us on the plain, because I count on the troops of the cities.
72 Find out, and you will know who I am and who are those who help us: they say that you cannot resist us, since your fathers were defeated twice in their own country.
73 Now you will not be able to face the cavalry and such a large army on this plain, where there is not a stone, not a rock, not a place to take refuge.
74 When Jonathan heard Apollonius' message, he was deeply troubled. Then he chose ten thousand men and left Jerusalem. His brother Simon joined him to help him.
75 Then he camped in front of Joppa, but the inhabitants of the city closed the gates to him because there was a garrison of Apollonius there. As soon as the attack began,
76 The inhabitants of the city, terrified, opened the gates to him, and thus Jonathan took possession of Joppa.

77 Upon hearing this, Apollonius put three thousand cavalry and a large infantry on the warpath, and set out in the direction of Azotus, as if he were passing through; but at the same time he was entering into the
plain, confident in his numerous cavalry.
78 Jonathan pursued him in the direction of Azotus, and the two armies engaged in battle.
79 Apollonius had left a thousand horsemen hidden behind them.
80 But Jonathan realized that they were lying in wait behind him. The enemies surrounded his army, shooting arrows at them all day long.
81 The troops stood firm, as Jonathan had commanded, while the enemy's horses grew tired.
82 Then Simon advanced his squadrons and attacked the infantry, because the cavalry was exhausted: thus he defeated them and forced them to flee.
83 The cavalry scattered across the plain, and the fugitives fled to Azotus and entered the House of Dagon, the temple of their idol, to safety.
84 Jonathan burned Azotus and the surrounding cities and took the spoils. He also burned the temple of Dagon, with all those who had taken refuge in it.
85 Those who perished by sword or by fire were about eight thousand men.
86 Then Jonathan departed from there and camped in front of Ashkelon, whose inhabitants came out to welcome him with great honors.
87 Then he returned with his people to Jerusalem, taking with him great booty.
88 When King Alexander heard of all this, he granted new honors to Jonathan;
89 He sent him a golden pin, as is customary to grant to the relatives of kings, and he gave him Aharon and his entire kingdom.
1 The king of Egypt gathered an army as numerous as the sand on the seashore and a great fleet, because he intended to seize Alexander's kingdom by cunning and unite it with his own.

2 Then he went to Syria under peaceful pretexts, and the inhabitants of the cities opened the doors to him and came out to meet him, because Alexander had given orders to receive him, since it was their
father-in-law
3 As Ptolemy entered the cities, he left a garrison in each of them.

4 When he was near Azotus they showed him the temple of Dagon burned down, the city and its surroundings in ruins, the corpses scattered and the charred remains of those who had been burned in
the battle, because they had piled them up where the king was going to pass.
5 Then they told the king everything that Jonathan had done, hoping that he would disapprove, but the king remained silent.
6 Jonathan, for his part, went to meet the king in Joppa with great pomp; they both greeted each other and spent the night there.
7 Then Jonathan accompanied the king to the river called Eleutheros, and from there he returned to Jerusalem.
8 King Ptolemy took over the coastal cities as far as Seleucia Maritima. Meanwhile, he was plotting his plans against Alexander.

9 To this end, Ptolemy sent an embassy to King Demetrius, with this message: “Let us make an alliance between us. I will give you my daughter, the one that Alexander now has, and you will be king in your kingdom.
father.
10 I am sorry for having given it to him, since he tried to kill me.
11 In reality, he made these charges because he coveted his kingdom.
12 Then he took his daughter from Alexander and gave her to Demetrius: thus he broke with Alexander and their enmity became evident.
13 Then he entered Antioch and put on the crown of Asia, thus putting on his forehead two crowns, that of Egypt and that of Asia.
14 At that time King Alexander was in Cilicia, because the people of that region had rebelled.
15 As soon as he heard about it, he went out to fight him, but Ptolemy mobilized a powerful army and defeated him.
16 Alexander fled to Arabia in search of refuge, and King Ptolemy was in control of the situation.
17 The Arab Zabdiel cut off Alexander's head and sent it to Ptolemy.
18 But three days later Ptolemy also died, and the inhabitants of the strongholds killed the Egyptians stationed there.
19 Demetrius began to reign in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.
20 At that time, Jonathan gathered the inhabitants of Judea to attack the Citadel of Jerusalem and to that end he built numerous war machines.
21 Some renegades, enemies of their own nation, came to the king and told him that Jonathan was besieging the Citadel.

22 This news angered him and he immediately set out and went to Ptolemais. At the same time, he wrote to Jonathan, ordering him to suspend the siege and go as soon as possible to Ptolemais to
interview him.
23 When Jonathan heard about this, he ordered the siege to continue and decided to face the danger himself: he chose a group of elders and priests from Israel,
24 And he went to Ptolemais to meet the king, taking with him silver, gold, clothing, and many other gifts. In this way, he gained the favor of the king
25 Some renegades from his nation accused him,
26 But the king treated him as his predecessors had done and honored him in the presence of all his Friends.
27 He confirmed him in the high priesthood and in all the high positions he had previously held, and gave him a preeminent place among his leading Friends.
28 Jonathan asked the king to exempt Judea and the three districts of Samaria from taxes, promising him three hundred talents in return.
29 The king approved it and sent Jonathan a document about what was discussed, in the following terms:
30 «King Demetrius greets his brother Jonathan and the Jewish people.
31 For your information, we enclose a copy of the letter we wrote about you to our relative Lasthenes.
32 King Demetrius greets his father Lasthenes.
33 Because of their good feelings towards us, we have decided to favor the Jewish People, who are our Friend and respect our rights.

34 We confirm to you the territorial limits of Judea, with the three districts of Apherema, Lydda and Ramataim. These, with all their adjacencies, were separated from Samaria and annexed to
Judea, for the benefit of those who offer sacrifices in Jerusalem, in
compensation for the royal taxes that the king received from them each year,
about the products of the earth and the fruits of the trees.

35 As regards our other rights – the tithes, the taxes due to us from the salt mines, and the golden crowns – from now on, we declare them exempt from
all obligation.
36 None of these concessions will be repealed from now on.
37 Have a copy of this document made, to give it to Jonathan and display it on the Holy Mountain, in a clearly visible place.

38 King Demetrius saw that the whole country was calm under his command and that he encountered no obstacles. Then he discharged his army, sending each one to his home, except the
foreigners whom he had recruited in the islands of the nations. By
For this reason, he attracted the hostility of all the troops of his ancestors.
39 Trypho, a former supporter of Alexander, seeing that all those troops were protesting against Demetrius, went to see the Arab Imalcué, tutor of Antiochus, the son of Alexander.

40 He pressed him to hand him over to him, so that he might reign in his father's place; He informed him of everything Demetrius had done and of the hatred his troops had for him, and he remained there.
long time.
41 Meanwhile, Jonathan asked King Demetrius to remove the garrisons from the Citadel of Jerusalem and the strongholds, because they were continually harassing Israel.

42 Demetrius commanded Jonathan to say, "Not only will I do for you and your nation what you ask of me, but I will shower you and your nation with honor as soon as a favorable opportunity presents itself."
43 But now you would do well to send some men to my aid, because all my troops have deserted.
44 Jonathan sent three thousand brave soldiers to Antioch, and when they presented themselves to the king, he was glad at their arrival.
45 But the inhabitants of the city, about one hundred and twenty thousand men, rioted in the streets, intending to kill the king.
46 He took refuge in his palace, while the people occupied the streets and the attack began.
47 Then the king asked the Jews for help, and they all gathered around him. Then they dispersed throughout the city, and that day they killed about a hundred thousand people.
48 Then they burned the city and collected a large amount of booty that same day, thus saving the king.
49 When the people saw that the Jews completely dominated the city, they became discouraged and began to plead with the king:
50 «Let's make peace! "Let those Jews stop attacking us and the city!"
51 And they laid down their weapons and made peace. The Jews covered themselves with glory before the king and all his vassals, and returned to Jerusalem with abundant booty.
52 Thus King Demetrius established himself on his royal throne, and the country was pacified under his rule.
53 But then he failed to keep his promises and distanced himself from Jonathan, not reciprocating the services he had given him and causing him great suffering.
54 After a while, Trypho returned, accompanied by Antiochus, who was still very young, and he took the throne, putting on the crown.
55 All the troops killed by Demetrius took his side and fought against Demetrius, defeated him and forced him to flee.
56 Trypho seized the elephants and occupied Antioch.

57 Then the young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan, "I confirm you in the high priesthood, I make you head of the four districts, and I want you to be numbered among the
Friends of the king.
58 At the same time, he sent him gold tableware and a complete table set, authorizing him to drink from gold cups, to dress in purple, and to wear a gold pin.
59 He appointed his brother Simon as commander from the Ladder of Tire to the border of Egypt.

60 Jonathan went out to tour the region and the cities on this side of the Euphrates, where all the Syrian troops joined him as war allies. When
He arrived at Ashkelon, its inhabitants came out to welcome him with many honors.
61 From there he went to Gaza, but the inhabitants closed the doors to him. He then besieged the city and looted and burned its surroundings.

62 The inhabitants of Gaza came to ask him for mercy, and Jonathan made peace with them, but he took the sons of the chiefs as hostages and sent them to Jerusalem. Then he crossed the
country heading to Damascus.
63 Jonathan learned that Demetrius's generals were near Kedes of Galilee with a large army, to make him desist from his project.
64 So he left his brother Simon in the country and went out to meet them.
65 Simon camped in front of Bethsur, attacked it for many days, and besieged it.
66 Its inhabitants made him a proposal of peace and he accepted, but he forced them to evacuate the city, and took possession of it, placing a garrison there.
67 Jonathan and his army camped by the lake of Gennesaret, and early in the morning they came to the plain of Ashor.
68 The foreign army met them on the plain, leaving some men in ambush in the mountains. As the army advanced forward,
69 those who were in ambush left their positions and entered into combat.
70 Jonathan's men fled, and not a single one was left except Mattathias son of Absalom and Judas son of Calphi, generals of the army,
71 Jonathan tore his clothes, covered his head with dust, and prayed.
72 Then he resumed the fight, defeated the enemy and put them to flight.
73 When Jonathan's fleeing men saw this, they joined him again, pursued the enemy together to their camp at Kedesh, and camped there.
74 That day about three thousand men of the foreign army fell. Then Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
1 Jonathan, seeing that circumstances were favorable to him, chose a few men and sent them to Rome to confirm and renew friendship with the Romans.
2 He also sent letters to the Spartans and other places in the same sense.

3 When the Jews arrived in Rome and appeared before the Senate, they said, "The high priest Jonathan and the nation of the Jews have sent us so that you may renew with them the
friendship and the pact, as previously established.
4 The Senate gave them safe passage to the different countries, so that they could reach the country of Judah safely.
5 This is the copy of the letter that Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:
6 «Jonathan, High Priest, the council of the nation, the priests and all the Jewish People greet their brothers in Sparta.

7 Already in times past, Areios, who reigned among you, sent a letter to the High Priest Onias in which he told him that you are our brothers, as the copy attests
attached.
8 Onias received the ambassador with all honors, and accepted the letter that spoke clearly of pact and friendship.
9 Now we, although we have no need of these things, because we find comfort in the holy Books that are in our hands,

10 we have allowed ourselves to send ambassadors to you to renew the fraternal friendship that binds us to you, in order not to behave like strangers, since a long time has passed
since they wrote to us.

11 We remember you at all times, especially on festivals and other appropriate days, when we offer sacrifices and make prayers, since it is right
and it is convenient to remember the brothers.
12 We rejoice greatly in your glory.
13 We, however, have been involved in many tribulations and wars, and have been attacked by neighboring kings.
14 But we did not want to disturb you or our other allies and friends because of these wars,
15 because we have the help of Heaven that constantly assists us. Thus we were freed from our enemies and they were humiliated.
16 Now we have chosen Numenius, son of Antiochus, and Antipater, son of Jason, and have sent them to the Romans to renew with them our ancient covenant of friendship,
17 Furthermore, we ordered them to go and greet you and give you the letter with which we want to renew our brotherhood.
18 Now be kind enough to answer us.
19 This is the copy of the letter that had been sent to Onias:
20 «Areios, king of the Spartans, greet Onias, High Priest.
21 In a document dealing with the Spartans and the Jews, it is stated that they are brothers and that they belong to the race of Abraham.
22 Now that we know this, please write to us to see how they are doing.

23 We, for our part, write to you: Your livestock and all your possessions are ours, and ours are yours. Consequently, we order that a message be sent to them
to communicate this to you."
24 Jonathan heard that Demetrius's generals had returned with a larger army than before to fight against him.
25 He then left Jerusalem and went to confront them in the region of Jamat, without allowing them time to invade his domain.
26 He sent spies to the enemy camp, and when they returned, they told him that the Syrians were preparing to attack them during the night.
27 As the sun set, Jonathan ordered his men to keep watch all night with weapons in hand, ready to engage in battle, and he established outposts around the camp.
28 When the enemies learned that Jonathan and his men were prepared for battle, they were greatly afraid and lit fires in their camp.
29 But Jonathan and his men, seeing the fires burning, did not notice his departure until dawn.
30 Jonathan pursued them, but could not overtake them, because they had already crossed the river Eleutherus.
31 Then Jonathan turned against the Arabs called the Sabbadians, defeated them, and seized the spoils.
32 Then he resumed his march toward Damascus and traveled through the entire region.
33 Simon, for his part, made an expedition to Ashkelon and the neighboring fortresses. Then he turned to Joppa and took it,
34 because he had learned that its inhabitants wanted to hand over the stronghold to Demetrius's men. That is why he left a garrison there to defend it.
35 Upon his return, Jonathan gathered the elders of the people together and decided with them to build fortresses in Judea.

36 He also resolved to raise the walls of Jerusalem and to build a great wall between the Citadel and the rest of the city, in order to separate them, so that the Citadel would be isolated and
its inhabitants could not buy or sell.
37 Then they gathered together to rebuild the city, because the part of the wall facing the eastern torrent had fallen, and the part called Cafenata was also restored.
38 Simon, for his part, rebuilt Adidah in Shephelah, fortified it, and secured it with gates and bolts.
39 Meanwhile, Tryphon aspired to reign over Asia and take on the crown, eliminating King Antiochus.
40 Fearing that Jonathan would prevent him and make war on him, he looked for a way to stop him and get rid of him. Then he set out and came to Bethshan.
41 Jonathan went out to meet them with forty thousand men chosen for war and also came to Bethshan.
42 Trypho, seeing that he appeared with such a large army, did not dare to confront him.
43 He received him with great honors, recommended him to all his Friends, gave him gifts and ordered his Friends and his troops to obey him as himself.
44 Then he said to Jonathan, “Why have you exhausted all these people if there is no war between us?

45 Send them home now, stay with a small escort, and come with me to Ptolemais. I will hand it over to you with the other strongholds, the rest of the troops and all the
officials. "I will return immediately, because that is why I have come."
46 Jonathan trusted him and did as Tryphon had told him: he discharged the troops, and they withdrew to the country of Judea,
47 and he reserved only three thousand soldiers, leaving two thousand in Galilee and having the other thousand accompany him.
48 But as soon as Jonathan entered Ptolemais, its inhabitants closed the doors, seized him, and put all those who had entered with him to the edge of the sword.
49 Then Trypho sent troops and cavalry to Galilee and the Great Plain to destroy all of Jonathan's supporters.

50 But when they realized that Jonathan had been captured and had perished with all his companions, they encouraged one another and advanced in very compact ranks,
determined to fight.
51 Their pursuers, seeing that they were determined to risk their lives, began to retreat.
52 Thus they were able to return safely to the country of Judah, where they mourned Jonathan and his companions, in the midst of great fear. There was great mourning in Israel,

53 and all the neighboring towns tried to exterminate them, because they said: "They no longer have a leader or anyone to help them. Let's attack them right now, and erase their memory from among the
men."
1 Simon learned that Tryphon had gathered a large army to invade and devastate Judea.
2 Seeing that the people were in a panic, he went up to Jerusalem and gathered its inhabitants
3 And he exhorted them, saying, “You know very well all that I and my brothers and my father's family have done for the laws and the Sanctuary, and the wars and tribulations that we have endured.
4 Because of this, all my brothers have died for Israel and I am left alone.
5 But far be it from me to try to save myself in times of danger, since I am not worth more than my brothers!
6 On the contrary, I will avenge my nation, the Sanctuary, your women and your children, because all the peoples, out of hatred for us, have united to exterminate us.
7 When they heard these words, the spirit of the people was inflamed.
8 and they all answered him with one voice: “You are our leader, in; place of Judas and your brother Jonathan:
9 direct our war, and we will do everything you command us.
10 Then he gathered all the men fit for war, and hastened to finish the walls of Jerusalem and fortified all around it.
11 Immediately he sent Jonathan son of Absalom to Joppa with a large number of men, and he expelled its inhabitants and settled there.
12 Tryphon set out from Ptolemais at the head of a large army to invade the country of Judah, taking Jonathan prisoner with him.
13 Then Simon camped in Addidah, opposite the plain.
14 When Trypho learned that Simon had succeeded his brother Jonathan in command and was prepared to fight with him, he sent messengers to him saying:
15 “We have your brother Jonathan in our possession for debts incurred to the royal treasury in the performance of his office.
16 Send us a hundred talents of silver and two of his sons as hostages, lest once he is released he turns against us. Only then will we release him."
17 Simon, although he realized the deception, ordered the money and the children to be brought, so as not to provoke strong opposition from the people,
18 who otherwise would have said, "Because I didn't send him the money and the children, Jonathan died."
19 Then he sent the children, along with the hundred talents, but Trypho broke his word and did not release Jonathan.
20 After this, he set out to invade the country and devastate it. He detoured along the road to Adorah, while Simon and his army followed him wherever he went.
21 At the same time, those of the Citadel sent messengers to Tryphon, urging him to come through the desert and bring them provisions.
22 Trypho prepared all his cavalry to go, but that night so much snow fell that they could not advance. So he left and went to Gilead.
23 Near Bascamah, he had Jonathan killed and buried there.
24 Then Trypho turned around and returned to his country.
25 Simon ordered the remains of his brother Jonathan to be collected and buried them in Modin, the city of his fathers.
26 All Israel mourned for him greatly and wept for him for many days.
27 Simon built a mausoleum high above the tomb of his father and brothers, so that it could be seen, covering it behind and in front with polished stones.
28 He built seven pyramids, one facing the other, dedicated to his father, his mother and his four brothers.

29 He decorated them, surrounding them with large columns and placed shields with weapons on them, in eternal remembrance. Along with the weapons, he had some ships sculpted, so that those who could see them could see them.
They sail through the sea.
30 This is the mausoleum that he built in Modín and that exists to this day.
31 Trypho, who acted insidiously with the young king Antiochus, ended up killing him.
32 He took his throne and put on the crown of Asia, wreaking great havoc on the country.
33 Simon, for his part, repaired the fortresses of Judea, surrounded them with high towers and great walls with gates and bars, and stored provisions in them.
34 Then he chose some men and sent them to King Demetrius, so that he could grant the country a remission of taxes, since Tryphon had done nothing but commit depredations.
35 King Demetrius agreed to his request, and wrote him this letter:
36 «King Demetrius greets Simon, High Priest and friend of kings, the elders and the nation of the Jews.

37 We have received the golden crown and the palm branch that you sent us and we are ready to grant you complete peace and to order the officials to grant you peace.
exemption from debts.
38 Everything that We have decreed for you will remain in force, and the fortresses that you have built will remain in your power.
39 We pardon them for the errors and crimes committed to this day and we renounce the crown they owe us. If any other tax was collected from Jerusalem, it will no longer be required.
40 If any of you are suitable to join our entourage, you can register. And may there be peace between us.
41 In the one hundred and seventieth year Israel was freed from the yoke of the nations.
42 From then on, the people began to write in the documents and contracts: "First year of Simon, distinguished High Priest and chief general of the Jews."
43 In those days Simon camped in front of Gazara and besieged it with his troops. He built a mobile assault tower and brought it closer to the city; Thus he attacked one of the bastions and took it.
44 Those who were in the tower jumped into the city, and there was a great commotion among the people.
45 The inhabitants of the city, with their women and children, went up to the wall, tearing their clothes and crying out to Simon to grant them peace.
46 "Do not treat us, they said, according to our iniquities, but according to your mercy."

47 Then Simon was reconciled to them and stopped attacking them, but he expelled them from the city and purified the houses where there were idols. So he entered the city, singing hymns and
blessings.
48 After cleansing it of all impurity, he settled people there who practiced the Law, fortified it, and built a residence for himself.

49 Those who occupied the Citadel of Jerusalem, since they could not go back and forth in the region to buy and sell, were beset by famine, and many of them died of
starvation.
50 Then they cried out to Simon, asking him for peace. He granted it to them, but expelled them from there and purified the Citadel of all contamination.

51 The Jews entered it on the twenty-third day of the second month of the one hundred and seventy-first year, with cheers and clapping, to the sound of harps, cymbals, and zithers, and singing hymns and songs,
for a great enemy had been exterminated from Israel.
52 Simon ordered that this day be celebrated every year with joy. He then fortified the Temple Mountain along the Citadel and settled there with his people.
53 And when he saw that his son John was now a man, he appointed him general of all the troops. Juan lived in Gazara.
1 In the one hundred and seventy-second year, King Demetrius gathered his troops and went to Media to obtain help to fight Tryphon.
2 Arsaces, king of Persia and Media, hearing that Demetrius had entered his territory, sent one of his generals to capture him alive.
3 He set out and defeated the army of Demetrius; He took him prisoner and brought him before Arsaces, who had him imprisoned.
4 While Simon lived, the land of Judah enjoyed peace. He sought the well-being of the nation; His authority and magnificence were always accepted by everyone.
5 He added to his many glorious actions, the conquest of Joppa as a port, and opened an outlet to the islands of the sea.
6 He extended the borders of his nation and held the country in his hands.
7 He distributed many captives; He conquered Gazara, Bethsur and the Citadel, and purified them of all impurity, without encountering any resistance.
8 The land was cultivated in peace, the soil produced its crops and the trees of the plain their fruits.
9 The elderly sat in the squares, everyone commented on the prevailing well-being, and the young people were dressed in colorful military uniforms.
10 He supplied the cities with food and equipped them with means for their defense, so that the renown of his glory reached to the ends of the earth.
11 He restored peace to his nation, to the great joy of Israel:
12 each one sat under his vine and his fig tree without anyone disturbing him.
13 The enemies disappeared from the country and in those days the kings were destroyed.
14 He protected the humble of his people, faithfully observed the Law and eliminated the wicked and the wicked.
15 He gave new splendor to the Temple and enriched it with many sacred vessels.
16 When it became known in Rome and Sparta that Jonathan had died, they were very sorry.
17 But when he heard that his brother Simon had succeeded him as high priest and had taken over the government of the country and its cities,
18 They wrote to him on bronze plates to renew with him the pact of friendship that they had established with their brothers Judas and Jonathan.
19 The text was read in Jerusalem before the assembly.

20 This is the copy of the letter sent to the Spartans: "The magistrates and the city of the Spartans greet the High Priest Simon, the elders, the priests and the rest
of the Jewish People, our brothers.
21 The ambassadors sent to our people have told us about your glory and prestige. That is why we have been glad of your coming.

22 We have recorded their statements in the records of the people as follows: Numenius, son of Antiochus, and Antipatros, son of Jason, ambassadors of the Jews, have
presented to renew your friendship with us.

23 It was the people's pleasure to receive them with all the honors and to deposit the copy of their speeches in the public archives, so that they could serve as a reminder to the Spartan people. It has been
made a copy of this for the High Priest Simon.
24 Then Simon sent Numenius to Rome with a large golden shield weighing a thousand minas, to confirm the agreement with them.
25 When the people heard these things, they said, “How will we express our gratitude to Simon and his sons?

26 For he and his brothers and all his father's family have fought steadfastly and driven out the enemies of Israel, and have secured his freedom. Then they recorded

1 Yes, vain by nature are all men who have ignored God, who, starting from visible things, were not able to know "Him who is", considering their
works, they did not recognize the Artificer.
2 Instead, they took the fire, the wind, the subtle air, the starry vault, the rushing water, or the luminous stars of the sky as ruling gods of the universe.

3 Now if, fascinated by the beauty of these things, they considered them as gods, think how much more excellent is the Lord of all of them, since the same Author of beauty
He is the one who created them.
4 And if you were impressed by their power and energy, understand from them how much more powerful is He who formed them.
5 Because, starting from the greatness and beauty of things, if he manages, by analogy, to contemplate his Author,
6 However, these men do not deserve a serious rebuke, because perhaps they go astray seeking God and wanting to find Him;
7 As they live busy with their works, they investigate them and allow themselves to be seduced by what they see: so beautiful is the spectacle of the world!
8 But even so they are not excusable:
9 If they have been able to acquire so much knowledge to scrutinize the course of the entire world, how did they not find the Lord of all more quickly?

10 Wretched, because they have put their hope in dead things, those who called gods works made by the hands of man, gold and silver worked with art, figures of animals,
or a worthless stone sculpted by an ancient hand!
11 Take, for example, a woodcutter: he cuts down a tree that is easy to overturn with a saw, skilfully removes all the bark, works it with skill, and makes of it a useful object for common use.
12 With the leftover kindling he heats his food and satisfies his appetite.

13 But there is still a remnant that is useless, a twisted trunk full of knots: he takes it, sculpts it to fill his leisure time, he carves it with skill in his free moments, and
gives human form
14 or makes him like a vile animal. Afterwards, he covers it with minium, colors the surface red, and hides all its effects with a plaster;
15 prepares a suitable place for it, places it on the wall and secures it with a nail.
16 In this way, take precautions so that he does not fall, knowing that he cannot help himself, because he is nothing more than an image and needs help.
17 However, when he prays for his possessions, for his home or his children, he is not ashamed to speak to that lifeless object: he demands health from a cripple,
18 implores life from a dead person, asks for help from the most inexperienced; When embarking on a journey, pray to those who are unable to take a step;
19 For your profits, your companies and the success of your work, ask for strength from those who do not have any strength in their hands!
1 Another embarks ready to ride the wild waves and invokes a wood more decayed than the ship that carries him.
2 Because that ship was conceived by the desire for profit and built by artisanal wisdom,
3 but it is your Providence, Father, that directs the rudder. Yes, you have made a way in the sea and a safe path among the waves,
4 thus showing that you can save from all danger, even if one embarks without any experience.
5 You do not want the works of your Wisdom to be sterile: that is why men entrust their lives to a simple piece of wood, and safely cross the waves on a fragile boat.

6 Thus, in the beginning, while the proud giants perished, the hope of the world took refuge in a weak boat, which, directed by your hand, left the germ of new things to the future.
generations.
7 Blessed is the wood that has become an instrument of justice,
8 But cursed is the idol made by human hands, both it and its maker: this one because he made it and the other because, being corruptible, he was called god.
9 For God equally hates the wicked and their wickedness,
10 and the manufactured object will be punished along with its author.

11 For this reason the idols of the nations will also be judged, since they have become an abomination among God's creatures, a cause of scandal to the souls of the nations.
men and a trap for the feet of fools.
12 The invention of idols is the origin of fornication, and their discovery is the corruption of life.
13 They did not exist in the beginning nor will they exist forever,
14 but they entered the world through human superstition: therefore a quick end is in store for them.

15 A father, afflicted by premature mourning, commissions an image of his son so soon taken away, and who before was nothing more than a corpse, he now honors as a god and transmits mysteries to his people.
and rituals,
16 Then, in time, this unholy custom is observed as a law.

17 Likewise, by order of the sovereigns, the statues were worshiped: since they could not be honored in person, due to the distance, they reproduced that distant figure, making a visible image of the
king they revered; Thus the absent person was fervently flattered as if he were
present.
18 The artist's ambition helped to spread this cult, attracting even those who did not even know the king,
19 because he, undoubtedly desirous of pleasing the sovereign, used all his art to make him more beautiful than he was;
20 and the people, seduced by the charm of the work, turned into an object of adoration the one they had previously honored as a man.
21 And this turned out to be a threat to the living, since men, victims of misfortune or tyranny, attributed the incommunicable Name to stones and wood.
22 But it was not enough for them to make mistakes in the knowledge of God, but, struggling in the tremendous struggle caused by ignorance, they give the name of peace to so many evils.
23 With its infanticidal rites, its hidden mysteries and its frenetic orgies of extravagant customs,
