24 they no longer keep their lives or marriages pure; one eliminates the other by treason or afflicts him by adultery.
25 Chaos reigns everywhere: blood and death, theft and fraud, corruption, disloyalty, agitation, perjury,
26 vexation of the good, forgetfulness of benefits, contamination of souls, sexual perversion, disorder in marriage, adultery and debauchery.
27 For the worship of nameless idols is the beginning, cause and end of all evil,
28 whether they amuse themselves to the point of delirium or utter false predictions, whether they live in injustice or perjure in complete tranquility;
29 And since they put their trust in lifeless idols, they expect no harm from their false oaths.

30 But they will receive what they deserve for a double reason: because, by giving themselves over to idols, they have formed a false idea of God, and because they have sworn unjustly and falsely, despising holiness.
31 For it is not the power of those by whom one swears, but the just punishment reserved for sinners, which always falls on the transgression of the unrighteous.
1 But you, our God, are kind and faithful, you are patient and you administer everything with mercy.
2 Even when we sin, we belong to you, since we recognize your sovereignty; but we will not sin, knowing that you have counted us as your own.
3 For knowing you is perfect justice and recognizing your sovereignty is the root of immortality.
4 We have not been led astray by the inventions of a perverse human art nor by the sterile efforts of painters of chimeras: those figures daubed with variegated colors,
5 the contemplation of which excites the passion of fools and makes them desire the inanimate figure of a lifeless image.
6 Lovers of evil and worthy of such hopes are those who make them, desire them and worship them!

7 Thus a potter laboriously kneads the soft earth and models each of the objects we use. With the same clay he models objects intended for a noble use and others that will have a
contrary destiny; but it is the potter who decides what the function of
each of them.

8 Then, with a misused effort, he uses the same clay to model a false god, and the one who does this is a man who was born from the earth shortly before and will soon return to the earth.
from where he was taken, when asked to return his soul.

9 However, instead of worrying that he will soon die and that his life will be short, he competes with the goldsmiths and silversmiths, imitates the bronze smiths, and takes pride in making
what is false.
10 Their heart is nothing but ashes, their hope is baser than the earth, and their life is more contemptible than clay.
11 Because he does not know the one who modeled him, who gave him a soul capable of acting and transmitted to him a vital breath.
12 He thinks that our life is a game and existence, a fair to obtain profits: "It is necessary, he says, to win by all means, even if they are bad."
13 Because he knows well that he sins more than anyone else when he makes fragile objects and statues from earthly matter.
14 But the most foolish of all, and more unhappy than the soul of a child, are the enemies who oppressed your people,

15 since they had as gods all the idols of the nations, who cannot use their eyes to see, nor their noses to breathe, nor their ears to hear, nor their fingers.
hands to touch, and whose feet are no good for walking.
16 For it is a man who made those idols, one who received breath on loan, who fashioned them, but no man can fashion a god like himself:
17 Being mortal, with his impious hands, he can only produce a dead work. He is worth more than the objects he adores, since he has life, but those will never have it.
18 They worship even the most disgusting animals, which surpass all others in stupidity,
19 to those who do not even have the beauty that makes other animals attractive, and are excluded from the praise and blessing of God.
1 Therefore, with all justice they were punished with similar beings and tormented with an infinity of vermin.
2 Instead of that punishment, you were kind to your people, and to satisfy their voracious appetite, you prepared for them an exquisite delicacy: quails!

3 Thus the Egyptians, despite their desire to eat, lost their natural appetite, due to the disgusting appearance of the animals sent against them; your people, however, subjected to deprivation for a short time
time, partook of an exquisite delicacy.
4 Because it was necessary that inevitable hardship should come upon those oppressors and that they should only be made to see how their enemies were tormented.
5 Even when the terrible fury of ferocious animals was unleashed on your people, and they perished from the bite of fleeing serpents, your anger did not last to the end.
6 By way of warning, they were troubled for a short time, already having a pledge of salvation so that they would remember the commandment of your Law;
7 in fact, he who turned to her was saved, not by what he saw, but by you, the Savior of all.
8 Thus you showed our enemies that it is you who delivers from all evil:
9 They died from the bite of locusts and flies, and no remedy could be found for their lives, because they deserved to be punished by those animals.
10 But not even the teeth of poisonous snakes could defeat your children, because your mercy came to meet them and healed them.
11 So that they would remember your words, they were stinged and healed quickly, lest they fall into deep forgetfulness and thus be excluded from your beneficent action.
12 And it was not herbs or ointments that healed them, but your word, Lord, which heals everything.
13 Because you have power over life and death, you bring down to the gates of the Abyss and bring up from there.
14 Man, in his malice, can kill, but he does not bring back the spirit once it has left, nor does he free the soul received by the Abyss.
15 It is impossible to escape from your hand.
16 The wicked who refused to know you were struck by the strength of your arm: unusual rains, hailstorms, relentless downpours beset them, and fire consumed them.
17 But the strangest thing was that in water, which extinguishes everything, the fire burned brighter, because the universe fights in defense of the righteous.
18 Sometimes, the flames were subdued so as not to burn the animals sent against the wicked, and so that, upon seeing them, they would feel persecuted by a judgment from God.
19 Other times, even within the water, the flames burned with a force greater than that of fire, to destroy the crops of an unjust land.

20 Instead, you nourished your people with the food of angels, and without their tiring, you sent them from heaven ready-made bread, capable of providing all the delights and
adapted to all tastes.
21 And the sustenance that you gave them manifested your sweetness towards your children, because, adapting to the taste of the one who ate it, it was transformed according to the desire of each one.

22 The snow and ice resisted the fire without melting, so that they would know that only the fruits of the enemies were destroyed by the fire that burned in the midst of the
hail and glittered in the rain;
23 while, on the contrary, that same fire forgot even its own power, to respect the food of the righteous.
24 Because creation, which is at the service of you, its Creator, is tense to punish the unjust and is relaxed to benefit those who trust in you.
25 Therefore also then, completely transformed, she was at the service of your generosity, which feeds everyone, according to the desire of those who begged you.

26 Thus the children whom you have loved, Lord, had to learn that it is not the various kinds of fruits that feed man, but that it is your word that sustains those who believe in
you.
27 Because what the fire could not destroy melted with the simple heat of a faint ray of sunlight,
28 so that it would become clear that we must anticipate the sun to give you thanks and meet you at dawn.
29 But the hope of the ungrateful will be diluted like the winter frost and will flow like useless water.
1 Great and unspeakable are your judgments, therefore, ignorant souls went astray.

2 For when the wicked thought they could oppress a holy nation, they lay chained in darkness, prisoners of a long night, shut up under their roofs, excluded from the
eternal providence.
3 They thought to remain hidden with their secret sins, under the dark veil of oblivion, but they were scattered, prey to terrible fear, and terrified by ghosts.
4 Because the stronghold that protected them did not preserve them from fear; Shocking noises echoed around them and lugubrious ghosts, with gloomy faces, appeared to them.
5 No fire was strong enough to give light, nor could the brilliant splendor of the stars illuminate that horrible night.

6 Only a mass of fire shone for them that ignited by itself, spreading terror, and once that vision disappeared, they were terrified and considered what they had seen worse than
what it was.
7 The artifices of magic were ineffective, and their supposed science was shamefully disproved,
8 because those who promised to free sick souls from fears and shocks were, themselves, sick with a ridiculous fear.
9 Although nothing terrifying made them afraid, they were horrified by the passage of the vermin and the hissing of the reptiles,
10 They were scared to death, and even refused to look at the air, from which no one can escape.
11 Because evil is cowardly and its own testimony condemns it: harassed by conscience, it always imagines the worst.
12 Fear, in fact, is nothing more than the abandonment of the help that reflection gives:
13 the less one has this internal security, the more serious it is considered to ignore the cause of the torment.
14 During that truly impotent night, emerging from the depths of the impotent Abyss, immersed in the same dream,
15 were both persecuted by monstrous specters and paralyzed by the fainting of their soul, because a sudden and unexpected terror had invaded them.
16 Thus, anyone who fell into that state was a prisoner, locked in that prison without irons.
17 Whether he was a farmer or a shepherd, or worked in lonely places, when he was surprised, he had to endure the inescapable need,
18 because they were all bound by the same chain of darkness. The whistle of the wind, the melodious song of the birds in the grove, the lilting noise of the waters in their impetuous flow,

19 the violent roar of rocks falling in avalanches, the invisible race of rearing animals, the roar of the wildest beasts, the echo that reverberates in the hollows of the
mountains, everything filled them with terror and paralyzed them.
20 For the whole world was illuminated by a brilliant light and was freely engaged in its work;
21 Only a heavy night spread over them, an image of the darkness that was reserved for them. But more than the darkness, they felt the weight of themselves.
1 For your saints, however, an intense light shone. The Egyptians, who heard their voices, without distinguishing their figure, considered them happy because they did not have to suffer like them,
2 They thanked them because they did not take revenge for the damage they had received, and asked their forgiveness for their hostile attitude.
3 Instead of that darkness, you gave your people a pillar of fire, to serve as a guide on an unknown path and as a harmless sun in its glorious emigration.
4 But those who had held your children captive, through whom the incorruptible light of the Law was to be transmitted to the world, deserved to be deprived of light and prisoners of darkness.

5 As they had resolved to perish the little children of the saints and the children exposed to danger, only one was saved to punish them, you took a great number from them
of their children and caused them to perish all together in the rushing waters.
6 That night was made known in advance to our fathers, so that, knowing with certainty which oaths they had believed, they might feel comforted.
7 Your people hoped, at the same time, for the salvation of the righteous and the destruction of their enemies;
8 because with the punishment that you inflicted on our adversaries, you covered us with glory, calling us to you.

9 Therefore the holy sons of the righteous offered sacrifices in secret, and established this divine law by common agreement: that the saints would equally share the same goods and the
same dangers; and then they sang the songs of the Fathers.
10 The confused cry of his enemies echoed him, and the pitiful cries of those who mourned their children spread.
11 The same punishment hurt the slave and the owner, the man of the people suffered the same as the king.

12 Everyone alike had innumerable corpses, struck down by the same kind of death. The survivors could not afford to bury them, because in an instant there were
the best of his lineage has been destroyed.
13 Thus, those who, due to the spells, had become totally unbelieving, faced with the loss of their firstborn, confessed that these people were children of God.
14 When a peaceful silence enveloped all things, and the night had reached the middle of its rapid course,

15 your omnipotent Word was launched from heaven, from the royal throne, like an implacable warrior, in the middle of the country condemned to extermination. Wielding your decree like a sharp sword
irrevocable,
16 it stopped and spread death everywhere: while it touched the sky, it advanced on the earth.
17 Then, suddenly, visions of horrible nightmares startled them, and unexpected terrors invaded them.
18 Lying half dead everywhere, they made known the cause of their death,
19 because the dreams that had agitated them had warned them in advance, so that they would not perish without knowing why they suffered these evils.
20 The righteous also experienced death, and a multitude was slaughtered in the desert. But the divine wrath did not last long,

21 because very soon a blameless man came to his defense, with the weapons of his own ministry: prayer and atoning incense. He faced divine wrath and put an end to the calamity,
thus proving that he was your servant.

22 He overcame divine animosity, not by force of body nor by power of arms, but by word he brought the one who inflicted the punishment to reason, reminding him of the
alliances and the oaths made to the Fathers.
23 When the corpses lay piled up one on top of the other, he stepped in, restrained the divine wrath, and blocked the way to those who were still alive.

24 For on his priestly vestments was the whole world, on the four rows of precious stones were engraved the glorious names of the Fathers, and on the diadem of his head
Your Majesty was there.
25 At this, the Exterminator retreated in fear, since a single proof of your anger was enough.
1 But merciless wrath fell on the wicked to the end, because God had foreseen what they would do:
2 After letting the people go, and anointing them to leave hastily, they, changing their minds, would go out in pursuit.

3 In fact, while they were still celebrating their funeral rites and mourning at the graves of their dead, they conceived another crazy plan: to those whom they themselves had begged to leave
They began to pursue them as fugitives.
4 The force of things rightly dragged them to that extreme and made them forget what had happened, so that they could finish suffering the punishment that was still missing from their torments:
5 Thus, while your people embarked on a wonderful journey, they would meet an unusual death.
6 Because the entire creation, obeying your orders, acquired new forms in its own nature, so that your children would be preserved unharmed.
7 The cloud was seen covering the camp with its shadow and the dry land emerging from what was before water; A clear path and a green plain appeared in the Red Sea, between the impetuous waves:
8 An entire town passed through there, protected by your hand, contemplating admirable wonders.
9 They were like horses in a pasture and frolicked like lambs, praising you, Lord, their deliverer.

10 They still remembered what had happened in their exile: how the mosquitoes, instead of reproducing naturally, were produced by the earth, and how the frogs, instead of being born from others
aquatic animals, were vomited by the River in large quantities.
11 Later, they also saw a new way of being born to birds: when, excited by gluttony, they demanded delicate delicacies,
12 to comfort them, quails came up from the sea.

13 But the punishments fell on the sinners, not before being foreshadowed by the fury of the lightning: in all justice, they suffered because of their wickedness, since they had taken it to the extreme.
his hatred against the foreigner.
14 For others did not welcome the strangers who came, but they reduced beneficent guests to slavery.
15 Furthermore, those – and this will be taken into account – showed hostility towards the foreigner from the beginning;
16 But these, on the other hand, after welcoming your people with celebrations, and making them participate in their same rights, mistreated them with terrible labors.
17 For this reason they were punished with blindness, like those others at the gates of the righteous when, surrounded by deep darkness, each one sought access to his gate.

18 Thus, the elements exchanged their properties among themselves, as in a string instrument the sounds change their rhythm, always remaining the same tonality. This is what is inferred
clearly when examining what happened:
19 terrestrial beings became aquatic, those that swim moved on land;
20 the fire surpassed its own strength in the water and the water forgot its power to quench;
21 The flames, on the contrary, did not consume the flesh of the corruptible beings that passed through them, nor did they melt that divine food, similar to frost and so easy to dissolve.
22 By all means, Lord, you have magnified and glorified your people, and you have not failed to assist them in all times and places.
1 All wisdom comes from the Lord, and is with him forever.
2 Who can number the sand of the seas, the drops of rain and the days of eternity?
3 Who can measure the height of the sky, the extent of the earth, the deep, and wisdom?
4 Wisdom and foresighted intelligence was created before all things, from eternity.
5 The fountain of wisdom is the word of God on high, and its channels are the eternal commandments.
6 To whom was the root of wisdom revealed and who knew its secret plans?
7 To whom was the science of wisdom manifested and who understood the diversity of its ways?
8 Only one is wise, extremely fearsome: the Lord, who sits on his throne.
9 He himself created it, saw it and measured it, and poured it out on all his works:
10 He gave it to all men, according to his generosity, and poured it abundantly on those who love him.
11 The fear of the Lord is glory and a reason for pride, it is joy and a crown of gladness.
12 The fear of the Lord delights the heart, gives joy, gladness and long life.
13 Everything will end well for him who fears the Lord, he will be blessed on the day of his death.
14 The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord: she is created together with the faithful in the maternal womb.
15 He dwells among men forever and will remain faithfully with his descendants.
16 The fullness of wisdom is the fear of the Lord and it intoxicates you with its fruits:
17 He fills their house with precious goods and fills their barns with their products.
18 The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord: it causes well-being and good health to flourish.
19 The Lord saw it and measured it, rained down knowledge and knowledge, and exalted the glory of those who possess it.
20 The root of wisdom is the fear of the Lord and its branches are long life.
21 The fear of the Lord drives away sins: he who perseveres in it turns away divine wrath.
22 An improper outburst cannot be justified, because the impetus of passion leads to one's own ruin.
23 The patient man endures until the opportune moment, but at the end he will be filled with joy:
24 He reserves his words until the opportune time, and the wise of many will proclaim his understanding.
25 In the treasures of wisdom are the enigmas of science, but the sinner hates religiosity.
26 If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord will give it to you abundantly.
27 For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction: faithfulness and meekness please him.
28 Do not be reluctant to fear the Lord or approach him with a double heart.
29 Do not be hypocritical before men and pay attention to your words.

30 Do not exalt yourself, lest you fall and bring dishonor upon yourself: the Lord will reveal your secrets and humiliate you in the midst of the assembly, because you did not draw near to the fear of the
Lord and because your heart is full of falsehood.
1 Son, if you decide to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for the test.
2 Straighten your heart, be firm, and do not worry in the time of misfortune.
3 Join yourself to the Lord and do not separate, so that at the end of your days you may be exalted.
4 Accept willingly everything that happens to you, and be patient in the vicissitudes of your humiliation.
5 For gold is purified in fire, and those who please God in the crucible of humiliation.
6 Trust in him, and he will come to your aid, make your paths straight and wait for him.
7 Let those who fear the Lord wait for his mercy, and do not go astray, lest they fall.
8 Let those who fear the Lord trust in him, and they will not lack their reward.
9 Let those who fear the Lord wait for his benefits, for lasting joy and mercy.
10 Look at past generations and see: Who trusted in the Lord and was confused? Who persevered in his fear and was abandoned? Who invoked it and was it not taken into account?
11 For the Lord is merciful and compassionate, forgives sins and saves in time of affliction.
12 Woe to the cowardly hearts and the hands that fail, and the sinner who goes two ways!
13 Woe to the heart that fails, because it has no confidence! Because of that it will not be protected.
14 Woe to you, those who have lost their perseverance! What are you going to do when the Lord visits you?
15 Those who fear the Lord do not disobey his words, and those who love him faithfully follow his ways.
16 Those who fear the Lord try to please him, and those who love him are satisfied with his Law.
17 Those who fear the Lord have a clear heart and humble themselves before him:
18 "Let us abandon ourselves to the hands of the Lord and not to the hands of men, because as is his greatness, so is his mercy."
1 Children, listen to me, who am your father; Do what I tell you, and thus you will be saved.
2 Because the Lord wants the father to be respected by his children and confirmed the mother's right over them.
3 He who honors his father atones for his sins
4 and he who respects his mother is like one who accumulates treasure.
5 He who honors his father will find joy in his children and when he prays, he will be heard.
6 He who respects his father will have a long life and he who obeys the Lord gives peace of mind to his mother.
7 He who fears the Lord honors his father and serves as his masters to whom he was given life.
8 Honor your father in deed and word, so that his blessing may come upon you,
9 For a father's blessing strengthens his children's house, but a mother's curse uproots its foundations.
10 Do not seek your glory at the expense of your father's dishonor, for his dishonor is no glory to you:
11 A man's glory comes from his father's honor, and a mother despised is a disgrace to her children.
12 My son, help your father in his old age and do not cause him sadness while he lives.
13 Even if he loses his lucidity, be lenient with him; do not despise it, you who are in full vigor.
14 The help given to a father will not be forgotten and will serve as reparation for your sins.
15 When you are in affliction, the Lord will remember you, and your sins will dissolve like frost with heat.
16 He who abandons his father is like a blasphemer, and he who provokes his mother is cursed by the Lord.
17 My son, do your works with modesty and you will be loved by those who please God.
18 The greater you are, the more humble you must be, and thus you will obtain favor from the Lord,
19 [There are many men who are haughty and glorious, but the Lord reveals his secrets to the humble.]
20 because the power of the Lord is great and he is glorified by the humble.
21 Do not seek what is too difficult for you, nor try to search for what is beyond your strength:
22 reflect on what has been commanded you, because secret things do not concern you.
23 Do not worry about things that are above you: what has been revealed to you is already too much for intelligence.
24 For many went astray through their speculations and their perverse imagination distorted their thoughts.
25 If you do not have pupils, you will lack light; If you lack science, do not affirm anything.
26 A stubborn man ends badly, and he who loves danger will perish in it.
27 A stubborn heart will endure many evils, and the sinner piles one sin on top of another.
28 There is no remedy for the evil of the proud, because an evil plant has taken root in him.
29 The intelligent heart meditates on proverbs and the wise man desires to have an attentive ear.
30 Water extinguishes the flames of fire and alms atones for sins.
31 He who returns favors thinks about what will come next, and when he is about to fall, he will find support.
1 My son, do not deprive the poor of their sustenance nor cause the eyes of the needy to languish.
2 Do not make the hungry suffer nor irritate the destitute.
3 Do not exasperate even more the one who is irritated nor make the one who needs it wait for your gift.
4 Do not reject the supplication of the afflicted nor turn your face from the poor.
5 Do not turn your eyes away from the needy or allow anyone to curse you:
6 because if he curses you with bitterness in his soul, his Creator will hear his prayer.
7 Try to make yourself loved by the assembly and bow your head before a powerful one.
8 Turn your ear toward the poor and return his greeting sweetly.
9 Pluck the oppressed from the hands of the oppressor and do not be afraid to do justice.
10 Be a father to the orphans and like a husband to their mother: so you will be like a son of the Most High and he will love you more than your own mother.
11 Wisdom exalts her children and cares for those who seek her.
12 He who loves it, loves life, and those who ardently seek it will be filled with joy.
13 He who possesses it will inherit the glory, and wherever he goes, the Lord will bless him.
14 Those who serve her worship the Holy One and those who love her are loved by the Lord.
15 He who listens to it will judge the nations, and he who pays attention to it will live in safety.
16 He who trusts in it will inherit it, and his descendants will also possess it.

17 At first, she will lead him along a winding path, instilling fear and trembling in him and making him suffer with her discipline, until she has confidence in him and has tested him with her
demands.
18 Then he will return to him on the right path, make him happy and reveal his secrets to him.
19 If he goes astray, she will abandon him and leave him to his own fall.
20 Keep in mind the moment and beware of evil, and do not be ashamed of yourself.
21 For there is one shame that leads to sin, and there is another shame that is glory and grace.
22 Do not harm yourself by considering others, and do not let shame cause your fall.
23 Do not stop speaking when necessary, nor hide your wisdom.
24 For wisdom is recognized in words, and instruction in speech.
25 Do not say anything contrary to the truth and be ashamed of your lack of instruction.
26 Do not be ashamed to confess your sins nor try to oppose the flow of a river.
27 Do not abase yourself before a foolish man or be partial to the powerful.
28 Fight to the death for the truth, and the Lord God will fight for you.
29 Do not be bold with your tongue, nor lazy and careless in your actions.
30 Do not be like a lion within your house, and a coward among your servants.
31 Do not have your hand open to receive and closed when you have to give.
1 Do not trust in your wealth or say, "This is enough for me."
2 Do not let your desire and your strength lead you to act according to your whims.
3 Do not say, "Who can control me?" because the Lord gives each person what they deserve.
4 Do not say, "I sinned, and what happened to me?" for the Lord is patient.
5 Do not be so sure of forgiveness, while you commit one sin after another.
6 Do not say, “His compassion is great; He will forgive the multitude of my sins,” because in him is mercy, but also wrath, and his indignation falls on sinners.
7 Do not delay in returning to the Lord, letting day after day pass, because the wrath of the Lord will break out suddenly and you will perish at the time of punishment.
8 Do not trust in wealth acquired unjustly: it will be of no use to you in the day of misfortune.
9 Do not let yourself be carried away by every wind or go any way: this is how the sinner who speaks double acts.
10 Be firm in your convictions and let your word be one.
11 Always be willing to listen and be slow to respond.
12 If you know, answer your neighbor; otherwise, stay quiet.
13 Words bring glory or dishonor, and a man's tongue can cause his downfall.
14 May they not call you a gossip, and do not be insidious in your speech, for shame weighs on the thief and severe condemnation on the one who speaks twice.
15 Don't be lacking in big or small things, and don't be a friend, don't become an enemy,
1 For a bad name will inherit shame and disgrace: this is the fate of the sinner who speaks twice
2 Do not let yourself be carried away by the caprice of your passion, lest you be torn to pieces like a bull:
3 You would devour your branches, you would lose your fruits and you would become a dry trunk.
4 A violent passion loses the one who has it and makes his enemies laugh at him.
5 Sweet words multiply friends and kind language favors good relationships.
6 Let there be many who greet you, but let the one who advises you be one among a thousand.
7 If you win a friend, win him in the test, and do not give him confidence too soon.
8 Because there are occasional friends, who cease to be friends on the day of affliction.
9 There are friends who become enemies, and to shame you, they reveal the reason for the dispute.
10 There are friends who share your table and cease to be friends on the day of affliction.
11 As long as it goes well with you, they will be like you and will speak openly with your servants;
12 But if things go badly for you, they will turn against you and hide from your sight.
13 Separate yourself from your enemies and be careful with your friends.
14 A faithful friend is priceless, there is no way to estimate his value.
15 A faithful friend is priceless, there is no way to estimate his value.
16 A faithful friend is a balm of life, found by those who fear the Lord.
17 He who fears the Lord directs his friendship well, because as he is, so will he also be his friend.
18 My son, from your youth, seek instruction, and even in your old age, you will find wisdom.
19 Approach it like one who plows and one who sows, and wait patiently for its good fruits: while cultivating it, you will be a little tired, but very soon you will eat its products.
20 How harsh it seems to the ignorant! The fool does not remain faithful to her:
21 She presses him like a heavy stone and it doesn't take him long to get it off him.
22 For wisdom lives up to its name and does not appear to many.
23 Listen, my son, accept my doctrine and do not reject my advice.
24 Put your feet in his stocks and your neck in his collar.
25 Bow your shoulders and carry her, and do not be angered by her chains.
26 Draw near to her with all your soul and stay on her path with all your strength.
27 Follow her footsteps and seek her: wisdom will be made known to you, and once you have it, do not leave it,
28 because at last you will find rest in it and it will become your joy.
29 Their stocks will be a powerful refuge and their necklaces a mantle of glory.
30 His yoke will be an ornament of gold, and his chains will be a cloth of hyacinth.
31 You will put on it like a robe of glory and you will wear it like a crown of joy.
32 If you want, my son, you will be taught, and if you put effort, you will know how to develop.
33 If you like to listen, you will learn, and if you pay attention, you will become wise.
34 Frequent the meetings of the elders and if there is a wise man, adhere to him.
35 Try to listen to everything that refers to God and do not miss the profound maxims.
36 If you see an intelligent man, go immediately to him and let your feet walk over the threshold of his door.
37 Examine carefully the precepts of the Lord and meditate on his commandments without ceasing: he himself will establish your heart and give you the wisdom you desire.
1 Do not do evil, and evil will not take hold of you;
2 depart from injustice, and it will depart from you.
3 Do not sow, my son, in the furrows of injustice, lest you reap seven times as much.
4 Do not ask the Lord for an important position or the king for a seat of honor.
5 Do not want to appear righteous before the Lord or act wise before the king.
6 Do not aspire to the position of judge, lest you be unable to eradicate injustice or allow yourself to be intimidated by a powerful person, and thus endanger your righteousness.
7 Do not offend the city assembly or degrade yourself before the crowd.
8 Do not commit sin twice, for not a single one will go unpunished.
9 Do not say, “The Lord will appreciate the multitude of my gifts; When you present them to the Most High God, he will accept them."
10 Do not stop praying confidently nor forget to give alms.
11 Do not mock the man who is bitter, for there is Someone who humiliates and also exalts.
12 Do not lie against your brother, nor against a friend.
13 Never tell a lie, because that habit does not lead to anything good.
14 Do not talk too much in the assembly of elders or repeat words in your prayer.
15 Do not hate hard work or field work, created by the Most High.
16 Do not add yourself to the multitude of sinners: remember that the wrath of the Lord will not tarry.
17 Be deeply humble, for fire and worms are the punishment of the wicked.
18 Do not exchange a friend for money or a true brother for the gold of Ophir.
19 Do not turn away from a wise and good woman, for her charm is worth more than gold.
20 Do not mistreat the servant who works faithfully or the laborer who gives himself completely.
21 Love an intelligent servant with your heart and do not deprive him of his freedom.
22 If you have livestock, take good care of it, and if it gives you profit, keep it.
23 If you have children, educate them and demand obedience from their childhood.
24 If you have daughters, take care of them so that they are chaste and do not be too soft with them.
25 Marry your daughter, and you will have done a great work, but give her to an intelligent man.
26 If you love your wife, do not divorce her, but if you do not love her, do not trust her.
27 Glorify your father with all your heart and do not forget the sorrows of your mother;
28 remember that you owe them your life: how will you repay them for what they did for you?
29 Reverence the Lord with all your soul and venerate his priests.
30 Love your Creator with all your strength and do not abandon his ministers.

31 Fear the Lord and glorify the priest, give him his portion, as you have been commanded: the firstfruits, the sacrifice of reparation and the loin of the victims, the consecrated offerings and the firstfruit of
the holy things.
32 Reach out your hand also to the poor, and you will be fully blessed;
33 be generous to all the living and do not deny your mercy to the dead;
34 do not turn your back on those who cry and share the affliction of those who suffer;
35 do not stop visiting the sick: with such works you will make yourself loved.
36 In all your actions, remember your end and you will never sin.
1 Do not dispute with a powerful man, lest you fall into his hands.
2 Do not enter into a dispute with a rich man, lest he bring his whole weight against you: for gold was the ruin of many and turned away the hearts of kings.
3 Do not argue with a charlatan, do not add fuel to his fire.
4 Do not joke with a rude man, so that your ancestors will not be reviled.
5 Do not reproach the sinner who repents: remember that we are all guilty.
6 Do not despise a man in his old age because we too grow old.
7 Don't be happy about anyone's death: remember that we all have an end.
8 Do not despise the conversation of the wise: return to their maxims again and again, because from them you will receive the instruction and the art of serving the great.
9 Do not deviate from the conversation of the elders, because they themselves learned from their fathers: from them you will learn to be intelligent and to give an answer at the right time.
10 Do not stir the embers of the sinner, lest you be burned by their slats.
11 Do not give way in the presence of an insolent person, for he would be like a trap set before your mouth.
12 Do not lend to a man stronger than you, and if you lend, consider him lost.
13 Do not offer collateral beyond your means, and if you do, be prepared to pay.
14 Do not enter into a dispute with a judge: because of his dignity, they will rule in his favor.
15 Do not set out with an adventurer, lest he become a burden to you, for he will act according to his whim, and his folly will cause you to perish along with him.
16 Do not fight with an angry man, nor cross the desert with him, because blood is worthless in his eyes and when you are defenseless, he will strike you down.
17 Do not consult your affairs with a fool, for he is incapable of keeping secrets.
18 Do not do to a stranger what should be hidden, because you do not know what he may come out with.
19 Don't open your heart to anyone or let anyone do you a favor.
1 Do not be jealous of the woman you love, so as not to incite her to behave badly towards you.
2 Note that you blindly give yourself over to a woman, to the point that she dominates you.
3 Do not approach a prostitute, lest you fall into her trap.
4 Do not entertain yourself with a singer, lest you be caught by her tricks.
5 Do not look too much at a young woman, lest you incur the same sentence.
6 Do not give yourself to prostitutes, so as not to ruin your property.
7 Do not go looking through the streets of the city or wander around its lonely places.
8 Take your eyes off the beautiful woman and do not fix your eyes on the beauty of others: many have been led astray by the beauty of a woman, and because of her desire burns like fire.
9 Never sit next to a married woman or drink wine with her at banquets, lest your heart be inclined toward her and you fall into ruin through your passion.
10 Do not abandon an old friend, because a new one is not worth as much as him. A new friend is like new wine: let it get old, and you will drink it with pleasure.
11 Do not envy the glory of the sinner, for you do not know what his fate will be.
12 Do not delight in what delights the wicked: remember that they will go down into the Abyss without being justified.

13 Stay away from him who has the power to kill and you will not experience the fear of death. If you approach him, do not commit any fault, lest he take your life: keep in mind that you advance
between ties and that you walk along the battlements of the city.
14 As much as possible, turn to your neighbors and seek the advice of the wise.
15 Frequent contact with intelligent people and always talk about the Law of the Most High.
16 May righteous men be your guests and may your pride be in the fear of the Lord.
17 By the hand of the artist, the work is worthy of praise, and the leader of the people is shown to be wise by his words.
18 The charlatan is the terror of his city and the excessive speech becomes hateful.
1 A wise ruler educates his people and the authority of the intelligent man is exercised with order.
2 As the ruler of a people, so are his ministers, and as the ruler of the city, so are its inhabitants.
3 An ignorant king is the ruin of his people and a city prospers because of the intelligence of princes.
4 In the hands of the Lord is the dominion of the earth and, at the right moment, he sends the appropriate man.
5 The success of a man is in the hands of the Lord, and he will bring his glory to the person of the lawgiver.
6 Do not hold a grudge against your neighbor for any injury or do anything in a fit of violence.
7 Pride is hateful to the Lord and to men, and injustice is offensive to both.
8 Royalty passes from one nation to another, because of injustice, arrogance and greed.
9 What is he who is dust and ashes proud of, if even in life his bowels are full of rot?
10 A long illness baffles the doctor, and he who is king today will die tomorrow.
11 When a man dies, he receives larvae, wild animals, and worms as his inheritance.
12 Pride begins when man turns away from the Lord and his heart turns away from the one who created him.
13 For the beginning of pride is sin, and he who persists in it sends down abomination; therefore the Lord sent unforeseen calamities and laid waste to the proud until he destroyed them.
14 The Lord brought down the thrones of the powerful and enthroned the meek in their place.
15 The Lord uprooted the nations and planted the humble in their place.
16 The Lord laid waste the territories of the nations and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
17 Some he destroyed and made them disappear, and he blotted out even the memory of them from the earth.
18 Pride was not created for man, nor the outburst of anger for those born of women.

19 What race is worthy of honor? The human race. What race is worthy of honor? Those who fear the Lord. What race is despicable? The human race. What race is despicable? Those who do not comply
the Law.
20 Among brothers, the one who is their leader is honored, but the Lord honors those who fear him.
21 [The beginning of acceptance is the fear of the Lord, and the beginning of rejection is hardening and pride.]
22 For the rich, the illustrious or the poor the only glory is the fear of the Lord.
23 It is not right to despise a poor intelligent man nor is it right to glorify a sinful man.
24 The great, the magistrate, and the powerful are worthy of honor, but he who fears the Lord is superior to them all.
25 Free men will serve a wise slave, and the man who understands will not take it amiss.
26 Do not pretend to be wise when you do your task nor glorify yourself in the time of hardship.
27 Better is the one who works and lives in abundance than the one who goes around boasting and has nothing to eat.
28 My son, glorify yourself with due modesty and estimate yourself according to your just worth.
29 Who will justify him who harms himself and who will glorify him who despises himself?
30 The poor are honored for their knowledge and the rich for their riches.
31 He who is glorified in poverty, how much more will he be glorified in riches! He who is despised in wealth, how much more will he be despised in poverty!
1 The wisdom of the humble makes him lift up his head, and makes him sit among the powerful.
2 Do not praise a man for his good looks nor despise anyone for his appearance.
3 The bee is small among the animals that fly, but what it produces is sweeter than everything.
4 Do not boast about the clothing that covers you nor be proud in the days of glory, for the works of the Lord are admirable and are hidden from the eyes of men.
5 Many tyrants sat on the ground and the one who least thought about it put on his diadem.
6 Many potentates sank into dishonor and illustrious men fell into the hands of others.
7 Do not censure before you find out: reflect first, and then reproach.
8 Don't respond before listening and don't interrupt when someone else is speaking.
9 Do not argue about what does not belong to you nor meddle in the disputes of sinners.
10 My son, do not try to do too many things: if you do, you will not be free from guilt. If you try too hard, you won't reach it and even if you want to run away, you won't escape.
11 There are those who make an effort, get tired and hurry, and look even more destitute.
12 Another is weak, in need of help, lacking in strength and full of hardships; but the Lord looks upon him kindly and lifts him up from his humiliation;
13 The Lord lifts up his head and many are amazed because of him.
14 Good and evil, life and death, poverty and wealth come from the Lord.
15 [Wisdom, science, and knowledge of the Law come from the Lord; love and the way of good works proceed from him.]
16 [Foolishness and darkness have been created for sinners; those who delight in evil grow old in it.]
17 The gift of the Lord remains with the good and his benevolence ensures their success forever.
18 A man becomes rich through hard work and savings, and what reward does he get?
19 When he says, "I can rest now, now I will enjoy my goods," he does not know how long it will be until he dies and leaves his goods to others.
20 Be faithful to your obligation, dedicate yourself to it, and grow old in your job.
21 Do not admire the works of the sinner: trust in the Lord and persevere in your work, because it is an easy thing in the eyes of the Lord to enrich the needy in one fell swoop.
22 The blessing of the Lord is the reward of the good, and in an instant he causes his blessing to flourish.
23 Don't say, "What do I need?" What goods can I still expect?
24 Do not say, “I have enough; What evils can still befall me?
25 On good days the bad are forgotten, and on bad days the good are forgotten.
26 For it is easy for the Lord, on the day of death, to reward each man according to his conduct.
27 An hour of misfortune makes happiness forgotten, and a man's works are revealed at the end of his life.
28 Do not proclaim anyone happy before his end comes, because it is only at the end that a man is known well.
29 Do not let anyone into your house, because the false lays many ambushes.
30 The heart of the proud is like a bait, just like a spy, waiting for you to take a wrong step.
31 It lies in wait to distort good into evil and is capable of staining the cleanest things.
32 A spark lights many coals and the sinner lays bloody ambushes.
33 Beware of the evildoer, for he breeds evil, lest he leave you stained forever.
34 Host a stranger, and he will bring trouble to you, and make you a stranger to your own relatives.
1 If you do good, look to whom you do it, and they will thank you for your benefits.
2 Do good to a good man, and you will have your reward, if not from him, then certainly from the Most High.
3 He who persists in evil and he who does not appreciate alms does not receive goods.
4 Give to the good man, but do not help the sinner.

5 Be good to the humble, but do not give to the wicked: refuse him his bread, do not give it to him, lest he come to dominate you, and then you will receive double evil for all the good you have done to him.
6 For the Most High also hates sinners and will repay the wicked.
7 Give to a good man, but do not help a sinner.
8 It is not in good times that a friend is known, nor in bad times is the enemy hidden.
9 In good times, enemies become sad, and in bad times, even a friend walks away.
10 Never trust your enemy, because evil corrodes him like rust on metal:
11 Even if he pretends to be humble and walks stooped, be very careful and be alert against him; Treat it like someone polishing a mirror, to see if the rust hasn't finished corroding it.

12 Do not place him next to you, lest he overthrow you to take your place; do not make him sit at your right, lest he claim your same seat, and at last you will understand my words and feel sorry for him.
remember them.
13 Who pities the charmer bitten by the snake or the tamer of wild animals?
14 The same thing happens to anyone who approaches a sinner and becomes involved in his sins.
15 He will stay with you for an hour, but if you hesitate, he will not give you a hand.
16 The enemy has honey on his lips, but inside he thinks how to throw you into the pit. The enemy has tears in his eyes, but when the time comes, there will be no blood to satisfy him.
17 If something bad happens to you, you will find it there before yourself; pretending to help you, he will trip you:
18 he will shake his head and applaud, he will mumble and put on another face.
1 He who touches bitumen becomes stained, and he who deals with the proud becomes equal to him.
2 Do not lift too heavy a load, nor deal with one stronger and richer than you: can the clay cup join the pot? This one will hit him and that one will break.
3 The rich man wrongs, and on top of that he becomes emboldened; The poor man is wronged, and on top of that he apologizes.
4 As long as you are useful to him, he will exploit you, but if you have nothing, he will abandon you.
5 If you possess anything, it will live with you and will despoil you without pity.
6 When he needs you, he will try to deceive you, he will smile at you and give you hope; He will speak beautiful words to you and ask you: "What do you need?"
7 He will engage you with his celebrations until he strips you two and three times, and in the end he will mock you; Then, when he sees you, he will walk past you and shake his head at you.
8 Pay attention, so as not to be deceived or humiliated by your foolishness.
9 When a powerful person invites you, stay at a distance, and he will invite you with more insistence.
10 Do not rush, lest you be rejected, nor stay too far, lest you be forgotten.
11 Don't try to talk to him as an equal or trust him if he talks too much: he tests you with his talkativeness and examines you between laughs.
12 He who does not moderate his speech is ruthless, and will not spare you either blows or chains.
13 Look carefully and pay close attention, because you are walking on the brink of your ruin.
14 [When you hear this in your dream, wake up; love the Lord all your life and call on him for your salvation.]
15 Every animal loves its like, and every man, his like;
16 Every living being unites itself with its own kind, and man with one like him.
17 What do the wolf and the lamb have in common? So it is with the sinner and the good man.
18 What peace can there be between the hyena and the dog? And what peace between the rich and the poor?
19 Wild donkeys in the desert are the prey of lions: so the poor are food for the rich.
20 Humiliation is abominable to the proud: so the rich abhors the poor.
21 When a rich man takes a bad step, his friends support him; When a poor man falls, his friends reject him.

22 If a rich man slips, many run to his aid; He says unrepeatable things, and they agree with him. The humble slips, and they criticize him; He expresses himself sensibly, and no one pays attention to him.
23 If the rich man speaks, everyone is silent and puts his words to the skies; The poor man speaks, and they ask: "Who is this?", and if he stumbles, they give him a push.
24 Riches are good, if they are free from sin, and poverty is evil in the judgment of the wicked.
25 The heart of a man causes him to change his countenance, both for good and for evil:
26 a happy face reflects the joy of the heart, and the invention of proverbs requires painful reflections.
1 Happy is the man who has not failed with his tongue nor is tormented by remorse!
2 Happy is he who does not have to reproach himself and does not see his hope fade away!
3 Of what use is wealth to the miser and for what purpose does the miser have his fortune?
4 He who accumulates, depriving himself of everything, accumulates for others, and others will live a good life with his possessions.
5 He who is bad to himself, to whom will he be good? Not even he himself enjoys his fortune.
6 There is no one worse than the miser toward himself, and that is the just payment for his wickedness.
7 If he does any good, he does it carelessly, and ends up revealing his malice.
8 He who looks with envy is a wicked man, who turns away and despises others.
9 The eye of the ambitious is not satisfied with his part, and vileness dries up the soul.
10 The miserable man stings his bread and has his table always empty.
11 To the extent of your resources, live well, my son, and present worthy offerings to the Lord.
12 Remember that death will not take long and that the covenant of the Abyss has not been revealed to you.
13 Before you die, do good to your friend and give generously, to the extent of your strength.
14 Do not deprive yourself of a pleasant day or waste your share of legitimate joy.
15 Will you not leave the fruit of your labors and your toil to another, so that they may share it as an inheritance?
16 Give and receive, forget your worries, because there is no need to look for delights in the Abyss.
17 Every living thing ages like a garment, because the old saying stands: "You must die."
18 In the foliage of a dense tree, some leaves fall and others sprout: such are the generations of flesh and blood, one dies and another is born.
19 Every corruptible work disappears, and the one who made it will go with it.
20 Happy is the man who deals with wisdom and the one who reasons intelligently,
21 he who reflects on the ways of wisdom and penetrates its secrets!
22 He follows her like a tracker and lies in wait for her steps;
23 spy through their windows and listen carefully at their doors;
24 He seeks shelter near his house and drives a stake into its walls;
25 He sets up his tent near her and takes shelter in the best of dwellings;
26 He puts his children under its shelter and lives in the shade of its branches:
27 she protects him from the heat and he dwells in her glory.
1 He who fears the Lord does all this, and he who holds fast to the Law will gain wisdom.
2 She will meet him like a mother and receive him like a young wife,
3 He will feed him with the bread of understanding and make him drink the water of wisdom.
4 He will lean on her, and will not waver, he will cleave to her, and will not be confounded.
5 She will exalt him above his companions and open his mouth in the midst of the assembly.
6 He will find joy and the crown of gladness and will inherit an everlasting name.
7 Those who lack understanding will never possess it, nor will sinful men ever see it.
8 She keeps away from pride, and liars do not think about her.
9 There is no room for praise on the lips of a sinner, because the Lord does not send it to him:
10 Without wisdom there is no praise, and it is the Lord who inspires it.
11 Do not say: "It was the Lord who made me give up," because he never does what he hates.
12 Do not say, "He led me astray," for he does not need a sinful man.
13 The Lord hates every abomination, and nothing abominable is loved by those who fear it.
14 He made man in the beginning and left him to his own will.
15 If you want, you can keep the commandments and faithfully do what pleases you.
16 He has set fire and water before you: toward whatever you wish, you will stretch out your hand.
17 Before men are life and death: to each one will be given what he prefers.
18 For great is the wisdom of the Lord, he is strong and powerful, and sees all things.
19 His eyes are fixed on those who fear him, and he knows all the works of man.
20 He commanded no one to be wicked nor gave anyone permission to sin.
1 Do not desire a large number of useless children, nor rejoice in wicked children.
2 No matter how many they are, do not rejoice over them if they lack the fear of the Lord.
3 Do not expect them to live long or feel secure because they are numerous: one is better than a thousand and it is better to die without children than to have ungodly ones.
4 With just one intelligent person a city is populated, but the race of lawless men is destroyed.
5 My eyes have seen many such things, and my ears have heard even worse things.
6 Fire burns in the gathering of sinners, and anger burns against the rebellious nation.
7 The Lord did not spare the ancient giants who rebelled with all their might.
8 He did not spare the city where Lot lived, those whom he abhorred because of their pride.
9 He did not take pity on the nation condemned to extermination. of those who were expelled because of their sins.
10 This is how he also treated the six hundred thousand soldiers who mutinied because of the hardness of their hearts.
11 Even if there were only one obstinate man, it would be a miracle if he remained unpunished, because in him is mercy, but also wrath, he is as unforgiving as he is lavish in wrath.
12 As great as his mercy is his reprobation: he judges each one according to his works.
13 The sinner will not escape with his prey nor will the perseverance of the good be disappointed.
14 He considers every alms and each one will receive according to his works.
15 [The Lord hardened Pharaoh so that he would not recognize him in order to make his works known under heaven.]
16 [His mercy is manifested to all creation; He distributed his light and his darkness to the children of Adam.]
17 Do not say, "I will hide myself from the Lord, and up above, who will remember me?" Among so many people I will go unnoticed: who am I in the immense creation?
18 Look: the sky and the highest heaven, the Abyss and the earth are moved when he visits them:
19 The mountains along with the foundations of the earth tremble with fear under his gaze.
20 But no one reflects on these things, and who pays attention to his plans?
21 Like a storm that breaks out without man realizing it, so most of his works remain hidden.
22 «Who announces the works of righteousness? Who waits for them? Because the alliance is far away»:
23 This is how he who has no understanding reasons; The foolish, the lost, only think foolish things.
24 Listen, my son, and be instructed, pay close attention to my words.
25 I will reveal my teaching with restraint and expound knowledge accurately.
26 By the decision of the Lord his works existed from the beginning: from the time they were made, he set their limits.
27 He ordained his works forever, and his government for all generations. They do not suffer hunger or fatigue and never interrupt their activity.
28 They do not clash against each other and they never disobey their word.
29 Then the Lord fixed his eyes on the earth and filled it with his good things.
30 He covered it with all kinds of living things and everyone will return to it.
1 The Lord created man from the earth and makes him return to it again.
2 He appointed him a number of days and a certain time, and put the things of the earth under his control.
3 He clothed it with strength like his own and made it after his own image.
4 He made all living things fear him, so that he might dominate the wild beasts and the birds.
5 [They received the use of the five operations of the Lord; As a sixth gift, he granted them intelligence; and seventh, the language that interprets the works of God.]
6 He gave him a tongue, eyes and ears, the power to discern and a heart to think.
7 He filled men with knowledge and understanding, and showed them good and evil.
8 He gave them his own light, to show them the greatness of his works,
9 and allowed them to boast of their wonders forever:
10 Thus they will praise his holy Name, proclaiming the greatness of his works.
11 He also granted them knowledge and gave them as an inheritance a Law of life;
12 He established an eternal alliance with them and made his decrees known to them.
13 They saw with their eyes the greatness of his glory and heard with their ears the glory of his voice.
14 He said to them, “Beware of all unrighteousness,” and he gave each one precepts regarding his neighbor.
15 The ways of men are always before him and cannot be hidden from his eyes.
16 [Their ways lead to evil from their youth, and they are not able to transform their hearts of stone into hearts of flesh.]
17 He assigned a leader to each nation, but Israel is the Lord's portion.
18 He is his firstborn, whom he nurtured with his instruction, and when he dispenses the light of love, he does not abandon him.
19 All his works are clear to him as the sun, and his eyes are fixed on his ways.
20 Their injustices are not hidden from the Lord and all their sins are before him.
21 [But the Lord is kind and knows his creature; He does not leave them nor abandon them, but forgives them.]
22 A man's alms is to him as a seal, and he counts a favor as the pupil of his eye.
23 Then he will rise up to repay them and will place the reward they deserve on their heads.
24 He allows those who repent to return and comforts those who have lost their perseverance.
25 Return to the Lord and stop sinning, plead before his face and stop offending him.
26 Return to the Most High, turn away from injustice and deeply hate every abomination.
27 Who will praise the Most High in the Abyss, if the living do not pay homage to Him?
28 the dead, the one who no longer exists, stops praising him: the one who is alive and healthy must praise the Lord.
29 How great is the generosity of the Lord and his forgiveness for those who return to him!
30 A man cannot have it all, because the human being is not immortal.
31 Is there anything brighter than the sun? And yet, he too is eclipsed! How much more the flesh and blood, which only conceive evil!
32 The Lord reviews the host of heaven, how much more so men, who are earth and ashes!
1 He who lives forever created all things equally;
2 Only the Lord will be found righteous and there is no other besides him.
3 He rules the world with the palm of his hand and everything obeys his will, since he, by his power, is the King of all things and separates the sacred from the profane.
4 He gave no one the power to proclaim his works: who will track down his greatness?
5 Who can measure the magnitude of his strength and who can claim to narrate his mercies?
6 There is nothing to take away, nothing to add, and it is impossible to trace the wonders of the Lord.
7 When man comes to the end, he is only at the beginning; when he stops, he doesn't come out of his stupor.
8 What is man? What is it for? What is its good and what is its evil?
9 A man's life lasts a hundred years at most:
10 Like a drop of the sea and like a grain of sand, your few years are compared to eternity.
11 Therefore the Lord is patient with them and showers his mercy on them.
12 He sees and knows how miserable his end is, and therefore multiplies his forgiveness.
13 A man has mercy only on his neighbor, but the Lord is merciful to all living. He rebukes, corrects and teaches, and makes them return like the shepherd to his flock.
14 He has mercy on those who accept instruction and is always ready to carry out his decrees.
15 My son, do not blame the benefits you do or accompany your gifts with offensive words.
16 Does not the dew calm the burning heat? Thus, a good word is more than a gift.
17 Isn't a word worth more than a gift? But the charitable man knows how to unite the two things.
18 The fool rebukes without regard, and the gift of the miser makes tears flow.
19 Before you speak, educate yourself, and take care of yourself before you fall ill.
20 Before you judge, examine yourself, and you will find forgiveness when the Lord visits you.
21 Humble yourself before you fall ill and repent as soon as you have sinned.
22 Let nothing prevent you from fulfilling your vows at the due time, and do not wait until death to be in order.
23 Before you make a vow, prepare to fulfill it, and do not be like a man who tempts the Lord.
24 Remember the wrath of the last days and the time of punishment, when the Lord will turn away his face.
25 In the time of plenty, remember the time of famine, and in the days of wealth, poverty and hardship.
26 From morning to evening, the time changes, and everything passes quickly before the Lord.
27 The wise man is always alert, and in the occasion of sin, he takes care not to fail.
28 Every prudent man knows wisdom and pays homage to him who finds it.
29 Those who speak sensibly are themselves wise and pour out wise proverbs like rain.
30 Do not be guided by your passions, but restrain your desires.
31 If you give in to the impulses of passion, it will make you the derision of your enemies.
32 May your joy not consist of indulging in every pleasure nor do you go into debt to pay what they cost.
33 Don't make yourself poor by going to parties with borrowed money, when you have nothing in your pocket.
1 A hard-drinking worker will never get rich, and he who is careless in small things will fall little by little.
2 Wine and women lead the intelligent astray, and he who goes with prostitutes is even more reckless:
3 rot and worms will take possession of him, and the reckless man will be cut off.
4 He who trusts too soon is a frivolous spirit, and he who sins harms himself.
5 He who delights in evil will be condemned,
6 and he who hates talkativeness is freed from evil.
7 Never repeat what you have heard, and you will lose nothing.
8 Do not tell it to anyone, whether friend or enemy, and unless you commit sin, do not reveal it:
9 They would listen to you, but they would be on their guard against you and, when the time came, they would hate you.
10 Have you heard anything? Let him die with you; Don't be afraid, it won't make you burst.
11 A fool suffers when he keeps a secret, like a woman in labor for her child.
12 Like an arrow stuck in the thigh is the secret in the breast of a fool.
13 Clarify things with your friend: maybe he didn't do anything, and if he did, so that he doesn't do it again.
14 Clarify things with your neighbor: perhaps he didn't say anything, and if he did, so that he doesn't repeat it.
15 Clear things up with your friend: people often slander, and you should not trust everything that is said.
16 A mistake can be made unintentionally, and who has not sinned with their tongue?
17 Clear things up with your neighbor before threatening him, and then give place to the Law of the Most High.
18 [Begin by fearing the Lord, and he will accept you; If you have wisdom, he will love you.]
19 [Knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is life-giving instruction; Those who do what pleases Him will gather the fruits of the tree of immortality.]
20 All wisdom is the fear of the Lord and all wisdom involves the practice of the Law.
21 [The servant who says to his master, "I will not do what pleases you," even if he does it afterwards, irritates the one who feeds him.]
22 It is not wisdom to know how to do evil and there is no prudence in the counsel of sinners.
23 There is cunning that is abominable, and he who lacks wisdom is foolish.
24 The unintelligent one who fears the Lord is preferable to the very intelligent one who breaks the Law.
25 There is a subtle but unjust cunning, and there are those who use tricks to assert their right.
26 There is a wicked man who is bowed down with sadness, but his insides are full of falsehood:
27 He covers his face and pretends not to hear, but if no one sees him, he takes advantage of you.
28 If he lacks the strength to sin, when he finds an opportunity, he will harm you.
29 A man is recognized by his look, and a wise man by his appearance.
30 The man's clothing, his way of laughing, and his entire bearing reveal what he is.
1 There are rebukes that are inappropriate, and there are silences that reveal the prudent man.
2 It is better to rebuke than to hold back anger,
3 and he who confesses his fault is freed from misfortune.
4 Like a gelding who longs to deflower a young woman, so is he who wants to do justice by force.
5 One remains silent and is considered wise, and another becomes hateful because of his talkativeness.
6 One remains silent because he has nothing to respond and another because he waits for the opportunity.
7 The wise man remains silent until the opportune moment, but the petulant and foolish man does not pay attention to time.
8 He who talks too much becomes abominable and he who tries to impose himself becomes hateful.
9 Sometimes adversity is taken advantage of, and sometimes luck ends in misfortune.
10 There are gifts that do not benefit you, and there are others that pay twice as much.
11 There are misfortunes that come from honors, and there are humble people who were able to raise their heads.
12 There are those who buy a lot at a low price, and then pay seven times as much.
13 The wise man makes himself loved by his words, but the compliments of the fool fall into emptiness.
14 The fool's gift will not benefit you, because he expects much more in return:
15 He gives little and blames much, opens his mouth like a preacher, lends today and demands tomorrow. How detestable is such a man!
16 The fool says, “I have not a single friend; no one appreciates my benefits;
17 Those who eat my bread have forgetful tongues. How many and how many times will they laugh at him!
18 It is better to slip on the floor than on your tongue; This is how the wicked suddenly fall.
19 A rude man is like an inopportune story, which is always in the mouths of the ill-mannered.
20 No one approves of a proverb said by a fool, because he never says it at the right time.
21 For some, poverty preserves them from sin, and when they rest, they feel no remorse.
22 There are those who are lost through timidity, and are lost through fear of a fool.
23 There are those who, out of timidity, make promises to a friend and uselessly make an enemy.
24 A lie is an infamous stain for man: it is always in the mouths of the ignorant.
25 A thief is preferable to an inveterate liar, although both will inherit destruction.
26 He who makes a habit of lying falls into dishonor and his ignominy constantly accompanies him.
27 A wise man makes way with his words, and a prudent man pleases the powerful.
28 He who cultivates the land raises his heap high, and he who pleases the great is forgiven for injustice.
29 Gifts and gifts blind the wise and are like a muzzle that silences criticism.
30 Hidden wisdom and hidden treasure: what good are one or the other?
31 The man who hides his foolishness is preferable to the one who hides his wisdom.
1 Have you sinned, my son? Don't do it again, and apologize for your past mistakes.
2 Flee from sin as from a snake, because if you come near, it will bite you; His teeth are lion's teeth, which take the lives of men.
3 Every transgression is like a two-edged sword: there is no remedy for its wound.
4 Violence and pride cause wealth to be lost: thus the house of the proud will be destroyed.
5 The prayer of the poor goes from his mouth to the ears of the Lord, and the divine sentence is not long in coming.
6 He who hates rebuke follows in the footsteps of the sinner, but he who fears the Lord repents from the heart.
7 The charlatan is recognized from afar, the thoughtful man discovers his mistakes.
8 He who builds his house with other people's money is like he who piles up stones for the winter.
9 A band of evildoers is like a heap of tow, and its end is the flame of fire.
10 The path of sinners is cleared of stones, but it ends in the depths of the Abyss.
11 He who observes the Law controls his inclinations, and the fear of the Lord is the culmination of wisdom.
12 He who is not skilled cannot learn, but there is a skill that produces bitterness.
13 The knowledge of the wise grows like a flood and his advice is like a source of life.
14 The mind of a fool is like a broken glass: it retains no knowledge.
15 If a learned man hears a wise word, he approves it and adds something of his own to it; If a madman hears it, he dislikes it and throws it behind his back.
16 The conversation of a fool is like a burden to the traveler, but the lips of the intelligent cause delight.
17 The opinion of the prudent is required in the assembly, and everyone reflects on his words.
18 Wisdom is like a broken house to a fool, and the knowledge of a fool is a series of inconsistencies.
19 Instruction is to a fool like a trap on his feet and like manacles on his right hand.
20 The fool laughs out loud, but the wise man smiles barely and without a noise.
21 Instruction is to the wise as a gold ornament and as a bracelet on the right arm.
22 The foot of a fool enters the house quickly, but a man of experience approaches with shame.
23 The fool searches the house from the door, but the well-educated stays outside.
24 It is impolite to listen at the door: the prudent man's face would fall in shame.
25 The lips of charlatans speak only through hearsay, but the prudent weigh their words well.
26 Fools always speak without thinking; The wise think, and then they speak.
27 When the wicked curses his adversary, he curses himself.
28 A gossip defiles himself and is detested by those around him.
1 The sluggard is like a dirty stone: everyone hisses contemptuously at his disgrace.
2 The lazy man is like a pile of excrement: he who picks it up shakes off his hands.
3 The shame of a father is to have a poorly educated son, and if it is a daughter, she comes into the world for his misfortune.
4 The wise daughter will have a husband as her inheritance, but the shameless one will be her father's sorrow.
5 The insolent daughter shames her father and her husband, and is despised by both.
6 Inopportune words are music in a duel, but punishment and discipline are wisdom at all times.
7 Children who lead an honest life and have enough to feed themselves hide the humble origins of their parents.
8 Boastful and poorly educated children dishonor the noble origin of their family.
9 To teach a fool is to repair a broken vessel or wake someone from a deep sleep.
10 To reason with a fool is to reason with a sleepy person: in the end he will say: "What is it about?"

11 Cry for a dead person, because he has lost the light; He cries for a fool, because he has lost his intelligence: he cries serenely for a dead man, because he is at rest; The life of a fool, however, is worse than
death.
12 Mourning for a dead person lasts seven days; for the fool and the wicked, all the days of his life.

13 Do not talk too much to a fool or go with one who has no understanding; take care of him, so as not to have discomfort and not get splashed when he shakes; stay away from him: you will be calm and his
stupidity will not bother you.
14 What thing is heavier than lead, and what else can you call it but "fool"?
15 Sand, salt and a mass of iron weigh less than a man without intelligence.
16 Construction joined together with wooden beams does not crumble due to an earthquake: thus, a heart affirmed in a mature conviction will not be dismayed when the time comes.
17 A heart supported by intelligent reflection is like the stucco that adorns a well-polished wall.
18 A palisade placed on a height cannot resist the attacks of the wind: thus, a heart cowed by foolish ideas is unable to resist fear.
19 He who hurts an eye causes tears to flow; He who hurts the heart, makes feelings appear.
20 He who throws a stone at the birds scares them away; He who insults a friend breaks the friendship.
21 If you have drawn the sword against a friend, do not despair: it is possible to turn back;

22 If you have opened your mouth against a friend, do not worry: reconciliation is possible. But in the face of affront, pride, the revelation of a secret and the treacherous blow, in the face of those things, he will flee.
any friend.

23 Earn the trust of your neighbor in his poverty, so that you may be satisfied with him in his prosperity; remain with him in the time of affliction, and if he inherits, you will share his inheritance.
24 Before the fire, there is steam and smoke in the furnace: thus insults precede spilled blood.
25 I will not be ashamed to protect a friend nor hide from his presence;
26 And if any harm happens to me because of him, everyone who hears about it will take care of him.
27 Who would put a watchman on my mouth and on my lips a seal of discretion, so that I do not fall because of them and my tongue does not lead me to ruin!
1 Lord, Father and Owner of my life, do not abandon me to the whim of my lips nor let me fall because of them!
2 Who will apply the whip to my thoughts and to my heart, the discipline of wisdom, so that my errors are not forgiven and my sins are not overlooked?
3 Thus my errors will not be multiplied nor my sins will become excessive, nor will I fall before my adversaries, nor will my enemy mock me.
4 Sir. Father and God of my life, do not give me haughty eyes
5 and remove evil desires from me.
6 Do not let sensuality and lust dominate me, do not give me over to shameful passions!
7 Listen, children, how the tongue is trained: whoever observes this will not fall into the trap.
8 The sinner is entangled in his own words, the slanderer and the proud fall because of them.
9 Do not get your mouth used to swearing nor get used to pronouncing the name of the Saint.
10 Just as a servant who is constantly watched never escapes a blow, so he who swears and pronounces the Name at all times will not be cleansed from sin.

11 He who swears constantly is full of iniquity, and the scourge will not depart from his house. If he breaks his oath, he incurs a sin; If he despises it, he sins doubly; if he swore in vain, no
He will be justified and his house will be filled with misfortunes.
12 There is a language comparable to death: may it not be found in Jacob's inheritance! Good men are far from all those things: let them not wallow in sins!
13 Do not accustom your mouth to speaking rude things, because by saying them one sins with the word.

14 Remember your father and mother when you sit among the great, lest you forget them in their presence and behave like a fool. Because then you'd rather not
having been born and you would curse the day of your birth.
15 A man accustomed to slanderous words will not be able to be corrected throughout his life.
16 Two kinds of men multiply sins, and a third attracts wrath:
17 A passion burning like burning fire will not cease until the fire burns it up; To the lustful all food is sweet, and he will not be calm until he has died.

18 The man who sins against his own bed says in his heart, “Who sees me? Darkness surrounds me and walls cover me, no one sees me: what can I fear? The Almighty will not remember
my sins."

19 What he fears is the eyes of men, and he does not know that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, which observe all the ways of men and penetrate
in the most hidden corners.
20 Before they were created, all things were known to him, and they are known also after they were finished.
21 That man will be punished in the squares of the city, he will be captured where he least expected it.
22 So also is the woman who abandons her husband and bears him an heir born to a stranger.

23 Because, first, he has disobeyed the Law of the Lord; second, she has committed an offense against her husband; third, she has prostituted herself with her adultery, having children with a strange man
24 She will be taken to the assembly and the punishment will fall on her children.
25 Their children will not take root and their branches will not produce fruit.
26 She will leave her memory as a curse and her infamy will not be erased.
27 Thus those who come after will know that there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord and nothing sweeter than obeying his commandments.
1 Wisdom praises herself and boasts among her people,
2 He opens his mouth in the assembly of the Most High and glories before his Power:
3 “I came out of the mouth of the Most High and covered the earth like a mist.
4 I pitched my tent on high, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud.
