5 I alone traveled the circuit of heaven and walked through the depths of the abysses.
6 Over the waves of the sea and over all the earth, over every people and nation, I exercised my dominion.
7 Among all of them I looked for a place of rest, I asked myself in what inheritance I could reside.
8 Then the Creator of all things gave me a command, he who created me made me pitch my tent, he said to me: “Pitch your tent in Jacob and fix your inheritance in Israel.”
9 He created me before the ages, from the beginning, and forever I will not cease to exist.
10 Before him I ministered in the holy Dwelling, and so I established myself in Zion;
11 He also made me rest in the Favorite City, and my authority is exercised in Jerusalem.
12 I took root in a glorious People, in the Lord's portion, in his inheritance.
13 I grew like a cedar in Lebanon and like a cypress in the mountains of Hermon;
14 I grew like a palm tree in Engedi and like the rose bushes in Jericho; Like a beautiful olive tree in the valley, and like a banana, I rose high.
15 I exhaled perfume like cinnamon, like fragrant aspalatus and choice myrrh, like galbanum, sweet-smelling nail and stacte, and like the smoke of incense in the Dwelling.
16 I spread my branches like a terebinth, and they are branches of glory and grace.
17 I, like a vine, made grace germinate, and my flowers are a fruit of glory and wealth.
18 [I am the mother of beautiful love, fear, science and holy hope. I, who remain forever, am given to all my children, to those who have been chosen by God.]
19 Come to me, those who desire me, and be satisfied with my products!
20 For my remembrance is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance is sweeter than a honeycomb.
21 Those who eat me will still be hungry, those who drink me will be thirstier.
22 He who obeys me will not be ashamed, and those who serve me will not sin.
23 All this is the book of the Covenant of the Most High God, the Law that Moses prescribed for us as an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob.
24 [Do not stop seeking your strength in the Lord; remain united to him, so that he may strengthen you. The Lord Almighty is the only God and, apart from him, there is no other savior.]
25 She makes Wisdom overflow like the Pishon and like the Tigris in the days of the first fruits;
26 floods with intelligence like the Euphrates and like the Jordan in harvest times;
27 He lavishes instruction like the Nile, like the Gihon in the days of the vintage.
28 The first did not finish knowing her and the last does not even glimpse her.
29 For his thought is vaster than the ocean and his plan deeper than the great Abyss.
30 As for me, like a canal flowing out of a river, like a ditch, I came out into a garden
31 and I said, "I will water my garden and soak my flowerbeds." Suddenly, my channel became a river, and my river became a sea!
32 I will still make instruction shine like the dawn and I will radiate its light as far as possible;
33 I will still pour out the teaching as a prophecy and leave it for future generations.
34 For I have not worked for myself alone, but for all who seek wisdom.
1 With three things I adorn myself and present myself beautified before the Lord and men: concord between brothers, friendship between neighbors, and a wife and husband who get along well.
2 But there are three kinds of people that I hate and who irritate me because of their way of life: a poor arrogant man, a rich liar, and an old adulterer who has lost his mind.
3 If you haven't saved in your youth, how are you going to find anything in your old age?
4 What a beautiful decoration for gray hair it is to know how to judge and for the elderly to be men of counsel!
5 How beautiful is the wisdom of the elderly, the reflection and advice of respectable people!
6 The crown of the elderly is a rich experience, and their pride is the fear of the Lord.
7 There are nine imaginable things that I consider happy, and the tenth, I am also going to mention: a man who is happy with his children and one who sees in life the fall of his enemies.
8 Happy is he who lives with an intelligent wife, who has not committed a fault with his tongue, and who has not served an employer unworthy of him!
9 Happy is he who has found prudence and he who exposes it to an attentive audience!
10 How great is he who found wisdom! But no one surpasses him who fears the Lord:
11 the fear of the Lord surpasses all others, and whoever has it, to whom can he be compared?
12 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of his love, and it is by faith that one begins to unite with him.
13 Any wound, except that of the heart! Any evil, except that of a woman!
14 Any misfortune, except that caused by hatred! Any revenge, except that of an enemy!
15 There is no worse poison than that of a serpent, nor worse fury than that of a woman.
16 I would rather live with a lion or a dragon than live with a bad woman.
17 The wickedness of a woman disfigures her countenance and makes her face sullen like a bear.
18 Her husband goes to sit among his neighbors and cannot suppress his bitter groans.
19 All wickedness is small compared to that of a woman: may the fate of the sinner fall upon her!
20 A sandy slope for the feet of an old man is a talkative wife for a peaceful husband.
21 Do not be captivated by a woman's charms or become passionate about her.
22 Outburst of anger, infamy and great shame await the man who is supported by his wife.
23 Dejected heart, gloomy face and sorrow of soul is a bad woman. Inert hands and paralyzed knees is the woman who does not make her husband happy.
24 Through a woman sin began, and because of her we all died.
25 Do not let the water run or give freedom to a bad woman.
26 If she does not walk as you tell her, tear her out of your own flesh.
1 Happy is the husband of a good wife: the number of his days will be doubled!
2 A hardworking wife is her husband's joy and he will live in peace until the end of his days.
3 A good wife is a great fortune, reserved for those who fear the Lord:
4 whether rich or poor, your heart will be happy and your face will be radiant at all times.
5 There are three things that inspire me with fear, and for the fourth I implore mercy: a divided city, a rioting crowd, and false accusation are more painful than death.
6 But sorrow and mourning is a woman who is jealous of her rival, and the scourge of the tongue is present in everything.
7 An ill-fitting yoke is a bad woman: to try to hold her is to catch a scorpion.
8 A drinking woman provokes indignation: she will not be able to hide her ignominy.
9 in the impudence of her gaze and in her pupils the procacity of a woman is recognized.
10 Redouble your guard against a daring young woman, lest she discover an opportunity and take advantage.
11 Beware of provocative looks and don't be surprised if they incite you to evil.
12 She opens her mouth like a thirsty traveler and drinks all the water offered to her; He sits before any stake and opens his quiver to all arrows.
13 A woman's grace delights her husband and her good judgment fills him with vigor.
14 A discreet woman is a gift from the Lord and a well-educated wife is priceless.
15 A modest woman is the greatest of graces and there is no scale to measure one who is master of herself.
16 As the sun rises from the heights of the Lord, so is the charm of a good wife is an orderly house.
17 As a lamp shines on the sacred lampstand, so is the beauty of the face on a slender body.
18 Columns of gold on a plinth of silver are beautiful legs on firm heels.

28 There are two things that sadden me and for a third my anger is kindled: a warrior plunged into destitution, intelligent men treated with contempt, and he who returns from
justice for sin: the Lord destines this to the sword.
29 A merchant will hardly be exempt from sin, and a businessman will not be exempt from sin.
1 Many have sinned for the love of gain, and he who seeks to get rich acts as one who does not see.
2 The stake is driven between the joints of the stones, and sin slips between buying and selling.
3 He who does not resolutely cling to the fear of the Lord will soon see his house in ruins.
4 When the sieve is shaken, the residue remains: thus the residue of a man appears in his words.
5 The kiln tests the potter's vessels, and the test of man is in his conversation.
6 The well-cultivated tree is manifested in its fruits; Thus the word expresses the nature of each one.
7 Do not praise anyone before you hear him reason, because that is where men are tested.
8 If you seek righteousness, you will obtain it, and you will put on it like a glorious robe.
9 Birds seek the company of their peers and the truth returns to those who practice it.
10 The lion is on the lookout for his prey and for sin, for those who practice injustice.
11 The conversation of a good man is always wise, but a fool is changeable like the moon.
12 Measure your time when you are among fools, but stay long among people of judgment.
13 The conversation of fools is hateful, and only rampant vice is amusing to them.
14 Those who swear constantly make your hair stand on end, and when they argue, you have to cover your ears.
15 The disputes of the proud cause blood to flow and it is pitiful to listen to their invectives.
16 He who reveals secrets causes people to lose trust and will never find a close friend.
17 Be affectionate and trusting toward your friend, but if you have revealed his secrets, do not run after him,
18 For as a murderer destroys his victim, so you have destroyed the friendship of your neighbor:
19 Like a bird that you have let escape from your hand, so you have lost your friend, and you will never get him back.
20 Do not run after him, because he is very far away, he fled like a gazelle from the net.
21 For a wound can be bandaged, and for injuries there can be reconciliation, but he who reveals secrets can hope for nothing.
22 He who winks an eye is up to something bad, and no one will be able to dissuade him.
23 Before your eyes, his mouth is all sweetness and he is enraptured by your words, but behind him he changes his language and sets a trap with your very words.
24 I hate many things, but most of all him, and the Lord also hates him. In sin, the punishment
25 He who throws a stone upward throws it on his head, and a treacherous blow also wounds the one who strikes it.
26 He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who spreads a net will be entangled.
27 The evil that is committed falls on oneself, without even knowing where it comes from.
28 Sarcasm and insults are typical of the proud, but punishment stalks them like a lion.
29 Those who rejoice at the fall of the good will fall into the net, and pain will consume them before their death.
30 Resentment and anger are also abominable, and both are the property of a sinner.
1 The vengeful man will suffer the vengeance of the Lord, who will keep an exact account of all his sins.
2 Forgive your neighbor's wrong and then, when you pray, your sins will be absolved.
3 If a man keeps his anger against another, how does he expect the Lord to heal him?
4 He has no mercy for a man like him and dares to implore for his sins!
5 He, a mere mortal, holds a grudge: who will forgive him his sins?
6 Remember the end, and stop hating; think of corruption and death, and be faithful to the commandments;
7 Remember the commandments, and do not bear a grudge against your neighbor; think of the Covenant of the Most High, and overlook the offense.
8 Avoid altercations and you will sin much less, because an angry man stirs up disputes.
9 The sinner sows confusion among friends and creates division among those who lived in peace.

10 The fire burns according to the fuel, and dispute burns according to the measure of stubbornness; According to his strength, will be the fury of a man, and according to his wealth, will he give free course to his anger.
11 A sudden discord kindles a fire, and a hasty dispute causes blood to flow.
12 If you blow a spark, it catches fire; If you spit on it, it goes out, and both things come out of your mouth.
13 Curse the gossiper and the double-tongued: they have ruined many people who lived in peace.
14 The threefold tongue has staggered many and scattered them from nation to nation; She destroyed fortified cities and destroyed the houses of potentates;
15 He put away valiant women and deprived them of the fruit of their labors.
16 He who pays attention to it finds no more rest and can no longer live in peace.
17 A blow of the whip leaves a mark, but a blow of the tongue breaks the bones.
18 Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but they are fewer than those who have fallen because of the tongue.
19 Happy is he who is sheltered from her and has not been exposed to her fury, who has not pulled her yoke nor been bound by your chains!
20 For his yoke is a yoke of iron and his chains are chains of bronze.
21 Disastrous death is what the Abyss inflicts and is preferable to such a tongue!
22 But she has no power over good men and they will not burn in her flames.
23 Those who abandon the Lord will be her victims: she will burn them without being extinguished, she will attack them like a lion and destroy them like a panther.
24 Therefore, surround your possession with a hedge of thorns, guard your silver and your gold well;
25 Make yourself a scale and a weight for your words, and a door and a lock for your mouth.
26 Pay attention, lest you slip because of the tongue and fall before those who lie in wait.
1 He who practices mercy lends to his neighbor, and he who comes to his aid observes the commandments.
2 Lend to your neighbor when he is in need, and restore to him in turn at the appointed time.
3 Keep your word and be loyal to him, and you will find what you need at all times.
4 Many consider the loan a bargain and put those who have helped them in trouble.

5 Until they receive, they kiss the hands of the people and speak humbly of their neighbor's riches, but at the moment of giving back, they ask for an extension, they only give back with plaintive words and throw away.
blame the circumstances.

6 If they pay, the creditor receives only half and has to accept it as a favor. If not, they strip him of his wealth, and he uselessly gains an enemy who pays him with curses and
insults and returns contempt instead of honoring him.
7 Thus many refuse to lend, not out of malice, but out of fear of being robbed without reason.
8 But be lenient with the humble and do not make him wait for your alms.
9 Help the poor to fulfill the commandment and, in their need, do not send them away empty-handed.
10 Lose your money for a brother and a friend: lest it rust under a stone and you lose it.
11 Deposit your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High and it will bring you more profit than gold;
12 Let the treasure locked up in your barns be alms, and it will preserve you from all evil:
13 Better than a strong shield and a heavy spear will fight in your favor against the enemy.
14 A good man becomes his neighbor's guarantor, but he who has lost his shame leaves him abandoned.
15 Do not forget the favors of your surety, because he has risked his life for you.
16 The sinner squanders the assets of his guarantor and the ungrateful abandons the one who saved him.
17 The surety lost many who lived prosperously, it shook them like a wave of the sea;
18 He forced powerful men to expatriate, who were fugitives in strange countries.
19 The sinner who offers himself as surety and seeks advantage exposes himself to prosecution.
20 Help your neighbor to the extent of your resources, but be careful not to ruin yourself.
21 The essential things for life are water, bread, clothing, and a house to shelter with dignity.
22 Better a poor life in a cabin than exquisite food in someone else's house.
23 Be content with what you have, whether little or much, and you will not hear people reproach you for being a stranger.
24 It is a sad life to walk from house to house: where you are a stranger, you cannot open your mouth.
25 You serve food and drink to ungrateful people, and on top of that you have to hear bitter things:
26 “Come here, stranger, prepare the table, and if you have anything at hand, give me something to eat.”
27 –»Leave the place for someone more important; "My brother is coming to stay, and I need the house."
28 How hard it is for a sensitive man to be reproached for hospitality and to have a debt thrown in his face!
1 He who loves his son punishes him regularly, so that he can rejoice in him in the future.
2 He who educates his son well will find satisfaction in him and will feel proud among his acquaintances.
3 He who instructs his son will make his enemy envious and will be happy in front of his friends,
4 The father dies, and it is as if he did not die, because he leaves behind him someone equal to him.
5 While he lives, he rejoices to see him, and at his death, he feels no regret:
6 He leaves someone who will avenge him on his enemies and return favors to his friends.
7 He who pampers his child will bind up his wounds and with every cry he gives, his insides will be moved.
8 An untamed horse becomes reluctant, and a spoiled son becomes insolent.
9 Spoil your son, and he will make you tremble; Play with it, and it will fill you with sadness.
10 Do not make jokes with him, so as not to suffer with him or grind your teeth at the end.
11 Do not give them free rein in their youth,
12 Beat him without fear while he is a child, lest he become rebellious and disobey you.
13 Educate your son and train him well, so that you do not have to endure his shamelessness.
14 Better poor, healthy and vigorous, than rich, full of infirmities.
15 Health and vigor are worth more than all gold and a robust body, more than an immense fortune.
16 There is no greater wealth than the health of the body nor greater happiness than the joy of the heart.
17 Death is preferable to a bitter life and eternal rest to an incurable disease.
18 Delicacies poured over a closed mouth are the food placed on a grave:
19 Of what use is the offering to the idol if it cannot eat or taste? This is what happens with the man persecuted by the Lord:
20 He looks with his eyes and sighs, like a eunuch when he embraces a virgin.
21 Do not let sadness take over you or torment yourself with your musings.
22 A joyful heart is the life of a man, and joy lengthens the number of his days.
23 Live with hope and comfort your heart, and keep sadness far from you, because sadness was the downfall of many and no benefit is derived from it.
24 Envy and anger shorten life and worries make you grow old before your time.
25 A man with a cheerful heart has a good appetite and what he eats is beneficial to him.
1 The rich man's worries end up consuming him and the desire for riches makes him lose sleep.
2 Worry about sustenance prevents sleep, and deprives sleep more than a serious illness.
3 The rich man gets tired of accumulating a fortune, and if he rests, it is to fill himself with pleasures;
4 The poor man grows tired of accumulating a fortune, and if he rests, he falls into poverty.
5 He who loves gold can never be righteous, and the desire for gain leads a man astray.
6 Many became ruined because of gold and faced their own destruction,
7 because gold is a trap for those who are crazy about it, and all fools allow themselves to be caught.
8 Happy is the rich man who remains intact and does not run after gold!
9 Who is he? And we will congratulate him because he has done wonders in his town.
10 Who passed this test and proved to be perfect? He has good reason to glory. Who could transgress and did not transgress, do evil and did not do it?
11 Their property will be secured, and their profits will be published by the assembly.
12 Are you sitting at a great man's table? Don't say, licking your lips: "There are so many things here!"
13 Remember that it is wrong to have a greedy eye: has anything worse than the eye been created? That's why she sheds tears for anything.
14 Do not reach out your hand to everything you see, lest you trip over your neighbor at the plate.
15 Judge your neighbor by what you yourself feel and reflect whenever you do something.
16 Eat what is put before you like an educated person and do not chew loudly, so as not to make yourself hateful.
17 Be the first to stop eating, out of good manners, and do not be insatiable, so as not to crash.
18 If you are sitting among many diners, do not extend your hand before others.
19 How little is enough for a well-educated man! That's why he doesn't suffocate when he's in bed.
20 A sober stomach, healthy sleep: one gets up early, and is wide awake. Painful insomnia, nausea and cramps: that awaits the insatiable man.
21 And if you have been forced to overeat, get up, go away and vomit and you will feel relief.
22 Listen to me, my son, do not despise me, and in the end you will understand my words: be moderate in all your actions and you will never fall ill.
23 The lips bless him who serves good food and the testimony of his generosity is worthy of faith.
24 The city murmurs about him who is stingy with his bread, and the testimony of his stinginess is accurate.
25 Do not act brave with wine, because wine has been the downfall of many.
26 As the forge tests the temper of steel, wine tests man in the disputes of the arrogant.
27 Wine is like life to man, as long as he drinks it in moderation. What is life when the wine is missing? For he was created for the joy of men.
28 Joy of the heart and joy of the soul is wine drunk at its proper time and in the appropriate measure.
29 Bitterness of the soul is wine drunk in excess, with the intention of challenging and provoking.
30 Drunkenness angers a fool to the point of scandal, weakens his strength and causes wounds.
31 While drinking wine, do not rebuke your neighbor or humiliate him if he becomes cheerful; Do not address him with insulting words or bother him with complaints.
1 Is it your turn to preside over the table? Do not be conceited: behave towards others as one of them and serve them well before sitting down.
2 Once you have completed all your duties, take your place to rejoice because of the guests and see yourself crowned because everything is in order.
3 Speak, old man, because it is yours to do so, but with discretion and without interrupting the music.
4 While listening, do not start chatting or act wise out of time
5 Ruby seal on a gold jewel is a musical concert while drinking wine;
6 emerald seal in a gold setting is melodious music over the sweetness of wine.
7 Speak, young man, when necessary, but twice at most, and if they ask you.
8 Speak concisely, say much in a few words: be like one who knows and yet remains silent.
9 In the midst of the great, do not try to equal them, and if another speaks, be sparing in your words.
10 The lightning shines before the thunder and charm precedes the modest man.
11 Get up on time, if you are the last to leave, go straight to your house, without stopping along the way.
12 Have fun there as you like, but without sinning with arrogant words.
13 And for all that, bless your Creator, who intoxicates you with his goods.
14 He who fears the Lord agrees to be instructed, and those who ardently seek him will obtain his favor.
15 He who seeks the Law will be satisfied with it, but he who pretends to observe it will become a stumbling block.
16 Those who fear the Lord discover what is right and make his precepts shine like a lamp.
17 Sinful man does not tolerate any reproach and finds pretexts to do what he wants.
18 The man of counsel does not neglect reflection; the wicked and the arrogant proceed recklessly.
19 Do nothing without proper advice and you will not regret your actions.
20 Do not go along a path full of obstacles and you will not stumble against stones.
21 Don't trust the clear path
22 and take care of even your children.
23 In everything you do, be true to yourself, for that is also keeping the commandments.
24 He who trusts in the Law pays attention to the commandments, and he who trusts in the Lord will not be harmed.
1 He who fears the Lord will suffer no evil and will be delivered in trial again and again.
2 A wise man never hates the Law, but he who pretends to observe it is like a ship in a storm.
3 An intelligent man trusts in the Law and has as much faith in it as in a divine oracle.
4 Prepare what you are going to say, so you will be heard, summarize what you know, and then respond.
5 The feelings of a fool are a cartwheel, and his conversation is like a turning axle.
6 A mocking friend is like a horse in heat: he neighs under any rider.
7 Why is one day more important than another, if light comes from the sun every day of the year?
8 It is the knowledge of the Lord that made them different, and he diversified the times and the festivals:
9 He exalted and consecrated some days, and counted others among the ordinary days.
10 All men come from the ground, and Adam was created from the ground;
11 But, in his great wisdom, the Lord distinguished them and made them go on different paths:
12 some he blessed and exalted, consecrated them and brought them close to him; others he cursed and humiliated, and struck down from their posts.
13 As the clay is in the hands of the potter, who disposes of it according to his will, so men are in the hands of their Creator, and he will reward them according to his decision.
14 In the face of evil, there is good, and in the face of death, life: thus, in front of the good man, there is the sinner.
15 Consider also all the works of the Most High: they are two by two, one facing the other.
16 I, the last to arrive, remained alert as one who gathers behind the vineyards.
17 By the blessing of the Lord, I have arrived on time, and like a vinedresser, I have filled the winepress.
18 Know that I did not labor for myself alone, but for all who seek instruction.
19 Listen to me, leaders of the people, and you leaders of the assembly, pay attention to me.
20 Whether son or wife, brother or friend, give no one authority over you while you live. Also do not give your property to another, lest you regret it and have to claim it.
21 As long as you live and have breath, do not allow yourself to be alienated by anyone:
22 It is better that your children ask you than to have your eyes fixed on their hands.
23 In everything you do, be the one who directs, and do not tarnish your reputation with anything.
24 When the days of your life come to an end, at the hour of death, divide your inheritance.
25 To the donkey the fodder, the staff and the burden; to the servant bread, discipline and work.
26 Force your slave to work, and you will find rest; leave him unoccupied, and he will seek freedom.
27 The yoke and the reins bend the neck, and for the perverse servant, there is torture and torment.
28 Force him to work, so that he does not remain idle, because idleness teaches many bad things.
29 Force him to work as he should, and if he does not obey, bind his feet with chains.
30 But ask no one for more than necessary, and do nothing without justice.
31 If you have only one servant, consider him as yourself, because you have acquired him with blood;
32 If you have only one servant, treat him as a brother, because you need him as much as yourself.
33 If you mistreat him and he ends up running away, which way will you go to find him?
1 Vain and deceitful are the hopes of a fool, and dreams give wings to fools.
2 Trying to grab a shadow or run after the wind is giving credence to dreams.
3 Dream visions are nothing more than a mirage: a face in the reflection of its own image.
4 Can something pure come out of the impure or can the truth come out of a lie?
5 Divinations, omens and dreams are vain things, pure fantasies, like those of a woman in labor.
6 Unless the Almighty sends them on a visit, pay no attention to them.
7 For dreams have led astray many who have fallen by hoping in them.
8 The Law must be fulfilled without falsehood, and wisdom faithfully expressed is perfect.
9 He who has traveled widely knows many things, and the man of experience speaks intelligently.
10 He who has not been tested knows few things, but he who has traveled far acquires great skill.
11 I have seen many things in the course of my travels, and I know much more than I could express.
12 Many times I was in danger of death, and thanks to all that I escaped safely.
13 The spirit of those who fear the Lord will live, because they have put their hope in him who saves them.
14 He who fears the Lord is not intimidated by anything, nor is he dismayed, because he is his hope.
15 Happy is the soul of him who fears the Lord! Who does it rely on and what is its support?

16 The eyes of the Lord look upon those who love him: he is a powerful shield and a sure support, a refuge from the scorching wind and the heat of midday, a safeguard against stumbling and a help.
against the fall.
17 He lifts the spirit and illuminates the eyes, gives health, life and blessing.
18 To offer the fruit of unrighteousness as a sacrifice is to present a defective offering, and the gifts of the wicked are not accepted.
19 The Most High does not accept the offerings of the wicked, and it is not because of the number of victims that He forgives sins.
20 Like sacrificing a son before his father's eyes, it is presenting a victim with goods taken from the poor.
21 A crust of bread is the life of the needy: he who deprives them of it is bloodthirsty.
22 He who deprives him of sustenance kills his neighbor, he who withholds the wages of a hired worker sheds blood.
23 If one builds and another destroys, what do they gain by that but toil?
24 If one begs and another curses, whose voice will the Master of all listen to?
25 He who touches a dead person again after washing, what has he gained by being purified?
26 So is the man who helps for his sins and then commits them again. Who will listen to his prayer and what has he gained by humbling himself?
1 Observing the Law is like presenting many offerings and being faithful to the commandments is offering a sacrifice of communion;
2 to return a favor is to make an oblation of flour and to give alms is to offer a sacrifice of praise.
3 The way to please the Lord is to turn away from evil, and turning away from unrighteousness is a sacrifice of atonement.
4 Do not appear before the Lord empty-handed, for all this is prescribed by the commandments.
5 When the offering of the righteous greases the altar, its fragrance reaches the presence of the Most High.
6 The sacrifice of the righteous is accepted and his memorial will not be forgotten.
7 Glorify the Lord generously and do not be stingy with the firstfruits of your hands.
8 Always give with a radiant face and consecrate the tithe with joy.
9 Give to the Most High according to what he gave you, and generously, according to your resources,
10 because the Lord knows how to reward and will give you seven times as much.
11 Do not try to bribe him with a gift, because he would not accept it, and do not rely on an unjust sacrifice.
12 For the Lord is judge and makes no distinction between persons:
13 is not partial to the poor and listens to the plea of the oppressed;
14 He does not ignore the prayer of the orphan, nor the widow, when she expresses her complaint.
15 Do not tears run down the widow's cheeks and does her cry not accuse him who causes them to be shed?
16 He who renders worship that pleases the Lord is accepted, and his prayer reaches to the clouds.
17 The supplication of the humble pierces the clouds and until it reaches its destination, he is not consoled:
18 does not give up until the Most High intervenes to judge the righteous and do them justice.
19 The Lord will not delay and will not be patient with the wicked,
20 until the power of the ruthless is broken and the nations are rewarded;
21 until the multitude of the arrogant is wiped out and the scepter of the unrighteous is broken;
22 until he rewards each man according to his actions, rewarding men's works according to their intentions;
23 until he judges the cause of his people and cheers them with his mercy.
24 How beautiful is mercy in the time of affliction, like rain clouds in the time of drought!
1 Have mercy on us, sovereign Lord, God of all things, and behold, put your fear in all nations.
2 Raise your hand against foreign nations and let them see your dominion.
3 Just as you showed them your holiness by punishing us, let us also show your greatness by punishing them;
4 and may they recognize you, as we have recognized that there is no other God besides you, Lord.
5 Renew the signs and repeat the wonders, glorify your hand and your right arm.
6 Awaken your fury and pour out your wrath, suppress the adversary and exterminate the enemy.
7 Make haste the hour and remember the oath, so that your deeds may be told.
8 May the fugitive be devoured by the heat of the fire, and may those who mistreat your people find their destruction.
9 Crush the heads of the enemy leaders, who say, "There is no one besides us!"
10 Gather together all the tribes of Jacob, and give them their inheritance, as at the beginning.
11 Have mercy, Lord, on the people who are called by your name, on Israel, whom you treated as a firstborn.
12 Have compassion on the holy city, Jerusalem, the place of rest.
13 Fill Zion with praise for your triumph, and fill your people with your glory.
14 Bear witness on behalf of those whom you created in the beginning, and fulfill the prophecies announced in your Name.
15 Give the reward to those who wait for you, and let the truth of your prophets be proven.
16 Hear, Lord, the prayer of those who pray to you, according to Aaron's blessing on your people,
17 so that all who live on earth may recognize that you are the Lord, the eternal God.
18 The stomach assimilates all kinds of foods, but some are better than others.
19 The palate distinguishes delicacies and the intelligent heart discovers lies.
20 A crooked heart causes trouble, but a man of experience gives it what it deserves.
21 A woman accepts any husband, but some girls are better than others.
22 The beauty of a woman gladdens the face and surpasses all the desires of man.
23 If there is kindness and sweetness on her lips, her husband is no longer one of many men.
24 He who acquires a woman has the beginning of fortune, a help suitable for him and a pillar to lean on.
25 Where there is no fence, property is plundered, and where there is no woman, the man groans and drifts.
26 Who can trust a robber who goes quickly from city to city?
27 So it is with the man without a nest, who takes shelter where the night surprises him.
1 Every friend says: "I am also your friend," but there are friends who are friends only in name.
2 Doesn't it sadden even to death to see a dear friend become an enemy?
3 Perverse inclination! Where have they rolled you from to cover the earth with falsehood?
4 A companion shares the joys of his friend and in the moment of affliction, turns against him!
5 Another suffers with his friend to fill his belly, and at the time of combat, he takes up the shield!
6 Never forget a good friend, and remember him when you have riches.
7 Everyone who advises recommends his advice, but there are those who advise thinking only of themselves.
8 Be careful with the one who gives advice and find out first what he needs, because then he will advise what is best for him; lest one thing or another does not matter to you
9 and tells you: “You are on the right path,” while he stands in front of you to see what is happening to you.
10 Do not consult him who underestimates you, and hide your plans from him who is jealous of you.

11 Do not ask advice from a woman about her rival, nor from a coward about war, nor from a merchant about a deal, nor from a buyer about a sale, nor from an envious person about gratitude, nor from a
a ruthless one about a profit, nor a lazy one about any work, nor a
to someone who works by the hour on the completion of a work, nor to a servant
slacker about a difficult job: don't count on these for any advice.
12 But turn assiduously to a godly man, who you know keeps the commandments, who is able to feel what you yourself feel, and who will suffer with you if you stumble.
13 Let yourself be guided by what your heart tells you, because no one will be more faithful to you than him:
14 The soul of a man often warns better than seven lookouts stationed on a height.
15 And above all I pray to the Most High, to direct your steps in truth.
16 The beginning of all work is conversation, and before all action, there is advice.
17 The heart is the root of thoughts, and it causes four branches to sprout:
18 good and evil, life and death, and the one that always decides in all this is the tongue.
19 A man may be able to instruct many and yet be useless to himself.
20 He who is wise with lip service becomes hateful and will end up without anything to eat:
21 The favor of the Lord was not granted to him, because he was devoid of all wisdom.
22 If a man is wise in himself, the fruits of his understanding are in his mouth and are worthy of faith.
23 A wise man instructs his own people and the fruits of his intelligence are worthy of faith.
24 A wise man is showered with blessings and, seeing him, everyone congratulates him.
25 Man's days are numbered, but Israel's days are numberless.
26 A wise man gains the trust of his people and his name survives forever.
27 My son, for your eating regimen, test yourself: see what is wrong with you and deprive yourself of it.
28 Because not everything is suitable for everyone nor does everyone like the same thing.
29 Do not be insatiable with pleasures or overindulge in food.
30 Because excess food brings disease and gluttony causes colic.
31 Gluttony caused the death of many, but he who takes care will prolong his life.
1 Honor the doctor for his services, as is appropriate, because the Lord has also created him.
2 Healing comes from the Most High, and the doctor receives gifts from the king.
3 The doctor's science strengthens his prestige and he gains the admiration of the greats.
4 The Lord made medicinal plants grow, and the wise man does not despise them.
5 Did not a branch sweeten the water, so that its properties might be known?
6 The Lord gave men knowledge, to be glorified by his wonders.
7 With these remedies the doctor cures and removes pain, and the pharmacist prepares his ointments.
8 Thus the works of the Lord have no end, and from him comes health to the surface of the earth.
9 If you are sick, my son, do not be negligent, pray to the Lord, and he will heal you.
10 Do not commit sin, amend your conduct and purify your heart from all sin.
11 Offer the sweet aroma and memorial of flour, present a rich offering, as if it were the last.
12 Then let the doctor act, because the Lord created him; May he not leave you, because you need him.
13 In some cases, your improvement is in their hands,
14 and they themselves will pray to the Lord to allow them to give relief and heal the sick person, so that he may recover.
15 The man who sins before his Creator, let him fall into the hands of the doctor!
16 My son, for a dead person, shed tears and sing a lament, like someone who suffers terribly. Bury his corpse in the established manner and do not neglect his burial.
17 Cry bitterly, beat your chest, and observe the mourning that he deserves, for a day or two, to avoid comments, and then console yourself for your sadness.
18 Because sadness leads to death and a broken heart takes away strength.
19 In misfortune sadness is permanent, and the heart curses a miserable life.
20 Do not let yourself be carried away by sadness, push it away, remembering your end.
21 Never forget: there is no way back! To the dead, you will not be able to be useful and you will harm yourself.
22 "Remember my destiny, which will also be yours: yesterday to me and today to you."
23 Since the dead man rests, leave his memory in peace, and try to console yourself, because his spirit has departed.
24 The wisdom of the scribe requires time and dedication, and he who is not absorbed by other tasks will become wise.
25 How will he become wise who handles the plow and is proud to wield the cattle prod, who guides the oxen, works with them, and knows only how to talk about bulls?
26 He puts all his effort into opening the furrows and goes out of his way to provide fodder for the calves.

27 It is the same with the craftsman and the builder, who work day and night; with whom they engrave the effigies of the seals and patiently modify the designs: they dedicate themselves to
reproduce the model and work late to finish the work.

The noise of the hammer deafens his ears and his eyes are fixed on the model of the
object; He puts all his effort into finishing his works and goes out of his way to leave them well.
finished.

30 with his arm he shapes the clay and with his feet he overcomes its resistance; He puts all his effort into finishing the varnishing and works hard to clean the oven.
31 They all trust in their hands, and each one proves wise in his craft.
32 Without them no city would be built, no one would inhabit it or move through it.
33 But they will not be sought for the council of the people nor will they have preeminence in the assembly; They will not sit in the judge's court nor be versed in the decrees of the Covenant.

1 The same does not happen with those who dedicate their lives to reflecting on the Law of the Most High. He seeks the wisdom of all the ancients and spends his time studying the prophecies;
2 preserves the sayings of famous men and penetrates into the subtleties of parables;
3 investigates the hidden meaning of proverbs and endlessly studies enigmatic sentences.
4 He serves among the great and is seen in the presence of the leaders; He travels through foreign countries, because he knows from experience the good and the bad of men.
5 With all his heart, early in the morning, he turns to the Lord, his Creator, and pleads in the presence of the Most High; He opens his lips to pray and asks for forgiveness for his sins.

7 he will direct his rabbit and his science aright and reflect on the secrets of God;

9 Many will praise his intelligence, which will never be forgotten; His memory will never be erased and his name will live forever.
10 The nations will speak of his wisdom and the assembly will proclaim his praise.
11 If he lives a long time, he will have more fame than a thousand others; If he enters into rest, that will be enough for him.
12 I am going to continue exposing my reflections, because I am filled like the full moon.
13 Listen to me, holy children, and grow like a rose bush that springs up by the stream of water.
14 Breathe out a sweet fragrance like incense and bloom like a lily; spread aroma and sing a song, bless the Lord for all his works.
15 Know that his Name is great, give thanks to him, proclaiming his praise, with songs on your lips and with harps, and say in thanksgiving:

its moment.

18 He commands it, and his will is done, and no one can undermine his saving work.
19 The works of every living creature are before him and nothing can be hidden from his eyes.

26 The most indispensable things for the life of man are water and fire, iron and salt, wheat flour, milk and honey, the blood of the vine, oil and clothing:

28 There are winds that were created for punishment, and in their fury, he makes them more impetuous: at the time of destruction, they unleash their violence and appease the fury of
the one who made them.
29 Fire, hail, famine and pestilence: all these were created for punishment.
30 The teeth of wild beasts, scorpions and vipers, and the avenging sword that destroys the wicked,
31 All of them rejoice at his commands and are on earth ready to serve him: when the time comes, they will not transgress his word.
32 Therefore, from the beginning, I was convinced of this, I reflected, and I wrote it down:
33 The works of the Lord are all good, and in due season he provides for every need.
34 There is no reason to say: "This is worse than that," because in time everything will be recognized as good.
35 And now, with all your heart and with a loud voice, sing hymns and bless the name of the Lord.
1 A painful task has been imposed on every man and a heavy yoke burdens the children of Adam, from the day they leave the mother's womb, until the day they return to the common mother.
2 The anxious anticipation of the day of death gives them much to think about and fills them with fear.
3 From him who sits on a glorious throne to him who is humbled in dust and ashes;
4 from he who wears purple and a crown to he who is dressed miserably, they feel only anger and envy, confusion and restlessness, fear of death, resentment and rivalry;
5 and at the time when each one rests in his bed, the sleep of the night disturbs his thoughts.
6 He rests a little, almost nothing, and begins to struggle as if in broad daylight, agitated by his own nightmares, like someone fleeing a battlefield.
7 At the moment of feeling safe, he wakes up and sees with surprise that his fear was unfounded.
8 This applies to every living creature, whether man or animal, but to sinners seven times more:
9 death, blood, rivalry and sword, adversity, hunger, destruction and scourge.
10 All this was created for the wicked, and because of them the flood came.
11 Whatever comes out of the earth returns to the earth, and whatever comes out of the water returns to the sea.
12 Bribery and injustice will disappear, but faithfulness remains forever.
13 The wealth of the unrighteous will dry up like a torrent, it is like the roar of thunder that breaks in the storm.
14 When one of them seizes something, he rejoices, but the transgressors will disappear completely.
15 The shoots of the wicked do not multiply their branches, and the impure roots are on a steep rock.
16 A reed that sprouts in any water and on the edge of a river will be uprooted before all other grass.
17 Generosity is like a lush orchard and almsgiving endures forever.
18 Sweet is the life of one who is self-sufficient and of one who works, but even more so is that of one who finds treasure.
19 Having children and founding a city perpetuate the name, but an irreproachable woman is valued more highly.
20 Wine and music gladden the heart, but the love of wisdom even more.
21 The flute and the harp make melodious sounds, but even more so a sweet tongue.
22 Grace and beauty attract the eye, but the greenness of the fields even more so.
23 The friend and the companion help each other in a timely manner, but the wife and the husband even more so.
24 Brothers and benefactors are useful in adversity, but almsgiving saves even more.
25 Gold and silver make you march with a firm step, but advice is even more appreciated.
26 Wealth and strength comfort the heart, but the fear of the Lord even more. With the fear of the Lord, nothing is missing, and it is no longer necessary to seek other help.
27 The fear of the Lord is like a lush garden, and it protects more than any glory.
28 My son, do not live by begging, because it is better to die than to beg.

29 The life of someone who is attentive to another's table does not deserve to be called life. He stains his mouth with other people's food, and the educated and well-educated man takes care to do so.
30 In the mouth of the shameless, begging is sweet, but in his belly it will be a burning fire.
1 Death, how bitter your memory is for the one who lives peacefully in the midst of his goods, for the carefree man, for whom everything is going well and still has the strength to enjoy life!
2 Death, your sentence is welcome for the needy and powerless man, worn out by the years and full of anxieties, who rebels and has exhausted his patience!
3 Do not fear your death sentence, remember those who preceded you and will follow you.

4 This is the sentence of the Lord for every living being: why oppose the will of the Most High? Even if you live ten, a hundred or a thousand years, in the Abyss they will not blame you for what you have done.
lived.
5 The children of sinners are abominable people who frequent the houses of the wicked.
6 The inheritance of the children of sinners goes to ruin, with their descendants their infamy is perpetuated.
7 An ungodly father attracts the reproaches of his children, because it is to him that they owe their infamy.
8 Woe to you, wicked men, who have forsaken the Law of the Most High God!
9 If you are born, you are born to the curse, and if you die, the curse will be your lot.
10 Everything that comes out of the earth returns to the earth: thus the wicked pass from curse to ruin.
11 Men mourn because their bodies perish. and as for sinners, even their bad name will be erased.
12 Take care of your good name, because that will remain with you much more than a thousand treasures of gold.
13 A happy life has its days numbered, but a good name remains forever.
14 My children, observe my teaching in peace. Hidden wisdom and invisible treasure: what good are one and the other?
15 The man who hides his foolishness is preferable to the one who hides his wisdom.
16 Therefore, be ashamed of what I am going to tell you, because it is not right to be ashamed of anything, nor does every shame deserve to be equally approved.
17 Be ashamed of fornication before your father and mother, and of lying before a ruler and a powerful man;
18 of crime before a judge and a magistrate, and of iniquity before the assembly of the people;
19 of injustice before a companion and a friend, and of theft before his neighborhood;
20 of violating an oath and a covenant, and of resting one's elbows on the table;
21 to give or receive with disdain, and not to return the greeting;
22 from looking at a prostitute, and from turning away from a relative;
23 from taking from another his share or the gift he received, and from looking at a married woman;
24 of being intimate with your servant, do not go near her bed!
25 of saying hurtful words to your friends, whatever you say to them, don't hold it against them!
26 of repeating what you have heard and revealing secrets.
27 Then you will feel real shame, and you will be well regarded by all men.
1 But do not be ashamed of the following and do not sin for fear of those who will think of you:
2 do not be ashamed of the Law of the Most High and of the Covenant, nor of the sentence that gives justice to the wicked;
3 to settle accounts with old companions, nor to share an inheritance with others;
4 to use exact weights and measurements, nor to obtain large or small profits;
5 to make profits in trade, to frequently correct your children, nor to make the backs of a bad servant bleed.
6 It is advisable to put an unfaithful woman under seal, and where there are many hands to keep things under lock and key.
7 Count and weigh well what you deposit, and what you give and receive, that it is all in writing.

8 Do not be ashamed to correct the foolish and the foolish, nor the decrepit old man who competes with the young. This way you will show that you are truly educated and you will be esteemed by everyone.
world.
9 A daughter is a secret cause of insomnia for her father, and worry about her keeps him from sleeping: when she is young, she can outgrow her age, and if she is married, she can be hated.
10 While she is a virgin, she can be raped and become pregnant in her father's house. If she has a husband, she may be unfaithful, if she already lives together, she may be sterile.

11 If your daughter is bold, watch over her carefully, lest she make you a mockery of your enemies, the gossip of the city and the gossip of the people, and she covers you with shame.
everyone's eyes.
12 Do not fix your eyes on anyone's beauty or treat women with familiarity.
13 Because a moth comes out of clothing, and a woman's malice comes out of a woman.
14 Better the malice of a man than the kindness of a woman: a woman brings shame to ignominy.
15 Now I am going to remember the works of the Lord, what I have seen, I am going to relate: through the words of the Lord his works exist.
16 The bright sun contemplates all things, and the work of the Lord is full of his glory.
17 It has not been possible for the saints of the Lord to relate all his wonders, which the Lord almighty solidly established so that the universe would be established in its glory.
18 He probes the abyss and the heart, and penetrates into their secret plans, because the Most High possesses all knowledge and observes the signs of the times.
19 He announces the past and the future, and reveals the traces of hidden things:
20 no thought escapes him, no word is hidden from him.
21 He arranged in order the great works of his wisdom, because it has existed forever and ever; nothing has been added, nothing has been taken away, and he had no need of any counselor.
22 How desirable are all his works! And what we see is just a spark!
23 Everything has life and endures forever, and everything obeys a certain end.
24 All things are in pairs, one against the other, and he has made nothing incomplete:
25 one thing ensures the good of the other. Who will be satisfied with seeing his glory?
1 The pride of the sky is the clarity of the firmament, and the celestial vault is a magnificent spectacle.
2 The sun, when it appears, proclaims at its rising how admirable is the work of the Most High.
3 At noon the earth dries up, and who can resist its heat?
4 The furnace for the forge is stoked, but three times as much the sun scorches the mountains; He exhales the burning vapors and with the brilliance of his rays he blinds the eyes.
5 How great is the Lord who created it! At his command, he begins his rapid career.
6 Also the moon, always at the precise moment, marks the epochs and marks the times.
7 Its course determines the festivals: it is a star that decreases after its full moon.
8 From her the month gets its name; It grows admirably in its cycles, it is the insignia of the armies camped on high, which shines in the firmament of heaven.
9 The glory of the stars is the beauty of the sky, a luminous decoration in the heights of the Lord:
10 By the word of the Holy One, they remain in order and do not defect from their guard posts.
11 Look at the rainbow and bless him who made it: what magnificent splendor!
12 He traces a halo of glory in the sky; The hands of the Most High have extended it.
13 At his command the snow falls, and he releases the lightning bolts that execute his decrees;
14 This is how the reserves open and the clouds fly like birds.
15 With his great power, he condenses the clouds, which are pulverized into hail.
16a At his sight the mountains are moved,
17a the sound of his thunder shakes the earth;
16b the south wind blows at its will,
17b the northern hurricane and cyclones.
18 Like a flock of birds, he scatters the snow, and when it comes down, it settles like a locust; The brilliance of its whiteness dazzles the eyes and the spirit is enraptured to see it fall.

20 The cold wind blows from the north and the ice freezes on the water, settling on every body of water and covering it like a shell,
21 Another wind devours the mountains, burns the desert and consumes the grass like a fire.
22 A sudden fog cures all this, and the dew cools after the scorching wind.
23 According to his plan, he subdued the Abyss, and planted the islands there.
24 Those who navigate the sea tell of their dangers and their stories seem incredible to us:
25 There are strange and wonderful things there, animals of all kinds and sea monsters.
26 Thanks to him, his messenger arrives safely, and by his word all things are ordered.
27 No matter how much we say, we will never finish; In a single word: he is everything.
28 Where to find the strength to glorify him? For he is the Great, superior to all his works,
29 Fearsome and sovereignly great Lord: his power is admirable.
30 Glorify the Lord, exalt him as much as you can, and he will always be above! To exalt it, redouble your strength, do not get tired, because you will never finish.
31 Who has seen it, to be able to describe it? Who will praise her according to what she is?
32 There are many hidden things that are even greater, because we have only seen some of his works.
33 The Lord has made all things and gave wisdom to good men.
1 Let us praise the illustrious men, the ancestors of our race.
2 The Lord filled them with glory, manifested his greatness from ancient times.

4 They guided the people with their advice, with their intelligence to instruct them and with the wise words of their teaching;
5 others composed melodious songs and wrote poetic stories;
6 Others were rich men, full of power, who lived in peace in their homes.
7 All of them were honored by their contemporaries and were the pride of their time.
8 Some of them left a name and are still mentioned with praise.
9 But there are others who fell into oblivion and disappeared as if they had not existed; They passed away as if they had not been born, just like their children after them.
10 This is not the case with those, good men, whose works of justice have not been forgotten.
11 With their descendants the rich inheritance that comes from them is perpetuated.
12 Their descendants were faithful to the alliances and so were their grandchildren, thanks to them.
13 His descendants will endure forever, and their glory will not fade away.
14 Their bodies were buried in peace, and their name survives through the generations.
15 The people proclaim his wisdom, and the assembly declares his praise.
16 Enoch pleased the Lord and was translated, he is a model of conversion for future generations.

21 Therefore God assured him with an oath that the nations would be blessed in his descendants, that he would multiply them like the dust of the earth, that he would exalt his descendants
like the stars, and would give them the land as an inheritance, from one sea to the other.
and from the River to the ends of the earth.

parts and distributed them among the twelve tribes.

7 He established him under an irrevocable covenant and conferred on him the priesthood of the people. He adorned him with splendid ornaments and girded him with glorious clothing.
8 He clothed it with all splendor and confirmed it with the insignia of power: the trousers, the tunic, and the ephod;

9 He put pomegranates around his cloak and surrounded it with numerous golden bells, so that they would tinkle with each of his steps, making their sound heard in the Temple, as a memorial for the children of his
town.

11 with precious stones, engraved in the form of seals and set in gold – the work of a jeweler – to serve as a memorial, by the engraved inscription, according to the number of the tribes of Israel;
12 the golden diadem on top of the turban, engraved with the sign of its consecration: a badge of honor, magnificent work, an ornament that is a pleasure to behold.
13 Before him, nothing so beautiful was seen, and no foreigner ever dressed like that, but only his children and his descendants forever.
14 Their sacrifices are consumed entirely, twice a day, continuously.

15 Moses conferred on him the investiture and anointed him with holy oil. This was an eternal covenant for him and his descendants, as long as heaven lasts, to serve God as priests and
Bless the people in his name.

19 When the Lord saw this, he was displeased, and they were destroyed by the fierceness of his anger: he worked wonders against them, consuming them with his burning fire.

20 He increased Aaron's glory still more, and gave him an inheritance: he assigned to him the firstfruits of the first fruits as a share and assured him, first of all, food in
abundance,
21 For they feed on the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave to Aaron and his descendants.
22 But in the land of the people, he has no inheritance, nor is there any part for him among the people, because "I myself am your part and your inheritance."

23 Pinchas son of Eleazar was the third in glory, because of his zeal in the fear of the Lord, and because he stood firm against the rebellion of the people, with the generous ardor of his spirit: it was like this
how he atoned for Israel's sin.

silencing perverse murmurings.

born from him.

real, than to be these false gods.

1 There was a man in Babylon named Jehoiachin.

5 That year, two elders of the people had been chosen as judges. The word of the Lord refers to them: "Iniquity came out in Babylon from the elders and the judges who considered themselves leaders of the people."
6 These elders frequented Joachim's house and everyone who had a dispute came to them.
7 Around noon, when everyone had already retired, Susanna was going to walk in the garden with her husband.
8 The two old men, who saw her come in every day for a walk, began to desire her.
9 They lost their minds and averted their eyes so as not to look at Heaven and not remember His righteous judgments.
10 They both burned with passion for her, but they hid their torment from each other,
11 because they were ashamed to confess their desire to sleep with her,
12 and they managed to see her every day.
13 One day, after saying to each other, "Let's go home, it's time for lunch," they separated and went their separate ways.

14 But both of them retraced their steps and found themselves face to face. Forced to give each other an explanation, they both confessed their passion and agreed to look for the moment when
They could surprise Susana alone.

15 Once, while they were waiting for a favorable opportunity, Susanna entered as in the previous days, accompanied only by two young servants, and since it was hot, she wanted to bathe in the
garden.

17 She said to the servants, "Bring me the cream and the perfumes, and close the garden gate so I can bathe."

19 As soon as the servants left, they stood up and fell on her and said,
20 «The garden gate is closed and no one sees us. We burn with passion for you; consent and sleep with us.
21 If you refuse, we will bear witness against you, saying that a young man was with you and that is why you had sent out your servants.

23 But I would rather fall into their hands without having done anything than sin before the Lord.

25 and one of them ran to open the garden gate.

31 Susanna was a very delicate and beautiful woman,

33 All her relatives were crying, as was everyone who saw her.
34 The two elders stood up in the middle of the assembly and placed their hands on his head.
35 She, bathed in tears, raised her eyes to heaven, because her heart was full of trust in the Lord.

40 As for her, we seized her and asked her who this young man was,
41 but she didn't want to say it. We are witnesses of all of this. The assembly believed them because they were elders and judges of the people, and Susanna was sentenced to death.
42 But she cried out with a loud voice, "Everlasting God, you who know secrets, you who know all things before they come to pass,
43 You know that they have raised false testimony against me. "I am going to die without having done anything that their malice has plotted against me."
44 The Lord heard his voice:
45 When she was being led to death, she raised up the holy spirit of a young man named Daniel,

1 Genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham:
2 Abraham was the father of Isaac; Isaac, father of Jacob; Jacob, father of Judah and his brothers.
3 Judah was the father of Perez and Zarah, and their mother was Tamar. Perez was the father of Aram;
4 Aram, father of Amminadab; Aminadab, father of Naasón; Naasón, father of Salmon.
5 Salmon was the father of Boaz, and his mother was Rahab. Boaz was the father of Obed, and his mother was Ruth. Obed was the father of Jesse;
6 Jesse, father of King David. David was the father of Solomon, and his mother was the one who had been Uriah's wife.
7 Solomon was the father of Rehoboam; Rehoboam, father of Abijah; Abijah, father of Asa;
8 Asa, father of Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat, father of Jehoram; Joram, father of Ozias.
9 Uzziah was the father of Joatam; Joatam, father of Ahaz; Ahaz, father of Hezekiah;
10 Hezekiah, father of Manasseh. Manasseh was the father of Josiah;
11 Josiah, father of Jeconiah and his brothers, during the exile in Babylon.
12 After the exile in Babylon: Jeconiah became the father of Shealtiel; Shealtiel, father of Zerubbabel;
13 Zerubbabel, father of Abiud; Abiud, father of Eliacim; Eliacim, father of Azor.
14 Azor was the father of Zadok; Zadok, father of Achim; Akim, father of Eliud;
15 Eliud, father of Eleazar; Eleazar, father of Mattan; Matan, father of Jacob.
16 Jacob was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

17 The total number of generations is therefore: from Abraham to David, fourteen generations; from David to the exile in Babylon, fourteen generations; from exile in
Babylon to Christ, fourteen generations.

19 Joseph, her husband, who was a righteous man and did not want to denounce her publicly, decided to leave her secretly.

of the Holy Spirit.
