4 so that your alms may remain secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.

5 When you pray, do not do as the hypocrites do: they like to pray standing in the synagogues and on street corners, to be seen. I assure you that they already have their
reward.
6 But when you pray, go to your room, close the door, and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
7 When you pray, do not talk much, as the pagans do: they believe that if they talk much they will be heard.
8 Do not do as they do, because the Father in heaven knows well what you need before you ask him.
9 Pray this way: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be your Name,
10 May your Kingdom come, may your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
11 Give us this day our daily bread.
12 Forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who have trespassed against us.
13 Do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
14 If you forgive others their faults, your Father in heaven will also forgive you.
15 But if you do not forgive others, the Father will not forgive you either.

16 When you fast, do not make a sad face, as the hypocrites do, who disfigure their faces so that it can be seen that they are fasting. I assure you that with that, you have already received your reward.
17 But when you fast, perfume your head and wash your face,
18 so that your fast may not be known to men, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
19 Do not store up treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume them, and thieves break through the walls and steal them.
20 Instead, store up treasures in heaven, where there is no moth or rust to consume them, nor thieves to break in and steal.
21 Where your treasure is, your heart will be also.
22 The lamp of the body is the eye. If the eye is healthy, the whole body will be illuminated.
23 But if the eye is sick, the whole body will be in darkness. If the light that is in you is darkened, how much darkness there will be!
24 No one can serve two masters, because he will hate one and love the other, or he will be interested in the first and despise the second. You cannot serve God and Money.

25 Therefore I tell you: Do not worry about your life, thinking about what you will eat, or about your body, thinking about what you will wear. Is not life worth more than food and the body more than
dress?
26 Look at the birds of the air: they do not sow or reap, nor store up in barns, and yet the Father in heaven feeds them. Aren't you worth more than them?
27 Which of you, no matter how much he worries, can add a single moment to his life?
28 And why do you worry about the dress? Look at the lilies of the field, how they grow without toiling or weaving.
29 Truly I say to you, not even Solomon, in the splendor of his glory, was dressed like one of them.
30 If God thus clothes the grass of the fields, which exists today and tomorrow will be thrown into the fire, how much more will he do for you, O men of little faith!
31 Then do not worry, saying, "What shall we eat, or what shall we drink, or what shall we wear?"
32 It is the pagans who are after these things. The Father in heaven knows well that you need them.
33 Seek first the Kingdom and its righteousness, and everything else will be added to you.
34 Do not worry about tomorrow; Tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day is enough for its affliction.
1 Do not judge, lest you be judged.
2 For with the criterion with which you judge you will be judged, and the measure with which you measure will be used for you.
3 Why do you notice the speck that is in your brother's eye and do not notice the log that is in your own?
4 How can you say to your brother, “Let me take the speck out of your eye,” if there is a log in your eye?
5 Hypocrite, first take the plank out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
6 Do not give sacred things to dogs, nor throw your pearls to swine, lest they trample them and then turn against you and destroy you.
7 Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and it will be opened to you.
8 For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks, finds; and to him who knocks, it will be opened.
9 Which of you, when your son asks for bread, gives him a stone?
10 Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a snake?
11 If you, who are evil, know how to give good things to your children, how much more will the heavenly Father give good things to those who ask him!
12 As many as you wish others to do for you, do it for them: this is the Law and the Prophets.
13 Enter through the narrow gate, for the gate is wide and the way is broad that leads to destruction, and there are many who go there.
14 But the gate is narrow and the path that leads to Life is narrow, and there are few who find it.
15 Beware of false prophets, who appear covered in sheepskins, but inside they are ravenous wolves.
16 By their fruits you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thorns or figs from thistles?
17 Thus every good tree produces good fruit, and every bad tree produces bad fruit.
18 A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor can a bad tree produce good fruit.
19 A tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
20 By their fruits, then, you will recognize them.
21 It is not those who say to me, "Lord, Lord," who will enter the Kingdom of Heaven, but those who do the will of my Father in heaven.
22 Many will say to me on that day, “Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name? Did we not cast out demons and perform many miracles in your Name?
23 Then I will tell them: “I never knew you; Depart from me, you who do evil."
24 Thus, everyone who hears the words I have just said and puts them into practice can be compared to a sensible man who built his house on rock.
25 The rains fell, the torrents rushed, the winds blew and shook the house; but it did not collapse because it was built on rock.
26 On the contrary, he who listens to my words and does not do them can be compared to a foolish man who built his house on sand.
27 The rains fell, the torrents rushed, the winds blew and shook the house: it collapsed, and its ruin was great.
28 When Jesus finished saying these words, the crowd was amazed at his teaching,
29 because he taught them as one who had authority and not as his scribes.
1 When Jesus came down from the mountain, a large crowd followed him.
2 Then a leper came and bowed before him and said, "Lord, if you wish, you can purify me."
3 Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, "I want him, be cleansed." And immediately he was purified of his leprosy.
4 Jesus said to him, "Do not tell anyone, but go and present yourself to the priest and give the offering that Moses commanded as a testimony to them."
5 As he entered Capernaum, a centurion approached him, begging him.
6 "Sir, my servant is at home sick with paralysis and suffering terribly."
7 Jesus said to him, "I myself will go and heal him."
8 But the centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter my house; Just say a word and my servant will be healed.

9 For when I, who am but a junior officer, say to one of the soldiers under my command, "Go," he goes, and to another, "Come," he comes; and when I say to my servant: "You must
do this, he does it.
10 When Jesus heard this, he was amazed and said to those who followed him: “I tell you the truth, I have not found anyone in Israel who has such faith.
11 Therefore I tell you that many will come from the East and from the West, and will sit at table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, in the Kingdom of Heaven;
12 But the heirs of the kingdom will be thrown outside into darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
13 And Jesus said to the centurion, “Go, and let it happen as you have believed.” And the servant was cured at that very moment.
14 When Jesus arrived at Peter's house, he found his mother-in-law in bed with a fever.
15 He touched her hand and her fever went away. She got up and began to serve him.
16 In the evening, many demon-possessed people were brought to him, and he expelled the spirits with his word and healed all who were sick.
17 so that what had been announced by the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled: "He took our weaknesses and took our infirmities upon himself."
18 Seeing himself surrounded by so many people, Jesus ordered his disciples to cross to the other bank.
19 Then a scribe came to him and said, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
20 Jesus answered him, “The foxes have their holes and the birds of the air have their nests; but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head.
21 Another of his disciples said to him, "Lord, let me first go and bury my father."
22 But Jesus answered him, "Follow me, and let the dead bury their dead."
23 Then Jesus got into the boat and his disciples followed him.
24 Suddenly a storm broke out on the sea so great that the waves covered the boat. Meanwhile, Jesus slept.
25 Coming to him, his disciples woke him up, saying, “Save us, Lord, we are sinking!”
26 He answered them, "Why are you afraid, you of little faith?" And he got up and rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.
27 The men then said to each other, full of admiration: "Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?"

28 When Jesus reached the other side, to the region of the Gadarenes, two demon-possessed men coming out of the tombs met him. They were so ferocious, that no one could pass through that
way.
29 And they began to shout: “What do you want from us, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before our time?
30 At some distance there was a large herd of pigs grazing.
31 The demons begged Jesus, "If you are going to cast us out, send us to that herd."
32 He said to them, “Go.” They went out and entered the pigs: they rushed into the sea from the top of the cliff, and were drowned.
33 The caretakers fled and went to the city to bring the news of everything that had happened to the demon-possessed people.
34 The whole city came out to meet Jesus, and when they saw him, they begged him to leave their territory.
1 Jesus got into the boat, crossed the lake and returned to his city.
2 Then they brought him a paralyzed man lying on a stretcher. Seeing the faith of those men, Jesus said to the paralytic: "Be confident, son, your sins are forgiven."
3 Some scribes thought, “This man is blaspheming.
4 Jesus, reading their thoughts, said to them, “Why do you think evilly?
5 Which is easier to say: "Your sins are forgiven you," or "Get up and walk"?
6 So that you may know that the Son of Man has the power on earth to forgive sins - he said to the paralytic - get up, take your mat and go home.
7 He got up and went home.
8 When the crowd saw this, they were afraid and glorified God for having given such power to men.
9 As Jesus left there, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax collection table, and said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him.
10 While Jesus was eating in the house, many tax collectors and sinners came and sat down to eat with him and his disciples.
11 When the Pharisees saw this, they said to the disciples, "Why does your Master eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
12 Jesus, who had heard, answered: “It is not the healthy who need the doctor, but the sick.
13 Go and learn what it means: I want mercy and not sacrifices. For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.
14 Then John's disciples came and said to him, "Why don't your disciples fast, as we and the Pharisees do?"
15 Jesus answered them, “Can the bridegroom's friends be sad while the bridegroom is with them? The time will come when the husband will be taken from them, and then they will fast.
16 No one uses a piece of new material to mend an old garment, because the added piece pulls on the garment and the tear becomes larger.

17 Nor do you put new wine into old wineskins, because the wineskins burst, the wine is spilled, and the wineskins are lost. No, new wine is put into new wineskins, and so both are
they preserve!
18 While Jesus was telling them these things, a high leader came and fell down before him and said, "Lord, my daughter has just died, but come lay your hand on her and she will live."
19 Jesus got up and followed him with his disciples.
20 Then a woman who had been suffering from hemorrhages for twelve years came up behind him and touched the fringes of his cloak.
21 thinking, "If I just touch his cloak, I will be healed."
22 Jesus turned around, and when he saw her, he said to her, "Be confident, daughter, your faith has saved you." And from that moment the woman was cured.
23 When he arrived at the chief's house, Jesus saw those playing funeral music and people shouting, and he said,
24 "Retreat, the girl is not dead, but sleeps." And they laughed at him.
25 When they had sent the people out, he went in, took her by the hand, and she stood up.
26 And this news spread throughout that region.
27 When Jesus left, two blind men followed him, shouting, "Have mercy on us, Son of David."
28 When he arrived at the house, the blind men approached him and he asked them, "Do you believe that I can do what you ask of me?" They answered him: "Yes, Lord."
29 Jesus touched their eyes, saying, "Let it happen as you have believed."
30 And their eyes were opened. Then Jesus warned them: “Be careful! Let no one know."
31 But as soon as they left, they spread their fame throughout that region.
32 As soon as the blind men left, they presented him with a mute man who was demon-possessed.
33 The demon was cast out and the mute began to speak. The crowd, amazed, commented: "Nothing like it has ever been seen in Israel."
34 But the Pharisees said, "He casts out demons by the Prince of demons."
35 Jesus traveled through all the cities and towns, teaching in the synagogues, proclaiming the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing all diseases and illnesses.
36 When he saw the crowds, he had compassion, because they were weary and downcast, like sheep without a shepherd.
37 Then he said to his disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
38 Ask the owner of the fields to send workers for the harvest.
1 Jesus called together his twelve disciples and gave them the power to cast out impure spirits and to cure any illness or disease.
2 The names of the twelve Apostles are: first, Simon, surnamed Peter, and his brother Andrew; then, James, son of Zebedee, and his brother John;
3 Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew, the publican; Santiago, son of Alfeo, and Thaddeus;
4 Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, the same one who betrayed him.
5 Jesus sent these Twelve with the following instructions: “Do not go to pagan regions, nor enter any city of the Samaritans.
6 Go instead to the lost sheep of the people of Israel.
7 Along the way, proclaim that the Kingdom of Heaven is near.
8 Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons. You have received freely, give also freely.
9 Do not carry gold or silver or coins on you,
10 nor provisions for the journey, nor two tunics, nor shoes, nor staff; because he who works deserves his livelihood.
11 When you enter a city or a town, look for some respectable person and stay in his house until it is time to leave.
12 As you enter the house, greet it, invoking peace upon it.
13 If that house deserves it, may peace descend upon it; but if it is unworthy, may that peace return to you.
14 And if they do not receive you or want to listen to your words, when you leave that house or that city, shake off the dust from your feet.
15 I tell you, on the day of judgment, Sodom and Gomorrah will be treated less harshly than that city.
16 I send you out like sheep in the midst of wolves: then be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.
17 Beware of men, for they will hand you over to the courts and flog you in the synagogues.
18 Because of me, they will be brought before governors and kings, to testify before them and before the pagans.
19 When you are handed over, do not worry about how you will speak or what you will say: what you are to say will be made known to you at that time,
20 for it will not be you who will speak, but the Spirit of your Father will speak in you.
21 A brother shall hand over his brother to be put to death, and a father his son; The children will rebel against their parents and cause them to die.
22 You will be hated by all because of my Name, but he who endures to the end will be saved.

23 When they persecute you in one city, flee to another, and if they persecute you in this one, flee to a third. I assure you that you will not finish exploring the cities of Israel before the Son of God arrives.
man.
24 The disciple is not more than the teacher nor the servant more than his master.
25 It is enough for the disciple to be like his teacher and for the servant to be like his master. If they called the owner of the house Beelzebul, how much more so those in his house!
26 Do not fear them. There is nothing hidden that should not be revealed, and nothing secret that should not be known.
27 What I say to you in the dark, repeat it in broad daylight; and whatever you hear in your ear, proclaim it from the tops of your houses.
28 Do not fear those who kill the body, but cannot kill the soul. Rather fear him who can throw soul and body into Gehenna.
29 Can't you sell a couple of birds for a few coins? However, not a single one of them falls to the ground, without the consent of the Father who is in heaven.
30 You have counted all your hairs.
31 Do not fear then, for you are worth more than many birds.
32 Whoever acknowledges me openly before men, I will acknowledge before my Father who is in heaven.
33 But I will deny before my Father who is in heaven anyone who denies me before men.
34 Do not think that I have come to bring peace on earth. I did not come to bring peace, but the sword.
35 For I have come to confront the son with his father, the daughter with her mother, and the daughter-in-law with her mother-in-law;
36 and so a man will have those of his own household as enemies.
37 He who loves his father or his mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he who loves his son or his daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
38 He who does not take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me.
39 He who finds his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for me will find it.
40 He who receives you receives me; and he who receives me, receives him who sent me.
41 He who receives a prophet because he is a prophet will have the reward of a prophet; and he who receives a righteous man will have a righteous man's reward.
42 I tell you the truth, whoever gives one of these little ones a drink of even a glass of fresh water because he is my disciple will not go unrewarded."
1 When Jesus finished giving these instructions to his twelve disciples, he left from there to teach and preach in the cities of the region.
2 John the Baptist heard in prison about the works of Christ, and he sent two of his disciples to ask him:
3 "Are you the one who is to come or should we wait for another?"
4 Jesus answered them, “Go tell John what you hear and see:
5 the blind see and the paralyzed walk; lepers are purified and the deaf hear; The dead are resurrected and the Good News is announced to the poor.
6 And happy is he to whom I am not a cause of scandal!
7 As John's messengers were leaving, Jesus began to speak about him to the crowd, saying, “What did you go to the desert to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
8 What did they go to see? A man dressed with refinement? Those who dress that way live in the palaces of kings.
9 What did they go to see then? A prophet? I assure you that yes, and more than a prophet.
10 He is the one of whom it is written: "I send my messenger before you to prepare the way for you."
11 Truly I say to you, no greater man has been born than John the Baptist; and yet the least in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he.
12 From the time of John the Baptist until now, the Kingdom of Heaven is violently fought, and the violent try to take it away.
13 For all the Prophets, as well as the Law, have prophesied until John.
14 And if you want to create me, he is that Elijah who must return.
15 He who has ears, let him hear!
16 Who can I compare this generation to? He looks like those boys who, sitting in the square, shout to others:
17 “We played the flute for you, and you didn't dance! We sang dirges, and they did not cry!
18 Because John came, who neither eats nor drinks, and you say, "He has lost his mind!"
19 The Son of Man came, eating and drinking, and they say, "He is a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners." But Wisdom has been justified by his works.
20 Then Jesus began to reproach those cities where he had performed the most miracles, because they had not converted.

21 “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed among you had been done in Tire and Sidon, you would have converted long ago, putting on sackcloth and covering yourself.
with ash.
22 I assure you that on the day of Judgment, Tire and Sidon will be treated less harshly than you.

23 And you, Capernaum, do you think you will be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be rushed to hell. For if the miracles performed in you had been done in Sodom, that city would still
would exist.
24 I tell you the truth, on the day of judgment the land of Sodom will be treated less harshly than you.
25 On that occasion, Jesus said: “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, for having hidden these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them to little ones.
26 Yes, Father, because you have wanted it that way.
27 Everything has been given to me by my Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, just as no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.
28 Come to me, all you who are afflicted and burdened, and I will give you relief.
29 Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am patient and humble of heart, and thus you will find relief.
30 For my yoke is easy and my burden is light.
1 At that time, Jesus was passing through some fields and it was a Sabbath day. As his disciples felt hungry, they began to pluck and eat the ears.
2 When the Pharisees saw this, they said to him, "Look, your disciples are doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath."
3 But he answered them, "Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
4 How did he enter the House of God and eat the loaves of the offering, which neither he nor his companions were allowed to eat, but only the priests?
5 And have you not also read in the Law that the priests, in the Temple, violate the Sabbath rest, without incurring a fault?
6 Now I tell you that here is someone greater than the Temple.
7 If they had understood what it means: I want mercy and not sacrifices, they would not condemn the innocent.
8 For the Son of Man is master of the Sabbath.
9 From there Jesus went to the synagogue of the Pharisees,
10 where there was a man who had a paralyzed hand. In order to accuse him, they asked him: "Is it permissible to heal on the Sabbath?"
11 He said to them, "Which of you, if you have just one sheep and it falls into a well on the Sabbath, will not take it out?"
12 How much more valuable is a man than a sheep! Therefore, it is permissible to do a good deed on the Sabbath.”
13 Then he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He extended it, and the sick hand remained as healthy as the other.
14 Immediately the Pharisees came out and conspired to find a way to put an end to him.
15 When Jesus heard this, he left there. Many followed him, and he healed them all.
16 But he sternly ordered them not to make it known,
17 so that what was announced by the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled:
18 "This is my servant, whom I have chosen, my beloved, on whom I have chosen. I will pour out my Spirit on him and he will announce justice to the nations.
19 He will not argue or shout, and no one will hear his voice in the streets.
20 He will not break the bent reed and will not quench the smoldering wick, until he makes justice triumph;
21 and the nations will put hope in his name."
22 Then they brought to him a blind and mute demon-possessed man, and Jesus healed him, giving him speech and sight.
23 The crowd was amazed and said, "Could this not be the Son of David?"
24 The Pharisees, hearing this, said, "This man casts out demons by the power of Beelzebul, the Prince of demons."
25 Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “A kingdom where there is internal strife is going to ruin; and a divided city or family cannot survive.
26 Now if Satan casts out Satan, he fights against himself; So how can his kingdom survive?
27 And if I drive out demons by the power of Beelzebul, by what power do your disciples drive them out? Therefore, you will have them as judges.
28 But if I drive out demons by the power of the Spirit of God, it means that the Kingdom of God has come to you.
29 Can anyone enter a strong man's house and steal his things unless he first ties him up? Only then can he loot the house.
30 He who is not with me is against me; and he who does not gather with me scatters.
31 Therefore I tell you that every sin or blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
32 Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven; But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven either in this world or in the future.
33 Suppose the tree is good: the fruit will also be good. Suppose the tree is bad: the fruit will also be bad. Because the tree is known by its fruit.
34 Breed of vipers, how can you say good things when you are evil? Because the mouth speaks of the abundance of the heart.
35 A good man brings out good things from his treasure of goodness; and the evil man brings out evil things from his treasury of evil.
36 But I say to you, on the day of Judgment, men will give an account for every vain word they have spoken.
37 For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.
38 Then some scribes and Pharisees said to him, “Teacher, we want you to show us a sign.”
39 He answered them, “This wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but no other sign will be given to it than that of the prophet Jonah.
40 For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the fish, so will the Son of Man be in the bosom of the earth three days and three nights.

41 On the Day of Judgment, the men of Nineveh will rise up against this generation and condemn it, because they were converted by the preaching of Jonah, and here is someone who is
more than Jonah.

42 On the day of Judgment, the Queen of the South will rise against this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and here is
someone who is more than Solomon.
43 When the unclean spirit goes out of a man, it wanders through deserted places in search of rest, and when it does not find it,
44 thinks: "I will return to my house, where I came from." When he arrives, he finds it empty, swept and tidy.

45 Then he goes to look for seven other spirits worse than himself; They come and settle there. And in the end, that man feels worse than at the beginning. This is what will happen with this generation
evil."
46 He was still speaking to the crowd when his mother and brothers, who were outside, tried to talk to him.
47 Someone said to him, "Your mother and your brothers are out there and they want to talk to you."
48 Jesus answered her, "Who is my mother and who are my brothers?"
49 And pointing with his hand to his disciples, he added: “These are my mother and my brothers.
50 For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother, my sister, and my mother.
1 That day, Jesus left the house and sat on the seashore.
2 A large crowd gathered around him, so he had to get into a boat and sit in it, while the crowd remained on the shore.
3 Then he spoke to them at length in parables. He told them: «The sower went out to sow.
4 As he scattered the seeds, some fell on the roadside and the birds ate them.
5 Others fell on rocky ground, where there was not much soil, and they sprang up immediately, because the soil was shallow;
6 But when the sun rose, they were scorched, and for lack of root, they withered.
7 Others fell among thorns, and these, as they grew, choked them.
8 Others fell on good ground and bore fruit: some a hundred, some sixty, some thirty.
9 He who has ears, let him hear!
10 The disciples came and said to him, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”
11 He answered them, “It has been given to you to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven, but not to them.
12 For to him who has, more will be given and he will have abundance, but from him who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
13 Therefore I speak to you in parables: because they look and do not see, they hear and do not listen or understand.
14 And thus the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled in them, which says: "No matter how much they hear, they will not understand, no matter how much they see, they will not know,

15 Because the heart of this people is hardened, they have stopped their ears and closed their eyes, so that their eyes do not see, and their ears do not hear, and their heart does not understand, and they do not know.
convert, and I will not heal them."
16 But happy are your eyes, because they see; happy are their ears, because they hear.
17 Truly I say to you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see and did not see it, to hear what you hear but did not hear it.
18 Listen, then, to what the parable of the sower means.
19 When someone hears the Word of the Kingdom and does not understand it, the Evil One comes and snatches away what had been sown in his heart: this is the one who received the seed by the wayside.
20 The one who receives it on rocky ground is the man who, upon hearing the Word, immediately accepts it with joy,
21 but he does not allow it to take root, because it is fickle: as soon as tribulation or persecution occurs because of the Word, it immediately succumbs.
22 He who receives the seed among thorns is the man who hears the Word, but the worries of the world and the seduction of riches choke it, and it cannot bear fruit.
23 And the one who receives it on fertile land is the man who hears the Word and understands it. This one produces fruit, either a hundred, or sixty, or thirty times one."
24 And he proposed another parable to them: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field;
25 But while everyone was sleeping their enemy came, sowed tares among the wheat, and left.
26 When the wheat grew and the ears appeared, the tares also appeared.
27 The laborers then went to the owner and said to him, “Sir, hadn't you sown good seed in your field? How come there are tares in it now?
28 He answered them, "Some enemy has done this." The laborers replied: "Do you want us to go and tear it out?"
29 “No,” the owner told them, “because by uprooting the tares, you are in danger of uprooting the wheat as well.

30 Let them grow together until the harvest, and then I will say to the harvesters: First uproot the tares and tie them in bundles to burn them, and then gather the wheat in my

ready: Come to the weddings".

Well-disposed people.

3 He then began to travel around the entire region of the Jordan River, announcing a baptism of conversion for the forgiveness of sins,
4 as it is written in the book of the prophet Isaiah: "A voice cries in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make straight his paths.
5 The valleys will be filled, the mountains and the hills will be made flat. Winding paths will be straightened and uneven paths leveled.
6 Then all men will see the Salvation of God."
7 John said to the crowd that came to be baptized by him: “Breed of vipers, who taught you to escape the approaching wrath of God?
8 Produce the fruits of a sincere conversion, and do not think: "We have Abraham as our father." For I tell you that from these stones God can raise up the son of Abraham.
9 The ax is already laid at the root of the trees; "The tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire."
10 The people asked him, “What should we do then?”
11 He answered them, “Whoever has two tunics, give one to him who has none; and whoever has something to eat, let him do the same.
12 Some tax collectors also came to have him baptized and asked him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
13 He answered them, "Do not demand more than what is stipulated."
14 Some soldiers asked him, “What should we do?” Juan replied: "Do not extort anyone, do not make false complaints and be content with your salary."
15 As the people were in expectation and everyone was wondering if John was not the Messiah,

16 He spoke and said to them, “I baptize you with water, but one who is more powerful than I is coming, and I am not even worthy to untie the strap of his sandals; he will baptize them in the
Holy Spirit and in the fire.
17 He has the fork in his hand to clean his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his barn. But he will consume the chaff in the unquenchable fire."
18 And through many other exhortations, he announced the Good News to the people.
19 Meanwhile Herod the tetrarch, whom John blamed because of Herodias, his brother's wife, and because of all the crimes she had committed,
20 he committed one more by having Juan imprisoned.
21 All the people were baptized, and Jesus was also baptized. And while he was praying, heaven opened.
22 and the Holy Spirit descended on him in bodily form, like a dove. Then a voice was heard from heaven: "You are my very dear Son, in whom I have placed all my predilection."
23 When Jesus began his ministry, he was about thirty years old and was considered the son of Joseph. Joseph was the son of Eli;
24 Eli son of Mattath; Matah, son of Levi; Levi, son of Melchi; Melki, son of Hanai; Janai, son of Joseph;
25 Joseph, son of Mattathias; Mattathias, son of Amos; Amos, son of Naum; Naum, son of Esli; Eslí, son of Nagai;
26 Nagai, son of Maat; Maat, son of Mattathias; Mattathias, son of Shemein; Shemein, son of Yoshek; Iosek, son of Iodah;
27 Yoda, son of Joanan; Joanan, son of Rezah; Resah, son of Zerubbabel. Zerubbabel was the son of Shealtiel; Salatiel, son of Neri;
28 Neri, son of Melchi; Melqui, son of Adi; Adi, son of Cosam; Cosam, son of Elmadam; Elmadam, son of Er;
29 Er, son of Jesus; Jesus, son of Eliezer; Eliezer, son of Jorim; Jorim, son of Matat; Matat, son of Levi;
30 Levi, son of Angel; Angel, son of Judah; Judah, son of Joseph; Joseph, son of Jonam; Jonam, son of Eliakim;
31 Eliakim son of Meleah; Meleah, son of Menah; Menah, son of Matatá; Matatah, son of Nathan; Nathan, son of David.
32 David was the son of Jesse; Jesse, son of Jobed; Jobed, son of Boaz; Boaz, son of Shelah; Shelah son of Nahshon;
33 Nahshon son of Amminadab; Aminadab, son of Admin; Admin, son of Arni; Arni, son of Esrom; Esrom, son of Perez; Phares, son of Judah;
34 Judah, son of Jacob; Jacob, son of Isaac; Isaac, son of Abraham. Abraham was the son of Terah; Terah, son of Nahor;
35 Nahor, son of Seruch; Serúj, son of Ragau; Ragau, son of Peleg; Peleg, son of Eber; Eber, son of Shelah;
36 Shelah son of Cainan; Cainan, son of Arphaxad; Arphaxad, son of Shem. Shem was the son of Noah; Noah, son of Lamech;
37 Lamech, son of Methuselah; Methuselah, son of Enoch; Enoch, son of Jareth; Jareth, son of Malaleel; Malaleel, son of Cainan;
38 Cainan, son of Enos; Enos, son of Seth; Seth, son of Adam; Adam, son of God.
1 Jesus, filled with the Holy Spirit, returned from the banks of the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,
2 where he was tempted by the devil for forty days. He did not eat anything during those days, and at the end of them he was hungry.
3 The demon then said to him: "If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread."
4 But Jesus answered him, "The Scripture says, 'Man does not live by bread alone.'"
5 Then the demon took him to a higher place, showed him in an instant all the kingdoms of the earth
6 and said to him, “I will give you all this power and splendor of these kingdoms, because they have been handed over to me, and I give them to whomever I will.
7 If you bow down before me, all that will belong to you.
8 But Jesus answered him, "It is written, 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only you shall worship.'"
9 Then the demon took him to Jerusalem, put him on the highest part of the Temple and said to him: "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here,
10 because it is written: "He will give orders to his angels so that they will take care of you."
11 And also: "They will carry you in their hands so that your foot does not strike against any stone."
12 But Jesus answered him, "It is written, 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'"
13 Once all forms of temptation had been exhausted, the demon left him until the opportune time.
14 Jesus returned to Galilee with the power of the Spirit, and his fame spread throughout the region.
15 He taught in the synagogues and everyone praised him.
16 Jesus went to Nazareth, where he had grown up; On Saturday he entered the synagogue as usual and stood up to read.
17 They presented him with the book of the prophet Isaiah and, opening it, he found the passage where it was written:

18 "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has consecrated me by anointing. He sent me to bring Good News to the poor, to announce deliverance to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to
give freedom to the oppressed
19 and proclaim a year of favor from the Lord."
20 Jesus closed the Book, returned it to the helper and sat down. Everyone in the synagogue had their eyes fixed on him.
21 Then he began to say to them, “Today this passage of Scripture that you have just heard has been fulfilled.”
22 Everyone testified in his favor and was filled with admiration for the gracious words that came out of his mouth. And they said, "Is this not Joseph's son?"

23 But he answered them, "No doubt you will quote to me the proverb: 'Physician, heal yourself.' Also carry out here, in your homeland, everything that we have heard that happened in
Capernaum.
24 Then he added, “I tell you the truth, no prophet is welcomed in his own land.
25 Truly I say to you, there were many widows in Israel in the time of Elijah, when there was no rain from heaven for three years and six months and famine struck the entire land.
26 However, Elijah was not sent to any of them, except to a widow in Zarephath, in the country of Sidon.
27 There were also many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, but none of them was healed except Naaman the Syrian.
28 When everyone in the synagogue heard these words, they were furious.
29 And they got up and pushed him out of the city to a steep place on the hill on which the city stood, intending to throw him off the cliff.
30 But Jesus passed through their midst and continued on his way.
31 Jesus went down to Capernaum, a city in Galilee, and taught on the Sabbaths.
32 And everyone was amazed at his teaching, because he spoke with authority.
33 In the synagogue there was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon; and began to scream loudly;
34 «What do you want from us, Jesus of the Nazarene? Have you come to finish us off? I already know who you are: the Holy One of God.
35 But Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Shut up and get out of this man.” The demon came out of him, throwing him to the ground in the middle of everyone. without doing any harm.
36 Fear took hold of everyone, and they said to each other, “What does his word mean? Command the impure spirits with authority and power, and they come out!
37 And his fame spread everywhere in that region.
38 When he left the synagogue, he entered Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law had a high fever, and they asked him to do something for her.
39 Leaning over her, Jesus rebuked the fever and it disappeared. Immediately, she got up and began to serve them.
40 In the evening, all those who had sick people with various ailments were brought away, and he laid his hands on each of them and healed them.
41 Demons came out of many, shouting, “You are the Son of God!” But he rebuked them and did not let them speak, because they knew he was the Messiah.
42 When it was morning, Jesus left and went to a deserted place. The crowd began to look for him, and when they found him, they wanted to hold him back so that he would not go away from them.
43 But he said to them, "I must also announce the Good News of the Kingdom of God to the other cities, because that is why I have been sent."
44 And he preached in the synagogues of all Judea.
1 On one occasion, the crowd was gathering around Jesus to hear the Word of God, and he was standing on the shore of the Lake of Gennesaret.
2 From there he saw two boats by the shore of the lake; The fishermen had come down and were cleaning their nets.
3 Jesus got into one of the boats, which belonged to Simon, and asked him to move a little away from the shore; Then he sat down and taught the crowd from the boat.
4 When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, "Sail out into the deep, and let down your nets."
5 Simon answered him, "Master, we worked all night and got nothing, but if you say so, I will let down the nets."
6 They did so, and they caught such a quantity of fish that the nets were about to break.
7 Then they signaled to the companions in the other boat to come and help them. They came and filled the two boats so much that they were almost sinking.
8 When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus' feet and said to him, "Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinner."
9 Fear had taken hold of him and those who accompanied him, because of the number of fish they had collected;
10 And the same thing happened to James and John, sons of Zebedee, companions of Simon. But Jesus said to Simon: "Do not be afraid, from now on you will be a fisher of men."
11 They docked the boats on the shore and, abandoning everything, followed him.
12 While Jesus was in a city, a man covered with leprosy appeared. Seeing Jesus, he fell down before him and begged him, "Lord, if you want, you can purify me."
13 Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, "I want him, be cleansed." And immediately the leprosy disappeared.
14 He ordered him not to tell anyone, but added: "Go present yourself to the priest and give the offering that Moses commanded for your purification, so that it may serve as a testimony to them."
15 His fame spread more and more and large crowds came to hear him and be cured of their illnesses.
16 But he withdrew to desert places to pray.

17 One day, while Jesus was teaching, there were among those present some Pharisees and doctors of the Law, who had come from all the regions of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. The
strength of the Lord gave him power to heal.
18 Then some people arrived carrying a paralyzed man on a stretcher and were looking for a way in to take him to Jesus.

19 Since they did not know where to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up to the terrace and, from the roof, they lowered him with his stretcher into the middle of the crowd and placed him before Jesus.
20 Seeing his faith, Jesus said to him, “Man, your sins are forgiven.”
21 The scribes and the Pharisees began to ask, “Who is this blasphemer? Who can forgive sins, but only God?
22 But Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “What are you thinking?
23 Which is easier to say, "Your sins are forgiven," or "Get up and walk"?
24 "So that you may know that the Son of Man has the power on earth to forgive sins," he said to the paralytic, "I command you, get up, take up your mat and return to your house."
25 Immediately he got up in the sight of everyone, took his mat and went home praising God.
26 Everyone was amazed and glorified God, saying with great fear, "Today we have seen wonderful things."
27 Then Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax collection table, and he said to him, “Follow me.”
28 Leaving everything, he got up and followed him.
29 Levi offered Jesus a great banquet in his house. There were numerous publicans and other people who were at table with them.
30 The Pharisees and the scribes murmured and said to Jesus' disciples, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
31 But Jesus spoke up and said to them, “It is not the healthy who need the doctor, but the sick.
32 "I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance."
33 Then they said to him, “The disciples of John fast frequently and pray, just as the disciples of the Pharisees do; But yours eat and drink.
34 Jesus answered them, “Are you planning to make the bridegroom's friends fast while he is with them?
35 The time will come when the husband will be taken away from them; then they will have to fast.
36 He also made this comparison to them: “No one cuts a piece of a new garment to mend an old one, because the new one will be torn, and the piece taken from it will not fit the old garment.
37 Nor do you put wine into old wineskins, because it will burst the wineskins; then the wine will be spilled and the wineskins will no longer be useful.
38 New wine, new wineskins!
39 No one, after having tasted old wine, wants new wine, because they say: The old is better.
1 One Sabbath, when Jesus was passing through some fields, his disciples plucked ears of grain and, rubbing them between their hands, ate them.
2 Some Pharisees said to them, "Why do you do what is not permitted on the Sabbath?"
3 Jesus answered them, "Haven't you even read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
4 How he entered the House of God and, taking the loaves of the offering, which only priests may eat, did he eat and feed his companions?
5 Then he said to them, "The Son of Man owns the Sabbath."
6 On another Sabbath, he entered the synagogue and began to teach. There was a man there whose right hand was paralyzed.
7 The scribes and the Pharisees watched Jesus carefully to see if he would heal on the Sabbath, because they wanted to find something to accuse him of.
8 But Jesus, knowing their intentions, said to the man whose hand was withered, "Get up and stand before everyone." He got up and remained standing.
9 Then he said to them, "I ask you: Is it permissible on the Sabbath to do good or evil, to save a life or to lose it?"
10 And looking at everyone, he said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He stretched it out and his hand was healed.
11 But they were angry, and they deliberated among themselves to see what they could do against Jesus.
12 In those days, Jesus retired to a mountain to pray, and spent the whole night in prayer with God.
13 When it was day, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, to whom he gave the name Apostles:
14 Simon, whom he called Peter, Andrew, his brother, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew,
15 Matthew, Thomas, James, son of Alphaeus, Simon, called the Zealot,
16 Judas, son of James and Judas Iscariot, who was the traitor.

17 As he went down with them, he stopped on a plain. Many of his disciples were there, as well as a large crowd that had come from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the surrounding region.
coast of Tire and Sidon,
18 to listen to him and be cured of his illnesses. Those who were tormented by impure spirits were healed;
19 and all the people wanted to touch him, because a force came out of him that healed everyone.
20 Then Jesus, looking at his disciples, said, “Blessed are you poor, for the Kingdom of God belongs to you!
21 Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be satisfied! Happy are you, those who cry now, because you will laugh!
22 Blessed are you, when men hate you, exclude you, insult you, and outlaw you, considering you vile, and banishing you, considering you disgraceful because of the Son of Man!
23 Rejoice and be filled with joy on that day, for your reward will be great in heaven. The same way their fathers treated the prophets!
24 But woe to you who are rich, for you already have your consolation!
25 Woe to you who are now satisfied, for you will be hungry! Woe to you who laugh now, for you will know affliction and tears!
26 Woe to you when everyone praises you! In the same way their fathers restrain false prophets!
27 But I say to you who hear me: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you.
28 Bless those who curse you, pray for those who slander you.
29 To him who strikes you on one cheek, turn the other also; Whoever takes your cloak, do not deny him your tunic.
30 Give to everyone who asks you, and do not ask back from anyone who takes yours.
31 For the rest, do what you want men to do for you.
32 If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Because even sinners love those who love them.
33 If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Sinners do that too.
34 And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Sinners also lend to sinners, to receive the same from them.

35 Love your enemies, do good and lend without expecting anything in return. Then your reward will be great and you will be children of the Most High, because he is good to the
ungrateful and bad.
36 Be merciful, as your Father is merciful.
37 Do not judge and you will not be judged; do not condemn and you will not be condemned; forgive and you will be forgiven.
38 Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure will be poured onto their laps, pressed, shaken and overflowing. For the measure with which you measure will also be used for you.
39 He also made this comparison to them: “Can a blind man guide another blind man? Won't they both fall into a well?
40 The disciple is not superior to the teacher; When the disciple becomes perfect, he will be like his teacher.
41 Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye and do not see the beam in your own eye?

42 How can you say to your brother, "Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye," you, who do not see the beam in your eye? Hypocrite, first take the plank out of your eye, and then
You will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye.
43 There is no good tree that bears bad fruit, nor bad tree that bears good fruit:
44 each tree is recognized by its fruit. Figs are not gathered from thorns nor grapes harvested from brambles.
45 The good man draws good from the treasure of goodness that he has in his heart. The evil one brings out evil from evil, because out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
46 Why do you call me, "Lord, Lord," and do not do what I tell you?
47 I will tell you who everyone who comes to me and listens to my words and practices them is like.

48 It is like a man who, wanting to build a house, dug deep and laid the foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the waters rushed with force against that house,
but they could not tear it down, because it was well built.

49 But he who hears the Word and does not put it into practice is like a man who built his house on the ground, without a foundation. When the waters rushed against her, she immediately
collapsed, and the disaster that befell that house was great.
1 When Jesus finished saying all these things to the people, he entered Capernaum.
2 There was a centurion there who had a sick servant, about to die, whom he loved very much.
3 When he had heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to beg him to come and heal his servant.
4 When they were near Jesus, they begged him earnestly, saying, "He deserves this favor from you,
5 because he loves our nation and has built the synagogue for us.
6 Jesus went with them, and when he was near the house, the centurion sent word to him through some friends: “Lord, do not be troubled, for I am not worthy that you should enter my house;
7 That's why I didn't consider myself worthy of going to see you personally. Just say one word and my servant will be healed.

8 For I, who am but a junior officer, but have soldiers under my command, when I say to one, "Go," he goes; and to another: "Come," he comes; and when I say to me
servant: "You have to do this!", he does it.
9 When Jesus heard these words, he was amazed at him and, turning to the crowd that followed him, he said, "I tell you the truth, not even in Israel have I found such faith."
10 When the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant completely healthy.
11 Immediately Jesus went to a city called Naim, accompanied by his disciples and a large crowd.
12 Just as she approached the city gate, the only son of a widowed woman was being buried, and many local people accompanied her.
13 When the Lord saw her, he was moved and said to her, "Do not cry."
14 Then he approached and touched the coffin. Those who were carrying them stopped and Jesus said: "Young man, I command you, get up."
15 The dead man sat up and began to speak. And Jesus gave him to his mother.
16 Everyone was overcome with fear and praised God, saying, "A great prophet has appeared among us and God has visited his people."
17 The rumor of what Jesus had just done spread throughout Judea and throughout the surrounding region.
18 John was informed of all this by his disciples, and calling two of them,
19 He sent them to say to the Lord, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?"
20 When they appeared before him, they said to him, "John the Baptist sent us to ask you, 'Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?'"
21 On that occasion, Jesus healed many people of their illnesses, diseases, and evil spirits, and restored sight to many blind people.

22 Then he answered the messengers: "Go tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind see, the paralyzed walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the
The dead are raised, the Good News is announced to the poor.
23 And happy is he to whom I am not a cause of scandal!
24 When John's messengers left, Jesus began to speak about him to the crowd, saying, “What did you go out to see in the wilderness? A reed shaken by the wind?
25 What did they go out to see? A man dressed with refinement? Those who wear sumptuous clothing and live in opulence are in the palaces of kings.
26 What did they go out to see then? A prophet? I assure you that yes, and more than a prophet.
27 He is the one of whom it is written: I send my messenger before you to prepare the way for you.
28 Truly I say to you, there is no man greater than John, and yet the least in the Kingdom of God is greater than him.
29 All the people who heard him, including the publicans, recognized the righteousness of God, receiving the baptism of John.
30 But the Pharisees and the doctors of the Law, by not being baptized by him, frustrated God's plan for them.
31 «With whom can I compare the men of this generation? Who do they look like?

32 They are like those boys who sit in the square and say to each other, "We played the flute for you, and you did not dance! We sang funeral songs, and you did not dance."
They cried!"
33 Because John the Baptist came, who neither eats bread nor drinks wine, and you say, "He has lost his mind!"
34 The Son of Man came, eating and drinking, and they say, "He is a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!"
35 But Wisdom has been recognized as righteous by all her children.
36 A Pharisee invited Jesus to eat with him. Jesus entered the house and sat down at the table.
37 Then a sinful woman who lived in the city, hearing that Jesus was eating in the Pharisee's house, came with a bottle of perfume.
38 And standing behind him, she began to weep at his feet and began to bathe them with her tears; She dried them with her hair, covered them with kisses and anointed them with perfume.
39 When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he thought, "If this man were a prophet, he would know who the woman touching him is and what she is: a sinner!"
40 But Jesus said to him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” «Say, Master!, he replied.
41 “A moneylender had two debtors: one owed him five hundred denarii, the other fifty.
42 Since they had nothing to pay, he forgave both of their debts. Which of the two will love more?
43 Simon answered, "I think the one he forgave the most." Jesus said to him: "You have judged well."

44 And turning to the woman, he said of Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered your house and you did not pour water on my feet; Instead, she bathed them with her tears and wiped them with
their hair.
45 You did not kiss me; She, however, since I entered, has not stopped kissing my feet.
46 You did not anoint my head; She poured perfume on my feet.
47 That is why I tell you that his sins, his many sins, have been forgiven because he has shown much love. But he who is forgiven little, shows little love.
48 Then he said to the woman, “Your sins are forgiven.”
49 The guests thought, "Who is this man, who goes so far as to forgive sins?"
50 But Jesus said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you, go in peace.”
1 Afterwards, Jesus toured the cities and towns, preaching and announcing the Good News of the Kingdom of God. The Twelve accompanied him
2 and also some women who had been healed of evil spirits and diseases: Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out;
3 Joanna, wife of Cusa, Herod's steward, Susanna and many others, who helped them with their goods.
4 As a large crowd gathered and people from all the cities came to Jesus, he said to them, using a parable:
5 «The sower went out to sow his seed. While sowing, some of the seed fell to the side of the road, where it was trampled and eaten by the birds of the sky.
6 Another part fell on the stones and, as it sprang up, it withered for lack of moisture.
7 Another fell among the thorns, and they sprang up at the same time and choked it.
8 Another part fell on fertile ground, sprouted and produced fruit a hundredfold. And once he had said this, he exclaimed: "He who has ears to hear, let him hear!"
9 His disciples asked him what this parable meant,

10 and Jesus said to them, “It has been given to you to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of God; The rest, however, are spoken in parables, so that they look without seeing and hear without
understand.
11 The parable means this: The seed is the Word of God.
12 Those who are on the side of the way are those who listen, but then the devil comes and snatches the Word from their hearts, so that they do not believe and are saved.

13 Those who are on the stones are those who receive the Word with joy, they barely hear it; but they have no roots: they believe for a time, and in the moment of temptation they turn
back.
14 What fell among thorns are those who listen, but with the worries, riches and pleasures of life, they allow themselves to be drowned little by little, and do not mature.
15 What fell on fertile ground are those who hear the Word with a well-disposed heart, retain it, and bear fruit thanks to their perseverance.
16 You don't light a lamp to cover it with a container or put it under a bed, but you put it on a lampstand, so that those who enter can see the light.
17 For there is nothing hidden that will not be discovered one day, nor anything secret that should not be known and revealed.
18 Pay attention and listen carefully, because to him who has, more will be given, but to him who does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away.
19 His mother and brothers went to see him, but they could not get close because of the crowd.
20 Then they announced to Jesus, “Your mother and your brothers are out there and want to see you.”
21 But he answered them, "My mother and my brothers are those who hear the Word of God and do it."
22 One day, Jesus got into a boat with his disciples and said to them, "Let's go to the other side of the lake." They left,
23 and while they were sailing, Jesus fell asleep. Then a strong gale broke out over the lake; The boat was filling with water, and they were in danger.
24 The disciples came and woke him up, saying, “Master, Master, we are sinking!” He woke up and rebuked the wind and the waves; These subsided and calm ensued.

25 Then he said to them, "Where is your faith?" And they, full of fear and admiration, said to one another: "Who is this that commands even the wind and the waves, and commands them?"
Do they obey?
26 Then they came to the region of the Gerasenes, which is located opposite Galilee.

27 Jesus had just disembarked when a man from the city who was possessed by a demon came out to meet him. He had not dressed for a long time, and he had not lived in a
house, but in the tombs.
28 When he saw Jesus, he began to cry out, fell at his feet, and said in a loud voice, “What do you want from me, Jesus, Son of God, the Most High? I beg you not to torment me.

29 Jesus, in effect, was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of that man. Many times the spirit had taken possession of him, and although they tied him with chains and fetters to restrain him, he
He broke his bonds and the demon dragged him to deserted places.
30 Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” "Legion," he answered, because there were many demons that had entered him.
31 And they begged him not to order them to rush into the abyss.
32 There was a large herd of pigs feeding on the mountain. The demons begged Jesus to allow them to enter the pigs. He allowed it.
33 Then they left the man and entered the pigs, and from the top of the cliff the herd rushed into the sea and was drowned.
34 When the caretakers saw what had happened, they fled and spread the news in the city and in the villages.

35 Immediately the people went to see what had happened. When they came to where Jesus was, they saw the man from whom the demons had come out sitting at his feet, dressed and in his right mind.
They were filled with fear.
36 Those who had witnessed the event told them how the demon-possessed man had been cured.

1 One Saturday, Jesus went to eat at the house of one of the leading Pharisees. They watched him carefully.
2 Before him was a man sick with dropsy.
3 Jesus asked the doctors of the Law and the Pharisees: "Is it permissible to heal on the Sabbath or not?"
4 But they were silent. Then Jesus took the sick man by the hand, healed him, and sent him away.
5 And turning to them, he said, "If one of you has his son or his ox fall into a well, don't you take him out immediately, even though it is the Sabbath?"
6 To this they could not answer anything.
7 And when he noticed how the guests were seeking the first places, he told them this parable:
8 "If you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not put yourself first, for it may happen that another person more important than you has been invited,
9 and when the one who invited you both arrives, he has to tell you: "Leave him the place", and so, full of shame, you have to put yourself in last place.

10 On the contrary, when you are invited, go and place yourself in the last place, so that when the one who invited you arrives, he will say to you, "Friend, come closer," and then you will be well.
in front of all the guests.
11 For everyone who exalts will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.”

12 Then he said to the one who had invited him, "When you give lunch or dinner, do not invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives, or rich neighbors, lest they
invite them in turn, and so you have your reward.
13 On the contrary, when you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the paralyzed, the blind.
14 Blessed are you, because they have no way of repaying you, and so you will have your reward in the resurrection of the righteous!
15 When one of the guests heard these words, he said to him, “Happy is he who sits at table in the Kingdom of God!”
16 Jesus answered him, “A man prepared a great banquet and invited many people.
17 At dinner time, he ordered his servant to tell the guests, "Come, everything is ready."
18 But everyone, without exception, began to make excuses. The first one said to him: "I just bought a field and I have to go see it. Please excuse me."
19 The second said, "I have bought five yoke of oxen and I am going to test them. Please excuse me."
20 And a third answered, "I have just gotten married and for that reason I cannot go."

21 Upon his return, the servant told all this to the owner of the house, who, irritated, said to him: "Go immediately through the squares and streets of the city, and bring here the poor, the crippled, the
blind and paralyzed.
22 The servant returned and said, "Sir, your orders have been fulfilled and there is still room."
23 The master answered him, "Go to the roads and along the fences, and urge the people to come in, so that my house will be filled.
24 For I assure you that none of those who were previously invited will taste my supper."
25 A large crowd was with Jesus, and he turned and said to them:
26 “Anyone who comes to me and does not love me more than his father and mother, his wife and children, his brothers and sisters, and even his own life, cannot be my disciple.
27 He who does not carry his cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
28 Which of you, if he wants to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the costs, to see if he has enough to finish it?
29 Lest once the foundation is laid, it cannot be finished, and everyone who sees it laughs at it, saying:
30 "This man began to build and could not finish."
31 And what king, when he goes out on campaign against another, does not first sit down to consider whether with ten thousand men he can confront the one who comes against him with twenty thousand?
32 On the contrary, while the other king is still far away, he sends an embassy to negotiate peace. ]
33 In the same way, anyone of you who does not renounce everything he has cannot be my disciple.
34 Salt is an excellent thing, but if it loses its flavor, with what will it be salted again?
35 It is no longer useful for soil or fertilizer: it must be thrown away. "He who has ears to hear, let him hear!"
1 All the tax collectors and sinners came to Jesus to listen to him.
2 The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them."
3 Jesus then told them this parable:
4 "If someone has a hundred sheep and loses one, doesn't he leave the ninety-nine in the field and go in search of the one that was lost until he finds it?
5 And when he finds it, he carries it on his shoulders, full of joy,
6 And when he got home he called his friends and neighbors and said to them, "Rejoice with me, because I have found my lost sheep."
7 I tell you the truth, in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who do not need to be converted."
8 And he also said to them, "If a woman has ten drachmas and loses one, doesn't she light the lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it?"
9 And when she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors and says to them, "Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma that I had lost."
10 I tell you the truth, in the same way the angels of God rejoice over just one sinner who repents."
11 Jesus also said, “A man had two sons.
12 The youngest of them said to his father, "Father, give me my share of the inheritance." And the father distributed his property to them.
13 A few days later, the youngest son gathered everything he had and went to a far country, where he squandered his wealth on a licentious life.
14 He had already spent everything, when great misery occurred in that country, and he began to suffer hardships.
15 Then he entered the service of one of the inhabitants of that region, who sent him to his field to tend pigs.
16 He would have liked to satisfy his hunger with the acorns that the pigs ate, but no one gave them to him.
17 Then he reconsidered and said, "How many of my father's hired servants have plenty of bread, and here I am dying of hunger!"
18 Right now I will go to my father's house and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against Heaven and against you;
19 I no longer deserve to be called your son, treat me like one of your hired workers."
20 Then he departed and returned to his father's house. While he was still far away, his father saw him and was deeply moved. He ran to meet him, hugged him and kissed him.
21 The young man said to him, "Father, I have sinned against Heaven and against you; I do not deserve to be called your son."
22 But the father said to his servants, "Bring the best clothes at once and dress him, put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
23 Bring the fatted calf and kill it. Let's eat and celebrate,
24 for my son was dead and is alive again, he was lost and is found." And the party began.
25 The eldest son was in the field. When he returned, close to the house, he heard the music and the choirs that accompanied the dance.
26 And calling one of the servants, he asked him what that meant.
27 He answered him, "Your brother has returned, and your father had the calf killed and fattened, because he has recovered it safely."
28 He was angry and would not go in. His father came out to beg him to come in,
29 But he answered him, "I have served you for so many years without ever having disobeyed a single one of your orders, and you never gave me a goat to have a party with my friends.
30 And now that your son has returned, after having spent your property on women, you have the fatted calf killed for him!"
31 But the father said to him, "My son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
32 It is right that there should be celebration and joy, because your brother was dead and has come to life, he was lost and has been found.
1 He also said to his disciples: “There was a rich man who had a manager, whom they accused of wasting his property.
2 He called him and said, "What have I been told about you? Give me an account of your administration, because you will no longer occupy that position."
3 The administrator then thought: "What am I going to do now that my lord takes my position from me? Dig? I don't have the strength. Beg? I'm ashamed.
4 I already know what I am going to do so that, when I leave my post, there will be those who welcome me into their home!"
5 He called his master's debtors one by one and asked the first, "How much do you owe my master?"
6 "Twenty barrels of oil," he replied. The administrator told him: "Take your receipt, sit down immediately, and write down ten."

7 Then he asked another, "And you, how much do you owe?" "Four hundred quintals of wheat," he replied. The administrator told him: "Take your receipt and write down
three hundred."
8 And the lord praised this dishonest administrator for having acted so skillfully. Because the children of this world are more astute in their dealings with others than the children of light.
9 But I say to you: Make friends with the money of injustice, so that on the day when it fails, they will receive you into eternal homes.
10 He who is faithful in a little is also faithful in much, and he who is dishonest in a little is also dishonest in much.
11 If you are not faithful in the use of unrighteous money, who will trust you with true good?
12 And if you are not faithful with what belongs to others, who will trust you with what belongs to you?
13 No servant can serve two masters, for he will hate one and love the other, or he will be interested in the first and despise the second. "You cannot serve God and Money."
14 The Pharisees, who were friends of money, heard all this and mocked Jesus.
15 He said to them, “You appear righteous before men, but God knows your hearts. Because what is estimable in the eyes of men is contemptible with God.
16 The Law and the Prophets reach John. Since then the Kingdom of God has been proclaimed, and everyone has to strive to enter it.
17 It is easier for heaven and earth to cease to exist than for one comma of the Law to disappear.
18 He who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and he who marries a woman abandoned by her husband commits adultery.
19 There was a rich man who dressed in purple and fine linen and made splendid banquets every day.
20 At his door, covered with sores, lay a poor man named Lazarus,
21 who longed to be satisfied with what fell from the rich man's table; and even the dogs went to lick his sores.
22 The poor man died and was carried by the angels to Abraham's bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
23 In the abode of the dead, in the midst of torment, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham far away, and Lazarus next to him.

24 Then he exclaimed, "Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in the water and cool my tongue, because these flames
torment."
25 "My son," Abraham replied, "remember that you received your good things in life and Lazarus, on the other hand, received bad things; now he finds his consolation here, and you find his torment.

26 Furthermore, a great chasm opens between you and us. So those who want to go from here to there cannot do so, and neither can one go from there to
here."
27 The rich man answered, "I beg you then, father, to send Lazarus to my father's house,
28 For I have five brothers: may he prevent them, lest they also fall into this place of torment."
29 Abraham replied, "They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to them."
30 "No, Father Abraham, the rich man insisted. But if any of the dead come to see them, they will repent."
31 But Abraham answered, "If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, even if someone rises from the dead, they will not be convinced."
1 Then he said to his disciples: “It is inevitable that there will be scandals, but woe to him who causes them!
2 It would be better for him if a grinding stone were tied around his neck and he were thrown into the sea than to offend one of these little ones.
3 Therefore, be careful! If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.
4 And if he sins seven times a day against you, and returns to you seven times a day, saying, "I repent," forgive him."
5 The Apostles said to the Lord: "Increase our faith."
6 He answered, "If you had faith the size of a mustard seed and said to that mulberry tree over there, 'Be uprooted and planted in the sea,' it would obey you.
7 Suppose one of you has a servant to plow or tend cattle. When he returns from the field, will he say to him: "Come quickly and sit at the table"?
8 Will he not rather say to him, "Prepare dinner for me and gather up your tunic to serve me until I have eaten and drunk, and you will eat and drink afterwards"?
9 Should you be grateful to your servant because he did what he was told?
10 So you also, when you have done everything that is commanded, say: 'We are mere servants, we have only done our duty.'"
11 While on his way to Jerusalem, Jesus weighed through Samaria and Galilee.
12 As he entered a town, ten lepers met him and stopped at a distance.
13 and they began to shout to him: “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
14 When Jesus saw them, he said to them, "Go and present yourself to the priests." And along the way they were purified.
15 When one of them found that he was cured, he turned back, praising God with a loud voice.
16 and he threw himself at Jesus' feet with his face on the ground, thanking him. He was a Samaritan.
17 Jesus then said to him, “Why, were the ten not purified? The other nine, where are they?
18 Has no one returned to give thanks to God except this foreigner?
19 And he added, “Get up and go, your faith has saved you.”
20 The Pharisees asked him when the Kingdom of God will come. He answered them: «The Kingdom of God does not come ostensibly,
21 and it will not be possible to say: "It is here" or "It is there." For the Kingdom of God is among you.
22 Jesus then said to his disciples: “The time will come when you will desire to see just one of the days of the Son of Man and you will not see it.
23 They will say to you, "He is here" or "He is there," but do not run to look for him.
24 As lightning shines from one end of the sky to the other, so will the Son of Man be when his Day comes.
25 But first he will have to suffer many things and will be rejected by this generation.
26 In the days of the Son of Man it will happen as in the time of Noah.
27 The people ate, drank, and married, until the day Noah entered the ark and the flood came, causing them all to die.
28 It will be like in Lot's time: people ate and drank, bought and sold, planted and built.
29 But on the day Lot left Sodom, a rain of fire and sulfur fell from heaven and killed them all.
30 The same thing will happen on the Day when the Son of Man is revealed.
31 On that Day, whoever is on the roof and has his things in the house, do not go down to look for them. Likewise, whoever is in the field, do not turn back.
32 Remember Lot's wife.
33 He who tries to save his life will lose it; and whoever loses it will keep it.
34 Truly I say to you, on that night, of two men who are eating together, one will be taken and the other left;
35 Of two women who are grinding together, one will be taken and the other left.
36 [Of two that are in a field, one will be taken and the other left.]
37 Then they asked him, “Where will this happen, Lord?” Jesus answered them: "Where the corpse is, the vultures will gather."
1 Then he taught him with a parable that it was necessary to always pray without getting discouraged:
2 «In a city there was a judge who did not fear God nor care for men;
3 And in the same city there lived a widow who turned to him, saying, "I beseech you, give me justice against my adversary."
4 For a long time the judge refused, but then he said: "I do not fear God nor care for men,
5 But since this widow bothers me, I will give her justice so that she does not continually come to bother me."
6 And the Lord said, “Listen to what this unjust judge said.
7 And will not God give justice to his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night, even if he makes them wait?
8 Truly I tell you, he will bring justice to you in the blink of an eye. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?
9 And referring to some who considered themselves righteous and despised others, he also spoke this parable:
10 “Two men went up to the Temple to pray; one was a Pharisee and the other a publican.
11 The Pharisee stood and prayed: "My God, I thank you that I am not like other men, who are thieves, unjust, and adulterers, nor like that publican.
12 I fast twice a week and pay a tenth of all my income."

13 But the publican, standing at a distance, did not even dare to raise his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest, saying, "My God, have mercy on me, for I am a
sinner!"
14 Truly I say to you, the latter returned home justified, but not the former. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled and he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
15 They also presented little children to him, so that he could touch them; But when the disciples saw this, they rebuked them.
16 Then Jesus called for them and said, “Let the children come to me and do not stop them, because the Kingdom of God belongs to those like them.
17 Truly I say to you, whoever does not receive the Kingdom of God like a child will not enter it."
18 An important man asked him, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal Life?”
19 Jesus said to him: Why do you call me good? Only God is good.
