20 You know the commandments: You shall not commit adultery, you shall not kill, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness, honor your father and your mother.
21 The man answered him, “All this I have done from my youth.”
22 When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “You still lack one thing: sell everything you have and distribute it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come and follow me.
23 When the man heard these words, he was sad, because he was very rich.
24 Seeing it like this, Jesus said: “How difficult it will be for the rich to enter the Kingdom of God!
25 Yes, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of God.
26 Those who were listening said, "But then who can be saved?"
27 Jesus answered, “What is impossible with men is possible with God.”
28 Peter said to him, "We have left everything we had and followed you."
29 Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth, whoever has left home, wife, brothers, parents, or children for the Kingdom of God,
30 will receive much more in that world; and in the world to come, he will receive eternal Life.
31 Then Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them, “Now we are going up to Jerusalem, where everything that the prophets announced about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
32 He will be handed over to the pagans, they will mock him, they will insult him, they will spit on him
33 and after flogging him, they will kill him. But on the third day he will rise again.
34 They understood nothing of all this; It was dark to them and they did not understand the meaning of these words.
35 As he approached Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the roadside, begging for alms.
36 Hearing that many people were passing by, he asked what was happening.
37 They answered him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
38 The blind man began to shout, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
39 Those who were ahead rebuked him to keep quiet, but he shouted louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
40 Jesus stopped and ordered them to bring him to him. When he had him at his side, he asked him:
41 What do you want me to do for you? "Lord, may I see again."
42 And Jesus said to him, "Recover your sight, your faith has saved you."
43 At the same moment, the blind man regained his sight and followed Jesus, glorifying God. Seeing this, all the people praised God.
1 Jesus entered Jericho and passed through the city.
2 There lived a very rich man named Zacchaeus, who was the chief of the publicans.
3 He wanted to see who Jesus was, but he couldn't because of the crowd, because he was short.
4 Then he went ahead and climbed a sycamore tree so that he could see it, because he was going to pass by there,
5 When he reached that place, Jesus looked up and said to him, "Zacchaeus, come down quickly, because today I have to stay at your house."
6 Zacchaeus quickly came down and welcomed him with joy.
7 When everyone saw this, they murmured, saying, "He has gone to stay in the house of a sinner."
8 But Zacchaeus resolutely said to the Lord, "Lord, I will give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have wronged anyone, I will give them four times as much."
9 And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, since this man also is a son of Abraham,
10 For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.
11 As the people continued listening, he added a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they thought that the Kingdom of God was going to appear at any moment.
12 He said to them, “A man of noble family went to a far country to receive the royal investiture and return immediately.
13 He called ten of his servants and gave them each a hundred pieces of silver, saying, "Make them produce until I return."
14 But his fellow citizens hated him and sent an embassy after him to say, "We do not want this to be our king."
15 When he returned, clothed with royal dignity, he called for the servants to whom he had given the money, to find out what each one had earned.
16 The first one came forward and said to him, "Lord, your hundred pieces of silver have produced ten times as much."
17 "Well done, good servant," he replied, "since you have been faithful in so little, receive the government of ten cities."
18 The second came and said, "Lord, your hundred pieces of silver have produced five times as much."
19 To him he also said, "You will be in charge of five cities."
20 The other came and said to him, "Sir, here is your hundred silver coins, which I kept wrapped in a handkerchief.
21 Because I was afraid of you, for you are a demanding man, who wants to receive what you have not deposited and reap what you have not sown."
22 He answered him, "I judge you by your own words, bad servant. If you knew that I am a demanding man, that I want to receive what I did not deposit and reap what I did not sow,
23 Why didn't you lend my money? Upon my return I would have recovered it with interest."
24 And he said to those who were there, "Take the hundred coins from him and give them to the one who has ten times as much."
25 "But, sir," they answered, "you already have a thousand!"
26 "I tell you the truth, to him who has, more will be given; but to him who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
27 As for my enemies, who have not wanted me as king, bring them here and kill them in my presence.
28 After saying this, Jesus continued on, going up to Jerusalem.
29 When he approached Bethphage and Bethany, at the foot of the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples, saying to them:
30 “Go to the town opposite, and when you enter, you will find a donkey tied, which no one has yet ridden. Untie him and bring him;
31 And if anyone asks you, "Why do you untie it?" answer, "The Lord needs it."
32 The messengers set out and found everything just as he had told them.
33 When they untied the donkey, its owners said to them, "Why are you untying it?"
34 And they answered, "The Lord needs it."
35 Then they brought the donkey to where Jesus was and, putting their cloaks on it, made it ride.
36 As he went, the people spread their cloaks on the road.

37 As Jesus approached the slope of the Mount of Olives, all the disciples, filled with joy, began to praise God with a loud voice for all the miracles that had been done.
seen.
38 And they said, “Blessed be the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!
39 Some Pharisees who were in the crowd said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples.”
40 But he answered, "I tell you the truth, if they keep silent, the stones will cry out."
41 When he was near and saw the city, he began to weep for it,
42 saying: “If only you too had understood the message of peace on that day! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
43 Disastrous days will come for you, when your enemies will surround you with palisades, besiege you, and attack you on all sides.

44 They will destroy you and your children, who are within you, and will not leave one stone upon another in you, because you have not known how to recognize the time in which you were visited by God.
45 And when he entered the Temple, he began to drive out the sellers,
46 saying to them, "It is written: My house will be a house of prayer, but you have turned it into a den of thieves."
47 And he taught daily in the Temple. The high priests, the scribes and the most important of the people were looking for a way to kill him.
48 But they did not know how to do it, because all the people listened to him and heeded his words.
1 One day when Jesus was teaching the people in the Temple and announcing the Good News, the chief priests and the scribes with the elders came to him,
2 and they said to him, "Tell us by what authority you do these things or who has given you that authority."
3 Jesus answered them, “I also want to ask you something. Tell me:
4 Did John's baptism come from heaven or from men?
5 They reasoned this: "If we answer, 'From heaven,' he will say to us, 'Why didn't you believe in him?'
6 And if we answer, 'Of men,' all the people will stone us, because they are convinced that John is a prophet."
7 And they told him that they did not know where he came from.
8 Jesus answered them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do this.”
9 And then he told the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it to some tenants, and went abroad for a long time.

10 When the time came, he sent a servant to them to give him his share of the fruits. But the tenants beat him and threw him out with their hands.
empty.
11 He sent another servant, and this one also was beaten, abused, and sent away empty-handed.
12 Then he sent a third, and they also wounded him and threw him outside.
13 The owner of the vineyard then thought, "What will I do? I am going to send my very dear son: perhaps they will be considerate of him."
14 But when the tenants saw him, they said to themselves, "This is the heir, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours."
15 And throwing him out of the vineyard, they killed him. What will the owner of the vineyard do with them?
16 He will come and destroy those vinedressers and give the vineyard to others. Hearing these words, they said: "God forbid!"

17 But looking at them, Jesus said to them, "What then does it mean that it is written: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the
angular"?
18 "Whoever falls on this stone will be crushed, and whoever it falls on will be crushed."
19 The scribes and the chief priests wanted to stop him right then and there, because they understood that he had told this parable for them, but they feared the people.

20 They began to stalk him and sent spies to him, who pretended to be good men, in order to surprise him in some of his statements, and hand him over to the power and authority of the
governor.

21 And they said to him, "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach righteously and that you do not regard the condition of people, but that you teach with all faithfulness the way of
God.
22 Are we allowed to pay tax to Caesar or not?
23 But Jesus, knowing their cunning, said to them:
24 “Show me a denarius. Whose figure is it and the inscription on it? "Caesar's," they replied.
25 Jesus said to them, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
26 Thus they could not surprise him in any words before the people and, full of admiration for his response, they had to remain silent.
27 Some Sadducees, who deny the resurrection, came to him.
28 And they said to him, 'Teacher, Moses has commanded us: 'If anyone is married and dies without having children, let his brother, to give him offspring, marry the widow.'
29 Now there were seven brothers. The first married and died without having children.
30 The second
31 married the widow, and then the third. And so the seven died without leaving any descendants.
32 Finally, the woman also died.
33 When the dead are raised, whose wife will she be, since the seven had her as their wife?
34 Jesus answered them, "In this world men and women marry,
35 But those who are judged worthy to participate in the world to come and the resurrection will not marry.
36 They can no longer die, because they are like angels and are children of God, being children of the resurrection.
37 That the dead are going to rise, Moses has made it clear in the passage about the bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.
38 For he is not God of the dead, but of the living; everyone, in fact, lives for him.
39 Taking the floor, some scribes said to him, “Teacher, you have spoken well.”
40 And they no longer dared to ask him anything.
41 Jesus then said to them, "How can it be said that the Messiah is the son of David,
42 if David himself has said in the Book of Psalms: "The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right,
43 until I put your enemies under your feet"?
44 If David calls him 'Lord', how can he be his son?
45 And he said to the disciples, so that all the people could hear:
46 “Be careful of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes, be greeted in the squares, and occupy the first seats in synagogues and at banquets;
47 who devour widows' goods and pretend to make long prayers. "Those will be judged more severely."
1 Then, lifting up his eyes, Jesus saw some rich people putting their offerings into the Temple treasury.
2 He also saw a widow of very humble condition, putting two small copper coins,
3 and said, “I tell you the truth, this poor widow has given more than anyone else.
4 For all the others gave as an offering something of what they had left, but she, out of her need, gave everything she had to live on.
5 And as some, speaking of the Temple, said that it was adorned with beautiful stones and votive offerings, Jesus said:
6 "Of all that you see, one day not one stone will remain on another: everything will be destroyed."
7 They asked him, "Teacher, when will this take place, and what will be the sign that it will happen?"
8 Jesus answered, "Be careful not to be deceived, for many will come forward in my name, saying, 'It is I,' and also, 'The time is at hand.' Don't follow them.
9 When you hear about wars and revolutions, do not be alarmed; "This must happen sooner, but the end will not come so soon."
10 Then he said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
11 There will be great earthquakes; plague and famine in many places; Terrifying phenomena and great signs in the sky will also be seen.

12 But before all that, they will arrest them, they will persecute them, they will hand them over to the synagogues and they will be imprisoned; They will bring them before kings and governors because of my Name,
13 and this will happen to them so that they can testify about me.
14 Keep in mind that you will not have to prepare your defense,
15 For I myself will give you eloquence and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.
16 They will be handed over even by their own parents and brothers, by their relatives and friends; and many of you will be killed.
17 They will be hated by all because of my Name.
18 But not even a hair will fall from their heads.
19 Thanks to perseverance they will save their lives.
20 When you see Jerusalem besieged by armies, know that its ruin is near.
21 Those who are in Judea, let them take refuge in the mountains; Those who are within the city, let them move away; and those who are in the fields, let them not return to it.
22 For there will be days of punishment, in which everything that is written must be fulfilled.
23 Woe to those who are pregnant or nursing babies in those days! The misfortune of this country will be great and the wrath of God will weigh on this people.
24 They will fall by the edge of the sword, they will be taken captive to all nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by the pagans, until the time of the pagans is fulfilled.
25 There will be signs in the sun, in the moon and in the stars; and on land, the people will be afflicted by the roar of the sea and the violence of the waves.
26 Men will faint with fear for what will come to the world, because the stars will be shaken.
27 Then you will see the Son of Man coming on a cloud, full of power and glory.
28 When this begins to happen, be of good courage and lift up your heads, because deliverance is about to come to you.”
29 And Jesus made this comparison to them: “Look what happens with the fig tree or with any other tree.
30 When it begins to sprout, you realize that summer is approaching.
31 Likewise, when you see all these things happening, know that the Kingdom of God is at hand.
32 Truly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all this is accomplished.
33 Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
34 Be careful not to let yourself be dazed by excesses, drunkenness and the worries of life, so that that day does not suddenly fall upon you
35 like a trap, for it will come upon all men in all the earth.
36 Be prepared and pray incessantly, to be safe from everything that is to happen. Thus they will be able to appear safely before the Son of man.
37 During the day he taught in the Temple, and at night he retired to the Mount of Olives.
38 And all the people got up early to go to the Temple to hear him.
1 The festival of Unleavened Bread, called Passover, was near.
2 The chief priests and scribes were looking for a way to eliminate Jesus, because they had half of the people.
3 Then Satan entered into Judas, called Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve.
4 He went to discuss with the chief priests and the leaders of the guard how to hand him over.
5 They were glad and agreed to give him money.
6 Judas accepted and was looking for a suitable opportunity to hand him over without the people finding out.
7 The day of Unleavened Bread arrived, on which the Easter victim was to be immolated.
8 Jesus sent Peter and John, saying to them, "Go and prepare for us what we need for the Passover meal."
9 They asked him, “Where do you want us to prepare it?”
10 Jesus answered them, “As you enter the city, you will find a man carrying a jar of water. Follow him to the house where he enters,
11 and say to its owner: The Master commands to ask you: "Where is the room where I can eat the Passover with my disciples?"
12 He will show you a large room on the upper floor, arranged with cushions: prepare what you need there.
13 The disciples set out, found everything as Jesus had told them, and prepared the Passover.
14 When the time came, Jesus sat down at the table with the Apostles and said to them:
15 «I have ardently desired to eat this Passover with you before my Passion,
16 For I tell you, I will not eat it again until it is fully fulfilled in the Kingdom of God.
17 And taking a cup, he gave thanks and said, “Take it and share it among yourselves.
18 For I tell you the truth, from now on I will not drink any more of the fruit of the vine until the Kingdom of God comes.
19 Then he took the bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, “This is my Body, which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.
20 After dinner he did the same with the cup, saying: “This cup is the New Covenant sealed with my Blood, which is poured out for you.
21 The traitor's hand is on the table next to me.
22 For the Son of Man goes on the path that has been pointed out to him, but woe to him who betrays him.
23 Then they began to ask each other which of them would be the one who was going to do this.
24 And a dispute arose about who should be considered the greatest.
25 Jesus said to them, “The kings of the nations rule over them, and those who exercise power over the people call themselves benefactors.
26 But it should not be so among you. On the contrary, he who is greater, let him behave like the lesser, and he who governs, like a servant.
27 For who is greater, he who is at the table or he who serves? Isn't he the one at the table? And yet I am among you as one who serves.
28 You are the ones who have always remained with me in the midst of my trials.
29 Therefore I bestow upon you kingship, as my Father conferred it upon me,
30 And in my Kingdom, you will eat and drink at my table, and you will sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
31 Simon, Simon, see that Satan has asked for power to sift you like wheat,
32 But I have prayed for you, so that your faith may not fail. And you, after you have returned, confirm your brothers.
33 “Lord,” Peter said to him, “I am ready to go with you to prison and to death.”
34 But Jesus replied, "I assure you, Peter, today, before the rooster crows, you will have denied three times that you know me."
35 Then he said to them, "When I sent you away without purse, scrip, or sandals, did you lack anything?"

36 “Nothing,” they answered. He added: “But now whoever has a bag, let him carry it; He who has a saddle bag, let him carry it too; and whoever does not have a sword, let him sell his cloak to buy one.
37 For I say to you, this word of the Scripture must be fulfilled in me: He was numbered among the evildoers. Everything that refers to me is coming to an end.
38 "Sir, they said to him, here are two swords." He answered them: "Enough."
39 Immediately Jesus left and went as usual to the Mount of Olives, followed by his disciples.
40 When they arrived, he said to them, “Pray so that you will not fall into temptation.”
41 Then he went away from them, about a stone's throw away, and knelt down and prayed:
42 «Father, if you wish, take this cup away from me. But not my will, but yours, be done.
43 Then an angel from heaven appeared to him and comforted him.
44 In the midst of anguish, he prayed more intensely, and his sweat was like drops of blood running to the ground.
45 After praying, he got up and went to his disciples and found them asleep with sadness.
46 Jesus said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray so that you do not fall into temptation.
47 While he was still speaking, a crowd arrived, headed by the one called Judas, one of the Twelve. He approached Jesus to kiss him.
48 Jesus said to him, "Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?"
49 Those who were with Jesus, seeing what was going to happen, asked him, "Lord, shall we use the sword?"
50 And one of them struck the servant of the High Priest with his sword, cutting off his right ear.
51 But Jesus said, "Stop, that's it." And touching his ear, he healed him.
52 Then he said to the chief priests, the heads of the Temple guard, and the elders who had come to arrest him, "Am I a thief that you should come with swords and clubs?
53 Every day I was with you in the Temple and you did not arrest me. But this is your hour and the power of darkness.
54 After arresting him, they took him to the house of the High Priest. Pedro followed him from afar.
55 They lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard, and they sat around it, and Peter sat between them.
56 A servant girl who saw him by the fire looked at him intently and said, "This man was also with him."
57 Peter denied it, saying, “Woman, I do not know him.”
58 Soon after, another saw him and said, "You too are one of those." But Peter answered, "No, man, I am not."
59 About an hour later, another insisted, saying, “There is no doubt that this man was with him; Furthermore, he is also a Galilean.
60 "Man, said Peter, I don't know what you are saying." At that moment, while he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.
61 The Lord, turning, looked at Peter. He remembered the words that the Lord had said to him: "Today, before the rooster crows, you will have denied me three times."
62 And he went out and wept bitterly.
63 The men who were guarding Jesus abused him and beat him;
64 and covering his face, they said to him, "Prophesy, who hit you?"
65 And they uttered all kinds of insults against him.
66 When it was dawn, the council of the elders of the people met, together with the chief priests and the scribes. They brought Jesus before the court
67 and they said to him, "Tell us if you are the Messiah." He said to them: "If I answer you, you will not believe me,
68 and if I question them, they will not answer me.
69 But from now on the Son of Man will sit at the right hand of Almighty God.
70 Everyone asked, “Are you then the Son of God?” Jesus answered: "They are right, I am."
71 They said, "Do we need another testimony? We ourselves have heard it from his own mouth.
1 Then the whole assembly arose and brought him before Pilate.
2 And they began to accuse him, saying, "We found this man inciting our people to rebellion, preventing them from paying taxes to the Emperor, and pretending to be the Messiah king."
3 Pilate questioned him, saying, "Are you the king of the Jews?" "You say so," Jesus answered.
4 Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowd, "I find no cause for condemnation in this man."
5 But they insisted: “He revolts the people with his teaching throughout Judea. "It started in Galilee and has come here."
6 When Pilate heard this, he asked if the man was a Galilean.
7 And having made sure that it belonged to Herod's jurisdiction, he sent it to him. In those days, Herod was also in Jerusalem.
8 Herod was very happy to see Jesus. He had long wanted to see him, from what he had heard about him, and he hoped that he would perform some prodigy in his presence.
9 He asked him many questions, but Jesus did not answer him anything.
10 Meanwhile, the chief priests and the scribes stood there and vehemently accused him.
11 Herod and his guards, after treating him with contempt and making a fool of him, covered him with a magnificent cloak and sent him back to Pilate.
12 And that same day, Herod and Pilate, who were at enmity, became friends.
13 Pilate summoned the chief priests, the leaders, and the people,

14 and said to them, “You have brought this man to me, accusing him of inciting the people to rebellion. But I questioned him in front of you and found no reason for condemnation in the
charges against him;
15 nor Herod, since he has returned him to this court. You see, this man has done nothing that deserves death.
16 After I have taught him a lesson, I will release him.”
17 [On each festival, the governor used to release a prisoner.]
18 But the crowd began to shout, “Let this man die! Release Barabbas to us!
19 Barabbas had been imprisoned for a sedition that took place in the city and for murder.
20 Pilate spoke to them again with the intention of setting Jesus free.
21 But they kept shouting, “Crucify him! Crucify him!
22 A third time he said to them, “What evil has this man done? I find nothing in him that deserves death. After giving him a lesson, I will set him free.
23 But they insisted with shouts, demanding that he be crucified, and the shouting became more and more violent.
24 Finally, Pilate decided to grant the people's request.
25 He released the one they asked for, the one who had been imprisoned for sedition and murder, and handed Jesus over to their discretion.
26 As they were leading him away, they stopped a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was returning from the field, and loaded him with the cross to carry it behind Jesus.
27 Many of the people and a good number of women followed him, beating their breasts and lamenting for him.
28 But Jesus, turning to them, said to them, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me; rather cry for yourselves and for your children.
29 For the time is coming when it will be said: "Blessed are the barren, blessed are the breasts that did not conceive and the breasts that did not nurse!"
30 Then it will be said to the mountains, "Fall on us!" and to the hills, "Bury us!"
31 For if they treat the green wood like this, what will become of the dry wood?
32 Two other criminals were also taken with him to be executed.
33 When they came to the place called “the Skull,” they crucified him along with the criminals, one on his right and the other on his left.
34 Jesus said, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do." Then they divided their clothes, raffling them among themselves.
35 The people stood there and watched. Their leaders, mocking, said: "He has saved others: let him save himself, if he is the Messiah of God, the Chosen One!"
36 The soldiers also mocked him and approached to offer him vinegar.
37 They said to him, "If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself!"
38 Above his head was an inscription: “This is the king of the Jews.”
39 One of the crucified criminals insulted him, saying, "Are you not the Messiah? Save yourself and us.
40 But the other rebuked him, saying, "Do you not fear God, you who suffer the same punishment as him?
41 We suffer it justly, because we pay for our sins, but he has done nothing wrong.
42 And he said: "Jesus, remember me when you come to establish your Kingdom."
43 He replied, "I assure you that today you will be with me in Paradise."
44 It was around noon. The sun was eclipsed and darkness covered the entire land until three in the afternoon.
45 The veil of the Temple was torn in the middle.
46 Jesus, with a cry, exclaimed: "Father, into your hands I commend my spirit." And saying this, he expired.
47 When the centurion saw what had happened, he praised God, exclaiming, "Truly this man was a righteous man."
48 And the crowd that had gathered to watch the spectacle, seeing what had happened, returned beating their chests.
49 All his friends and the women who had accompanied him from Galilee remained at a distance, contemplating what had happened.
50 Then a member of the Council came, named Joseph, an upright and just man,
51 who had disagreed with the decisions and attitudes of others. He was from Arimathea, a city in Judea, and was waiting for the Kingdom of God.
52 He went to see Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
53 After taking him down from the cross, he wrapped him in a linen cloth and placed him in a tomb dug in the rock, where no one had been buried.
54 It was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath had already begun.
55 The women who had come from Galilee with Jesus followed Joseph, looked at the tomb, and saw how he had been buried.
56 Then they returned and prepared the balms and perfumes, but on the Sabbath they observed the rest prescribed by the Law.
1 On the first day of the week, at dawn, the women went to the tomb with the perfumes they had prepared.
2 They found the stone rolled away from the tomb
3 and they entered, but did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
4 While they were bewildered by this, two men in dazzling garments appeared to them.
5 As the women, filled with fear, did not dare to lift their eyes from the ground, they asked them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?
6 He is not here, he has risen. Remember what he told them when he was still in Galilee:
7 "The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinners, be crucified, and be resurrected on the third day."
8 And the women remembered his words.
9 When they returned from the tomb, they told this to the Eleven and everyone else.
10 They were Mary Magdalene, Joan, and Mary, the mother of James, and the other women who accompanied them. They told everything to the Apostles,
11 But it seemed to them that they were delirious and they did not believe them.
12 Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb, and when he looked out, he saw nothing but the sheets. Then he returned full of admiration for what had happened.
13 That same day, two of the disciples were going to a small town called Emmaus, located about ten kilometers from Jerusalem.
14 On the way they talked about what had happened.
15 While they were talking and arguing, Jesus himself approached and continued walking with them.
16 But something prevented their eyes from recognizing him.
17 He said to them, "What were you talking about on the way?" They stopped, with sad faces,
18 And one of them, named Cleopas, answered him, "You are the only stranger in Jerusalem who does not know what happened in these days!"
19 "What?" he asked them. They answered: "The matter of Jesus, the Nazarene, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
20 and how our high priests and our leaders handed him over to be condemned to death and crucified him.
21 We hoped that he would be the one to deliver Israel. But all of this has been three days since these things happened.
22 It is true that some women who are with us have confused us: they went to the tomb early in the morning
23 And when they did not find the body of Jesus, they returned saying that angels had appeared to them, assuring them that he is alive.
24 Some of us went to the tomb and found everything as the women had said. But they didn't see him.
25 Jesus said to them: “O men of hard understanding, how difficult it is for you to believe everything that the prophets announced!
26 Is it not necessary for the Messiah to endure these sufferings to enter into his glory?
27 And beginning with Moses and continuing in all the Scriptures what referred to him.
28 When they came near the town where they were going, Jesus made to move on.
29 But they insisted to him, "Stay with us, because it is already late and the day is ending." He came in and stayed with them.
30 And when he was at the table, he took the bread and blessed it; then he broke it and gave it to them.
31 Then the eyes of the disciples were opened and they recognized him, but he had disappeared from their sight.
32 And they said to each other, "Did not our hearts burn while he spoke to us on the road and explained the Scriptures to us?"
33 At that very moment, they set out and returned to Jerusalem. There they found the Eleven and the others who were with them gathered together,
34 and they said to them, “It is true, the Lord has risen and appeared to Simon!”
35 They, for their part, told what had happened to them on the way and how they had recognized him when they broke the bread.
36 While they were still talking about this, Jesus appeared among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.”
37 Astonished and filled with fear, they thought they saw a spirit,
38 But Jesus asked them, “Why are you troubled and these doubts arise?
39 Look at my hands and my feet, it is myself. Touch me and see. A spirit has no flesh or bones, as you see I have.
40 And saying this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
41 The joy and admiration of the disciples was such that they refused to believe. But Jesus asked them, "Do you have anything to eat here?"
42 They presented him with a piece of roasted fish;
43 He took it and ate it before everyone.
44 Then he said to them, "While I was still with you, I said to you, Everything that is written about me in the Law of Moses, in the Prophets, and in the Psalms must be fulfilled."
45 Then he opened their minds so that they could understand the Scriptures,
46 and added: "Thus it is written: The Messiah was to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
47 and beginning with Jerusalem, conversion for the forgiveness of sins was to be preached in his Name to all nations.
48 You are witnesses of all this.
49 And I will send you what my Father has promised you. Remain in the city, until you are clothed with the power that comes from above.
50 Then Jesus took them to the vicinity of Bethany and, raising his hands, blessed them.
51 While he was blessing them, he was separated from them and taken up to heaven.
52 The disciples, who had prostrated themselves before him, returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
53 and they remained continually in the Temple praising God.
1 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
2 In the beginning he was with God.
3 All things were made through the Word and without it nothing of all that exists was made.
4 In her was life, and life was the light of men.
5 The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness does not perceive it.
6 A man appeared, sent by God, whose name was John.
7 He came as a witness, to testify of the light, so that all might believe through him.
8 He was not light, but the witness of the light.
9 The Word was the true light that, upon coming into this world, illuminates every man.
10 She was in the world, and the world was made through her, and the world did not know her.
11 She came to her own, and her own did not receive her.

12 But to all who received her, who believe in her Name,
He gave them the power to become children of God.

13 They were not born of blood, nor by the work of the flesh,
nor of the will of man,
but they were begotten of God.

14 And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. And we have seen his glory,
the glory he receives from the Father as the only Son,
full of grace and truth.
15 John testifies of him, declaring: "This is he of whom I said, He who comes after me has gone before me, because he was before me."
16 Of its fullness we have all participated and received grace upon grace:
17 For the Law was given through Moses, but grace and truth came to us through Jesus Christ.
18 No one has ever seen God; The one who revealed it is the only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father.
19 This is the testimony that John gave, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, "Who are you?"
20 He confessed and did not hide it, but said clearly: "I am not the Messiah."
21 "Who are you then?" they asked him, "Are you Elijah?" John said, "No." "Are you the Prophet?" "Neither," he replied.
22 They asked, "Who are you, so that we can give an answer to those who sent us?" What do you say about yourself?
23 And he said to them, "I am a voice crying in the wilderness: Make straight the way of the Lord, as the prophet Isaiah said."
24 Some of those sent were Pharisees,
25 And they asked him again: "Why do you baptize, then, if you are not the Messiah, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?"
26 John answered, "I baptize with water, but among you there is someone whom you do not know:
27 "He is coming after me, and I am not worthy to untie the thong of his sandal."
28 All this happened in Bethany, on the other side of the Jordan where John was baptizing.
29 The next day, John saw Jesus approaching and said, “This is the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world.
30 I was referring to him when I said: After me comes a man who precedes me, because he existed before me.
31 I did not know him, but I came to baptize with water so that he might be revealed to Israel.
32 And John bore this testimony: “I saw the Spirit descend from heaven in the form of a dove and remain on him.
33 I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water said to me, "The one on whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining on him, this is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit."
34 I have seen him and bear witness that he is the Son of God.
35 The next day, John was there again with two of his disciples
36 And looking at Jesus as he passed by, he said, "This is the Lamb of God."
37 When the two disciples heard him speak thus, they followed Jesus.
38 He turned and, seeing that they were following him, asked them, "What do you want?" They answered him: “Rabbi – which translated means Teacher – where do you live?”
39 “Come and see,” he said to them. They went, saw where he lived and stayed with him that day. It was around four in the afternoon.
40 One of the two who heard John's words and followed Jesus was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother.
41 The first one he found was his own brother Simon, and he said to him, “We have found the Messiah,” which translated means Christ.
42 Then he brought him to where Jesus was. Jesus looked at him and said to him: "You are Simon, the son of John: your name will be Cephas," which translated means Peter.
43 The next day, Jesus decided to leave for Galilee. He found Felipe and said to him: "Follow me."
44 Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
45 Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found the one spoken of in the Law of Moses and the Prophets. It is Jesus, the son of Joseph of Nazareth.
46 Nathanael asked him, “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” "Come and see," Felipe told him.
47 Seeing Nathanael arrive, Jesus said, "This is a true Israelite, a man without double-crossing."
48 “Where do you know me from?” Nathanael asked him. Jesus answered him: "I saw you before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree."
49 Nathanael answered him, “Teacher, you are the son of God, you are the King of Israel.”
50 Jesus continued: “Because I told you, 'I saw you under the fig tree,' you believe. "You will see even greater things."
51 And he added: "I tell you the truth, you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man."
1 Three days later a wedding was celebrated in Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
2 Jesus was also invited with his disciples.
3 And since there was no wine, Jesus' mother said to him, "They have no wine."
4 Jesus answered her, “Woman, what do we have to do with it? My time has not come yet.
5 But his mother said to the servants, "Do whatever he tells you."
6 There were six stone jars there, intended for the purification rites of the Jews, containing about one hundred liters each.
7 Jesus said to the servants, “Fill these jars with water.” And they filled them to the brim.
8 "Take out now," added Jesus, "and take the person in charge of the banquet." So they did it.
9 The manager tasted the water that had been changed into wine, and since he did not know its origin, although the servants who had drawn the water knew, he called the husband.
10 and said to them, “The good wine is always served first, and when everyone has drunk well, the inferior wine is brought. You, however, have kept the good wine until this moment.
11 This was the first of Jesus' signs, and he did it in Cana of Galilee. Thus he manifested his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
12 After this, he went down to Capernaum with his mother, his brothers, and his disciples, and they stayed there a few days.
13 The Jewish Passover was approaching. Jesus went up to Jerusalem
14 And he found in the Temple the sellers of oxen, sheep, and doves, and the money-changers sitting at their tables.
15 He made a whip of cords and drove them all out of the Temple, along with their sheep and their oxen; He scattered the money changers' coins, overturned their tables
16 And he said to the dove sellers, "Take these out of here and do not make my Father's house a house of trade."
17 And his disciples remembered the words of the Scripture: Zeal for your House will consume me.
18 Then the Jews asked him, "What sign do you give us to do this?"
19 Jesus answered them, "Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up again."
20 The Jews said to him, "It took forty-six years to build this Temple, and you are going to build it in three days?"
21 But he was referring to the temple of his body.
22 Therefore, when Jesus was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word he had spoken.
23 While he was in Jerusalem during the Passover festival, many believed in his name when they saw the signs he performed.
24 But Jesus did not trust them, because he knew them all.
25 and he did not need to be informed about anyone: he knew what is inside man.
1 There was a man among the Pharisees named Nicodemus, who was one of the notables among the Jews.
2 He went to Jesus at night and said to him, "Teacher, we know that you have come from God to teach, because no one can perform the signs that you do unless God is with him."
3 Jesus answered him, "Truly, truly, I say to you, anyone who is not reborn from above cannot see the Kingdom of God."
4 Nicodemus asked him, “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter his mother's womb a second time and be born again?
5 Jesus answered him, “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless you are born of water and the Spirit, you cannot enter the Kingdom of God.
6 That which is born of the flesh is flesh, that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
7 Do not be surprised that I told you: "You have to be reborn from above."
8 The wind blows where it wishes: you hear its voice, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. The same thing happens with everyone who has been born of the Spirit.
9 “How is all this possible?” Nicodemus asked him again.
10 Jesus answered him, “You, who are a teacher in Israel, don't you know these things?
11 Truly I tell you, we speak of what we speak of what we know and we testify of what we have seen, but you do not accept our testimony.
12 If you do not believe when I tell you about the things on earth, how will you believe when I tell you about the things in heaven?
13 No one has ascended into heaven except He who came down from heaven, the Son of man who is in heaven.
14 Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up on high,
15 so that all who believe in him may have eternal life.
16 Yes, God so loved the world that he gave his only Son so that whoever believes in him should not die but have eternal life.
17 For God did not send his Son to judge the world, but that the world might be saved through him.
18 He who believes in him is not condemned; He who does not believe is already condemned, because he has not believed in the name of the only Son of God.
19 In this is the judgment: light has come into the world, and men preferred darkness to light, because their deeds were evil.
20 Everyone who does evil hates the light and does not approach it, for fear that his deeds will be discovered.
21 But he who works according to the truth draws near to the light, so that it may be evident that his works were done in God.
22 After this, Jesus went with his disciples to Judea. He remained there with them and baptized.
23 John continued to baptize in Aenon, near Salim, because there was a lot of water in that place and people came to be baptized.
24 John had not yet been imprisoned
25 A discussion then arose between John's disciples and a Jew about purification.
26 They went to John and said to him, "Teacher, he who was with you on the other side of the Jordan and of whom you have testified, also baptizes and everyone comes to him."
27 John answered, “No one can take credit for anything that he has not received from heaven.
28 You yourselves are witnesses that I said: "I am not the Messiah, but I have been sent before him."
29 At weddings, the one who marries is the husband; But the husband's friend, who is there and listens to him, is filled with joy when he hears his voice. That is why my joy is now perfect.
30 He must increase and I must decrease.
31 He who comes from above is above all. He who is of the earth belongs to the earth and speaks of the earth. The one who came from heaven
32 He testifies to what he has seen and heard, but no one receives his testimony.
33 He who receives his testimony certifies that God is true.
34 He whom God sent speaks the words of God, because God gives him the Spirit without measure.
35 The Father loves the Son and has put everything in his hands.
36 He who believes in the Son has eternal Life. He who refuses to believe in the Son will not see Life, but the wrath of God weighs on him.
1 When Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that he had more disciples and baptized more than John
2 –in reality he did not baptize, but his disciples–
3 He left Judea and returned to Galilee.
4 For that he had to go through Samaria.
5 He came to a city in Samaria called Sychar, near the land that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
6 There is Jacob's well. Jesus, tired from the journey, had sat down by the well. It was noon time.
7 A woman from Samaria went to draw water, and Jesus said to her, "Give me a drink."
8 His disciples had gone to the city to buy food.
9 The Samaritan woman answered him: “What! You, who are a Jew, ask me, a Samaritan, for a drink? The Jews, in fact, did not deal with the Samaritans.
10 Jesus answered her, "If you knew the gift of God and who it was that said to you, 'Give me a drink,' you yourself would have asked him, and he would have given you living water."
11 “Sir,” she said to him, “you have nothing to draw water from and the well is deep. Where do you get that living water?
12 Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well, where he drank, as well as his children and his animals?
13 Jesus answered her, "Whoever drinks this water will thirst again,
14 But whoever drinks the water that I will give him will never thirst again. The water that I will give him will become in him a spring that will flow to eternal Life.
15 "Sir," the woman said to him, "give me this water so that I won't be thirsty anymore and won't need to come here to draw it."
16 Jesus answered her, “Go, call your husband and come back here.”
17 The woman answered, “I have no husband.” Jesus continued: "You are right in saying that you have no husband,
18 because you have had five and the one you now have is not your husband; In that you have spoken the truth.
19 The woman said to him, “Lord, I see that you are a prophet.
20 Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you say that it is in Jerusalem that we should worship.
21 Jesus answered her, “Believe me, woman, the time is coming when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will the Father be worshiped.
22 You worship what you do not know; We worship what we know, because salvation comes from the Jews.
23 But the hour is coming, and has already come, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for those are the worshipers the Father wants.
24 God is a spirit, and those who worship him must do so in spirit and in truth.
25 The woman said to him, “I know that the Messiah, called Christ, must come. When he comes, he will announce everything to us.
26 Jesus answered him, "It is I who speak to you."
27 At that time his disciples arrived and were surprised to see him talking to a woman. However, no one asked him: "What do you want from her?" or "Why are you talking to her?"
28 The woman, leaving her water jar there, ran into the city and said to the people,
29 “Come see a man who told me everything I did. Will he not be the Messiah?
30 So they left the city and went to meet him.
31 Meanwhile, the disciples urged Jesus, saying, "Eat, Master."
32 But he said to them, "I have food to eat that you do not know."
33 The disciples asked each other, “Has someone brought him something to eat?”
34 Jesus answered them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to carry out his work.
35 You say that the harvest is still four months away. But I tell you: Lift your eyes and look at the fields: they are already ripening for the harvest.
36 Now the reaper receives his wages and gathers the grain for eternal Life; Thus he who sows and he who reaps share the same joy.
37 For in this the proverb is fulfilled: "One sows and another reaps."
38 And I sent you to harvest where you have not worked; Others have worked, and you reap the fruit of their efforts.
39 Many Samaritans in this city had believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified: "He told me everything I did."
40 Therefore, when the Samaritans came to Jesus, they begged him to stay with them, and he stayed there two days.
41 Many more believed in him because of his word.
42 And they said to the woman, “We no longer believe because of what you have said; "We ourselves have heard it and know that he is truly the Savior of the world."
43 After two days, Jesus left for Galilee.
44 He himself had declared that a prophet does not enjoy prestige among his own people.
45 But when he arrived, the Galileans welcomed him, because they had seen everything he had done in Jerusalem during the Passover; They too, in fact, had gone to the party.
46 And he went again to Cana of Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. There was a royal official there, who had his son sick in Capernaum.
47 When she heard that Jesus had arrived from Judea and was in Galilee, she went to him and begged him to come down and heal her dying son.
48 Jesus said to him, "If you do not see signs and wonders, you do not believe."
49 The official replied: "Sir, come down before my son dies."
50 “Go back to your house, your son lives,” Jesus said to him. The man believed the word that Jesus had told him and set out on his way.
51 As she was descending, her servants met her and announced that her son was alive.
52 He asked them what time he felt better. "Yesterday, at one in the afternoon, his fever went away," they replied.
53 The father remembered that it was the same time that Jesus had said to him: "Your son lives." And then he and all his family believed.
54 This was the second sign that Jesus did when he returned from Judea to Galilee.
1 After this, a festival of the Jews was celebrated, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem,
2 Next to the Sheep Gate in Jerusalem is a pool called Bethsata in Hebrew, which has five porches.
3 Under these porches lay a multitude of sick, blind, paralyzed, and crippled, waiting for the stirring of the water.
4 [Because the Angel of the Lord descended from time to time into the pool and moved the water. The first to enter the pool, after the water was agitated, was cured, whatever their illness.]
5 There was a man there who had been sick for thirty-eight years.
6 Seeing him lying there, and knowing that he had been like this for so long, Jesus asked him, "Do you want to be cured?"
7 He answered, “Lord, I have no one to immerse me in the pool when the water begins to stir; While I go, another descends first.
8 Jesus said to him, “Get up, take up your mat and walk.”
9 Immediately the man was healed, took up his mat and began to walk. It was a Saturday,
10 And the Jews then said to the one who had just been healed: “It is Saturday. You are not allowed to carry your stretcher.
11 He answered them, "He who healed me said to me, 'Take up your mat and walk.'
12 They asked him, "Who is this man who said to you, 'Take up your mat and walk?'"
13 But the sick man did not know it, because Jesus had disappeared into the crowd that was there.
14 Then Jesus found him in the Temple and said to him, “You have been healed; "Do not sin again, otherwise even worse things will happen to you."
15 The man went to tell the Jews that it was Jesus who had healed him.
16 They attacked Jesus, because he did those things on the Sabbath.
17 He answered them: "My Father always works, and I also work."
18 But for the Jews this was one more reason to kill him, because he not only violated the Sabbath, but also made himself equal to God, calling him their own Father.
19 Then Jesus spoke, saying, “I tell you the truth, the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father do; What the Father does, the Son also does.
20 Because the Father loves the Son and shows him everything he does. And he will show you even greater works, so that you will be amazed.
21 Just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so the Son gives life to whomever he wants.
22 For the Father judges no one: he has put all judgment into the hands of his Son,
23 so that everyone may honor the Son as they honor the Father. He who does not honor the Son, does not honor the Father who sent him.
24 Truly I say to you, whoever hears my word and believes in him who sent me has eternal life and is not subject to judgment, but has already passed from death to life.
25 Truly I say to you, the hour is approaching and has come when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God; and those who hear it will live.
26 Just as the Father disposes of Life, in the same way he has granted his Son to dispose of it,
27 and gave him authority to judge because he is the Son of man.
28 Do not be surprised: the hour is coming when all who are in the graves will hear his voice
29 and they will come out of them: those who have done good will rise to Life; Those who have done evil will be resurrected for judgment.
30 I can do nothing by myself. I judge according to what I hear, and my judgment is just, because what I seek is not to do my will, but that of him who sent me.
31 If I were to testify about myself, my testimony would be worthless.
32 But there is another who testifies about me, and I know that his testimony is true.
33 You yourselves sent to ask John, and he has testified to the truth.
34 It is not that I depend on the testimony of a man; If I say this it is for your salvation.
35 John was the lamp that burns and shines, and you wanted to enjoy his light for a moment.
36 But the testimony that I have is greater than that of John: they are the works that the Father commissioned me to carry out. These works that I do testify that my Father has sent me.
37 And the Father who sent me has testified about me. You have never heard his voice nor seen his face,
38 and his word does not remain in you, because you do not believe him whom he sent.
39 You examine the Scriptures, because in them you think you will find eternal Life: they testify about me,
40 and yet you do not want to come to me to have Life.
41 My glory does not come from men.
42 Furthermore, I know you: the love of God is not in you.
43 I have come in my Father's name and you do not receive me, but if another comes in his own name, you will receive him.
44 How can you believe, you who glorify one another and do not care about the glory that comes only from God?
45 Do not think that it is I who will accuse you before the Father; The one who will accuse you will be Moses, in whom you have placed your hope.
46 If you believed in Moses, you would also believe in me, because he has written about me.
47 But if you do not believe what he has written, how will you believe what I tell you?
1 After this, Jesus crossed the Sea of Galilee, called Tiberias.
2 A large crowd followed him, seeing the signs he did in healing the sick.
3 Jesus went up the mountain and sat there with his disciples.
4 The Passover, the Jewish festival, was approaching.
5 When Jesus looked up, he saw a large crowd coming to him and said to Philip, "Where can we buy bread to feed them?"
6 He said this to test him, because he knew well what he was going to do.
7 Philip answered him, "Two hundred denarii would not be enough for each one to eat a piece of bread."
8 One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, said to him:
9 "Here is a boy who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what is this for so many people?"
10 Jesus answered him, “Make them sit down.” There was a lot of grass in that place. They all sat down and there were one five thousand men.
11 Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed them to those who were sitting. He did the same with the fish, giving them everything they wanted.
12 When everyone was satisfied, Jesus said to his disciples, “Pick up the pieces that are left over, so that nothing is lost.”
13 They gathered them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces left over from the five barley loaves.
14 Seeing the sign that Jesus had just done, the people said, "This is truly the Prophet who must come into the world."
15 Jesus, knowing that they wanted to seize him to make him king, withdrew again to the mountain alone.
16 In the evening his disciples went down to the seashore
17 and they embarked to go to Capernaum, which is on the other side. It was already night and Jesus had not yet joined them.
18 The sea was rough, because a strong wind was blowing.
19 When they had rowed about three miles, they saw Jesus approaching the boat walking on the water, and they were afraid.
20 He said to them, "It is I, do not be afraid."
21 They wanted to take him into the boat, but it immediately touched land at the place where they were going.
22 The next day, the crowd that had remained on the other side saw that Jesus had not gone up with his disciples in the only boat there, but that they had left alone.
23 Meanwhile, some boats from Tiberias docked near the place where they had eaten the bread, after the Lord had given thanks.
24 When the crowd realized that Jesus and his disciples were not there, they got into boats and went to Capernaum in search of Jesus.
25 When they found him on the other side, they asked him, “Teacher, when did you arrive?”
26 Jesus answered them, “I tell you the truth, you are looking for me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate bread to your fill.
27 Work not for perishable food, but for that which endures to eternal Life, which the Son of Man will give you; for it is he whom God, the Father, marked with his seal.
28 They asked him, “What must we do to do the works of God?”
29 Jesus answered them, "God's work is for you to believe in the one he has sent."
30 And they asked him again: “What signs do you do so that we may see and believe in you? What work do you do?
31 Our fathers ate manna in the desert, as the Scripture says: He gave them bread that came down from heaven to eat.
32 Jesus answered, “I tell you the truth, it is not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven; my Father gives you the true bread from heaven;
33 because the bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.
34 They said to him, "Lord, always give us this bread."
35 Jesus answered them: “I am the bread of Life. He who comes to me will never hunger; He who believes in me will never thirst.
36 But I have already told you: you have seen me and yet you do not believe.
37 Everything that the Father gives me comes to me, and whoever comes to me I will not reject,
38 For I have come down from heaven, not to do my will, but that of him who sent me.
39 The will of him who sent me is that I should not lose anything that he gave me, but should raise it up on the last day.
40 This is the will of my Father: that he who sees the Son and believes in him may have eternal life, and that I may raise him up on the last day.
41 The Jews murmured at him, because he had said, "I am the bread that came down from heaven."
42 And they said, "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph? We know his father and mother. How can he say now: "I have come down from heaven"?
43 Jesus spoke and said to them, “Do not murmur among yourselves.
44 No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him; and I will raise him up on the last day.
45 It is written in the book of the Prophets: "All will be taught by God." Everyone who heard the Father and receives his teaching comes to me.
46 No one has ever seen the Father except he who comes from God: he alone has seen the Father.
47 I tell you the truth, he who believes has eternal life.
48 I am the bread of Life.
49 Their fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and died.
50 But this is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that he who eats it may not die.
51 I am the living bread that came down from heaven. "Whoever eats this bread will live forever, and the bread that I will give is my flesh for the Life of the world."
52 The Jews argued among themselves, saying, "How can this man give us his flesh to eat?"
53 Jesus answered them, “I tell you the truth, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you will have no life in you.
54 He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
55 For my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink.
56 He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him.
57 Just as I, who was sent by the Father who has Life, live because of the Father, so he who eats me will live because of me.
58 This is the bread that came down from heaven; not like the one their fathers ate and died. "Whoever eats this bread will live forever."
59 Jesus taught all this in the synagogue of Capernaum.
60 After hearing it, many of his disciples said, “This language is harsh! Who can hear it?
61 Jesus, knowing what his disciples were murmuring, said to them, “Does this offend you?
62 What will happen then, when you see the Son of Man ascend where he was before?
63 The Spirit is the one who gives Life, the flesh is of no use. The words I told you are Spirit and Life.
64 But there are some among you who do not believe. In fact, Jesus knew from the first moment who were those who did not believe and who was the one who was going to betray him.
65 And he added: "That is why I have told you that no one can come to me unless the Father grants it to him."
66 From that moment on, many of his disciples distanced themselves from him and stopped accompanying him.
67 Jesus then asked the Twelve: "Do you also want to leave?"
68 Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have words of eternal Life.
69 We have believed and know that you are the Holy One of God.
70 Jesus continued: “Am I not the one who chose you, the Twelve? However, one of you is a demon.
71 Jesus spoke of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve, the one who was going to betray him.
1 After this, Jesus traveled through Galilee; He did not want to travel through Judea because the Jews were trying to kill him.
2 The Jewish festival of Huts was approaching,
3 and his brothers said to him, “Do not stay here; Go to Judea, so that your disciples there may also see the works you do.
4 When one wants to make himself known, he does not act in secret; Since you do these things, manifest yourself to the world.
5 In fact, not even his own brothers believed in him.
6 Jesus said to them, “My time has not yet come, but any time is good for you.
7 The world does not have to hate you; He hates me, because I testify against him that his works are evil.
8 Go up to the party. "I'm not going up to that party, because my time has not yet come to an end."
9 After telling them this, he remained in Galilee.
10 However, when his brothers went up to the feast, he also went up, but secretly, without being seen.
11 The Jews looked for him during the festival and said, "Where is that one?"
12 Jesus was the comment of the crowd. Some said: "He is a good man." Others, however, said: "No, it deceives the people."
13 However, no one spoke about him openly, for fear of the Jews.
14 Halfway through the celebration of the festival, Jesus went up to the Temple and began to teach.
15 The Jews were amazed and said, "How do you know the Scriptures without having studied?"
16 Jesus answered them, “My teaching is not mine but his who sent me.
17 He who wants to do the will of God will know if this teaching is from God or if I speak on my own.
18 He who speaks on his own behalf seeks his own glory, but he who seeks the glory of him who sent him speaks the truth and there is nothing false in him.
19 Did not Moses give them the Law? But none of you fulfill it. Why do they want to kill me?
20 The crowd responded, “You are possessed by the devil: who wants to kill you?”
21 Jesus continued: “Because of one work that I did, you are amazed.
22 Moses gave you circumcision – although it does not come from Moses, but from the patriarchs – and you also practice it on the Sabbath.
23 If a man is circumcised on the Sabbath so as not to break the Law of Moses, how are you angry with me because I have completely healed a man on the Sabbath?
24 Do not judge according to appearances, but according to righteousness.
25 Some in Jerusalem said, “Isn't this the one they wanted to kill?
26 And look how he speaks openly and no one says anything to him! Have the authorities recognized that he is truly the Messiah?
27 But we know where this one is from; But when the Messiah comes, no one will know where he is from.

28 Then Jesus, who was teaching in the Temple, exclaimed, “So you know me and where I am from? However, I did not come of my own accord; but the one who sent me tells the truth,
and you don't know him.
29 I do know him, because I came from him and he is the one who sent me.
30 Then they wanted to arrest him, but no one laid hands on him, because his time had not yet come.
31 Many in the crowd believed in him and said, "When the Messiah comes, will he be able to do more signs than this man does?"
32 The Pharisees heard what the people were saying about him, and they sent guards to arrest him.
33 Then Jesus said, "I will be with you for a little while, and I will go to him who sent me."
34 You will look for me and not find me, because you cannot come where I am.”
35 The Jews said among themselves, “Where will he go so that we cannot find him? Will he go to join the Jews scattered among the pagans, to teach the pagans?
36 What did he mean by these words: "You will look for me and you will not find me, and you cannot come where I am"?
37 On the last day, the most solemn day of the festival, Jesus stood up and exclaimed, “Whoever is thirsty, let him come to me; and drink
38 he who believes in me. As the Scripture says: "Out of his womb will flow springs of living water."
39 He was referring to the Spirit that those who believed in him were to receive. For the Spirit had not yet been given, since Jesus had not yet been glorified.
40 Some of the crowd who had heard it said, "This is truly the Prophet."
41 Others said, "This is the Messiah." But others asked: "Will the Messiah come from Galilee?"
42 Does not the Scripture say that the Messiah will come from the lineage of David and from Bethlehem, the town where David was from?
43 And because of him, there was a division among the people.
44 Some wanted to stop him, but no one laid hands on him.
45 The guards went to the chief priests and the Pharisees, and they asked them, "Why didn't you bring him?"
46 They answered, “No one ever spoke like this man.”
47 The Pharisees answered, “Were you also deceived?
48 Has any of the leaders or the Pharisees believed in him?
49 On the other hand, those people who do not know the Law are cursed.
50 Nicodemus, one of them, who had come to see Jesus, said to them:
51 "Does our Law allow us to judge a man without first listening to him to know what he did?"
52 They answered him, “Are you also a Galilean? Examine the Scriptures and you will see that no prophet arises from Galilee.
53 And each one returned to his house.
1 Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
2 At dawn he returned to the Temple, and all the people came to him. Then he sat down and began to teach them.
3 The scribes and the Pharisees brought to him a woman who had been caught in adultery, and placing her in the middle of everyone,
4 They said to Jesus: “Teacher, this woman has been caught in flagrant adultery.
5 Moses, in the Law, commanded us to stone this class of women. And you, what do you say?
6 They said this to test him, so that they could accuse him. But Jesus, bending down, began to write on the ground with his finger.
7 When they insisted, he stood up and said to them, "Let him who is without sin cast the first stone."
8 And bowing down again, he continued writing on the ground.
9 When they heard these words, they all left, one after another, beginning with the oldest. Jesus was left alone with the woman, who remained there,
10 And standing up, he asked her, “Woman, where are your accusers? Has anyone condemned you?
11 She answered him, “No one, Lord.” «I don't condemn you either, Jesus said to him. Go, sin no more from now on.
12 Jesus spoke to them once again, saying: “I am the light of the world. "He who follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of Life."
13 The Pharisees said to him, "You testify about yourself: your testimony is worthless."
14 Jesus answered them, “Although I testify about myself, my testimony is valid because I know where I came from and where I am going; but you don't know where I come from or where I'm going.
15 You judge according to the flesh; I don't judge anyone,
16 And if I do, my judgment is valid because it is not I alone who judges, but I and the Father who sent me.
17 In your Law it is written that the testimony of two people is valid.
18 I bear witness of myself, and the Father who sent me also bears witness of me.
19 They asked him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered: “You do not know me or my Father; If you knew me, you would also know my Father.

22 The Jews asked themselves: "Will he think of killing himself to say: 'Where I am going, you cannot go'?"

24 Therefore I have said to you, "You will die in your sins." For if you do not believe that I Am, you will die in your sins.

30 While he spoke thus, many believed in him.
31 Jesus said to those Jews who believed in him: “If you remain faithful to my word, you will truly be my disciples:

35 The slave does not remain in the house forever; the son, however, remains forever.
36 Therefore, if the Son sets you free, you will truly be free.
37 I know that you are descendants of Abraham, but you try to kill me because my word does not penetrate you.
38 I say what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have learned from your father.
39 They replied, "Our father is Abraham." And Jesus said to them: “If you were Abraham's children, you would act like him.
40 But now they want to kill me, the man who tells them the truth that he has heard from God. Abraham didn't do that.
41 But you act like your father. They told him: “We were not born of prostitution; We have only one Father, who is God. Jesus continued:
42 «If God were your Father, you would love me, because I came from God and came from him. I have not come of myself, but he sent me.
43 Why don't you understand my language? It is because they cannot hear my word.

44 You have the devil as your father and you want to fulfill your father's wishes. From the beginning he was a murderer and has nothing to do with the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies,
He speaks according to what he is, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
45 But you don't believe me, because I tell you the truth.
46 Which of you will prove that I have sin? And if I tell you the truth. why don't you believe me?
47 He who belongs to God listens to the words of God; If you do not listen to them, it is because they are not from God.
48 The Jews replied, "Aren't we right in saying that you are a Samaritan and possessed by a demon?" Jesus answered:
49 “I am not possessed by a demon, but I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.
50 I do not seek my glory; There is someone who looks for her, and he is the one who judges.
51 I tell you the truth, whoever is faithful to my word will never die."
52 The Jews said to him, “Now we are sure that you are demon-possessed. Abraham died, the prophets too, and you say: "He who is faithful to my word will never die."
53 Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets also died. Who do you pretend to be?
54 Jesus answered, “If I glorified myself, my glory would be worth nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, the same one you call "our God,"
55 and whom, however, they do not know. I know him and if I said: "I don't know him," I would be, like you, a liar. But I know him and I am faithful to his word.
56 Abraham, your father, trembled with joy, waiting to see my Day: he saw it and was filled with joy.
57 The Jews said to him, "You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham?"
58 Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth, before Abraham was born, I AM."

1 As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth.
2 His disciples asked him, “Teacher, who sinned, he or his parents, that he was born blind?”
3 «Neither he nor his parents have sinned, Jesus answered; He was born this way so that the works of God could be manifested in him.
4 We must work on the works of him who sent me, while it is day; The night comes, when no one can work.
5 While I am in the world, I am the light of the world."
6 After he had said this, he spit on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and put it on the blind man's eyes.
7 saying to him, “Go wash in the pool of Siloam,” which means “Sent.” The blind man went, washed, and when he returned he could see.
8 The neighbors and those who had seen him begging before asked, "Isn't this the one who sat and begged?"

goes.

see."

21 When a woman is about to give birth, she feels anguish because her time has come; But when the child is born, he forgets his pain, because of the joy he feels when he sees that a man has come into the world.

1 After speaking thus, Jesus raised his eyes to heaven, saying, “Father, the hour has come: glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you,
2 since you gave him authority over all men, so that he would give eternal Life to all those whom you have given.
3 This is eternal Life: that they may know you, the only true God, and your Messenger, Jesus Christ.

5 Now, Father, glorify me with you, with the glory that I had with you before the world existed.

7 Now they know that everything you have given me comes from you,
8 because I told them the words that you gave me: they have truly recognized that I came from you, and they have believed that you sent me.

17 Consecrate them in the truth: your word is truth.
18 Just as you sent me into the world, I also send you into the world.
19 For their sake I consecrate myself, so that they also may be consecrated in the truth.
20 I pray not only for them, but also for those who, thanks to their word, will believe in me.
21 May they all be one: just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, may they also be one in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.
22 I have given them the glory that you gave me, so that they may be one, as we are one
23 –I in them and you in me– so that they may be perfectly one and the world may know that you have sent me, and that I loved them as you loved me.

15 They shouted, “Let him die! Let him die! Crucify him! Pilate said to them, "Am I going to crucify your king?" The chief priests answered: "We have no other king but the
Caesar.

because it was made of a single piece from top to bottom,

the soldiers did.

during the Sabbath, because that Saturday was very solemn.

1 Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been taken away.

look for it."

1 After this, Jesus appeared again to the disciples on the shores of the Sea of Tiberias. It happened like this:

"I love you." Jesus said to him: “Feed my sheep.

18 Truly I tell you, when you were young you dressed yourself and went wherever you wanted. But when you are old, you will stretch out your arms, and another will bind you and take you where you do not want to go.

are you going to deliver?

Does it matter?

1 In my first Book, dear Theophilus, I referred to everything that Jesus did and taught, from the beginning,

11 who said to them, “Men of Galilee, why do you keep looking at heaven? This Jesus who has been taken from you and taken up into heaven will come in the same way that you have seen him.
leave."

14 All of them, closely united, dedicated themselves to prayer, in the company of some women, Mary, the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.

24 And they prayed thus: "Lord, you who know the hearts of all, show us which of the two you chose

1 When the day of Pentecost arrived, they were all gathered in the same place.
2 Suddenly, a noise came from heaven, like a strong gust of wind, which echoed throughout the house where they were.
3 Then they saw tongues like fire appear and descend separately on each of them.

5 There were devout Jews in Jerusalem, coming from all the nations of the world.
6 When this noise was heard, the crowd gathered and was filled with astonishment, because each one heard them speaking in their own language.

8 How is it that each of us hears them in his own language?
9 Parthians, Medes, and Elamites, we who live in Mesopotamia or in Judea itself, in Cappadocia, in Pontus, and in Asia Minor,
10 In Phrygia and Pamphylia, in Egypt, in Libya Cyrenaica, the pilgrims from Rome,
11 Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs, we all hear them proclaiming in our languages the wonders of God.
12 They said to each other in astonishment, “What does this mean?”
13 Some mockingly commented, "They have had too much wine."
14 Then Peter, standing up with the Eleven, raised his voice and said, “Men of Judea and all who live in Jerusalem, pay attention, for I am going to explain to you what has happened.
15 These men are not drunk, as you suppose, since it is only nine in the morning,
16 but what the prophet Joel said is being fulfilled:
17 "In the last days, says the Lord, I will pour out my Spirit on all men and their sons and their daughters will prophesy; the young men will see visions and the old men will have prophetic dreams.
18 Furthermore, I will pour out my Spirit on my male and female servants, and they will prophesy.
19 I will do wonders in heaven above, and signs on earth below: you will see blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
