22 Israelites, listen: To Jesus of Nazareth, the man whom God accredited to you by performing miracles, wonders and signs that everyone knows,
23 You put to death that man who had been delivered according to God's plan and foresight, nailing him to the cross through the unbelievers.
24 But God raised him up, freeing him from the pangs of death, because it was not possible for her to have dominion over him.
25 In fact, referring to him, David said: "I constantly saw the Lord before me, for he is at my right hand so that I may not waver.
26 Therefore my heart rejoices and my tongue sings with joy. My body will also rest in hope,
27 for you will not give my soul to the Abyss, nor will you let your servant suffer corruption.
28 "You have made me know the ways of life and you will fill me with joy in your presence."
29 Brethren, let me tell you frankly that the patriarch David died and was buried, and his tomb is preserved among us to this day.
30 But since he was a prophet, he knew that God had sworn to him that one of his descendants would sit on his throne.

32 God raised this Jesus from the dead, and we are all witnesses.
33 Exalted by the power of God, he received the promised Holy Spirit from the Father, and has communicated it as you see and hear.
34 For it is not David who ascended into heaven; On the contrary, he himself affirms: "The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand,
35 until I put all your enemies under your feet."
36 Therefore, all the people of Israel must recognize that God has made this Jesus whom you crucified, Lord and Messiah.
37 When they heard these things, everyone was deeply moved, and said to Peter and the other Apostles: “Brothers, what should we do?”
38 Peter answered them, “Convert and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ so that your sins may be forgiven, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
39 For the promise has been made to you and to your children, and to all those who are far off, as many as the Lord our God wills to call.
40 And with many other arguments he testified to them and exhorted them to be safe from this perverse generation.
41 Those who received his word were baptized; and that day about three thousand joined them.
42 Everyone gathered regularly to listen to the teaching of the Apostles and participate in common life, in the breaking of bread and in prayers.
43 A holy fear took hold of them all, because the Apostles performed many wonders and signs.
44 All the believers remained united and put what they had in common:
45 They sold their property and goods, and distributed the money among themselves, according to each one's needs.
46 Intimately united, they frequented the Temple daily, broke bread in their homes, and ate together with joy and simplicity of heart;

1 On one occasion, Peter and John were going up to the Temple for evening prayer.
2 There they found a man paralyzed from birth, who was placed daily by the door of the Temple called "the Beautiful" to ask for alms from those who entered.

13 They also cannot prove to you what they accuse me of now.
14 But I do confess to you that I serve the God of my fathers, following the Way that my accusers consider a sect. I believe in everything that is contained in the Law and written in the Prophets,
15 and I have the same hope in God that they have: the hope that there will be a resurrection of the righteous and sinners.
16 That is why I always try to maintain a blameless conscience before God and men.
17 After a few years, I came to bring alms to my countrymen and to present offerings.
18 This is how some Jews from the province of Asia found me in the Temple: I had purified myself and was not causing any kind of riot or tumult.
19 They are the ones who should have come before you to accuse me, if they had any complaint against me.
20 At least let those here tell what crime they found me guilty of when I appeared before the Sanhedrin.
21 Unless it is the only thing I said, standing among them: "Today you judge me because of the resurrection of the dead."
22 Felix, who was very well informed about everything concerning the Way of the Lord, postponed the cause, saying: "When the tribune Lysias comes down from Jerusalem, I will decide on this matter."
23 Then he ordered the centurion to guard Paul, but leaving him a certain freedom and without preventing his friends from attending to him.
24 A few days later, Felix showed up with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Jesus Christ.

25 But when Paul began to discuss justice, continence, and future judgment, Felix, full of fear, answered him: “For now you can go; I will call you again at the first
occasion."
26 At the same time, he expected Paul to give him money, and so he called him frequently to talk with him.
27 After two years, Porcius Festus succeeded Felix; and since he wanted to ingratiate himself with the Jews, he left Paul in prison.
1 Three days after he had taken charge of his province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
2 The chief priests and the leading Jews then accused Paul in his presence,
3 and they asked him for the favor of having him transferred to Jerusalem. In reality they were preparing an ambush to kill him on the way.
4 But Festus replied that Paul must be taken into custody in Caesarea, and that he himself would go there immediately.
5 "Let those in authority among you, he added, come with me and present your accusation, if you have anything against him."
6 Festus stayed in Jerusalem about eight or ten days, and then went down to Caesarea. The next day, he sat down in court and had Paul appear.
7 As soon as he arrived, the Jews who had come from Jerusalem surrounded him and brought numerous and serious accusations against him that they could not prove.
8 Paul defended himself by saying: "I have not committed any offense against the Law of the Jews, nor against the Temple, nor against the Emperor."
9 Festus, wanting to win favor with the Jews, went to Paul and said, "Do you want to go up to Jerusalem to be judged there in my presence?"
10 Paul answered, “I am before the Emperor's court, and this is where I must be judged. I did no harm to the Jews, as you know perfectly well.

11 If I am guilty and have committed a crime that deserves death, I do not refuse to die, but if the accusations that the Jews make against me are unfounded, no one has the right to
give myself to them. I appeal to the Emperor.
12 Festus, after having consulted with his Council, replied: "Since you appealed to the Emperor, you will appear before him."
13 A few days later, King Agrippa and Berenice arrived in Caesarea and went to greet Festus.
14 As they remained several days, Festus explained Paul's case to the king, saying, "Felix has left a prisoner,
15 And during my stay in Jerusalem, the high priests and elders of the Jews presented complaints asking for his condemnation.
16 I answered them that the Romans do not have the custom of handing over a man before confronting him with his accusers and giving him the opportunity to defend himself.
17 They came here, and without any delay, I sat down in court and had that man appear the next day.
18 But when his accusers came forward, they did not bring any of the charges against him that I suspected.
19 What there was between them were I don't know what discussions about their religion, and about a certain Jesus who died and whom Paul claims is alive.
20 Not knowing exactly what side to take in a matter of this kind, I asked Paul if he wanted to go to Jerusalem to be judged there.
21 But since he appealed to the judgment of His Imperial Majesty, I ordered that he be left in custody until I sent him to the Emperor.
22 Agrippa then said to Festus, "I too would like to listen to that man." "Tomorrow you will hear it," replied Festus.

23 The next day, Agrippa and Berenice arrived with great pomp and entered the audience hall, surrounded by the tribunes and the most important men of the city. At an order from Festus,
They brought Paul.

24 Festus spoke, saying, "King Agrippa and all who are present here, you see this man, for whom the entire Jewish community has come to see me, both here and in Jerusalem,
insisting loudly that he should not be allowed to live any longer.
25 I have found nothing in him worthy of death; but since he himself has appealed to the Emperor, I have decided to send it to him.
26 Since I have nothing precise to write about him to the Sovereign, I made him appear before you, especially before you, King Agrippa; So, after this interrogation, I will have something to report.
27 Because it seems absurd to me to send a prisoner, without at the same time indicating the charges against him.
1 Agrippa said to Paul, “You are authorized to defend yourself.” Then Paul, stretching out his hand, began his defense, saying:
2 «King Agrippa, I consider myself happy to have to defend myself today, before you, against the accusations made against me by the Jews,
3 for you know all the customs and controversies of the Jews. That's why I ask you to listen to me patiently.
4 All Jews know how I have lived from the first days of my youth, among my people and in Jerusalem itself.
5 They have known me for a long time and if they want, they can attest that I have lived as a Pharisee, that is, following the most rigid sect of our religion.
6 And if I am now brought to trial, it is because of my hope in the promise made by God to our fathers,
7 the promise that our twelve tribes hope to see fulfilled, serving God fervently day and night. Accuse this hope, King Agrippa, I am accused by the Jews.
8 Why do you find it incredible that God raises the dead?
9 I, for my part, considered that I should combat the name of Jesus of Nazareth by all means.
10 This is what I did in Jerusalem: I myself imprisoned a large number of saints with the permission of the high priests, and when they were sentenced to death, my vote was favorable.
11 He frequently visited the synagogues and punished them to force them to renounce their faith. Full of rage against them, he persecuted them even in foreign cities.
12 Once, when I was going to Damascus with full powers and with the order of the high priests,
13 On the way, towards noon, I saw a light brighter than the sun, coming from heaven and surrounding me and those who accompanied me.
14 We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me in Hebrew: “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? You hurt yourself by kicking against the sting.
15 I answered, “Who are you, Lord?” And he said to me: «I am Jesus, whom you persecute.
16 Arise and stand, for I have appeared to you to be a minister and witness of the things you have seen and of those in which I will appear to you.
17 I will deliver you from the Jews and the pagan nations. I send you to them

18 that you may open their eyes, and that they may turn from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to the true God, and through faith in me may obtain forgiveness of sins and their share in the
inheritance of the saints.
19 From that moment on, King Agrippa, I was never unfaithful to that heavenly vision.

20 On the contrary, speaking first to the inhabitants of Damascus, then to those of Jerusalem and the whole country of Judea, and finally to the pagans, I preached to them that they must repent and
convert to God, manifesting his conversion with works.
21 Because of all this, the Jews detained me in the Temple and tried to kill me.

22 But with God's protection, I have been able to continue giving testimony to the small and the great to this day. And I never said anything outside of what the Prophets and Moses announced would happen,
23 that is, that the Messiah had to suffer and that, being the first to rise from the dead, he would announce the light to our people and to the pagans.
24 When Paul reached this point in his defense, Festus said out loud, “You are crazy, Paul; "Your excessive study has made you lose your mind."
25 To which Paul replied: “I am not mad, most excellent Festus, but I speak the truth and speak wisely.
26 The king is aware of all these things, so I turn to him with complete confidence: I do not believe that he is unaware of any of this, because these are not things that happened in a hidden place.
27 Do you believe in the prophets, King Agrippa? I know you believe in them.
28 Agrippa answered Paul: "A little more, and you will convince me to become a Christian!"
29 “It doesn't matter whether it takes a little or a lot to achieve it, said Paul. May God grant that not only you, but all those who listen to me today, become like me..., but without these chains!
30 Then the king stood up, as did the governor, Berenice, and those who were with them.
31 As they left, they commented to each other, "This man has done nothing that deserves death or imprisonment."
32 And Agrippa said to Festus: "He might be set free, if he himself had appealed to the Emperor."
1 When it was decided that we should embark for Italy, Paul and other prisoners were entrusted to a centurion of the imperial cohort, named Julius.
2 We boarded a ship from Adramicio that was bound for the coasts of Asia, and we set sail. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
3 The next day we arrived in Sidon. Julio treated Pablo with great consideration and allowed him to go see his friends and be cared for by them.
4 From there, we left and sailed to the shelter of the island of Cyprus, because contrary winds were blowing;
5 Then, crossing the sea of ​​Cilicia and Pamphylia, we arrived at Mira of Lycia.
6 There, the centurion found an Alexandrian ship that was going to sail for Italy, and he made us board it.
7 For several days we sailed slowly and, with difficulty, reached Cnidus. As the wind was unfavorable, we sailed to the shelter of the island of Crete towards Cape Salmoné,
8 and after having skirted it with great difficulty, we arrived at a point called Buenos Puertos, near the city of Lasea.
9 Enough time had already passed and navigation was becoming dangerous, because the time of the solemn Fast had passed. Then Paul warned them:
10 "Friends, I see that navigation will not be able to continue without risk and without serious losses, not only for the cargo and the ship, but also for our own lives."
11 But the centurion trusted the captain and the master of the ship more than in Paul's words;

12 and since the port was not suitable for wintering, the majority thought that it was better to leave and reach Phenice as soon as possible, a port in Crete that faces the southwest and northwest, to spend the winter there.
winter.
13 At that precise moment, a southerly breeze arose and they believed that they could carry out this project. They set sail and began to skirt the island of Crete.
14 But very soon a hurricane called Euraquilon was unleashed, coming from the island.
15 Since the boat could not resist the wind, it was carried away and we let ourselves drift.
16 Sailing under the cover of a small island, called Cauda, we barely managed to pick up the lifeboat.

17 After raising it, the reinforcement cables were used to secure the ship's hull. Then, for fear of running aground on the banks of Sirtes, the anchor was lowered, leaving it loose,
and so we drift.
18 The next day, as the storm was still raging, the sailors began to dump the cargo.
19 On the third day, they put the ship's rigging into the water with their own hands.
20 For several days neither the sun nor the stars had been seen, and the storm continued with the same violence, so that we had already lost all hope of salvation.

21 Since we had not eaten for a long time, Paul, standing in the middle of everyone, said to them: "Friends, you should have listened to me: if we had not left Crete, we would have been spared this risk and these
serious losses.
22 In any case, I beg you to have courage because none of you will perish; only the ship will be lost.
23 This night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve appeared to me,
24 and he said to me, “Do not be afraid, Paul. You must appear before the Emperor and God grants you the lives of all those who sail with you.
25 Therefore, friends, have courage. I trust that God will fulfill what he has told me.
26 But we will have to run aground against an island.
27 On the fourteenth night, we were still drifting along the Adriatic, when towards midnight, the sailors sensed the approach of dry land.

28 They took the probe into the sea and found that there was a depth of around thirty-six meters. A little further on, they kicked it out again and saw that there were some
twenty-seven meters.
29 Fearing that we were going to hit some rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern, anxiously awaiting dawn.
30 The sailors tried to escape from the ship, throwing the lifeboat into the sea, under the pretext of releasing the bow anchors.
31 But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "If these sailors do not remain on board, you will not be saved."
32 Then the soldiers cut the boat's ropes and let it fall.
33 While we were waiting for dawn, Paul advised everyone to eat something, saying, “You have been waiting for fourteen days without eating anything.
34 I advise you to eat something, because you are exposing your health. No one will lose a single hair on his head."
35 After he had said this, he took bread, thanked God in front of everyone, broke it, and began to eat.
36 The others cheered up and also began to eat.
37 There were a total of two hundred and seventy-six people on board.
38 Once they were satisfied, they began to lighten the ship by throwing the wheat into the sea.
39 When morning dawned, the sailors did not recognize the coast; They only saw a bay with a beach, and they did everything possible to take the ship in that direction.
40 They loosed the anchors and let them fall into the sea; At the same time, they loosened the rudder ropes. Then they spread the mainsail to the wind and headed towards the beach.
41 But they hit a sandbank and remained motionless, while the stern was dissolved by the violence of the waves.
42 Then the soldiers decided to kill the prisoners, for fear that some would escape by swimming.
43 But the centurion, who wanted to save Paul, prevented them from doing so, and ordered those who knew how to swim to jump into the sea first to reach land.
44 The rest would do it using boards or the remains of the ship. Thus everyone reached land safe and sound.

1 When we were safe, we found out that it was called Malta. 2 Its inhabitants showed us an unusual cordiality and welcomed us all around a
big fire that they had lit because of the rain and the cold.
3 Paul gathered some dry branches and threw them into the fire. The heat brought out a snake that coiled around his hand.

4 When the inhabitants of the place saw the reptile coiled in his hand, they began to say among themselves: "This man is surely a murderer: he has been saved from the sea, and now divine justice does not allow him."
allows us to survive."
5 But he threw the snake into the fire and no harm came to him.
6 They expected him to swell up or drop dead. After a long time, seeing that nothing was happening to him, they changed their minds and said: "He is a god."
7 There was an estate nearby belonging to the ruler of the island, named Publius. He welcomed us and provided us with cordial hospitality for three days.
8 Publius's father was in bed with fever and dysentery. Paul went to see him, prayed, laid his hands on him and healed him.
9 Following this, the other sick people on the island came forward and were healed.
10 They then showered us with all kinds of attention and when we embarked, they provided us with everything we needed.
11 After three months we embarked on a ship that had remained on the island during the winter; It was an Alexandrian ship that had the insignia of Castor and Pollux.
12 We stopped at Syracuse, where we stayed three days.
13 From there, skirting the coast we arrived at Reggio. The next day a south wind arose, and in two days we reached Pozzuoli,
14 where we found some brothers who invited us to stay with them for a week. Then we arrived in Rome.

15 The brothers of this city, we informed of our arrival, came out to meet us and overtook us at the height of the "Forum of Appius" and at the "Three Taverns." Paul, when he saw them, gave thanks to God and
he felt comforted.
16 When we arrived in Rome, he received permission to stay in a private house with a soldier to guard him.

17 Three days later he called together the leading Jews, and when they were assembled he said to them: “Brothers, without having done anything against the people or against the customs of our fathers, I was arrested in
Jerusalem and placed in the hands of the Romans.
18 After questioning me, they wanted to release me, because they found nothing in me that deserved death;
19 But faced with the opposition of the Jews, I was forced to appeal to the Emperor, without wanting to accuse my people of anything.
20 That is why I wanted to see them and speak to them, since because of the hope of Israel I wear these chains.
21 They answered him, “We have not received any letters from Judea concerning you, and none of the brothers who came have told us anything that is unfavorable to you.
22 But now we would like to hear you explain what you think, because we know that this sect is opposed everywhere.

23 So they fixed a day to meet him, and went in greater numbers to see him at the place where he was staying. Paul spoke to them all day long about the Kingdom of God, giving them all kinds of
testimony and trying to persuade them to believe in Jesus Christ,
starting from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
24 Some were convinced by his words, but others refused to believe,

25 And as they left without having come to an agreement, Paul said this single sentence: "The words that the Holy Spirit spoke to your parents are very true, for
through the prophet Isaiah:
26 "Go tell this people: No matter how much they hear, they will not understand, no matter how much they see, they will not know,

27 Because the heart of this people has been hardened, they have stopped their ears and closed their eyes, for fear lest their eyes see, their ears hear, their heart understand,
convert, and may I heal you."
28 Know then that this salvation of God is going to be announced to the pagans. "They will listen to it."
29 [When the Jews heard these words, they withdrew, arguing heatedly.]
30 Paul lived two whole years on his own, welcoming everyone who wanted to see him,
31 proclaiming the Kingdom of God, and teaching with complete freedom and without encountering any obstacles, what concerns the Lord Jesus Christ.
1 Letter of Paul, servant of Jesus Christ, called the Apostle, and chosen to announce the Good News of God,
2 which he had promised through his prophets in the Holy Scriptures,
3 concerning his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, born of the seed of David according to the flesh,
4 and constituted Son of God with power according to the sanctifying Spirit by his resurrection from the dead.
5 Through him we have received grace and the apostolic mission, to lead all pagan peoples to the obedience of faith, for the glory of his Name,
6 among whom are you also, who have been called by Jesus Christ.
7 To all who are in Rome, loved by God, called to be saints, may grace and peace come from God, our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
8 First of all, I thank my God through Jesus Christ, because of all of you, because your faith is praised throughout the world.
9 God, to whom I pay spiritual worship announcing the Good News of his Son, is witness that I constantly remember them,
10 always asking in my prayers that I may find, God willing, the favorable occasion to go visit them.
11 For I have a great desire to see you, that I may give you some gift of the Spirit that may strengthen you,
12 or rather, that we may comfort each other through the faith we have in common.

13 Brothers, I want you to know that many times I tried to visit you to collect some fruit also among you, as I have collected in other pagan towns; but until now I haven't
could do it.
14 I owe myself both to the Greeks and to those who are not, to the wise and to the ignorant.
15 Hence my burning desire to announce the Good News also to you, those who live in Rome.
16 I am not ashamed of the Gospel, because it is the power of God for the salvation of all who believe: for the Jews first, and then for those who are not.
17 In the Gospel the righteousness of God is revealed, by faith and for faith, according to what the Scripture says: The just will live by faith.
18 Indeed, the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against the impiety and injustice of men, who by their injustice hold the truth prisoner.
19 For everything that can be known about God is evident to them: God himself made it known to them,

20 since his invisible attributes – his eternal power and his divinity – have been made visible to the eyes of intelligence, since the creation of the world, through his works. By
Therefore, those have no excuse.
21 In fact, having known God, they did not glorify him or give thanks to him accordingly. On the contrary, they were lost in vain reasonings and their foolish minds were left in darkness.
22 Claiming to be wise, they became fools,
23 and they exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for images representing corruptible men, birds, four-footed animals, and creeping things.
24 Therefore, leaving them abandoned to the desires of their hearts, God gave them over to an impurity that dishonored their own bodies,
25 since they have substituted a lie for the truth of God, worshiping and serving creatures instead of the Creator, who is eternally blessed. Amen.
26 Therefore, God also gave them over to shameful passions: their wives exchanged natural relationships for others contrary to nature.

27 In the same way, the men, leaving the natural relationship with the woman, burned with desire for each other, having dishonest relations with each other and receiving in themselves the
deserved retribution for his loss.
28 And because they did not care to recognize God, he gave them over to their depraved mind to do what should not be done.
29 They are full of all kinds of injustice, iniquity, ambition and evil; filled with envy, crimes, fights, deceptions, depravity, defamations.
30 They are detractors, enemies of God, insolent, arrogant, conceited, skilled in evil, rebellious toward their parents,
31 foolish, disloyal, callous, ruthless.
32 And even though they know the decree of God, which declares those who do these things worthy of death, they not only practice them, but also approve of those who do them.
1 Therefore, you who claim to be a judge of others – no matter who you are – have no excuse, because by judging others, you condemn yourself, since you do the same thing that you condemn.
2 We know that God judges those who behave like this according to the truth,
3 You who judge those who do these things and commit the same thing, do you think you will escape the Judgment of God?
4 Or do you despise the richness of God's goodness, his tolerance and his patience, without recognizing that this goodness should lead you to conversion?
5 Because of your stubbornness in not wanting to repent, you are storing up wrath for the day of wrath, when the righteous judgments of God will be revealed,
6 who will reward each one according to his works.
7 He will give eternal Life to those who, through their perseverance in the practice of good, seek glory, honor and immortality.
8 Instead, he will punish the rebels with anger and violence, those who do not submit to the truth and allow themselves to be carried away by injustice.
9 That is, there will be tribulation and anguish for all who do evil: for the Jews first of all, and also for those who are not.
10 And there will be glory, honor and peace for all who do good: for the Jews, first of all, and also for those who are not,
11 because God is no respecter of persons.
12 Indeed, all who have sinned without having the Law of Moses will perish without that Law; and those who have sinned while having the Law will be judged by it,
13 because in the sight of God, not those who hear the Law are righteous, but those who do it.
14 When the pagans, who do not have the Law, guided by nature, fulfill the prescriptions of the Law, although they do not have the Law, they are a law to themselves,
15 and demonstrate that what the Law commands is written in their hearts. This is proven by the testimony of their own conscience, which sometimes accuses them and other times excuses them,
16 until the Day when God will judge the hidden intentions of men through Christ Jesus, according to the Good News that I preach.
17 But you, who pride yourself on being a Jew; you who rely on the Law and glorify yourself in God;
18 You who claim to know His will and, instructed by the Law, claim to discern what is best,
19 claiming to be a guide for the blind and a light for those who walk in darkness;
20 You who instruct the ignorant and are a teacher of the simple, because you have in the Law the standard of knowledge and truth;
21 You, who teach others, do not teach yourself!
22 You, who condemn adultery, also commit it. You, who hate idols, plunder their temples.
23 You, who glory in the Law, dishonor God by violating the Law.
24 For as the Scripture says: "Because of you, the name of God is blasphemed among the nations."
25 Circumcision is useful if you practice the Law, but if you do not practice it, it is the same as if you were uncircumcised.
26 On the contrary, he who is not circumcised, but observes the prescriptions of the Law, will be considered truly circumcised.
27 Furthermore, he who is not physically circumcised but observes the Law will judge you, who, having the letter of the Law and circumcision, do not practice the Law.
28 For he who is one outwardly is not a true Jew, nor is true circumcision what is seen in the flesh.

29 The true Jew is one internally, and the true circumcision is that of the heart, which is done according to the spirit and not according to the letter of the Law. Praise belongs to this one, not from the
men, but of God.
1 What then is the superiority of the Jew, and what is the use of circumcision?
2 The advantages are many from every point of view. First of all, God entrusted his Word to the Jews.
3 And what does it matter that some have not believed? Will your unbelief nullify God's faithfulness?
4 By no means: God is true, and every man is a liar, because as the Scripture says: "You will be recognized as righteous for what you say and you will triumph when you are judged."
5 Now, if our injustice highlights the justice of God, what conclusion will we draw? Will God be unjust – I express myself in human terms – by giving free rein to his anger?
6 Not at all. Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
7 But if with my lie, God's truth wins, to his glory, why should I still be condemned as a sinner?
8 Or must we do evil so that good may result, as some slanderers have us say? These do deserve to be condemned!
9 In short, then, are we or are we not superior to the pagans? By no means.
10 For we have just proven that everyone is subject to sin, both Jews and non-Jews. This is what Scripture states: "There is no righteous person, not even one;
11 There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.
12 All are lost, equally corrupted; no one practices good, not even one.
13 His throat is an open tomb; They deceive with their tongue, their lips drip the poison of vipers,
14 His mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.
15 His feet are quick to shed blood,
16 In their ways there is ruin and misery,
17 do not know the path of peace.
18 The fear of God is not before their eyes."

19 Now we know that everything that the Law says is valid only for those who are under the Law, so that no one can claim innocence and everyone can be found guilty.
before God.
20 For in the sight of God no one will be justified by the works of the Law, since the Law only makes us know sin.
21 But now, without the Law, the righteousness of God has been manifested, witnessed by the Law and the Prophets:
22 the righteousness of God, through faith in Jesus Christ, for all who believe. Because there is no distinction:
23 everyone has sinned and falls short of the glory of God,
24 but they are freely unjustified by his grace, by virtue of the redemption accomplished in Christ Jesus.
25 He was appointed by God as an instrument of propitiation by his own blood, thanks to faith. In this way, God wanted to show his justice:
26 in the time of divine patience, passing over sins previously committed, and in the present time, being righteous and justified to those who believe in Jesus.
27 What right then is there to boast? None. But under what law is that right excluded? By the law of works? No, but by the law of faith.
28 For we consider that a man is justified by faith apart from the works of the Law.
29 Is God only the God of the Jews? Is it not also true of the pagans? Obviously yes,
30 For there is but one God, who justifies both circumcised Jews and uncircumcised Gentiles through faith.
31 So, through faith, do we nullify the Law? Don't even think about it! On the contrary, we confirm it.
1 And what shall we say of Abraham, our father according to the flesh?
2 If he had been justified by works he would have something to boast about, but not before God.
3 For what does the Scripture say? Abraham believed in God and this was taken into account for his justification.
4 Now the worker is not given wages as a gift, but as something owed to him.
5 But whoever does nothing but believes in Him who justifies the wicked, his faith is counted toward his justification.
6 Therefore David proclaims the happiness of him to whom God confers righteousness without works, saying:
7 "Blessed are those whose transgressions have been forgiven and whose sins have been covered.
8 Happy is the man whose sin God does not take into account."

9 But is this happiness only for those who have been circumcised, or also for those who have not been circumcised? Let us consider what we have already said: Abraham's faith was taken into account for his
justification.
10 When was it taken into account? Before or after circumcision? Obviously before and not after.

11 And he received the sign of circumcision, as a seal of the righteousness that he obtained through faith, before he was circumcised. Thus he became the father of those who, despite
not being circumcised, they have the faith that is taken into account for their
justification.
12 And he is also the father of those who are circumcised but are not content with this, but follow the same path of faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
13 For the promise of inheritance of the world to Abraham and his posterity was not granted by virtue of the Law, but by the righteousness that comes from faith.
14 For if the inheritance belongs to those who are under the Law, faith has no purpose and the promise is worthless,
15 since the Law provokes anger and where there is no Law there is no transgression.

16 Therefore, the inheritance is obtained through faith, so that this inheritance is free and the promise is assured for all the descendants of Abraham, not only those who are descendants by the Law,
but also those who are so by faith. Because he is our common father

17 as the Scripture says: "I have made you the father of many nations." Abraham is our father in the eyes of him in whom he believed: the God who gives life to the dead and
He calls into existence things that do not exist.
18 Hoping against all hope, Abraham believed and became the father of many nations, as it had been announced to him: So will your descendants be.
19 His faith did not waver, considering that his body was as good as dead – it was almost a hundred years old – and that Sarah's womb was also dead.
20 He did not doubt the promise of God for lack of faith, but on the contrary, strengthened by that faith, he glorified God,
21 fully convinced that God has the power to fulfill what he promises.
22 Therefore, faith was taken into account for his justification.
23 But when the Scripture says, "God considered his faith," it does not refer only to Abraham, but also to us,
24 that we have faith in him who raised our Lord Jesus from the dead,
25 who was delivered for our sins and resurrected for our justification.
1 Being justified, then, by faith, we are at peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
2 Through him we have obtained, through faith, the grace in which we are established, and through him we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.
3 Furthermore, we boast even about tribulations themselves, because we know that tribulation produces perseverance;
4 perseverance, proven virtue; proven virtue, hope.
5 And hope will not be disappointed, because the love of God has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us.
6 In fact, while we were still weak, Christ, at the appointed time, died for sinners.
7 It is difficult to find anyone who will give his life for a righteous man; perhaps someone is capable of dying for a benefactor.
8 But the proof that God loves us is that Christ died for us while we were still sinners.
9 And now that we are justified by his blood, the more we will be delivered by him from the wrath of God.
10 For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more now that we are reconciled, we will be saved by his life.
11 And this is not all: we rejoice in God, through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
12 Therefore, through one man sin entered the world, and through sin death, and so death spread to all men, because all sinned.
13 Indeed, sin was already in the world before the Law, but when there is no Law, sin is not taken into account.
14 However, death reigned from Adam to Moses, even in those who had not sinned, committing a transgression similar to that of Adam, who is a type of him who was to come.

15 But there is no proportion between the gift and the lack. For if the lack of one caused the death of all, the grace of God and the gift conferred by the grace of one man, Jesus Christ, were
poured out much more abundantly on all.

16 Nor can this gift be compared with the consequences of the sin committed by a single man, since the judgment of condemnation came for a single fault, while the gift of grace leads to
the justification after many faults.

17 In fact, if through the lack of one man death reigned, much more will those who have abundantly received grace and gift live and reign through one man, Jesus Christ.
of justice.
18 Therefore, just as the fault of one caused the condemnation of all, so the righteous act of one will produce for all men the justification that leads to Life.
19 And just as through the disobedience of one man all became sinners, so through the obedience of one man all will become righteous.
20 It is true that the Law entered so that transgressions would multiply, but where sin abounded, grace abounded all the more.
21 For just as sin reigned in death, so grace will reign through righteousness leading to eternal Life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
1 What will we say then? What must we continue to sin so that grace may abound?
2 Don't even think about it! How is it possible for those of us who have died to sin to continue living in it?
3 Do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus have immersed ourselves in his death?
4 By baptism we were buried with him into death, so that just as Christ was resurrected through the glory of the Father, we too might live a new life.
5 For if we have identified ourselves with Christ through a death similar to his, we will also identify ourselves with him in the resurrection.
6 Let us understand it: our old man has been crucified with him, so that this body of sin would be destroyed, and thus we would no longer be slaves to sin.
7 For he who is dead owes nothing to sin.
8 But if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him.
9 We know that Christ, after being resurrected, dies no more, because death no longer has power over him.
10 When he died, he died to sin, once for all; and now that he lives, he lives for God.
11 Likewise, consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus.
12 Do not allow sin to reign in your mortal bodies, obeying your base desires.

13 Nor make your members instruments of injustice in the service of sin, but offer yourselves to God, as those who have passed from death to Life, and make your
members instruments of justice at the service of God.
14 Let sin no longer have dominion over you, since you are not subject to the Law, but to grace.
15 So what? Are we going to sin because we are not subject to the Law but to grace? By no means!

16 Don't you know that by submitting to someone as slaves to obey him, you become slaves to the one you obey, whether to sin, which leads to death, or to obedience, which leads to
justice?
17 But thanks be to God, you, after being slaves to sin, have sincerely obeyed the rule of doctrine, to which you were entrusted,
18 and now, freed from sin, they have become servants of righteousness.

19 I am going to speak to you in a human way, taking into account your natural weakness. If they first gave up their members, making them slaves of impurity and disorder until they reached their
excesses, put them now at the service of justice to achieve holiness.
20 When you were slaves to sin, you were free with respect to righteousness.
21 But what benefit did they then derive from the works that now shame them? The result of these works is death.
22 Now, however, you are free from sin and subject to God: the fruit of this is holiness and its result is eternal Life.
23 For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal Life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
1 Do you not know, brothers – I speak to people who understand the law – that a man is subject to the law only while he lives?
2 Thus a married woman remains bound by law to her husband as long as he lives; But when her husband dies, she is separated from the law that united her to him.

3 Therefore, she will be considered an adulteress if she joins another man during her husband's lifetime. On the other hand, if her husband dies, she will be free from the law, and will not be considered an adulteress if she marries another.
man.
4 In the same way, brothers, through union with the body of Christ, you have died to the Law, to belong to another, to him who was resurrected so that we might bear fruit for God.
5 For while we lived according to the carnal nature, the evil passions, stimulated by the Law, worked in our members to cause us to produce fruits of death.

6 But now, dead to all that held us enslaved, we have been freed from the Law, so that we can serve God with a new spirit and not according to a letter
aged

7 Shall we then say that the Law is sin? By no means! But I would not have known sin if it were not for the Law. In fact, I would have ignored covetousness, if the Law had not
said: "You shall not covet."
8 But sin, taking advantage of the opportunity that the precept gave it, provoked in me all kinds of greed, because without the Law, sin is a dead thing.
9 There was a time when I lived without the Law, but when the precept came, sin took life,
10 and I, however, died. So it turned out that the commandment that was supposed to give me life led me to death.
11 For sin, taking advantage of the opportunity that the precept gave it, seduced me and, through the precept, caused me to die.
12 Therefore the Law is holy, just as the precept is holy, just, and good.

13 But is it possible for good things to cause my death? No way! What happens is that sin, in order to show itself as such, used something good to cause my death, and thus sin, through
of the precept, reaches the fullness of its malice.
14 For we know that the Law is spiritual, but I am carnal, and sold as a slave to sin.
15 And I do not even understand what I do, because I do not do what I want but what I hate.
16 But if I do what I do not want, by that I acknowledge that the Law is good.
17 But then, it is not I who do that, but the sin that resides in me,
18 because I know that there is nothing good in me, that is, in my flesh. Indeed, the desire to do good is within my reach, but not the realization of it.
19 And so I do not do the good that I want, but the evil that I do not want.
20 But when I do what I do not want, it is not I who do it, but the sin that resides in me.
21 In this way, I come to discover this law: wanting to do good, evil comes my way.
22 For according to the inner man, I delight in the Law of God,
23 But I observe that there is another law in my members that fights against the law of my reason and binds me to the law of sin that is in my members.
24 Woe to me! Who can free me from this body that leads me to death?
25 Thank God, through Jesus Christ, our Lord! In a word, with my heart I serve the Law of God, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin.
1 Therefore, there is no longer condemnation for those who live united to Christ Jesus.
2 For the law of the Spirit, which gives Life, freed me, freed me, in Christ Jesus, from the law of sin and death.

3 What the Law could not do, reduced to impotence by the flesh, God did, sending his own Son, in a flesh similar to that of sin, and as a victim for sin. Thus he condemned
sin in the flesh,
4 so that the righteousness of the Law might be fulfilled in us, who no longer live according to the flesh but according to the spirit.
5 Indeed, those who live according to the flesh desire what is carnal; On the other hand, those who live according to the spirit desire what is spiritual.
6 Now the desires of the flesh lead to death, but the desires of the spirit lead to life and peace,
7 because the desires of the flesh are opposed to God, since they do not submit to his Law, nor can they do so.
8 Therefore, those who live according to the flesh cannot please God.

9 But you are not animated by the flesh but by the spirit, since the Spirit of God dwells in you. He who does not have the Spirit of Christ cannot be
Christ.
10 But if Christ lives in you, although the body is subject to death because of sin, the spirit lives because of righteousness.
11 And if the Spirit of him who raised Jesus dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus will also give life to your mortal bodies, through the same Spirit who dwells in you.
12 Brethren, we are not debtors to the flesh, to live in a carnal manner.
13 If you live according to the flesh, you will die. On the contrary, if you put to death the works of the body through the Spirit, then you will live.
14 All who are led by the Spirit of God are children of God.
15 And you have not received a spirit of slaves to fall back into fear, but the spirit of adopted children, which makes us call to God
16 The same spirit unites with our spirit to bear witness that we are children of God.
17 If we are children, we are also heirs, heirs of God and joint heirs of Christ, because we suffer with him to be glorified with him.
18 I consider that the sufferings of the present time cannot be compared with the future glory that will be revealed in us.
19 Indeed, the entire creation eagerly awaits this revelation of the children of God.
20 She was subjected to vanity, not voluntarily, but because of him who subjected her, but preserving a hope.
21 For the creation will also be freed from the bondage of corruption to share in the glorious freedom of the children of God.
22 We know that the entire creation, up to the present, groans and suffers labor pains.
23 And not only her: we also, who possess the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly longing for the redemption of our body to be accomplished.
24 Because only in hope are we saved. Now, when you see what you expect, you no longer expect: can you expect what you see?
25 On the other hand, if we hope for what we do not see, we hope for it with perseverance.
26 Likewise, the same Spirit comes to the aid of our weakness because we do not know how to pray properly; but he is the Spirit intercedes for us with ineffable groans.
27 And he who searches hearts knows the desire of the Spirit and knows that his intercession on behalf of the saints is in accordance with the divine will.
28 Furthermore, we know that God works all things for the good of those who love him, those whom he has called according to his plan.
29 Indeed, those whom God foreknew, he predestined to reproduce the image of his Son, so that he would be the firstborn among many brothers;
30 and those whom he predestinated, he also called; and those whom he called, he also justified; and those whom he justified, he also glorified.
31 What will we say after all this? If God is with us, who will be against us?
32 Will He who did not spare His own Son, but gave Him up for us all, grant us with Him all kinds of favors?
33 Who can accuse God's chosen ones? God is the one who justifies.
34 Who will dare to condemn them? Could it be Jesus Christ, the one who died, even more, the one who was resurrected, and is at the right hand of God and intercedes for us?
35 Who then can separate us from the love of Christ? The tribulations, the anguish, the persecution, the famine, the nakedness, the dangers, the sword?
36 As the Scripture says: For your sake we are continually handed over to death; We are considered like sheep destined for the slaughter.
37 But in all this we obtain a vast victory, thanks to him who loved us.
38 For I am certain that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities, nor things present nor things to come, nor spiritual powers,
39 Neither height nor depth, nor any other creature, will ever be able to separate us from the love of God, manifested in Christ Jesus, our Lord.
1 I speak the truth in Christ, I do not lie, and my conscience witnesses it to me in the Holy Spirit.
2 I feel great sadness and constant pain in my heart.
3 I myself would like to be cursed, separated from Christ, in favor of my brothers, those of my own race.
4 They are Israelites: to them belong filial adoption, glory, alliances, legislation, worship and promises.
5 To them also belong the patriarchs, and from them descends Christ according to his human form, who is above all, blessed God eternally. Amen.
6 It is not true that the word of God has fallen into a void. Because not all those who descend from Israel are really Israelites.
7 Just as not all Abraham's descendants are his children, but as the Scripture says: From Isaac your descendants will be born.
8 This means that the children of God are not those who are born of the flesh, and that the true offspring are the children of the promise.
9 For thus says the promise: At this same date I will return, and then Sarah will have a son.
10 And this is not all: there is also the case of Rebekah who conceived two children by one man, Isaac, our father.
11 Before children were born, before they could do good or evil – so that the freedom of divine choice would be highlighted,
12 which does not depend on the works of man, but on him who calls – God said to Rebekah: The older will serve the younger,
13 according to what the Scripture says: I preferred Jacob to Esau.
14 Shall we therefore say that God is unjust? By no means!
15 For he said to Moses, "I will be merciful to whomever I please, and I will have compassion on whomever I please."
16 Consequently, everything depends not on the will or effort of man, but on the mercy of God.
17 For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: "For this very reason I have exalted you, that my power may be manifested in you and that my Name may be celebrated in all the earth."
18 So God has mercy on whomever he pleases and hardens whomever he pleases.
19 You may object to me: Then what can God reproach us? Can anyone resist his will?
20 But you, who are you to argue with God? Can the modeled object say to the one who models it: Why do you make me like this?
21 Is not the potter master of his clay, to make a fine vessel or an ordinary one from the same material?
22 What can we reproach God for, if they want to manifest his wrath and make his power known, he endured with great patience those who attracted his wrath and deserved perdition?
23 And if he wanted to manifest the riches of his glory in those who received his mercy, in those whom he predestined to glory,
24 in us, who were called by him, not only from among the Jews, but also from among the Gentiles, what can we reproach him?
25 This is what God says through Hosea: "Whoever was not of my people I will call 'My people,' and whoever was not my beloved I will call 'My beloved.'"
26 And in the same place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' there you will be called 'Sons of the living God.'"
27 In turn, Isaiah proclaims about Israel: "Even if the Israelites were as numerous as the sand of the sea, only a remnant will be saved,
28 for the Lord will fully fulfill his word on the earth without delay."
29 And as the prophet Isaiah had anticipated: "If the Lord of the universe had not left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, we would have been like Gomorrah."
30 What conclusion will we draw from all this? That the pagans who did not seek justice, achieved justice, which comes from faith;
31 while Israel, which sought a law of righteousness, fell short of fulfilling that law.
32 For what reason? Because they did not resort to faith but to works. Thus they hit the stumbling block,
33 as the Scripture says: I put in Zion a stumbling block and a rock that causes people to fall, but whoever believes in him will not be confounded.
1 Brothers, my greatest wish and what I ask in my prayer to God is that they be saved.
2 I testify on their behalf that they have zeal for God, but a misunderstood zeal.
3 Because not knowing the righteousness of God and trying to establish their own, they refused to submit to the righteousness of God,
4 since the end of the Law is Christ, for the justification of everyone who believes.
5 Moses, in fact, writes about the justice that comes from the Law: "The man who practices it will live by it."
6 But the righteousness that comes from faith speaks like this: Do not say in your heart, Who will ascend into heaven? That is, to bring down Christ.
7 Or: Who will descend into the Abyss?, that is, to bring up Christ from the dead.
8 But what does justice say?: The word is close to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that is, the word of faith that we preach.
9 For if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
10 With the heart one believes to obtain righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses to obtain salvation.
11 This is what the Scripture says: "He who believes in him will not be confounded."
12 For there is no distinction between Jews and those who are not: they all have the same Lord, who fills those who call on him with good things.
13 For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
14 But how to invoke him without believing in him? And how can you believe, without having heard of it? And how can you hear about it, if no one preaches it?
15 And who will preach, if he does not send them? As the Scripture says: "How beautiful are the steps of those who announce good news!"
16 But not everyone accepts the Good News. This is what Isaiah says: "Lord, who believed our preaching?"
17 Faith, therefore, is born from preaching and preaching is carried out by virtue of the Word of Christ.
18 I wonder: Have they not heard it? Yes, of course: His voice spreads throughout the earth and his words reach the ends of the world.

19 But I ask myself again: Is it possible that Israel has not understood? Moses already said it: I will make them jealous with something that is not a people, I will irritate them with a foolish nation.
20 And Isaiah dares to say: "Those who did not seek me found me and I revealed myself to those who did not ask for me."
21 Of Israel, however, he says: "All day long I stretched out my hands to an unfaithful and rebellious people."
1 So I wonder: Has God rejected his People? Nothing of the sort! I myself am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham and a member of the tribe of Benjamin.
2 God has not rejected his People, whom he chose in advance. Do you not know what the Scripture says in the story of Elijah? He complained about Israel before God, saying:
3 "Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have destroyed your altars; I am left alone and they are trying to take my life."
4 And what did the divine oracle answer him?: "I have reserved for myself seven thousand men who did not bend their knee to Baal."
5 Thus, in the present time, there is also a freely chosen remnant.
6 And if it be by grace, it is not by works; Otherwise grace would not be grace.
7 What conclusion will we draw from this? That Israel did not achieve what it sought, but rather the chosen ones achieved it; As for the rest, they became hardened,
8 according to the word of Scripture: "God has dulled them, so that their eyes do not see and their ears do not hear to this day."
9 And David adds: "May your table become a trap and a snare, an occasion of fall and a just punishment.
10 Let their eyes be clouded so that they cannot see, and bow their backs forever."

11 I ask myself then: Will Israel's stumble mean its definitive fall? By no means. On the contrary, following his fall, salvation came to the pagans, in order to provoke jealousy
of Israel.
12 Now, if his fall enriched the world and his decline enriched the pagans, what will not achieve their total conversion?
13 To you, who are of pagan origin, I assure you that in my capacity as Apostle to the pagans, I honor my ministry
14 provoking the jealousy of my racial brothers, in the hope of saving some of them.
15 For if the exclusion of Israel brought about the reconciliation of the world, its reintegration, will it not be a return to life?
16 If the firstfruits are holy, so is the whole dough; If the root is holy, so are the branches.
17 If some of the branches were cut off, and you, who are a wild olive tree, were grafted in their place, becoming a partaker of the root and sap of the olive tree,
18 do not be proud in front of the branches. And if you do, remember that it is not you who supports the root, but the root supports you.
19 You will tell me: These branches were cut off so that I could be grafted in.
20 Okay, but they were cut off for their lack of faith; You, however, are firm thanks to faith. Don't be proud of it; rather, fear.
21 For if God did not spare the natural branches, he will not spare you either.

22 Consider both the goodness and the severity of God: he is severe toward those who fell and is good to you, as long as you are faithful to his goodness; otherwise you too will be
torn off.
23 And if they do not persist in their disbelief, they will also be grafted in, because God is powerful enough to graft them in again.

24 Indeed, if you were cut from a wild olive tree, to which you naturally belonged, and were grafted against your natural condition into the good olive tree, how much more can they be grafted into
their own olive tree, to which they belong by nature!
25 Brethren, I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, so that you do not boast about yourselves: the hardening of a part of Israel will last until all the pagans have entered.
26 And then all Israel will be saved, according to what the Scripture says: "The Deliverer will come from Zion. He will turn away wickedness from Jacob.
27 And this will be my covenant with them, when I purify them from their sins."
28 Now as far as the Good News is concerned, they are enemies of God, because of you; but from the point of view of divine election, they are loved out of respect for their parents.
29 Because the gifts and calling of God are irrevocable.
30 In fact, you previously disobeyed God, but now, because of their disobedience, you have obtained mercy.
31 In the same way, now that you have obtained mercy, they refuse to obey God. But this is so that they also may obtain mercy.
32 For God subjected everyone to disobedience, so that he would have mercy on everyone.
33 How deep and rich is the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unfathomable are his designs and how incomprehensible are his ways!
34 Who penetrated the mind of the Lord? Who was your advisor?
35 Who gave him something, so that he has the right to be repaid?
36 For everything comes from him, has been through him, and is for him. To him be glory forever! Amen.
1 Therefore, brothers, I urge you by the mercy of God to offer yourselves as a living victim, holy and pleasing to God: this is the spiritual worship that you should offer.

2 Do not take this world as a model. On the contrary, transform yourselves internally by renewing your mentality, so that you can discern what the will of God is: what is good, what
pleases, the perfect.

3 By virtue of the grace given to me, I say to each of you: do not think more highly of yourselves than is appropriate; but have a reasonable esteem for yourselves, according to the measure of the faith that God distributed to
each one.
4 For just as in one body we have many members with different functions,
5 We also all form one Body in Christ, and as far as each one is concerned, we are members one of another.
6 According to the grace that God has given us, we all have different abilities. He who has the gift of prophecy, let him exercise it according to the measure of faith.
7 He who has the gift of ministry, let him serve. He who has the gift of teaching, let him teach.

8 He who has the gift of exhortation, let him exhort. He who shares his goods, let him give with simplicity. He who presides over the community should do so with diligence. The one who practices
mercy, let him do it with joy.
9 Love with sincerity. Have a horror of evil and a passion for good.
10 Love each other cordially with brotherly love, esteeming others as more worthy.
11 With tireless diligence and fervor of spirit, serve the Lord.
12 Rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation and persevere in prayer.
13 Consider the needs of the saints as your own and practice hospitality generously.
14 Bless those who persecute you, bless and never curse.
15 Rejoice with those who are joyful, and weep with those who weep.
16 Live in harmony with each other, do not want to stand out, put yourself on the level of the most humble. Do not presume to be wise.
17 Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Seek to do good before all men.
18 As far as it depends on you, try to live in peace with everyone.
19 My dear ones, do not take justice into your own hands, but rather give way to the wrath of God. For it is written: I will punish. I will give retribution, says the Lord.
20 And elsewhere it is written: If your enemy is hungry, feed him; If he is thirsty, give him a drink. By doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head.
21 Do not let yourself be overcome by evil. On the contrary, defeat evil by doing good.
1 Everyone must submit to the established authorities, because there is no authority that does not come from God and those that exist have been established by him.
2 Consequently, he who resists authority opposes the order established by God, attracting condemnation upon himself.
3 Those who do good have nothing to fear from rulers, but those who do evil do. If you do not want to be afraid of authority, do well and you will receive its praise.

4 Because authority is an instrument of God for your good. But be afraid if you do evil, because she does not exercise her power in vain, but is at the service of God to do justice.
and punish those who do wrong.
5 That is why it is necessary to submit to authority, not only out of fear of punishment but also out of duty of conscience.
6 And for this reason too, you must pay taxes: rulers, in fact, are officials at the service of God charged with fulfilling this office.
7 Give to each one his due: to whom tax is owed, tax; to whom contribution, contribution is owed; to whom respect is due, respect; and honor, to whom it is due.
8 Let the only debt with others be that of mutual love: he who loves his neighbor has already fulfilled the entire Law.
9 For the commandments: Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not covet, and any other, are summed up in this: Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
10 Love does not make others better. Therefore, love is the fullness of the Law.
11 You know what time we live in and that it is time to wake up, because salvation is closer to us now than when we embraced faith.
12 The night is far advanced and the day is approaching. Let us abandon the works of the night and put on the armor of light.
13 As in broad daylight, let us proceed with dignity: no more excesses in food and drink, no more lust and debauchery, no more fighting or envy.
14 Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not worry about satisfying the lusts of the flesh.
1 Be understanding with those who are weak in faith, without entering into arguments.
2 While some believe that they are allowed to eat everything, the weak only eat vegetables.
3 He who eats everything should not despise him who abstains, and this in turn should not criticize him who eats everything, because God has also received this one.
4 Who are you to criticize another's servant? Whether he stands or falls is a matter for his owner, but he will stand because the Lord is able to sustain him.
5 Some have a preference for some days, while for others, all days are the same. Let each one stick to his own judgment.

6 He who distinguishes one day from another does so in honor of the Lord; and whoever eats, also does so in honor of the Lord, since he gives thanks to God; In the same way, he who abstains does so in honor of the
Lord, and also give thanks to God.
7 None of us lives for ourselves, nor dies for ourselves.
8 If we live, we live for the Lord, and if we die, we die for the Lord: both in life and in death, we belong to the Lord.
9 For Christ died and came to life to be Lord of the living and the dead.
10 Then by what right do you judge your brother? Why do you despise him? In fact, we will all have to appear before the court of God,
11 for it is written: "I swear that every knee will bow to me and every tongue will give glory to God," says the Lord.
12 Therefore, each of us will have to give an account of ourselves to God.
13 Let us then stop judging each other; Instead, try not to put anything in front of your brother that will cause him to stumble or fall.
14 I am fully convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is impure of itself; But if someone considers a thing to be impure, for him it is impure.
15 If you afflict your brother for food, you no longer act in accordance with love. Do not allow the one for whom Christ died to be lost because of a question of food!
16 Do not expose the good use of freedom to slander.
17 After all, the Kingdom of God is not a matter of food or drink, but of justice, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
18 He who serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and enjoys the approval of men.
19 Let us seek, therefore, what contributes to peace and mutual edification.
20 Do not ruin the work of God for food. In reality, everything is pure, but it becomes bad for those who eat, causing scandal.
21 It is best not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything that would scandalize your brother.
22 Keep to yourself, before God, what your own conviction dictates to you. Happy is he who has nothing to blame himself for what he chooses!
23 But he who eats despite his doubts is guilty because he acts in bad faith. And everything that is not done in good faith is sin.
1 We who are strong must bear the infirmities of the weak and not please ourselves.
2 Let each one try to please his neighbor for the common good and edification.
3 For neither did Christ seek his own pleasure, as the Scripture says: "The outrages of those who wrong you have fallen on me."
4 Now everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through the perseverance and comfort of the Scriptures we might maintain hope.
5 May the God of perseverance and consolation grant you to have the same feelings towards each other, after the example of Christ Jesus.
6 that with one heart and one voice you may glorify God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
7 Be welcoming to each other, just as Christ welcomed you to the glory of God.
8 For truly I say to you, Christ became a servant to the Jews to confirm the faithfulness of God, fulfilling the promises he made to our fathers,

9 and that the pagans might glorify God for his mercy. This is what the Scripture teaches when it says: "I will praise you among the nations, Lord, and I will sing in honor of your
Name".
10 And elsewhere it says: "Foreign peoples, rejoice with the People of God!"
11 And he also says: "Let all nations praise the Lord; let all people glorify him!"
12 And the prophet Isaiah says in turn: "The sprout of Jesse will appear, who will rise to rule the pagan nations: and all people will put their hope in him."
13 May the God of hope fill you with joy and peace in faith, so that hope may abound in you through the work of the Holy Spirit.
14 For my part, brothers, I am convinced that you are full of good dispositions and filled with the gift of knowledge, and also that you are able to advise each other.
15 However, I have written to you, in some passages with a certain boldness, to remind you of what you already know, thus corresponding to the grace that God has given me:

16 that of being a minister of Jesus Christ among the pagans, exercising the sacred office of announcing the Good News of God, so that the pagans may become a pleasing offering to God, sanctified
by the Holy Spirit.
17 I must boast in Christ Jesus, when it comes to the service of God!
18 For I would not dare to speak except of what Christ did through me, to lead the pagans to obedience, by word and deed,

19 by the power of signs and wonders and by the power of the Holy Spirit. From Jerusalem and its surroundings to Illyria, I have brought the Good News to its full fulfillment
of Christ,
20 making it a matter of honor not to preach the Good News where the name of Christ had already been invoked, so as not to build on a foundation laid by others.
21 Thus says the Scripture: "Those to whom it was not announced will see it, and those who had not heard of it will understand."
22 That's why in all this time I haven't been able to go see them.
23 But since I have already finished my work in those regions and for several years I have had a great desire to visit them,
24 I hope to see you when I go to Spain, and that you will help me continue my trip to that country, once I have enjoyed, even a little, your company.
25 But now, I am going to Jerusalem to bring help to the saints there.
26 For Macedonia and Achaia resolved to take a collection for the needy saints of Jerusalem.

27 They did it spontaneously, although in reality, they were indebted to them. Because if the pagans participated in their spiritual goods, they must in turn repay them with goods.
materials.
28 And once I have finished that mission and officially delivered the collected offering, I will go to Spain, passing through there.
29 And I am sure that I will come to you with the fullness of the blessings of Christ.
30 I beseech you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and for the love of the Holy Spirit, to fight together with me, interceding with God for me,
31 so that in Judea it may not fall into the hands of unbelievers, and that the saints in Jerusalem may receive with pleasure the offering that I bring to them.
32 This way I will have the joy of going to see you, and if God wants, I will be able to rest a little among you.
33 May the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
1 I recommend to you our sister Phoebe, deaconess of the Church of Cenchreae,
2 so that you may receive her in the Lord, as befits the saints, helping her in everything she needs from you: she has protected many brothers and also me.
3 Greet Priscilla and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus.
4 They risked their lives to save me, and not only I, but also all the churches of pagan origin, owe them a debt of gratitude.
5 Greet, likewise, the Church that meets in your house. Don't forget to greet my friend Epenetus, the first to convert to Christ in Asia Minor.
6 Greet Mary, who has worked so hard for you;
7 to Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and fellow prisoners, who are distinguished apostles and believed in Christ before me.
8 Greet Ampliatus, my dear friend in the Lord;
9 to Urban, our collaborator in Christ, and also to Stachys, my dear friend.
10 Greet Apelles, who has shown his fidelity to Christ, and also those of the family of Aristobulus.
11 Greet my relative Herodion, and those of the family of Narcissus who believe in Christ.
12 Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, who work so hard for the Lord; to dear Persis, who has also worked hard for the Lord.
13 Greet Rufus, the Lord's chosen one, and his mother, who is also mine;
14 to Asyncritus, to Phlegon, to Hermes, to Patrobas, to Hermas, and to the brothers who are with them.
15 Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, as well as Olympias, and all the saints who live with them.
16 Greet each other with the kiss of peace. All the Churches of Christ send you greetings.
17 I urge you, brothers, to beware of those who cause dissension and scandal, contrary to the teaching you have received. Avoid their treatment,
18 For they do not serve our Lord Jesus Christ, but only their own interests, seducing the simple with smooth and flattering words.
19 Your obedience is known everywhere, and this makes me happy; But I want them to be clever in good and simple in evil.
20 The God of peace will soon crush Satan, giving you victory over him. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
21 Timothy, my collaborator, sends greetings to you, as well as my relatives Lucius, Jason and Sosipater.
22 I, Tertius, who have served as amanuensis, greet you in the Lord.
23 Gaius also greets you, who welcomes me and the entire Church. Finally, greetings are sent to you by Erastus, the city treasurer, and our brother Cuartus.
24 [The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.]
25 Glory to God, who has the power to establish them, according to the Good News that I announce, proclaiming Jesus Christ, and revealing a mystery that was kept secret from eternity

26 and that has now been manifested! This is the mystery that, through the prophetic writings and according to the plan of the eternal God, was made known to all nations to lead them to obedience
of faith.
27 To God, the only wise one, through Jesus Christ, be glory forever! Amen.
1 Paul, called to be an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and his brother Sosthenes,

2 greet the Church of God residing in Corinth, those who have been sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be saints, together with all those who everywhere call on the name of
Jesus Christ, our Lord, their Lord and ours.
3 May grace and peace come to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
4 I never cease to thank God for you, for the grace he has given you in Christ Jesus.
5 Indeed, you have been filled in him with all kinds of riches, of speech and of knowledge,
6 to the extent that the testimony of Christ took root in you.
7 Therefore, while you wait for the Revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ, you do not lack any gift of grace.
8 He will keep you firm to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of the Coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
9 For God is faithful, and he called you to live in communion with his Son Jesus Christ, our Lord.

10 Brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, I urge you to agree: that there be no divisions among you and that you live in perfect harmony, having the same
way of thinking and feeling.
11 Because those of Chloe's family have told me that there is discord among you.
12 I mean that each one affirms: "I am of Paul, I of Apollo, I of Cephas, I of Christ."
13 Is Christ divided? Or was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
14 Fortunately I have not baptized any of you, except Crispus and Gaius.
15 So no one can say that he has been baptized in my name.
16 Yes, I have also baptized Stephanas' family, but I do not remember having baptized anyone else.
17 Because Christ did not send me to baptize, but to announce the Good News, and this without resorting to human eloquence, so that the cross of Christ does not lose its effectiveness.
18 The message of the cross is madness for those who are lost, but for those who are saved – for us – it is the power of God.
19 For it is written: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and reject the knowledge of the intelligent."
20 Where is the wise man? Where is the cultured man? Where is the subtle reasoner of this world? Has not God shown that the wisdom of the world is foolishness?
21 In fact, since the world, in its wisdom, did not recognize God in the works that manifest its wisdom, God wanted to save those who believe through the folly of preaching.
22 While the Jews ask for miracles and the Greeks search for wisdom,
23 We, however, preach a crucified Christ, a scandal to the Jews and madness to the Gentiles,
24 but strength and wisdom from God to those who have been called, both Jews and Greeks.
25 For the folly of God is wiser than the wisdom of men, and the weakness of God is stronger than the strength of men.
26 Brothers, consider who those who have been called are: there are not many wise among you, humanly speaking, nor are there many powerful or noble ones.
27 On the contrary, God chose what the world considers foolish, to confuse the wise; what the world considers weak, to confuse the strong;
28 what is vile and contemptible and what is worthless, to annihilate what is worth.
29 Thus no one will be able to boast before God.
30 Through him you are united to Christ Jesus, who by God's will became for us wisdom and righteousness, sanctification and redemption,
31 so that, as it is written: "He who boasts, let him glory in the Lord."
1 For my part, brothers, when I visited you to announce to you the mystery of God, I did not arrive with the prestige of eloquence or wisdom.
2 On the contrary, I did not want to know anything except Jesus Christ, and Jesus Christ crucified.
3 Therefore, I appeared before you weak, fearful and hesitant.
4 My speech and my preaching had nothing of the persuasive arguments of human wisdom, but were demonstrations of the power of the Spirit,
5 so that you would not base your faith on the wisdom of men, but on the power of God.

6 It is true that we proclaim wisdom among those who are spiritually mature people, but not the wisdom of this world nor that displayed by the rulers of this world,
condemned to destruction.
7 What we announce is a mysterious and secret wisdom from God, which he prepared for our glory before the world existed;
8 that which none of the rulers of this world were able to know, because if they had known it they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
9 We announce, as the Scripture says, what no one saw or heard or could even think about, what God prepared for those who love him.
10 God revealed all this to us through the Spirit, because the Spirit penetrates everything, even to the most intimate part of God.
