11 Who can know the innermost part of man, except the spirit of man himself? In the same way, no one knows the secrets of God except the Spirit of God.
12 And we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who comes from God, so that we may recognize the free gifts that God has given us.

13 We do not speak of these things in words learned from human wisdom, but in the language that the Spirit of God has taught us, expressing them in spiritual terms.
the realities of the Spirit.
14 The purely natural man does not value what comes from the Spirit of God: it is madness for him and he cannot understand it, because to judge it he needs the Spirit.
15 The spiritual man, on the other hand, judges everything, and cannot be judged by anyone.
16 For who penetrated into the mind of the Lord, that he might teach him? But we have the thought of Christ.
1 For my part, I could not speak to them as to spiritual men, but as to carnal men, as to those who are still babes in Christ.
2 I fed them with milk and not with solid food, because they could not tolerate it yet, any more than they do now,
3 since they are still carnal. Do not the jealousies and discords that exist among you prove that you are still carnal and behave in a purely human manner?
4 When one says, "I am from Paul," and the other, "I am from Apollo," are they not acting as any man would?

5 After all, who is Apollo, who is Paul? Simple servants, through whom you have believed, and each one of them is so according to what he has received from the
Sir.
6 I planted and Apollo watered, but God made it grow.
7 Neither he who plants nor he who waters is worth anything, but God, who makes it grow.
8 There is no difference between he who plants and he who waters; However, each one will receive his salary according to the work he has done.
9 For we are God's workers, and you are God's field, God's building.
10 According to the grace that God has given me, I laid the foundation as a good architect does, and another builds on it. Let everyone pay attention to how they build.
11 The foundation has already been laid and no one can lay another, because the foundation is Jesus Christ.
12 You can build on it with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, grass or straw:
13 Each person's work will appear as it is, because the day of Judgment, which will be revealed by fire, will make it manifest; and the fire will test the quality of each one's work.
14 If the work built on the foundation stands the test, the one who did it will receive the reward;
15 If the work is consumed, it will be lost. However, its author will be saved, like someone who is saved from fire.
16 Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?
17 If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him. Because the temple of God is sacred, and you are that temple.
18 Let no one be deceived! If any of you consider yourself wise in this world, let him become a fool in order to be truly wise.
19 For the wisdom of this world is foolishness before God. Indeed, the Scripture says: "He surprises the wise in their own cunning,"
20 and further: "The Lord knows the reasonings of the wise and knows that they are vain."
21 Therefore, let no one boast in men, for everything belongs to you:
22 Paul, Apollo or Cephas, the world, life, death, the present or the future. Everything is yours,
23 but you are Christ's and Christ is God's.
1 Men must regard us simply as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
2 Now, what is asked of an administrator is that he be faithful.
3 As for me, it matters little to me whether you judge me or a human court; I don't even judge myself.
4 It is true that my conscience reproaches me for nothing, but that does not mean I am justified: my judge is the Lord.

5 Therefore, do not make premature judgments. Let the Lord come: he will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will reveal the secret intentions of hearts. Then, each one will receive from God the praise that corresponds to him.

6 In all this, brothers, I gave you my example and that of Apollo, so that you may learn from us the saying: "Let us not go beyond what is written," so that no one will proudly take sides in favor of
of one against another.
7 Indeed, by what right do you distinguish yourself from others? And what do you have that you haven't received? And if you have received it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?

8 Maybe you are already satisfied! Could it be that they have become rich or have become kings, without needing us! I wish it were so, so that we could
reign with you!

9 I think that God has put us, the Apostles, in the last place, as condemned to death, since we have become a spectacle for the world, for the angels and the angels.
men.

10 We are considered fools because of Christ, but you are sensible in Christ. We are weak, and you are strong. You enjoy prestige, and
we are despised.
11 Until now we suffer hunger, thirst and cold. We are mistreated and live wandering.
12 We exhaust ourselves, working with our hands.

13 They insult us and we wish well. We suffer persecution and we endure it. They slander us and we console others. We have become like the trash of the world, an object of contempt
for everyone to this day.
14 I am not writing these things to shame you, but to rebuke you as beloved children.
15 For although they have ten thousand tutors in Christ, they do not have many fathers: it is I who have begotten them in Christ Jesus, through the preaching of the Good News.
16 I beg you, therefore, to follow my example.

17 For this very reason I sent you Timothy, my son, very dear and faithful in the Lord; He will remind you of my standards of conduct, which are those of Christ, and that I always teach in all
Churches.
18 Some of you, thinking that I would not return, have become filled with pride.
19 But soon I will come to see them, if the Lord so wishes, and then I will judge them, not by their words, but by the power they have.
20 Because the Kingdom of God is not a matter of words but of power!
21 What do you prefer? May he go to see them with the rod in his hand, or with love and a spirit of meekness?
1 It is a public thing that dishonest acts are committed among you, such as are not found even among the pagans, to such an extent that one lives with his father's wife!
2 And they are still proud, instead of mourning so that the one who committed that action may be expelled!
3 As for me, being absent with the body but present with the spirit, I have already judged it, as if I myself were there.
4 It is necessary that you and I come together spiritually, in the name and power of our Lord Jesus,
5 so that this man may be handed over to Satan: so his flesh will be lost, but his spirit will be saved on the Day of the Lord.
6 It's nothing to boast about! Don't you know that "a little yeast makes the whole dough ferment"?
7 Put off the old leaven, that you may be a new dough, for you yourselves are like unleavened bread. Because Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed.
8 Let us then celebrate our Passover, not with the old leaven of malice and perversity, but with the unleavened bread of purity and truth.
9 In a previous letter, I warned you not to mix with the dishonest.
10 I do not mean that they completely separate themselves from the dishonest of this world, from the covetous, from thieves, and from idolaters: if so, they would have to leave this world.

11 What I wanted to tell you is not to mix with those who, calling themselves brothers, are dishonest, covetous, idolaters, slanderers, drinkers or thieves: I advise you not even
eat with them.
12 It is not my business to judge those who are outside the Church. You judge those who are within;
13 because God judges those outside. Expel the wicked from among you.
1 How is it possible that when one of you has a conflict with another, you dare to demand justice from the unjust, instead of submitting to the judgment of the saints?
2 Don't you know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is going to be judged by you, how can you not be able to judge matters of minimal importance?
3 Do you not know that we are going to judge the angels themselves? All the more reason then, the affairs of this life.
4 And to think that when you have disputes, you look for those who are nobody to the Church as judges!
5 I say this to shame you: apparently, there is not even a sensible man among you, who is capable of serving as an arbitrator between his brothers!
6 One brother quarrels with another, and this, in front of those who do not believe!
7 It is already bad that there are disputes between you: is it not better to suffer injustice or be despoiled?
8 But no, you yourselves are the ones who commit injustice and defraud others, and this between brothers!
9 Do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the Kingdom of God? Have no illusions: neither the immoral, nor the idolaters, nor the adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor the perverted,
10 Neither thieves, nor the greedy, nor drinkers, nor slanderers, nor usurpers will inherit the Kingdom of God.
11 Some of you were like this, but now you have been purified, sanctified, and righteous in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
12 “Everything is permitted to me,” but not everything is expedient. "Everything is allowed to me," but I will not allow myself to be dominated by anything.

13 Food is for the stomach and the stomach is for food, and God will destroy both. But the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord is for the
body.
14 And God who raised the Lord will raise us also by his power.
15 Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? How am I going to take the members of Christ to become members of a prostitute? By no means.
16 Don't you know that he who joins himself to a prostitute becomes one body with her? For the Scripture says: The two will become one flesh.
17 But he who is united to the Lord becomes one spirit with him.
18 Avoid fornication. Any other sin committed by a man is external to his body, but he who commits fornication sins against his own body.
19 Or do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit, who dwells in you and which you have received from God? Therefore, you do not belong to each other,
20 but they have been bought, and at what price! Then glorify God in your bodies.
1 Now I will answer what you have asked me in writing: It is good for a man to abstain from women.
2 However, because of the danger of incontinence, let each man have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.
3 Let the husband fulfill his marital duties towards his wife; in the same way, the wife with her husband.
4 The woman is not the owner of her body, but the husband is; Neither is the husband the owner of his body, but the wife is.

5 Do not deny each other, except by mutual agreement and for a time, in order to be able to dedicate yourself more intensely to prayer; then return to live as before, so that Satan may not
take advantage of your incontinence and tempt you.
6 What I tell you is a concession and not an order.
7 My desire is for everyone to be like me, but each one receives his or her particular gift from the Lord: some this, others that.
8 I advise the unmarried and the widows to remain as I am.
9 But if they cannot contain themselves, let them marry; It is preferable to get married than to burn with bad desires.
10 But to those who are married, I command you—and this is not my command, but the Lord's—that the wife not separate from her husband.
11 If she separates, let her not remarry, or be reconciled to her husband. And let the husband not abandon his wife either.
12 As for the other questions, I tell you, not the Lord: If a believing man has a wife who does not believe, but she is willing to live with him, let him not abandon her.
13 And if a woman is in the same condition, let her also not separate from her husband.

14 For the husband who has no faith is sanctified by his wife, and the wife who has no faith is sanctified by the believing husband. If it were not so, your children would be impure; in
Instead, they are sanctified.
15 But if the unbelieving spouse wishes to separate, let him do so, and in that case, the believing spouse does not remain linked to the other, because God has called us to live in peace.
16 After all, what do you, who are the wife, know whether or not you can save your husband, and you, husband, whether you can save your wife?
17 Apart from this case, let each one continue to live in the condition that the Lord assigned him and in which he was when he was called. This is what I prescribe in all Churches.
18 If a man was circumcised before God called him, let him not hide the sign of circumcision; If the called one found him uncircumcised, let him not be circumcised.
19 What counts is not circumcision, but keeping the commandments of God.
20 Let each one remain in the state in which he was when God called him.
21 Were you a slave when you heard God's call? Don't worry about it, and even if you can become a free man, take advantage of your status as a slave.
22 For he who was a slave when the Lord called him is now a free man in the Lord; In the same way, he who was free when the Lord called him is now a slave of Christ.
23 You have been redeemed and at what price! Do not become slaves of men.
24 Brethren, let each one remain before God in the state in which he was when he was called.
25 Concerning virginity, I have no precept from the Lord. But I give a warning, as one who, by the mercy of the Lord, is worthy of trust.
26 I believe that, due to the difficulties of the present time, it is best for man to live without getting married.
27 Are you united to a woman? Don't separate yourself from her. Don't you have a wife? Don't look for it.
28 If you marry, you do not sin. And if a young woman marries, she does not sin either. But those who do so will suffer tribulations in their flesh that I would like to spare them.
29 What I want to say, brothers, is this: there is little time left. Meanwhile, those who have wives should live as if they did not have one;
30 those who cry, as if they did not cry; what they rejoice, as if they did not rejoice; those who buy, as if they possessed nothing;
31 those who enjoy the world, as if they did not enjoy it. Because the appearance of this world is fleeting.
32 I want you to live without worries. He who does not have a wife worries about the things of the Lord, seeking how to please the Lord.
33 On the other hand, he who has a wife worries about the things of this world, seeking how to please his wife,

34 and so his heart is divided. Also the single woman, like the virgin, worries about the things of the Lord, trying to be holy in body and spirit. The married woman, in
Instead, he worries about the things of this world, seeking how to please his
husband
35 I have told you these things for your good, not to hinder you, but so that you may do what is best and give yourself completely to the Lord.

36 If a man, being in full vitality, believes that he will not be able to behave correctly with the woman he loves, and that he must marry, let him do as he pleases: if they marry, he does not commit any
sin.
37 On the other hand, he who decides not to marry her, because he feels internally secure and can contain himself with full control of his will, also acts correctly.
38 Therefore, he who marries the woman he loves does well; but he who does not marry does even better.
39 The woman remains bound to her husband as long as he lives; On the other hand, if her husband dies, she is free to marry whoever she wants. But in this, she must be guided by the Lord.
40 However, you will be happier if you do not remarry, according to my advice. Now, I believe I have the Spirit of God.
1 Regarding meat sacrificed to idols, we all have due knowledge, we already know it, but knowledge fills us with pride, while love builds up.
2 If someone imagines that he knows something, he has not yet come to know it properly;
3 But he who loves God is recognized by God.
4 As for eating meat sacrificed to idols, we know well that idols are nothing and that there is only one God.
5 It is true that some are considered gods, whether in heaven or on earth: in fact, there are a number of gods and a number of lords.

6 But for us, there is only one God, the Father, from whom everything comes and to whom we are destined, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom everything exists and through
who we exist.

7 However, not everyone has this knowledge. Some, accustomed until recently to idolatry, eat the meat sacrificed to idols as if it were sacred, and their conscience, which is
weak, it is stained.
8 Certainly, it is not food that does not bring us closer to God: neither by stopping eating are we less, nor by eating are we more.
9 But be careful that the use of this freedom does not cause the weak to fall.

10 If someone sees you, who know how to act, sitting at table in a pagan temple, will he not feel authorized, because of the weakness of his conscience, to eat what has been sacrificed to
the idols?
11 And so you, who have proper knowledge, cause the weak to perish, that brother for whom Christ died!
12 By thus sinning against your brothers and wounding your conscience, which is weak, you sin against Christ.
13 Therefore, if food causes my brother to fall, I will never taste meat, so that I may not fall.
1 Am I not free? Am I not an Apostle? Have I not seen Jesus, our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
2 If for others I am not an Apostle, I am at least for you, because you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
3 This is my defense against those who accuse me!
4 Have we not the right to eat and drink,
5 to travel in the company of a believing woman, as the other Apostles, the brothers of the Lord and Cephas himself do?
6 Or are Barnabas and I the only ones who are forced to work to survive?
7 What soldier makes a campaign at his own expense? Or who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruits? Or who feeds a flock and is not fed with the milk of the sheep?
8 Although it may seem that I speak in too human terms, the Law teaches us the same thing.
9 For it is written in the Law of Moses: You shall not muzzle the threshing ox. Could it be that God cares about oxen?

10 Is it not that he speaks of us? Yes, this was written for us, because he who plows must plow with hope, and he who threshes grain must do so with hope of
collect your share.
11 If we have sown spiritual goods in you, what is strange that we reap temporal goods from you?

12 If others have this right over you, do we not have it all the more? However, we have never made use of it; On the contrary, we have endured everything so as not to hinder
the Good News of Christ.
13 Do you not know that the ministers of worship live by worship, and that those who serve the altar participate in the altar?
14 In the same way, the Lord commanded those who preach the Gospel to live by the Gospel.
15 Despite everything, I have not used any of these rights; and I do not tell them this to take advantage of them now; I would rather die. No, no one can deprive me of this reason for glory.
16 If I announce the Gospel, I do not do it to boast: on the contrary, it is an imperative need for me. Woe to me if I did not preach the Gospel!
17 If I carried out this task on my own initiative, I would deserve to be rewarded, but if I do it out of necessity, it means that I have been entrusted with a mission.
18 What then is my reward? Preach the Good News freely, renouncing the right that that Good News confers on me.
19 In fact, being free, I became a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.
20 I became a Jew with the Jews to win the Jews; I submitted to the Law, with those who are subject to it – although I am not – in order to win those who are subject to the Law.

21 And with those who are not subject to the Law, I, who do not live outside the Law of God - because I am subject to the Law of Christ - became one of them, in order to win those who are not subject to the Law.
to the Law.
22 And I became weak to the weak, that I might win the weak. I became everything for everyone, to win at least some, at any cost.
23 And all this, for the love of the Good News, in order to be able to share in its goods.
24 Don't you know that in the stadium everyone runs, but only one wins the prize? Run, then, so that you win it.
25 Athletes deprive themselves of everything, and they do it to obtain a crown that fades; we, however, for an incorruptible crown.
26 So I run, but not without knowing where; I fight, not like one who punches in the air.
27 On the contrary, I punish my body and subdue it, lest, after having preached to others, I myself be disqualified.
1 For you must not ignore, brothers, that all our fathers were guided by the cloud and all passed through the sea;
2 and for all, the march under the cloud and the passage of the sea was a baptism that united them to Moses.
3 Also they all ate the same food and drank the same spiritual drink.
4 In fact, they drank water from a spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.
5 Despite this, very few of them were pleasing to God, because their bodies were left lying in the desert.
6 All this happened symbolically for our example, so that we would not be carried away by evil desires, as our fathers did.
7 Do not worship false gods, as some of them did, as we read in the Scripture: The people sat down to eat and drink, and then got up to have fun.
8 Let us not commit fornication, like some of them, and that is why, as punishment, twenty-three thousand died in a single day.
9 Let us not provoke the Lord, as some of them did, and perished as victims of serpents.
10 Let us not rebel against God, like some of them, for which they died victims of the exterminating Angel.
11 All this happened to them symbolically, and is written as a lesson to those of us who live in the end time.
12 Therefore, he who thinks he is very secure, be careful not to fall!

13 Until now, you have had no temptations beyond your human strength. God is faithful, and he will not allow you to be tempted beyond your strength. On the contrary, at the time of
temptation, will give them the means to free themselves from it, and will help them to endure it.
14 Therefore, my dear ones, avoid idolatry.
15 I speak to you as to sensible people; Judge for yourselves what I am going to tell you.
16 Is not the cup of blessing that we bless communion with the Blood of Christ? And the bread we break, is it not communion with the Body of Christ?
17 Since there is one bread, all of us, although we are many, form one Body, because we partake of that one bread.
18 Let us think of Israel according to the flesh: are those who eat the victims not in communion with the altar?
19 Do I mean by this that meat sacrificed to idols has any value, or that the idol is something?
20 No, I simply affirm that the pagans offer their sacrifices to demons and not to God. Now, I do not want you to enter into communion with demons.
21 You cannot drink from the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; nor can they sit at the table of the Lord and at the table of demons.
22 Or do we want to provoke the Lord's jealousy? Do we pretend to be stronger than him?
23 “Everything is permitted,” but not everything is convenient. "Everything is permitted," but not everything is edifying.
24 Let no one seek his own interest, but that of others.
25 Eat everything that is sold in the market, without making inquiries because of scruples of conscience.
26 For the earth is the Lord's and everything in it.
27 If a pagan invites you to eat and you accept, eat whatever is served to you, without asking anything for reasons of conscience.
28 But if someone says to you, "This has been sacrificed to idols," then do not eat it, in consideration of Him who warned you and for reasons of conscience.
29 I am referring to their conscience, not yours: is my freedom going to be judged by another's conscience?
30 If I partake of the meal having given thanks, will I be rebuked for the very thing for which I have given thanks?
31 In short, whether you eat, whether you drink, or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.
32 Do not be a cause of scandal either to the Jews or to the pagans or to the Church of God.
33 Do as I do, who strive to please everyone in all things, not seeking my personal interest, but that of the greatest number, so that you may be saved.
1 Follow my example, just as I follow the example of Christ.
2 I congratulate you because you always remember me and keep the traditions as I have transmitted them to you.
3 However, I want you to know this: Christ is the head of man; The head of the woman is the man and the head of Christ is God.
4 Consequently, the man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head;
5 and the woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, exactly as if it were shaved.
6 If a woman does not cover herself with the veil, let her cut her hair. But if it is dishonorable for a woman to cut her hair or shave her head, let her wear the veil.
7 The man should not cover his head, because he is the image and reflection of God, while the woman is the reflection of the man.
8 In fact, it is not the man that comes from the woman, but the woman from the man;
9 nor was man created for woman, but woman for man.
10 For this reason, the woman must have a sign of subjection on her head, out of respect for the angels.
11 Of course, for the Lord, the woman does not exist without the man nor the man without the woman.
12 For if woman comes from man, then man is born from woman and everything comes from God.
13 Judge for yourselves: Do you think it is appropriate for a woman to pray with her head uncovered?
14 Doesn't nature itself teach us that it is a shame for a man to let his hair be long?
15 while for a woman it is a glory to wear it like this? Because the hair has been given to her as a veil.
16 Furthermore, if anyone is fond of arguments, we warn him that it is customary among us to wear the veil and also in the Churches of God.
17 And since I give you this warning, I cannot congratulate you for your meetings, which instead of benefiting you, harm you.
18 First of all, because I have heard that when you hold your assemblies, there are divisions among you, and I partly believe it.
19 However, it is necessary that parties be formed among you, so that those who have true virtue may be revealed.
20 When they come together, the least they do is eat the Lord's Supper,
21 Because as soon as they sit down at the table, each one rushes to eat his own food, and while one is hungry, the other gets drunk.

22 Do they not have their houses to eat and drink? Or do they have so little appreciation for the Church of God that they want to shame those who have nothing? What will I tell them? Am I going to praise them? In this,
I can't praise them.
23 What I received from the Lord, and in my turn I have transmitted to you, is this: The Lord Jesus, on the night in which he was betrayed, took the bread,
24 He gave thanks, broke it and said, “This is my Body, which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.
25 In the same way, after supper, he took the cup, saying: “This cup is the New Covenant that is sealed with my Blood. Whenever you drink it, do it in memory of me.
26 And so, whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you will proclaim the death of the Lord until he returns.
27 Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily will have to give an account of the Body and Blood of the Lord.
28 Let each one examine himself before eating this bread and drinking this cup;
29 For if you eat and drink without discerning the Body of the Lord, you eat and drink your own condemnation.
30 Therefore, among you there are many sick and weak, and many have died.
31 If we examined ourselves, we would not be condemned.
32 But the Lord judges us and corrects us so that we will not be condemned with the world.
33 So, brothers, when you come together to partake of the Supper, wait for one another.
34 And if anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that his assemblies will not be a reason for condemnation. I'll fix the rest when I go.
1 Regarding spiritual gifts, I do not want you, brothers, to live in ignorance.
2 You know that when you were still pagans, you let yourself be blindly drawn into the worship of inanimate gods.
3 Therefore I say to you that no one, moved by the Spirit of God, can say, “Cursed be Jesus.” And no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” if he is not moved by the Holy Spirit.
4 Certainly there are diversities of gifts, but they all come from the same Spirit.
5 There are diversity of ministries, but one Lord.
6 There are diversity of activities, but it is the same God who accomplishes everything in everyone.
7 In each one, the Spirit manifests for the common good.
8 The Spirit gives one wisdom to speak; to another, knowledge to teach, according to the same Spirit;
9 to another, faith, also the same Spirit. This is given the gift of healing, always in that one Spirit;

10 to that one, the gift of performing miracles; to one, the gift of prophecy; to another, the gift of judging the value of the gifts of the Spirit; to this, the gift of tongues; to him, the gift of
interpret them.
11 But in all this, it is the same and only Spirit that acts, distributing his gifts to each one individually as he wills.
12 Just as the body has many members, yet is one, and these members, though many, form but one body, so it is with Christ.
13 For we have all been baptized in one Spirit to form one Body – Jews and Greeks, slaves and free men – and we have all drunk of one Spirit.
14 The body is not made up of one member but of many.
15 If the foot said, "Since I am not a hand, I am not part of the body," would it not still be a part of it?
16 And if the ear said, "Since I am not an eye, I am no part of the body," would it cease to be a part of it?
17 If the whole body were an eye, where would the ear be? And if everything were heard, where would the sense of smell be?
18 But God has arranged each of the members in the body, according to an established plan.
19 For if they were all one member, where would the body be?
20 Indeed, there are many members, but the body is one.
21 The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," nor the head to the feet, "I have no need of you."
22 Furthermore, the members of the body that we consider weaker are also necessary,
23 and those we consider the least decorous are the ones we treat most decorously. Thus our less worthy members are treated with greater respect,
24 since others do not need to be treated that way. But God arranged the body, giving greater honor to the members who need it most,
25 so that there may be no divisions in the body, but that all the members may be mutually united.
26 Does a member suffer? Everyone else suffers with him. Is a member exalted? Everyone else participates in their joy.
27 You are the Body of Christ, and each one individually, members of that Body.

28 In the Church, there are some who have been established by God, first of all, as apostles; secondly, as prophets; thirdly, as doctors. Then come those who
They have received the gift of performing miracles, the gift of healing, the gift of helping others.
the needy, the gift of governing and the gift of tongues.
29 Are they all apostles? All prophets? All doctors? Do they all work miracles?
30 Does everyone have the gift of healing? Does everyone have the gift of languages ​​or the gift of interpreting them?
31 You, for your part, aspire to the most perfect gifts. And now I am going to show you an even more perfect path.
1 Even if I speak all the languages of men and angels, if I do not have love, I am like a ringing bell or a clanging cymbal.
2 Even if I had the gift of prophecy and knew all mysteries and all knowledge, even if I had all faith, a faith capable of moving mountains, if I do not have love, I am nothing.
3 Even if I distributed all my possessions to feed the poor and gave my body to the flames, if I do not have love, it is of no use to me.
4 Love is patient, it is helpful; love is not envious, it does not boast, it is not conceited,
5 They do not act basely, they do not seek their own interest, they are not irritated, they do not take into account the evil they have received,
6 does not rejoice in injustice, but rejoices in the truth.
7 Love excuses everything, believes everything, hopes everything, endures everything.
8 Love will never pass. The prophecies will end, the gift of tongues will end, science will disappear;
9 because our science is imperfect and our prophecies are limited.
10 When that which is perfect comes, that which is imperfect will cease.
11 While I was a child, I spoke like a child, I felt like a child, I reasoned like a child,

12 But when I became a man, I put aside childish things. Now we see as in a mirror, confusedly; Then we will see face to face. Now I know everything imperfectly; later I will know how God
know me.
13 In a word, there are now three things: faith, hope and love, but the greatest of all is love.
1 Seek to achieve that love, and also aspire to spiritual gifts, especially that of prophecy.
2 For he who speaks an incomprehensible language does not address men but God, and no one understands him: he says mysterious things in ecstasy.
3 But he who prophesies speaks to men to edify them, exhort them, and comfort them.
4 He who speaks an incomprehensible language edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the community.

5 My desire is for all of you to have the gift of tongues, but I prefer that you prophesy, because he who prophesies is superior to him who speaks an incomprehensible language. Unless the latter also
interpret that language, for the edification of the community.
6 Suppose, brothers, that I were to see you and speak to you in this way, what use would it be to you, if my word brought you neither revelation, nor knowledge, nor prophecy, nor teaching?
7 The same would happen as with musical instruments, for example, the flute or the zither. If the notes do not sound distinct, no one recognizes what is being played.
8 And if the trumpet makes a confused sound, who will go into battle?
9 So it is with you: if you do not speak intelligibly, how will what you say be understood? They would be talking in vain.
10 I don't know how many different languages there are in the world, and each one has its own words.
11 But if I do not know the meaning of the words, I will be like a stranger to him who speaks to me and he will be like a stranger to me.
12 Therefore, since you so desire spiritual gifts, try to abound in those that serve to build up the community.
13 For this reason, he who speaks an incomprehensible language must pray for the gift of interpreting it.
14 For if I pray in an incomprehensible language, my spirit prays, but my intelligence does not benefit.
15 What should I do then? Pray with the spirit and also with the intelligence, sing hymns with the spirit and also with the intelligence.
16 If you bless God with the spirit alone, how can the uninitiated say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since they do not understand what you are saying?
17 Without a doubt, your thanksgiving is excellent, but that does not serve as an edification for others.
18 I thank God because I have the gift of tongues more than all of you.
19 However, when I am in the assembly I would rather say five intelligible words, to instruct others, than ten thousand in an incomprehensible language.
20 Brothers, do not be like children to judge; Be it for malice, but judge as mature people.
21 In the Law it is written: I will speak to this people in strange tongues and by the mouth of foreigners; Yet they will not even listen to me, says the Lord.
22 This means that the gift of tongues is a sign, not for those who believe, but for those who refuse to believe; prophecy, on the other hand, is for those who have faith.

23 On the other hand, if when the assembly meets, everyone begins to speak in an incomprehensible language and some who are not initiated or who are not believers enter, they will surely think that
you guys are crazy.
24 But if everyone prophesizes and one of those men comes in, everyone will be able to convince him and examine him.
25 Thus the secrets of his heart will be revealed, and he will fall on his knees and worship God and proclaim that God is truly among you.

26 Brothers, what conclusion will we draw from all this? When they come together, one may sing psalms, another may teach, or convey a revelation, or give a speech in a language.
incomprehensible, or give the interpretation of it. May everything serve for
common building.
27 Do you have the gift of languages? Let two, or at most three, speak in turn, and let someone interpret.
28 If there is no interpreter, let them be silent and let each one speak with himself and with God.
29 Regarding the prophets, let two or three speak and let the rest judge what they say.
30 If any other attendant receives a revelation, let the speaker be silent.
31 Thus everyone will have the opportunity to prophesy, one by one, so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged.
32 Those who have the gift of prophecy must be able to control their inspiration,
33 because God wants peace and not disorder. As in all the Churches of the saints,
34 that women remain silent during the assemblies: they are not allowed to speak. Let them submit, as the Law mandates.
35 If they need any clarification, they should ask the husband at home, because it is not right for the wife to speak in the assemblies.
36 Has the Word of God come from you or are you the only ones who have received it?
37 If anyone considers himself a prophet or believes he is inspired by the Spirit, let him recognize that I am writing to you a command from the Lord,
38 and if anyone does not recognize him as such, it is because God has not recognized him.
39 In conclusion, brothers, aspire to the gift of prophecy and do not prevent it from being spoken in an incomprehensible language.
40 But everything must be done with decorum and orderly.
1 Brothers, I remind you of the Good News that I have preached to you, that you have received and to which you remain faithful.
2 By it you are saved, if you keep it just as I announced it to you; Otherwise, they will have believed in vain.
3 I have transmitted to you first what I myself received: Christ died for our sins, according to the Scripture.
4 He was buried and rose again on the third day, according to the Scripture.
5 He appeared to Peter and then to the Twelve.
6 Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at the same time, most of whom are still alive, and some of whom have died.
7 Furthermore, he appeared to James and again to all the Apostles.
8 Lastly, it also appeared to me, that I am like the fruit of an abortion.
9 For I am the last of the Apostles, and I do not even deserve to be called an Apostle, since I have persecuted the Church of God.
10 But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace was not fruitless in me, but I have worked harder than all of them, although it was not I, but the grace of God that is with me.
11 In short, both they and I preach the same thing, and this is what you have believed.
12 If it is announced that Christ has risen from the dead, how do some of you claim that the dead are not raised?
13 If there is no resurrection, Christ is not resurrected!
14 And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is in vain and your faith is also in vain.
15 We would even be false witnesses of God, because we testify that he raised Jesus Christ, which is impossible if the dead are not raised.
16 For if the dead are not raised, neither has Christ been raised.
17 And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is useless and your sins have not been forgiven.
18 Consequently, those who died with faith in Christ have perished forever.
19 If we have put our hope in Christ only for this life, we would be the most pitiful men.
20 But no, Christ rose from the dead, the first of all.
21 For death came into the world through a man, and also through a man comes the resurrection.
22 Indeed, just as all die in Adam, so all will be revived in Christ,
23 each one according to the order that corresponds to him: Christ, the first of all, then those who are united to him at the moment of his Coming.
24 The end will come immediately, when Christ will hand over the Kingdom to God, the Father, after having annihilated all Principality, Dominion and Power.
25 For Christ must reign until he puts all enemies under his feet.
26 The last enemy that will be defeated is death,
27 since God put everything under his feet. But when he says, "Everything is subdued," it will evidently be except for him who has subdued all things to him.
28 And when the entire universe is submitted to him, the Son himself will also submit to him who submitted all things to him, so that God may be all in all.
29 If it were not so, what is the use of being baptized for those who have died? If the dead are not resurrected, what is the point of being baptized for them?
30 And why do we ourselves expose ourselves to danger at every moment?
31 Every day I face death, and this is as true, brothers, as you are my pride in Christ Jesus, our Lord.
32 And what have I gained, if only for human reasons, I had to fight with the wild beasts in Ephesus? If the dead do not rise, "let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die."
33 Do not be fooled: "Bad company corrupts good customs."
34 Go back to your proper behavior and sin no more, because there are some among you who still know nothing about God: I say this to your shame.
35 Someone will ask: How are the dead resurrected? With what kind of body?
36 Your question doesn't make sense. What you sow does not come to life if it does not die first.
37 And what you sow is not the plant as it will sprout, but a simple grain, of wheat for example, or of any other plant.
38 And God gives to each seed the form that he wants, to each type of seed, the body that corresponds to it.
39 Not all bodies are identical: one is the flesh of men, another is that of animals, another is that of birds and another is that of fish.
40 There are heavenly bodies and terrestrial bodies, and each has its own radiance:
41 One is the brightness of the sun, another is that of the moon, and another is that of the stars, and even the stars differ one from another by their brightness.
42 The same thing happens with the resurrection of the dead: corruptible bodies are sown and they will rise incorruptible;
43 humiliated bodies are sown and they will rise glorious; Weak bodies are sown and they will rise full of strength;
44 Purely natural bodies are sown and spiritual bodies will be resurrected. Because there is a purely natural body and there is also a spiritual body.
45 This is what the Scripture says: The first man, Adam, was created as a living being; The last Adam, on the other hand, is a spiritual being who gives Life.
46 But the spiritual did not exist first but the purely natural; the spiritual comes later.
47 The first man comes from the earth and is earthly; but the second man comes from heaven.
48 Earthly men will be like the earthly man, and heavenly men like the heavenly man.
49 Just as we have been clothed with the image of the earthly man, we will also be clothed with the image of the heavenly man.
50 I assure you, brothers, that what is purely human can have no part in the Kingdom of God, nor can corruption inherit what is incorruptible.
51 I am going to reveal a mystery to you: Not all of us will die, but we will all be transformed.
52 In an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, when the final trumpet sounds – because this will happen – the dead will rise incorruptible and we will be transformed.
53 That which is corruptible must be clothed with incorruptibility, and that which is mortal must be clothed with immortality.

54 When what is corruptible puts on incorruptibility and what is mortal puts on immortality, then the word of the Scripture will be fulfilled: Death has
been defeated.
55 Where is your victory, death? Where is your sting?
56 For what causes death is sin and what gives strength to sin is the law.
57 Let us thank God, who has given us victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
58 Therefore, dear brothers, remain firm and immovable, constantly progressing in the work of the Lord, with the certainty that the efforts you make for him will not be in vain.
1 Regarding the collection for the saints of Jerusalem, follow the same instructions that I gave to the Churches of Galatia.
2 On the first day of the week, each of you keep in your house what you have been able to save, so that the donations are not only collected upon my arrival.
3 Once there, I will send those you have chosen to take these donations to Jerusalem with a letter of recommendation.
4 If it is convenient for me to go too, they will travel with me.
5 I will go to see them, after passing through Macedonia where I will be passing through.
6 Perhaps I will stay with you for a while, perhaps all winter, so that you can help me continue my journey to my destination.
7 Because I do not want to see you only in passing, but I hope to stay with you for some time, if the Lord allows it.
8 Meanwhile, I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost,
9 since a great door has been opened for my preaching, although the adversaries are numerous.
10 If Timothy comes first, see to it that he remains among you without any fear, because he works in the work of the Lord in the same way as I do.
11 Let no one despise him. Offer him the necessary means to meet me, because I am waiting for him with the brothers.
12 As for our brother Apollo, I strongly urged him to go and visit them with the brothers, but he flatly refused to do so for now: he will go when the opportunity presents itself.
13 Be attentive, remain firm in the faith, behave manly, be strong.
14 Whatever you do, do it with love.
15 One more recommendation, brothers. You know that Stephanas and her family – the first to embrace the faith in Achaia – have decided to dedicate themselves to the service of the brothers.
16 Therefore, I ask you, in turn, to be attentive to them, and not only to them, but to all those who collaborate in their work and efforts.
17 I was happy with the visit of Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaico. They filled the void that you had left,
18 and they have calmed my spirit and yours. Know how to appreciate them accordingly.
19 The churches of the province of Asia send you greetings. They are also greeted in the Lord by Aquila and Priscilla, along with the brothers who congregate in their house.
20 All the brothers send greetings to you. Greet each other with the holy kiss.
21 This is my greeting, in my own handwriting: Pablo.
22 If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be cursed! "The Lord is coming."
23 May the grace of the Lord Jesus remain with you.
24 I love you all in Christ Jesus.
1 Paul, Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and brother Timothy, greet the Church of God that resides in Corinth, together with all the saints who live in the province of Achaia.
2 May grace and peace come to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
3 Blessed be God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Father of mercies and God of all comfort,
4 who comforts us in all our tribulations, so that we can give to those who suffer the same comfort that we receive from God.
5 For just as we share abundantly in the sufferings of Christ, so through Christ our comfort abounds.

6 If we suffer, it is for your comfort and salvation; If we are comforted, it is also for your comfort, and this allows you to endure with perseverance the same sufferings that
we suffer.
7 Therefore we have a well-founded hope regarding you, knowing that if you share our tribulations, you will also share our comfort.

8 We want you, brothers, to know the tribulation that we had to suffer in the province of Asia: the burden was so great that we could not bear it, to the point of thinking that we were about to die.
lose your life.
9 We endured in our own flesh a sentence of death, and thus learned not to put our trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead.
10 He delivered us and will deliver us from that mortal danger. Yes, we hope that it will also free us in the future.
11 You will also help us with your prayer, and in this way, since there are many who intercede for us, there will also be many who will give thanks for the benefit received.

12 This is a source of pride for us: the testimony that our conscience gives us that we have always, and particularly in relation to you, behaved with holiness
and sincerity that come from God, moved not by a purely
human, but by the grace of God.
13 Indeed, our letters are not ambiguous: there is no more in them than you can read and understand. And I hope you will fully understand
14 – as you have already partially understood – that on the Day of our Lord Jesus, you will be able to feel proud of us, as we are of you.
15 Convinced of this, I decided to visit you first, to give you new joy,
16 and from there go to Macedonia. Then, upon my return from Macedonia, you would help me continue my journey to Judea.
17 In proposing this, did I act hastily? Or were my plans based on purely human motives, so that I say "yes" and "no" at the same time?
18 I assure you, through the faithfulness of God, that our language with you is not today "yes", and tomorrow "no."
19 For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whom we proclaimed among you—both Silvanus and Timothy, as well as myself—was not “yes” and “no,” but only “yes.”
20 Indeed, all the promises of God find their "yes" in Jesus, so that through him we say "Amen" to God, for his glory.
21 And it is God who comforts us and you in Christ; the one who has anointed us,
22 who has also marked us with his seal and put the firstfruits of the Spirit in our hearts.
23 I call God as my witness, and I swear on my own life, that if I did not return to Corinth it was out of consideration for you.
24 For we do not intend to impose our dominion over your faith, since you remain firm in the faith: what we want is to increase your joy.
1 I am determined not to pay you another visit that will cause you sadness.
2 For if I make them sad, who can make me happy but the same one whom I made sad?

3 And if I have written to you what you already know, it was so that I would not be sad when I arrived, because of those who should have made me happy, because I am convinced that my joy is also yours.
4 Truly I wrote to you with great affliction and anguish, and with many tears, not to sadden you, but to show you the deep affection I have for you.
5 If someone saddened me, it saddened not only me but also, to a certain extent – I say this without exaggeration – all of you.
6 I think the punishment that the majority has imposed on the offender is sufficient.
7 It is now advisable to forgive him and encourage him so that the poor person is not overwhelmed by excessive pain.
8 Therefore, I ask you to make love prevail in this case.
9 I wrote to you earlier to test you and see if you are able to obey in everything.
10 But now I also forgive him whom you forgave, and I do it in the presence of Christ for your sake,
11 so that Satan does not take advantage of us, since we know his intentions well.
12 When I came to Troas to announce the Good News of Jesus, although the Lord opened a door for my preaching,
13 I was very worried because I did not find my brother Tito; Therefore, I said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.
14 Let us give thanks to God, who always makes us triumph in Christ, and through us spreads the fragrance of his knowledge everywhere.
15 For we are the fragrance of Christ in the service of God, both among those who are saved and among those who are lost:
16 for these, an aroma of death, which leads to death; for those, aroma of life, which leads to Life. And who is capable of accomplishing such a task?
17 But we are not like many who traffic in the Word of God, but we speak sincerely in the name of Christ, as sent by God and in the presence of God himself.
1 Shall we start recommending ourselves again? Do we have to present or receive letters of recommendation from you, as some do?
2 You yourselves are our letter, a letter written in our hearts, known and read by all men.

3 Evidently you are a letter that Christ wrote through us, not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone, but of flesh, that is, in the
hearts.
4 It is Christ who gives us this security before God,
5 not because we can attribute something that comes from ourselves, since all our ability comes from God.
6 He has enabled us to be the ministers of a New Covenant, which resides not in the letter, but in the Spirit; because the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

7 Now, if the ministry that leads to death – engraved on stones – was inaugurated with such glory that the Israelites could not fix their eyes on the face of Moses, because of the brightness
–although temporary– of that face,
8 How much more glorious will be the ministry of the Spirit!
9 And if the ministry that led to damnation was so glorious, what will not be the glory of the ministry that leads to justice!
10 In reality, that which was glorious in a certain aspect is no longer so in comparison with this extraordinary glory.
11 For if what was temporary has been revealed with such glory, how much more glorious will be what is permanent!
12 Encouraged by this hope, we behave with absolute frankness,
13 and not like Moses, who covered his face with a veil to prevent the Israelites from seeing the end of a passing splendor.
14 But their understanding was darkened, and that same veil remains to this day in the reading of the Old Testament, because it is Christ who makes it disappear.
