1 Foolish Galatians, who has seduced you, before whom the image of Jesus Christ crucified was presented?
2 I want to know only one thing: did you receive the Spirit by the works of the Law or by believing the preaching?
3 Have they been so foolish that they went so far as to begin with the Spirit and now end in the flesh?
4 Could it have been in vain that they received so many favors? I hope it wasn't in vain!
5 Is he who lavishes the Spirit on you and is working miracles among you because of the works of the Law or because you have believed the preaching?
6 This is the case of Abraham, who believed in God, and this was taken into account for his justification.
7 Recognize, then, that the true children of Abraham are those who have faith.
8 The Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the pagans by faith, anticipated this good news to Abraham, promising him: "In you all nations will be blessed."
9 In this way, those who believe are those who participate in the blessing of Abraham, the believer.

10 Indeed, all those who trust in the works of the Law are under a curse, for the Scripture says: "Cursed is he who does not faithfully do everything that is written."
written in the book of the Law."
11 It is evident that before God no one is justified by the Law, since the righteous will live by faith.
12 The Law does not take faith into account, but whoever observes its precepts will live by them.
13 Christ freed us from this curse of the Law, becoming a curse for us, for it is also written: "Cursed is he who hangs on the scaffold."
14 And this, so that the blessing of Abraham might reach all the pagans in Christ Jesus, and we might receive the promised Spirit by faith.
15 Brothers, I want to give you an example from everyday life: when a man makes a will in due form, no one can annul it and add anything to it.

16 The promises were made to Abraham and his descendants. The Scripture does not say: "and to the descendants," as if it were many, but in the singular: and to their
offspring, that is, to Christ.
17 Now I tell you this: the Law enacted four hundred and thirty years later cannot annul a will formally established by God, thus rendering the promise void.
18 For if the inheritance is received by virtue of the Law, it is no longer by virtue of the promise. And in reality, God granted his grace to Abraham through a promise.

19 So what is the Law for? She was added to multiply the transgressions, until the descendant of Abraham, to whom the promise was intended, arrived; and was promulgated by angels,
through a mediator.
20 But there is no mediator when there is only one party, and God is only one.
21 Does this mean that the Law is opposed to God's promises? By no means! Because if we had received a Law capable of communicating Life, certainly justice would come from the Law.
22 But in fact, the written Law subjected everything to sin, so that the promise could be fulfilled in those who believe, thanks to faith in Jesus Christ.
23 Before faith came, we were held captive in the custody of the Law, awaiting the faith that was to be revealed.
24 Thus the Law served as a guide to bring us to Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
25 And now that faith has come, we need no more than a guide.
26 For you are all children of God through faith in Christ Jesus,
27 since all of you who were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
28 Therefore, there is neither Jew nor pagan, slave nor free man, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
29 And if you belong to Christ, then you are descendants of Abraham, heirs under the promise.
1 I will be more explicit: the heir, while he is a minor, even if he is the owner of all his property, is in no way different from a slave.
2 In fact, until the age set by his father, he is dependent on his guardians and administrators.
3 Likewise we, when we were minors, were subjected to the elements of the world.
4 But when the appointed time was fulfilled, God sent his Son, born of a woman and subject to the Law,
5 to redeem those who were subject to the Law and make us adopted children.
6 And the proof that you are children is that God breathed into our hearts the Spirit of his Son, who cries out to God calling him "Abba!", that is, Father!
7 Thus, you are no longer a slave, but a son, and therefore an heir by the grace of God.
8 Before, when you did not know God, you were serving gods who are not really gods.
9 But now, that you know God – or rather, that you are known by him – how is it possible that you turn again to those elements without strength or courage, to submit to them again?
10 Observe the days, months, seasons and years!
11 Frankly, I fear that I have worked for you in vain.
12 I beseech you, brothers, become like me, as I became like you. Actually, they haven't offended me at all.
13 You know that it was during an illness that I first preached the Good News to you.
14 Even though my physical appearance was a test for you, you did not disdain me or despise me; On the contrary, they received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
15 Where is the joy you felt then? I myself can attest that, if it were possible, they would have gouged out their eyes to give them to me.
16 And now have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?
17 The interest that others show in you is not good: what they want is to separate you from me, so that you may be interested in them.
18 It is okay to be interested in others, as long as that interest is true and forever, and not only when I am among you.
19 My children, for whom I am again suffering the pains of childbirth until Christ is formed in you!
20 Right now I wish I were there to speak to you in a different way, because I no longer know how to proceed with you.
21 You who want to submit to the Law, tell me: Do you not understand what the Law says?
22 For it is written that Abraham had two sons: one by his slave and another by his wife, who was free.
23 The son of the slave nation according to the flesh; On the other hand, the son of the free woman was born by virtue of the promise.
24 There is symbolism in all this: these two women represent the two Covenants. The first Alliance, that of Mount Sinai, which generated a people for slavery, is represented by Hagar,
25 because Mount Sinai is in Arabia, and corresponds to present-day Jerusalem, since she and her children live in slavery.
26 But there is another Jerusalem, the heavenly one, which is free, and she is our mother.

27 For the Scripture says: "Rejoice, you who are barren and do not give birth; break out into shouts of joy, you who do not know the pains of childbirth! For they will be more numerous
the children of the abandoned woman than the children of the one who has a husband.
28 We, brothers, are like Isaac, children of the promise.
29 And just as then the son born according to the flesh persecuted the son born of the Spirit, so it is now.
30 But the Scripture says: Cast out the slave woman and her son, because the son of the slave woman will not share the inheritance with the son of the free woman.
31 Therefore, brothers, we are not children of a slave, but of the free woman.
1 This is the freedom that Christ has given us. Stand firm so as not to fall again under the yoke of slavery.
2 I myself, Paul, tell you: if you become circumcised, Christ will be of no use to you.
3 I insist again: all those who are circumcised are obliged to fully observe the Law.
4 If you seek justice through the Law, you have broken with Christ and are outside the dominion of grace.
5 For we, the Spirit, make us hope for the good things of righteousness by faith.
6 Indeed, in Christ Jesus, circumcision and uncircumcision no longer count, but faith working through love.
7 You were doing so well...! Who prevented them from remaining faithful to the truth?
8 It will not have been at the request of the one who calls them!
9 "A little yeast makes the whole dough ferment."
10 I hope in the Lord that you will not change your mind. As for the one who is disturbing you, he will be punished, whoever he is.
11 Brethren, if I were still preaching circumcision, you would not persecute me. But then, the scandal of the cross would be over!
12 As for the agitators, I wish they would go as far as total mutilation.

13 You, brothers, have been called to live in freedom, but see to it that this freedom is not a pretext for satisfying carnal desires, but rather become servants of one another.
others, through love.
14 For the whole Law is fully summarized in this precept: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
15 But if you are biting and devouring each other, be careful because you will end up destroying each other.
16 I urge you to let yourselves be led by the Spirit of God, so that you will not be carried away by the desires of the flesh.
17 For the flesh desires against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh. You both fight each other, and because of that, you cannot do all the good you want.
18 But if they are animated by the Spirit, they are no longer subject to the Law.
19 It is well known what are the works of the flesh: fornication, impurity and debauchery,
20 idolatry and superstition, enmities and quarrels, rivalries and violence, ambitions and discord, sectarianisms, dissensions
21 and envy, drunkenness and orgies, and all excesses of this nature. I repeat to you again that those who do these things will not possess the Kingdom of God.
22 On the contrary, the fruit of the Spirit is: love, joy and peace, magnanimity, kindness, goodness and trust,
23 meekness and temperance. Faced with these things, the Law is unnecessary,
24 For those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and its evil desires.
25 If we live animated by the Spirit, let us also allow ourselves to be led by him.
26 Let us not seek vainglory, provoking one another and envying each other.
1 Brethren, if anyone is caught in any fault, you who are animated by the Spirit, gently correct him. Think that you too can be tempted.
2 Help each other carry the burdens, and thus you will fulfill the Law of Christ.
3 If someone imagines himself to be something, he is deceived, because in reality he is nothing.
4 Let each one examine his own conduct, and thus he will be able to find in himself and not in others, a reason for satisfaction.
5 Because each one has to carry his own burden.
6 He who receives the teaching of the Word, let him who instructs him share in all his goods.
7 Do not be deceived: no one mocks God. You reap what you sow:
8 He who sows to satisfy his flesh, of the flesh he will reap only corruption; and he who sows according to the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal Life.
9 Let us not get tired of doing good, because the harvest will come in its time if we do not give up.
10 Therefore, while we have time, let us do good to everyone, but especially to our brothers in the faith.
11 Do you see these big letters? I am writing to you with my own hand!
12 Those who want to impose circumcision on them only seek to look good on the outside, and to avoid being persecuted because of the cross of Christ.
13 For neither do those who are circumcised observe the Law; They only want you to be circumcised to boast about it.
14 I will only glory in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified to me, as I am to the world.
15 Being circumcised or not circumcised has no importance: what matters is being a new creature.
16 May all who practice this rule have peace and mercy, as does the Israel of God.
17 Let no one bother me from now on: I carry the scars of Jesus on my body.
18 Brethren, may the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ remain with you. Amen.
1 Paul, Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, greets the saints who believe in Christ Jesus.
2 May grace and peace come to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

3 Blessed be God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ
with all kinds of spiritual goods in heaven,

4 And he chose us in him, before the creation of the world, that we should be holy
and blameless in his presence, for love.

5 He predestined us to be his adopted children through Jesus Christ,
according to the good pleasure of his will,
6 to praise the glory of his grace, which he gave us in his dearly beloved Son.

7 In him we have been redeemed by his blood and have received forgiveness of sins,
according to the riches of his grace,
8 that God poured out on us, giving us all wisdom and understanding.

9 He made known to us the mystery of his will, according to his merciful plan
which he established beforehand in Christ,

10 that it might be fulfilled in the fullness of time: to gather together all things, things in heaven and things on earth,
under one head, who is Christ.
11 In him we have been made heirs, and ordained beforehand—according to the foreordination of him who works out all things according to his will—
12 to be those who have put their hope in Christ, to the praise of his glory.

13 In him, you who heard the Word of truth, the Good News of salvation,
and they believed in her,
They have also been marked with a seal
by the promised Holy Spirit.

14 That Spirit is the down payment of our inheritance and prepares the redemption of the people
which God acquired for himself,
to the praise of his glory.
15 Therefore, having learned of the faith that you have in the Lord Jesus and the love that you show for all the brothers,
16 I give thanks without ceasing for you, always remembering you in my prayers
17 May the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, grant you a spirit of wisdom and revelation that enables you to truly know Him.
18 May he enlighten your hearts, so that you may appreciate the hope to which you have been called, the treasures of glory that your inheritance among the saints contains,
19 and the extraordinary greatness of the power with which he works in us, believers, by the effectiveness of his strength. This is the same power
20 which God manifested in Christ, when he raised him from the dead and made him sit at his right hand in heaven,
21 elevating it above all Principality, Power, Power and Domination, and every other dignity that can be mentioned both in this world and in the future.
22 He put all things under his feet and made him, above all, Head of the Church,
23 which is his Body and the Fullness of him who completely fills all things.
1 You were dead because of faults and sins
2 that they committed, when they lived according to the criteria of this world, according to the Prince who rules in space, the same Spirit who continues to act in those who rebel.

3 All of us also behaved like this in former times, living according to our carnal desires and satisfying our lusts and our evil inclinations,
so that due to our condition we were condemned to anger, just like the
others.
4 But God, who is rich in mercy, because of the great love with which he loved us,
5 Just when we were dead because of our sins, he made us alive with Christ – you have been saved freely!
6 and with Christ Jesus raised us up and made us reign with him in heaven.
7 Thus, God wanted to demonstrate to future times the immense riches of his grace through the love he has for us in Christ Jesus.
8 For you have been saved by his grace, through faith. This does not come from you, but is a gift from God;
9 and it is not the result of works, so that no one can boast.
10 We are his creation: we were created in Christ Jesus to do those good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do.
11 Therefore, remember what you were before: pagans by birth, called "uncircumcised" by those who call themselves "circumcised" by virtue of a cut made in the flesh.
12 Then you did not have Christ and were excluded from the community of Israel, foreigners from the covenants of promise, without hope and without God in the world.
13 But now in Christ Jesus you who were once far away have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
14 For Christ is our peace; He has united the two peoples into one, breaking down the wall of enmity that separated them,
15 and abolishing in his own flesh the Law with its commandments and prescriptions. Thus he created with the two peoples a single new Man in his own person, reestablishing peace,
16 and reconciled them to God in one Body, through the cross, destroying the enmity in his person.
17 And he came to proclaim the Good News of peace, peace to you who were far away, peace also to those who were near.
18 Because through Christ, we all without distinction have access to the Father, in one Spirit.
19 Therefore, you are no longer foreigners or guests, but fellow citizens of the saints and members of the household of God.
20 You are built on the apostles and the prophets, who are the foundation, while the cornerstone is Jesus Christ himself.
21 In it, the entire building, well joined together, grows to constitute a holy temple in the Lord.
22 In it, you too are incorporated into the building, to become a dwelling place of God in the Spirit.
1 Therefore I, Paul, am imprisoned for Christ Jesus, because of you, those of pagan origin.
2 For you have surely heard of the grace of God, which has been given to me for your benefit.
3 It was through a revelation that this mystery was made known to me, as I have just explained it to you in a few words.
4 As you read them, you will realize the understanding I have of the mystery of Christ,
5 which was not revealed to past generations, but has now been revealed through the Spirit to his holy apostles and prophets.
6 This mystery consists in the fact that the pagans also participate in the same inheritance, are members of the same Body and beneficiaries of the same promise in Christ Jesus, through the Gospel.
7 Of this Gospel I was made a minister by the gift of grace which I received from God, by virtue of the effectiveness of his power.
8 I, the least of all saints, have received the grace to announce to the pagans the unsearchable riches of Christ,
9 and to reveal the dispensation of the mystery that was hidden from time immemorial in God, the creator of all things,
10 so that the Principalities and Heavenly Powers may know the infinite variety of God's wisdom through the Church.
11 This is the plan that God conceived from all eternity in Christ Jesus our Lord,
12 through whom we dare to approach God with complete confidence, through faith in him.
13 Therefore I ask you not to be discouraged because of the tribulations that I suffer for you: they are your glory!
14 Therefore I bow my knees before the Father,
15 from whom comes all fatherhood in heaven and on earth.
16 May he deign to strengthen you by his Spirit, according to the riches of his glory, so that the inner man may grow in you.
17 May Christ dwell in your hearts through faith, and may you be rooted and built up in love.
18 So you will be able to understand, with all the saints, what is the width and length, height and depth,
19 in a word, you will be able to know the love of Christ, which surpasses all knowledge, to be filled with the fullness of God.
20 To him who is able to do infinitely more than we can ask or think, by the power that works in us,
21 To him be glory in the Church and in Christ Jesus, to all generations and forever! Amen.
1 I, who am a prisoner for the Lord, exhort you to conduct yourself in a manner worthy of the vocation you have received.
2 With much humility, meekness and patience, bear with each other out of love.
3 Try to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.
4 There is one Body and one Spirit, just as there is one hope, to which you have been called, according to the vocation received.
5 there is one Lord, one faith, one baptism.
6 There is one God and Father of all, who is above all, pervades all, and is in all.
7 However, each of us has received his own gift, as Christ has distributed them.
8 That is why the Scripture says: "When he ascended on high, he took the captives with him and distributed gifts to men."
9 But if we say that he ascended, it means that he first descended to the lower regions of the earth.
10 He who descended is the same one who ascended beyond the heavens, to fill the entire universe.
11 He communicated to some the gift of being apostles, to others prophets, to others preachers of the Gospel, to others pastors or teachers.
12 Thus he organized the saints for the work of the ministry, for the building up of the Body of Christ,
13 until we all reach the unity of faith and knowledge of the Son of God, the state of perfect man and the maturity that corresponds to the fullness of Christ.
14 Thus we will cease to be children, tossed by the waves and carried by the wind of any doctrine, at the mercy of the malice of men and their cunning to teach error.
15 On the contrary, living in truth and love, we may grow fully, united to Christ. He is the Head,

16 and from it, the entire Body receives unity and cohesion, thanks to the ligaments that give life to it and the harmonious action of all the members. Thus the Body grows and is built
in love
17 I tell you and I recommend to you in the name of the Lord: do not act like the pagans, who allow themselves to be carried away by the frivolity of their thoughts.
18 and their minds are darkened. They are separated from the Life of God by their ignorance and their obstinacy,
19 and having lost their moral sense, they have given themselves over to vice, committing all kinds of impurities without restraint.
20 But that is not what you learned from Christ,
21 if indeed they heard him preached and were taught according to the truth that resides in Jesus.
22 From him they learned that it is necessary to renounce the life they led, putting aside the old man, which is being corrupted by the seduction of concupiscence,
23 to renew yourself in the most intimate part of your spirit
24 and put on the new man, created in the image of God in righteousness and true holiness.
25 Therefore, renounce lies and always tell the truth to your neighbors, since we are all members, one of another.
26 If you become angry, do not let yourselves be drawn into sin nor let the night catch you angry,
27 thus giving opportunity to the devil.
28 He who stole, let him stop stealing and start working honestly with his hands, so that he can help those who are in need.
29 Do not utter inconvenient words; On the contrary, let your words always be good, so that they may be edifying when necessary and do good to those who hear them.
30 Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, who has marked you with a seal for the day of redemption.
31 Avoid bitterness, outbursts, anger, shouting, insults and all kinds of evil.
32 Instead, be kind and compassionate to each other, forgiving one another as God has forgiven you in Christ.
1 Try to imitate God, as his very dear children.
2 Practice love, after the example of Christ, who loved us and gave himself for us, as an offering and sacrifice pleasing to God.
3 As for carnal sin and any kind of impurity or covetousness, do not even mention them among yourselves, as befits saints.
4 I say the same about obscenities, bad conversations and rude jokes: all of these are out of place. What you should do is give thanks to God.
5 And know it well: neither the lustful man, nor the impure man, nor the covetous man, who is an idolater, will have any part in the inheritance of the Kingdom of Christ and of God.
6 Do not be deceived by false reasons: all this attracts the wrath of God on those who refuse to obey him.
7 Do not become accomplices of those who act like this!
8 Once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Live as children of light.
9 Now the fruit of light is goodness, justice and truth.
10 Know how to discern what pleases the Lord,
11 and do not participate in the fruitless works of darkness; On the contrary, put them in evidence.
12 It is true that it is shameful to even mention the things that these people do secretly.
13 But when they are revealed, they appear illuminated by light,

14 because everything that is revealed is light. That is why it is said: Awake, you who sleep,
rise from the dead,
and Christ will enlighten you.
15 Be very careful with your conduct and do not act like fools, but like sensible people
16 who know how to make good use of the present moment, because these times are bad.
17 Do not be irresponsible, but try to know what the will of the Lord is.
18 Do not abuse wine that leads to debauchery; rather, be filled with the Holy Spirit.
19 When you come together, recite psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing and celebrating the Lord with all your heart.
20 Always and for whatever reason, give thanks to God, our Father, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
21 Submit to one another for Christ's sake.
22 Women must respect their husbands as they do the Lord,
23 because the man is the head of the woman, just as Christ is the Head and Savior of the Church, which is his Body.
24 Just as the Church is submitted to Christ, in the same way women must respect their husbands in everything.
25 Husbands, love your wives, as Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for her,
26 to sanctify it. He purified her with the baptism of water and the word,
27 because he wanted for himself a resplendent Church, without spot or wrinkle and without any defect, but holy and immaculate.
28 Likewise, husbands should love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself.
29 No one despises his own body, but nourishes it and takes care of it. This is what Christ does for the Church,
30 for us, who are the members of his Body.
31 Therefore a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.
32 This is a great mystery: and I say that it refers to Christ and the Church.
33 As for you, each one must love his wife as himself, and the wife must respect her husband.
1 Children, obey your parents in the Lord because this is right,
2 since the first commandment that contains a promise is this: Honor your father and your mother,
3 so that you are happy and have a long life on earth.
4 Parents, do not irritate your children; On the contrary, educate them, correcting them and advising them, according to the spirit of the Lord.
5 Slaves, obey your masters with fear and respect, without any kind of duplicity, as if you served Christ;
6 not with a feigned obedience that tries to please men, but as servants of Christ, fulfilling the will of God with all their heart.
7 Serve your masters willingly, as if it were the Lord and not men,
8 considering that the Lord will reward everyone for the good he has done, whether he is a slave or a free man.

9 And you, masters, behave in the same way towards your servants and put aside threats, knowing that their Lord, who is also yours, is in
heaven, and is no respecter of persons.
10 Finally, be strong in the Lord with the strength of his power.
11 Put on the armor of God, so that you can resist the attacks of the devil.

12 For our struggle is not against enemies of flesh and blood, but against the Principalities and Powers, against the Rulers of this world of darkness, against the spirits of evil
that live in space.
13 Therefore take up the armor of God, so that you may be able to resist in the evil day and stand firm after having overcome all obstacles.
14 Stand tall, girded with the belt of truth and putting on righteousness as your breastplate.
15 Shod your feet with zeal to spread the Good News of peace.
16 Always have the shield of faith in your hand, with which you will be able to extinguish all the flaming arrows of the Evil One.
17 Take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God.
18 Constantly raise up all kinds of prayers and supplications, animated by the Spirit. Dedicate yourselves with tireless perseverance to intercede for all the brothers,
19 and also for me, so that I may find suitable words to resolutely announce the mystery of the Gospel,
20 of which I am an ambassador in the midst of my chains. Then I can talk freely about him, as I should!
21 Tychicus, the dear brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will update you on how I am and what I am doing.
22 For this purpose, I sent him so that he could give you news of us and comfort you internally.
23 May peace, love and faith come to all brothers, which come from God, the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
24 May grace remain with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with an incorruptible love.
1 Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, greet all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, as well as those who preside over the community and the deacons.
2 May grace and peace come to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
3 I thank God every time I remember them.
4 Always and in all my prayers I ask with joy for all of you,
5 thinking about the collaboration they gave to the spread of the Gospel, from the beginning until now.
6 I am firmly convinced that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the Day of Christ Jesus.

7 And it is right that I have these feelings towards all of you, because I carry them in my heart, since you, whether when I am a prisoner or when I work in the defense and confirmation of the
Gospel, participate in the grace that I have received.
8 God is witness that I love you all dearly in the heart of Christ Jesus.
9 And in my prayer I ask that your love may grow more and more in knowledge and in full understanding,
10 so that you may discern what is best. Thus they will be found pure and blameless on the Day of Christ.
11 filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes from Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
12 I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has rather contributed to the progress of the Gospel.
13 Indeed, in the Praetorium and everywhere, it has become evident that it is for Christ that I wear the chains,
14 and most of the brothers, to whom my chains have restored courage in the Lord, have been encouraged to proclaim the Word of God without fear.
15 It is true that some preach Christ out of envy and a spirit of discord, but others do so with good intentions.
16 These work out of love, knowing that I have the mission of defending the Gospel.
17 Those, however, proclaim Christ out of a spirit of discord, for motives that are not pure, believing that in this way they increase the weight of my chains.
18 But what does it matter! After all, in one way or another, with or without sincerity, Christ is announced, and in this I rejoice and will always rejoice.
19 Because I know that this will help my salvation, thanks to your prayers and the help that the Spirit of Jesus Christ gives me.
20 So I look forward to it, and I will not be disappointed. On the contrary, I am completely sure that now, as always, whether I live or die, Christ will be glorified in my body.
21 For to me life is Christ, and death is gain.
22 But if life in this body allows me to continue working fruitfully, I no longer know what to choose.
23 I feel urged on both sides: I want to go away to be with Christ, because it is much better,
24 but for your sake it is better that he remain in this body.
25 I am fully convinced that I will stay and remain with all of you, so that you may progress and rejoice in the faith.
26 In this way, my return and my presence among you will give you a new reason for pride in Christ Jesus.

27 I only ask that you behave as worthy followers of the Gospel of Christ. In this way, whether I go to see you or hear about you while I am away, I will know that you persevere in a
same spirit, fighting with one accord and with one heart for the faith of the
Gospel,
28 and without being intimidated at all by the adversaries. This is a sure sign that they are going to ruin, and you to salvation. This comes from God,
29 who has given you the grace not only to believe in Christ but also to suffer for him,
30 maintaining the same fight in which you have seen me engaged and now you know that I continue to maintain.
1 If the exhortation in the name of Christ is of any value, if the comfort that comes from love or fellowship in the Spirit, or tenderness and compassion is worth anything,
2 I beg you to make my joy perfect, remaining united. Have the same love, the same heart, the same thought.
3 Do nothing out of a spirit of discord or vanity, and let humility lead you to esteem others as superior to yourselves.
4 Let each one seek not only his own interest, but also that of others.
5 Have the same feelings as Christ Jesus.
6 He, who was of divine condition, did not consider this equality with God something to be jealously guarded:

7 On the contrary, he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant and being born in the likeness of men.
And presenting himself with human appearance,
8 He humbled himself to the point of accepting death and death on a cross out of obedience.
9 Therefore God exalted him and gave him the Name that is above every name,

10 so that at the name of Jesus, every knee bows
in heaven, on earth and in the abysses,
11 and let every tongue proclaim to the glory of God the Father: “Jesus Christ is Lord.”
12 Therefore, my dear ones, you who have always obeyed me, work for your salvation with fear and trembling, not only when I am among you, but even more so now that I am absent.
13 For it is God who works in you to will and to do, according to his loving plan.
14 Proceed in everything without murmuring or arguing:
15 so you will be blameless and pure, children of God without blemish, in the midst of a lost and perverted generation, among whom you shine like beams of light in the world,
16 showing him the Word of Life. In this way, on the Day of Christ I will be able to boast that I have not worked or suffered in vain.
17 And although my blood should be poured out as a libation on the sacrifice and the sacred offering, which is your faith, I feel happy and share your joy;
18 You too, feel blessed and rejoice with me.
19 I hope, with the help of the Lord Jesus, to send Timothy to you very soon to hear from you and experience relief myself.
20 Because I cannot find another who takes your affairs as seriously as he does.
21 Everyone else seeks their own interests and not those of Christ Jesus.
22 You already know that he has shown proof of his virtue, because he served with me in the cause of the Gospel, like a son next to his father.
23 That is why I hope to send it, as soon as my situation is clarified.
24 On the other hand, I have confidence in the Lord that soon I will be able to go personally.
25 I have thought it necessary to send you again Epaphroditus, my brother, collaborator and fellow fighter, whom you sent to assist me in my needs.
26 He had a great desire to see you all again, and he was very worried because you had found out about his illness.
27 In fact, he was sick and about to die, but God had compassion on him, and not only on him, but also on me, so that I would not have any more pain besides what I already have.
28 Now I hasten to send it to you, so that your presence may fill you with joy, and I, for my part, may be less sad.
29 Receive him in the Lord with great joy, and have people like him in great esteem.

1 Meanwhile, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. It costs me nothing to write the same things, and for you it is a security.

3 For we are the truly circumcised, who offer worship inspired by the Spirit of God and glorify in Christ Jesus, instead of putting our trust in
the flesh, although I also have reasons to put my trust in it.
4 If anyone believes that he can trust in the flesh, I can do so with more reason;
5 circumcised on the eighth day; of the race of Israel and the tribe of Benjamin; Hebrew, son of Hebrews; regarding the Law, a Pharisee;
6 by the ardor of my heaven, persecutor of the Church; and as regards the justice that comes from the Law, from irreproachable conduct.
7 But everything that I until now considered gain, I consider loss because of Christ.

8 Furthermore, everything seems to me to be a disadvantage compared to the priceless knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord. For him I have sacrificed all things, which I consider waste, in order to
win christ
9 and be united to him, not with my own righteousness – that which comes from the Law – but with that which is born from faith in Christ, which comes from God and is founded on faith.
10 So I will be able to know him, know the power of his resurrection and share in his sufferings, until I become like him in death,
11 in order to reach, if possible, the resurrection from the dead.
12 This does not mean that I have reached the goal or achieved perfection, but I continue my race in the hope of reaching it, having myself been reached by Christ Jesus.
13 Brethren, I do not claim to have attained it. I only say this: forgetting the path I have traveled, I rush forward
14 and I run towards the goal, to obtain the prize of the heavenly call that God has given me in Christ Jesus.
15 This is how we who are mature should think; and if you think otherwise about anything, God will enlighten you.
16 In any case, whatever point we have reached, let us continue on the same path.
17 Follow my example, brothers, and watch closely those who follow the example I have given you.
18 Because I have warned you frequently and now I repeat to you crying: there are many who behave as enemies of the cross of Christ.
19 Their end is prediction, their god is the womb, their glory is in that which covers them with shame, and they only appreciate the things of the earth.
20 But we are citizens of heaven, and we earnestly wait for the Lord Jesus Christ to come from there as Savior.
21 He will transform our poor mortal body, making it like his glorious body, with the power he has to bring all things under his dominion.

4 Always rejoice in the Lord. I insist again, rejoice.
5 May your goodness be known to all men. The Lord is near.
6 Do not be anxious about anything, and in any circumstance, resort to prayer and supplication, accompanied by thanksgiving, to present your requests to God.
7 Then the peace of God, which surpasses all we can think, will take care of your hearts and thoughts in Christ Jesus.

8 Finally, my brothers, whatever is true and noble, whatever is just and pure, whatever is lovely and worthy of honor, whatever is virtuous and worthy of praise, must be
the object of your thoughts.
9 Put into practice what you have learned and received, what you have heard and seen in me, and the God of peace will be with you.
10 I had great joy in the Lord when I saw your good feelings towards me flourish; They certainly had them, but they lacked the opportunity to demonstrate them.
11 It is not necessity that makes me speak, because I have learned to face any situation.
12 I know how to live both in deprivation and in abundance; I am made for absolutely everything, for satiety as for hunger, for having plenty as for having nothing.
13 I can do everything in him who comforts me.
14 However, you did well to take an interest in my needs.
15 And you know, Philippians, that at the beginning of the evangelization, when I left Macedonia, no other church helped me financially. You were the only ones
16 that when I was in Thessalonica, on two occasions they sent me means to assist me in my needs.
17 It's not that I look for gifts; I just want to give you the opportunity to become increasingly richer before God.

18 For the moment, I have everything I need and even more. I have lived in abundance since Epaphroditus gave me your offering, as a perfume with a pleasant aroma, as an acceptable and pleasant sacrifice.
to God.

7 being instructed by Epaphras, our dear companion in the service of God. He is for you a faithful minister of Christ,

9 Therefore, since we heard about this, we have been praying and asking for you without ceasing, that God may make his will known to you perfectly, and give you abundantly wisdom and
the meaning of spiritual things.

11 Fully strengthened by the power of his glory, they will acquire true firmness and steadfastness of mind,
12 and they will give thanks with joy to the Father, who has made us worthy to share in the luminous inheritance of the saints.

15 He is the Image of the invisible God,
16 because in him all things were created,
17 He exists before all things

irreproachable

23 For this it is necessary that you remain firm and well founded in the faith, without turning away from the hope transmitted by the Good News that you have heard and that was preached to all people.
creatures that are under heaven and of which I myself, Paul, was made
minister.

26 the mystery that was hidden from all eternity and that God now wanted to reveal to his saints.

1 Yes, I want you to know how hard the fight I am for you, for the Laodiceans, and for so many others who do not know me personally.

Christ,
3 in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.

12 In baptism you were buried with him, and you were raised with him, through faith in the power of God who raised him from the dead.

15 As for the Principalities and Powers, he stripped them and publicly exposed them to ridicule, incorporating them into his triumphal procession.

18 Let no one deprive them of the prior, under the pretext of "humility" and a "worship of angels." These people take into account only the things they have seen and boast in pride.
of his carnal mentality.

19 but it is not held together with the Head, which gives life to the whole Body and gives it cohesion through the joints and ligaments, so that its growth takes place in

20 Since you have died with Christ, to the elements of the world, why do you submit to the prohibitions of
21 "do not drink", "do not eat" and "do not touch", as if they still lived in the world?
22 All of this refers to things destined to be destroyed by their very use and are nothing more than precepts and doctrines of men.
23 These doctrines have a certain appearance of wisdom due to their "religiosity", their "humility" and their "contempt of the body", but they are worthless and only satisfy the desires of the flesh.
1 Since you have been raised with Christ, seek the goods of heaven where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
2 Keep your thoughts on heavenly things and not on earthly things.
3 For you are dead, and your life is from now on hidden with Christ in God.
4 When Christ, who is our life, appears, then you also will appear with him, full of glory.
5 Therefore put to death in your members everything that is earthly: lust, impurity, inordinate passion, evil desires, and also covetousness, which is a form of idolatry.
6 These things provoke the wrath of God.
7 You yourselves behaved like this in the past, living disorderly.
8 But now you must put an end to anger, resentment, malice, slander, and rude talk.
9 Neither do you deceive one another. Because you put off the old man and his works
10 and they put on the new man, the one who advances toward perfect knowledge, constantly being renewed according to the image of his Creator.
11 Therefore there is no longer pagan or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian or foreigner, slave or free man, but only Christ, who is all and is in all.
12 As God's chosen ones, his saints and beloved, clothe yourselves with feelings of deep compassion. Practice benevolence, humility, gentleness, patience.
13 Bear with one another, and forgive each other whenever anyone has a complaint against another. The Lord has forgiven you: do the same.
14 Above all, put on love, which is the bond of perfection.
15 May the peace of Christ reign in your hearts: that peace to which you have been called, because we form one Body. And live in thanksgiving.

heart psalms, hymns and inspired songs.

20 Children, always obey your parents, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
21 Parents, do not exasperate your children, so that they do not become discouraged.

1 As for you, masters, grant to your servants what is just and reasonable, remembering that you too have a Lord in heaven.

4 and so that I know how to proclaim it in the proper way.
5 Behave sensibly in your relationships with those who do not believe, making good use of the present time.
6 May your conversations always be pleasant and timely, so that you know how to respond to each one appropriately.

9 Onesimus, our faithful and dear brother, who is one of you, will accompany him. They will keep you up to date with everything that happens around here.

1 Paul, Silvanus and Timothy greet the Church of Thessalonica, which is united to God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. May grace and peace come to you.
2 We always thank God for all of you, when we remember you in our prayers,
3 and we constantly remember before God, our Father, how you have manifested your faith with works, your love with toil, and your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ with firm perseverance.
4 We know, brothers loved by God, that you have been chosen.

5 Because the Good News that we have announced to you came to you, not only with words, but accompanied by power, the action of the Holy Spirit and all kinds of gifts. You already know how
we proceeded when we were there at your service.
6 And you, in turn, imitated our example and that of the Lord, receiving the Word in the midst of many difficulties, with the joy that the Holy Spirit gives.
7 Thus they became a model for all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia.
8 Indeed, from there came the Word of the Lord, which did not only resonate in Macedonia and Achaia: your faith in God has spread everywhere, so that it is not necessary to speak of this.
9 They themselves tell how you received me and how you converted to God, abandoning idols to serve the living and true God,
10 and wait for his Son, who will come from heaven, Jesus, whom he raised from the dead and who delivers us from the wrath to come.
1 You know very well, brothers, that the visit we paid to you was not in vain.
2 After being mistreated and insulted in Philippi, as you already know, God gave us the necessary audacity to announce his Good News to them in the midst of a painful combat.
3 Our preaching is not inspired by error, nor by impurity, nor by deception.

4 On the contrary, God found us worthy of entrusting us with the Good News, and we preach it, seeking to please not men, but God, who examines our
hearts.
5 You know – and God is a witness – that we have never had words of flattery, nor have we sought a pretext to earn money.
6 Nor have we coveted recognition from men, neither from you nor from anyone else,
7 although, as Apostles of Christ, we had the right to assert ourselves. On the contrary, we were so condescending to you, like a mother who feeds and cares for her children.
8 We felt so much affection for you that we wanted to give you not only the Good News of God, but also our own lives: so dear did you become to us.
9 Remember, brothers, our work and our fatigue when we preached to you the Good News of God, we worked day and night so as not to be a burden to you.
10 Our conduct towards you, the believers, was always holy, just and blameless: you are witnesses, and so is God.
11 And as you remember, we have exhorted and encouraged each of you personally, like a father to his children,
12 urging them to live a life worthy of the God who called them to his Kingdom and glory.

13 We, for our part, do not cease to thank God, because when you received the Word that we preached to you, you accepted it not as a human word, but as what it really is,
as the Word of God, which acts in you, those who believe.

14 Indeed, you, brothers, followed the example of the churches of God, united to Christ Jesus, which are in Judea, because you have suffered from your countrymen the same
treatment they suffered at the hands of the Jews.
15 They killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and they also persecuted us; They do not please God and are enemies of all men,
16 since they prevent us from preaching to the pagans so that they may be saved. Thus, they are constantly filling up the measure of their sins, but the wrath of God has fallen on them forever.
17 As for us, brothers – physically separated from you for a time, although not in heart – we feel an ardent and very vivid desire to see you again.
18 That's why we wanted to go there; I myself, Paul, tried several times, but Satan prevented me.
19 Who but you are our hope, our joy and the crown of which we will be proud before our Lord Jesus, on the Day of His Coming?
20 Yes, you are our glory and our joy!
1 Therefore, not being able to bear it any longer, we decided to stay in Athens
2 and send them Timothy, our brother and God's collaborator in announcing the Good News of Christ. We did it to strengthen and comfort them in the faith,
3 so that no one will be disturbed by these tribulations. You know that's what we're here for.
4 While we were still with you we warned you that we were going to have difficulties, and so it happened, as you were able to see.

5 Therefore, not being able to bear it any longer, I sent Timothy to you to inform me about your faith, fearing that the Tempter had tested you and all our work had been ruined.
sterile result.

7 Therefore, brothers, despite the anxieties and setbacks, we feel comforted by you, seeing your faith.
8 Yes, now we will live again, knowing that you remain steadfast in the Lord.
9 How can we thank God for you, for all the joy you make us feel in the presence of our God?
10 Day and night, we insistently ask that we be able to see you again in person, to complete what is still missing in your faith.
11 May God himself, our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, pave the way for us to go there.
12 May the Lord make you grow more and more in love for each other and for all others, similar to the one we have for you.

1 Finally, brothers, we beg you and exhort you in the Lord Jesus, to live according to what you have learned from us about how to behave to please God. In fact, you already live like this: make even greater progress.
2 You already know the instructions that I have given you in the name of the Lord Jesus.
3 God's will is for you to be holy, to abstain from carnal sin,
4 that each one knows how to use his body with holiness and respect,
5 without being carried away by unbridled passion, as the pagans do who do not know God.
6 Let no one dare to harm or harm his brother in this, because the Lord will give justice for all these things, as we have already told him and witnessed.
7 God, in fact, did not call us to impurity, but to holiness.
8 Therefore, whoever despises these regulations does not despise a man, but God, the God who has given them his Holy Spirit.
9 Concerning brotherly love, it is not necessary for me to write to you, because God himself has taught you to love one another,
10 and they are doing so with all the brothers in Macedonia. But I urge you, brothers, to make even greater progress.
11 May it be a matter of honor for you to live in peace, each one fulfilling his obligations and working with his hands, according to my directives.
12 Thus they will live a worthy life in the sight of the pagans and will lack nothing.
13 We do not want you, brothers, to live in ignorance about those who have already died, so that you will not be sad like the others, who have no hope.

16 For at the signal given by the voice of the Archangel and at the sound of the trumpet of God, the Lord himself will descend from heaven. Then those who died in Christ will be resurrected first.

18 Comfort each other with these thoughts.

5 You are all children of light, children of the day. We do not belong to the night or the darkness.
6 Let us not fall asleep, then, as others do: let us stay awake and be sober.
7 Those who sleep do so at night, and also those who get drunk.
8 We, on the other hand, let us be sober, since we belong to the day: let us put on the breastplate of faith and love, and let us cover ourselves with the case of the hope of salvation.
9 For God did not appoint us to wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
10 who died for us, so that, whether awake or sleeping, we might live united to him.
11 Encourage yourselves, then, and encourage each other, as you are already doing.

13 Cherish them deeply, and love them because of their care. Live in peace with each other.
14 We also exhort you to rebuke the undisciplined, encourage the timid, support the weak, and be patient with all.
15 See to it that no one returns evil for evil. On the contrary, strive to always do good to each other and to everyone.
16 Always be happy.
17 Pray without ceasing.
18 Give thanks to God on every occasion: this is what God wants from all of you, in Christ Jesus.
19 Do not extinguish the action of the Spirit;
20 do not despise prophecies;
21 Examine everything and keep the good.
22 Beware of evil in all its forms.
23 May the God of peace sanctify you completely, so that you may remain blameless in your entire being – spirit, soul and body – until the Coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
24 He who calls you is faithful, and he will do so.
25 Brothers, pray for us too.
26 Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
