4 We have complete confidence in the Lord that you comply and will continue to comply with our provisions.
5 May the Lord guide you towards the love of God and give you the perseverance of Christ.
6 We command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to separate yourself from every brother who leads an idle life, contrary to the teaching you received from us.
7 For you already know how you should follow our example. When we were among you, we did not live like idlers,
8 and no one gave us the bread we ate. On the contrary, we worked hard, day and night, until we were tired, so as not to be a burden to any of you.
9 Although we had the right to proceed differently, we wanted to give them an example to imitate.
10 On that occasion we imposed this rule on them: whoever does not want to work should not eat.
11 Now, however, we learn that some of you live idly, doing nothing and meddling in everything.
12 These we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ to work in peace to earn their bread.
13 As for you, brothers, do not grow weary in doing good.
14 If anyone does not obey the instructions of this letter, point him out, and let no one deal with him so that he may be ashamed.
15 But do not regard him as an enemy, but rebuke him as a brother.
16 May the Lord of peace grant you peace, always and in every way. The Lord be with you all.
17 The greeting is in my own handwriting. This is the characteristic sign of all my letters: this is how I, Paul, write.
18 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.
1 Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by command of God our Savior and Christ Jesus our hope,
2 greets Timothy, his true son in the faith. I wish you the grace, mercy and peace that come from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
3 When I left for Macedonia, I asked you to remain in Ephesus, to prevent certain people from teaching strange doctrines.

4 and pay attention to myths and endless genealogies. These things only provoke useless discussions, instead of serving the plan of God founded on the
faith.
5 I made this request of you in order to arouse the love that springs from a pure heart, a good conscience and a sincere faith.
6 Because some turned away from this, some ended up in mere talk.
7 and, pretending to be teachers of the Law, in reality they do not know what they say or what they affirm with such certainty.
8 We already know that the Law is good, if used properly,

9 that is, considering that it was not established for the righteous, but for the wicked and the rebellious, for the wicked and sinners, the sacrilegious and profaning, the
parricides and matricides, the murderers,
10 the impudent and perverted, the traffickers of human beings, the cheaters and the perjurers. In a word, the Law is against everything that opposes sound doctrine
11 of the Gospel that has been entrusted to me, and that reveals to us the glory of the blessed God.
12 I thank our Lord Jesus Christ, because he has strengthened me and deemed me trustworthy, calling me to his service
13 despite my previous blasphemies, persecutions and insolence. But I was treated with mercy, because when I did not have faith, I acted like this out of ignorance.
14 And the grace of our Lord abounded to me all the more, along with the faith and love of Christ Jesus.
15 It is a true and trustworthy doctrine that Jesus Christ came into the world to save sinners, and I am the worst of them.
16 If I found mercy, it was so that Jesus Christ could demonstrate all his patience in me, setting me as an example of those who will believe in him to achieve eternal Life.
17 To the eternal and universal King, to the incorruptible, invisible and unique God, honor and glory forever and ever! Amen.
18 My son, I give you this recommendation, according to what was said about you by inspiration of God, so that you may fight valiantly,
19 preserving faith and a good conscience. Because they did not have a good conscience, some failed in the faith,
20 among others, Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan so that they would learn not to blaspheme.
1 First of all, I recommend that petitions, prayers, supplications and thanksgivings be made for all men,
2 for the sovereigns and for all authorities, so that we can enjoy peace and tranquility, and lead a pious and dignified life.
3 This is good and pleasing to God our Savior,
4 because he wants everyone to be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth.
5 There is one God and one mediator between God and men: Jesus Christ, also a man,
6 who gave himself to rescue everyone. This is the testimony that he gave in due time,
7 and of which I was appointed herald and Apostle to teach the pagans the true faith. I tell the truth, and I don't lie.
8 Therefore, I want men to pray constantly, raising their hands to heaven with right intention, without outbursts or arguments.
9 Let the women, for their part, groom themselves decently, with modesty and modesty, without wearing elaborate hairstyles, or gold, or pearls, or expensive dresses.
10 Let them rather adorn themselves with good works, as is fitting for people who practice piety.
11 Let the women listen to the instruction in silence, with all respect.
12 I do not allow them to teach, nor to try to impose their authority on the husband: on the contrary, let them remain silent.
13 For first Adam was created, and then Eve.
14 And it was not Adam who allowed himself to be seduced, but Eve was deceived and fell into sin.
15 But the woman will be saved, fulfilling her duties as a mother, provided that she perseveres in faith, love and holiness, with due discretion.
1 This statement is very true: "He who aspires to preside over the community wishes to exercise a noble function."
2 Therefore, the one who presides must be a man beyond reproach, who has been married only once, sober, balanced, orderly, hospitable and suitable for teaching.
3 Let him not be fond of drink or quarrelsome, but indulgent, enemy of quarrels and disinterested.
4 May he know how to govern his own house and keep his children in obedience with all dignity.
5 For if you do not know how to govern your own house, how can you care for the Church of God?
6 And he must not be a recently converted man, lest pride cause him to lose his head and incur the same condemnation as the devil.
7 It is also necessary that he enjoy a good reputation among non-believers, so as not to expose himself to slander and the networks of the devil.
8 In the same way, deacons must be respectable men, of one word, moderate in the use of wine and enemies of dishonest gain.
9 May they preserve the mystery of faith with a pure conscience.
10 First they will be tested, and then, if there is nothing to blame them for, they will be admitted to the diaconate.
11 May women be equally dignified, discreet when speaking about others, sober and faithful in everything.
12 Deacons must be men married only once, who govern their children and their own household well.
13 Those who carry out their ministry well earn honor and achieve great firmness in the faith of Jesus Christ.
14 Although I hope to see you soon, I write these things to you
15 in case I'm late. Thus you will know how to behave in the house of God, that is, in the Church of the living God, pillar and foundation of the truth.
16 Indeed, the mystery we venerate is truly great:
1 The Spirit clearly states that in the last times there will be some who will renounce their faith, giving themselves over to seducing spirits and demonic doctrines,
2 seduced by lying and hypocritical people, whose conscience is marked with fire.
3 These people outlaw marriage and prohibit the consumption of certain foods that God created for believers and those who know the truth to eat with thanksgiving.
4 Everything that God has created is good, and nothing is despised, if it is received with thanksgiving,
5 because the Word of God and prayer sanctify it.
6 If you explain all this to your brothers, you will be a servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the teachings of faith and good doctrine that you always followed faithfully.
7 Reject those ridiculous myths, those old wives' tales, and exercise yourself in piety.
8 Physical exercises are of little use; Piety, on the other hand, is useful for everything, because it contains a promise of Life for the present and the future.
9 This is true doctrine and absolutely worthy of faith.
10 We toil and struggle because we have put our hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all men, especially of those who believe.
11 Preach this and teach it.
12 Let no one despise your youth: on the contrary, try to be a model for those who believe, in conversation, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity of life.
13 Until I come, devote yourself to the proclamation of the Scriptures, to exhortation, and to teaching.
14 Do not spoil the spiritual gift that is in you and that was conferred upon you through a prophetic intervention, by the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.
15 Reflect on these things and dedicate yourself entirely to them, so that everyone can see your progress.
16 Watch your conduct and your doctrine, and persevere in this attitude. If you do this, you will save yourself and those who listen to you.
1 Do not rebuke an elder, but exhort him as a father. Treat young people like brothers,
2 to the older women as mothers, and to the younger women as sisters, in all purity.
3 Honor and care for widows who are truly in need.
4 But if any widow has children or grandchildren, they must first learn to fulfill their family duties and be grateful to their parents, because that is what pleases God.
5 There are widows who are truly widows, because they have been left alone and have put their trust in God, consecrating their days and nights to supplication and prayer.
6 But she who leads a dissipated life, though she lives, is dead.
7 Instill this in them so that they may be blameless:
8 He who does not take care of his own, especially if they live with him, has renounced his faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
9 To be registered in the group of widows, a woman must be at least sixty years old and have been married only once.

10 Let her good works bear witness to her; He must have educated his children, exercised hospitality, washed the feet of his brothers, helped the needy and practiced
good in all its forms.
11 On the other hand, do not enroll younger widows, because when purely human desires prevail over their dedication to Christ, they want to remarry,
12 and they feel guilty for failing to fulfill their commitment.
13 Furthermore, if they have nothing to do, they end up going from house to house and spend their time chatting and browsing, busying themselves with things that don't matter to them.
14 Therefore I want young widows to marry, have children, and attend to their domestic duties, so as not to give rise to the slander of enemies.
15 Some of them have already abandoned the good path and follow Satan.

16 If a believing woman has widows in the family, let her take care of them. In this way, the Church will not be in charge of them and will be free to care for those who are really
needy.
17 Priests who exercise their office properly deserve double recognition, especially those who dedicate all their efforts to preaching and teaching.
18 For the Scripture says: You shall not muzzle the ox that threshes, and also: The worker has a right to his wages.
19 Do not admit accusations against a priest unless they are supported by two or three witnesses.
20 Those who commit sin, rebuke them publicly, so that they may serve as a lesson to others.
21 Before God, Jesus Christ and his chosen angels, I order you to observe these instructions, without prejudice and proceeding with impartiality.
22 Do not be quick to lay hands on anyone, and do not become an accessory to other people's sins. Keep yourself pure.
23 Because of your frequent stomach upsets, do not drink plain water: drink a little wine.
24 Some people's sins are so obvious that they do not need to be brought to trial; those of others, however, are only discovered later.
25 In the same way, good works are visible, and those that are not good will become evident.
1 Let slaves consider their owners worthy of all respect, so that the name of God and his doctrine will not be the object of blasphemy.

2 And if their owners are believers, let them not respect them any less because they are brothers. On the contrary, they should put greater effort into serving them, because in this way they benefit
dear brothers in the faith. He teaches all this, and insists on it.
3 If anyone teaches otherwise and does not adhere to the salutary precepts of our Lord Jesus Christ, nor to the doctrine that is according to godliness,
4 is ignorant and proud, eager for arguments and vain controversies. From there arise envy, discord, insults, evil suspicions.
5 and the endless conflicts, typical of men mentally corrupted and separated from the truth, who seek to make piety a source of profit.
6 Yes, it is true that piety brings great gains, but only if it is combined with selflessness.
7 For we brought nothing when we came into the world, and when we leave, we will be able to take nothing.
8 Let us be content with food and shelter.
9 Those who desire to be rich expose themselves to temptation, fall into the trap of innumerable ambitions, and commit fatal blunders that precipitate them into ruin and perdition.
10 Because greed is the root of all evil, and by being carried away by it, some lost faith and caused themselves innumerable sufferings.
11 As far as you are concerned, God man, flee from all this. Practice justice, piety, faith, love, perseverance, kindness.
12 Fight the good fight of faith, conquer eternal Life, to which you have been called and in view of which you made a magnificent profession of faith, in the presence of numerous witnesses.
13 I command you before God, who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus, who bore a good testimony before Pontius Pilate:
14 observe what is prescribed, remaining blameless and blameless until the Manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
15 Manifestation that will make appear in due time the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords,
16 who alone possesses immortality and dwells in an unapproachable light, whom no man has seen or can see. To him be honor and power forever! Amen.

17 Tell the rich of this world not to be proud. Let them not put their trust in the insecurity of riches, but in God, who provides us with all things in
abundance for us to enjoy.
18 May they practice good, may they be rich in good works, may they give generously and know how to share their wealth.
19 Thus they will acquire for the future a treasure that will allow them to achieve true Life.
20 Dear Timothy, preserve the good that has been entrusted to you. Avoid the impiety of vain talk and the objections of a so-called science,
21 since because they have professed it, some have departed from the faith. May the grace of God be with you.
1 Paul, Apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, to announce the promise of Life that is in Christ Jesus,
2 greets Timothy, his very beloved son. I wish you the grace, mercy and peace that come from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
3 I thank God, whom I serve with a pure conscience like my ancestors, constantly remembering you, day and night, in my prayers.
4 Remembering your tears, I feel a great desire to see you, so that my happiness is complete.
5 Because I remember the sincerity of your faith, that faith that your grandmother Loide and your mother Eunice had, and I am convinced that you also have.
6 Therefore I recommend that you revive the gift of God that you have received through the laying on of my hands.
7 For the Spirit that God has given us is not a spirit of fear, but of strength, love and sobriety.

8 Do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me, who am his prisoner. On the contrary, he shares with me the sufferings that must be endured for the Gospel, animated with the
strength of God.
9 He saved us and chose us by his holy calling, not by our works, but by his own initiative and by grace: that grace which he granted us in Christ Jesus, from all eternity,
10 and which has now been revealed in the Manifestation of our Savior Jesus Christ. Because he destroyed death and made incorruptible life shine, through the Good News,
11 of which I have been made herald, Apostle and teacher.

12 That is why I endure this trial. But I am not ashamed, because I know in whom I have placed my trust, and I am convinced that he is capable of preserving until that Day the good that he has entrusted to me.
13 Take as a rule the healthy lessons of faith and love of Christ Jesus that you have heard from me.
14 Preserve what has been entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
15 You know that all the people of Asia turned away from me, including Phygellus and Hermogenes.
16 May the Lord have mercy on the family of Onesiphorus, for he has comforted me many times and was not ashamed that I was in prison.
17 On the contrary, since he arrived in Rome, he did not stop looking for me until he found me.
18 May God, on that Day, allow you to obtain mercy before the Lord. You know better than anyone the services he provided me in Ephesus.
1 You, who are my son, be strengthened with the grace of Christ Jesus.
2 What you heard from me and is corroborated by numerous witnesses, entrust it to responsible men who will be able to teach others.
3 Share my fatigues, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
4 He who is under arms does not mix in the affairs of civil life, in order to carry out the orders of the one who enlisted him.
5 The athlete does not receive the prize if he does not fight according to the rules.
6 And the farmer who works hard is the first who has the right to gather the fruits.
7 Think about what I tell you, and the Lord, for his part, will help you understand everything.
8 Remember Jesus Christ, who rose from the dead and is a descendant of David. This is the Good News that I preach,
9 for which I suffer and am chained like an evildoer. But the word of God is not chained.
10 Therefore I endure these trials for the sake of the elect, so that they also may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus and share in eternal glory.
11 This doctrine is worthy of faith:
12 If we are steadfast, we will reign with him.
13 If we are unfaithful, he is faithful,
14 Do not stop teaching these things, or exhorting before God to avoid useless discussions, which only serve to destroy those who listen to them.
15 Strive to be worthy of God's approval, presenting yourself to him as a worker who need not be ashamed and as a faithful dispenser of the Word of truth.
16 Avoid empty and profane speeches, which only increase impiety
17 and they spread like gangrene. This is what happens with Hymenaeus and Philetus,
18 who have departed from the truth, claiming that the resurrection has already taken place, and thus have perverted the faith of some.

19 But the solid foundation that God has established remains unshakable, and the inscription that serves as its seal says: The Lord is like his own, and: He who calls on the name of the Lord, let him
apart from iniquity.

20 In a large house, not all the vessels are made of gold or silver, but there are also vessels of wood and clay. Some are intended for noble uses, and others for
common.
21 If anyone remains free from these errors, he will be like a noble and sanctified vessel, which lends usefulness to its owner for all kinds of good works.
22 Do not give in to the impulses of youth and seek justice, faith, love and peace, together with all those who call on the Lord with a pure heart.
23 Avoid stupid and meaningless questions: you already know that they cause serious altercations.
24 He who serves the Lord must not take part in quarrels. On the contrary, they have to be kind to everyone, teachable and patient in tests.
25 He must gently rebuke his adversaries, knowing that God can grant them conversion and lead them to the knowledge of the truth,
26 making them react and freeing them from the trap of the devil who holds them captive at the service of his will.
1 I want you to know that difficult times will come in recent times.
2 For men will be selfish, fond of money, boastful, arrogant, slanderers, rebellious toward their parents, ungrateful, ungodly,
3 incapable of love, implacable, slanderers, unrestrained, cruel, enemies of good,
4 traitors, adventurers, stubborn, more lovers of pleasure than of God;
5 And although they will make a show of piety, they will really lack it. Get away from those people!
6 Such are those who enter homes, seducing frivolous women full of sins, who allow themselves to be carried away by all kinds of passions,
7 those who are always learning, but never come to know the truth.
8 Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, they too will oppose the truth: they are men of corrupt minds, disqualified in matters of faith.
9 But they will not go far, because their folly will be revealed like theirs.
10 You, however, have closely followed my teaching, my way of life and my projects, my faith, my patience, my love and my perseverance,
11 as well as the persecutions and sufferings that he had to endure in Antioch, Iconium and Lystra. What persecutions I have not had to suffer! But the Lord delivered me from all of them.
12 For the rest, Jesus, they will have to suffer persecution.
13 Sinners and impostors, however, will go from bad to worse, and by deceiving others, they will deceive themselves.
14 But you remain faithful to the doctrine that you learned and of which you are fully convinced: you know from whom you have received it.
15 Remember that since childhood you have known the Holy Scriptures: they can give you the wisdom that leads to salvation, through faith in Christ Jesus.
16 All Scripture is inspired by God and is useful for teaching and arguing, for correction and for training in righteousness,
17 so that the man of God may be perfect and prepared to always do good.
1 I adjure you before God and Christ Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead, and in the name of his Manifestation and his Kingdom:
2 proclaims the Word of God, insists with or without occasion, argues, rebukes, exhorts, with tireless patience and eagerness to teach.
3 For the time will come when men will no longer endure sound doctrine; On the contrary, led by their inclinations, they will procure a multitude of teachers
4 Let their ears be flattered, and they will turn away from the truth to listen to fantastic things.
5 You, however, watch carefully, endure all trials, carry out your task as a preacher of the Gospel, fulfill your ministry perfectly.
6 I am already about to be poured out as a libation, and the time of my departure is approaching:
7 I have fought the good fight to the end, I have completed my race, I have kept the faith.

8 And now the crown of righteousness is prepared for me, which the Lord, as a righteous Judge, will give to me on that Day, and not only to me, but to all who have waited with love for his Manifestation.
9 Come see me as soon as possible,
10 because Demas has abandoned me for love of this world. He went to Thessalonica, Crescente set out on a journey to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.
11 Only Lucas has stayed with me. Bring Marcos with you, because he will serve me well.
12 I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
13 When you come, bring me the cloak that I left in Troas, in the house of Carpus, and also the books, especially the scrolls.
14 Alexander the blacksmith has done me great harm: the Lord will repay him according to his works.
15 Be careful of him, because he strongly opposed our teaching.
16 When I made my first defense, no one accompanied me, but everyone abandoned me. I hope it is not taken into account!
17 But the Lord was at my side, giving me strength, so that the message could be proclaimed through me and reach the ears of all the pagans. Thus I was delivered from the lion's mouth.
18 The Lord will deliver me from all evil and preserve me until I enter his heavenly Kingdom. To him be glory forever and ever! Amen.
19 Greetings to Prisca and Aquila, and to the family of Onesiphorus.
20 Erastus remained in Corinth, and I left Trophimus sick in Miletus. Hurry to come before winter.
21 Eubulo, Pudente, Lino, Claudia and all the brothers greet you.
22 The Lord be with you. Grace be with you.
1 Letter from Paul, servant of God and Apostle of Jesus Christ to lead God's elect to faith and the knowledge of true piety,
2 with the hope of eternal Life. This Life has been promised before all ages by the God who does not lie,
3 and in due time, he manifested his Word, proclaiming a message that was entrusted to me at the command of God, our Savior.
4 To Titus, my true son in our common faith, I wish the grace and peace that come from God, the Father, and from Christ Jesus, our Savior.
5 I left you in Crete, so that you could finish organizing everything and establish presbyters in each city according to my instructions.
6 All of them must be blameless, having only been married once and having believing children, who cannot be accused of misconduct or rebellion.

7 Because he who presides over the community, in his capacity as God's administrator, must be blameless. He must not be arrogant, nor choleric, nor a drinker, nor quarrelsome, nor greedy for
dishonest profits,
8 but hospitable, loving to do good, moderate, just, pious, self-possessed.
9 He must also be firmly attached to true teaching, which is in accordance with the standard of faith, to be able to exhort in sound doctrine and refute those who contradict it.
10 Indeed, there are many rebellious spirits, charlatans and seducers, especially among the circumcised.
11 It is necessary to stop their mouths, because they upset entire families, teaching what should not be done for vile gain.
12 One of them, their own prophet, has said: "Cretans, eternal liars, perverse animals, gluttons and sloths."
13 And this statement is true. Therefore rebuke them severely so that they remain upright in the faith,
14 instead of giving credence to Jewish fables and the precepts of people who turn their backs on the truth.
15 Everything is pure for the pure. On the other hand, for those who are contaminated and for the unbelievers, nothing is pure. His spirit and his conscience are stained.
16 They profess to know God, but by their actions, they deny him: they are abominable, rebellious people, incapable of any good work.
1 As for you, you must teach everything that is according to sound doctrine.
2 May the elderly be sober, dignified, moderate, upright in faith, love and perseverance.
3 Let older women behave as befits holy people. They should not be gossipers, nor indulge in drink. That through good advice,
4 teach the young women to love their husbands and their children,
5 to be modest, chaste, women of their house, good and respectful to their husband. Thus the Word of God will not be the object of blasphemy.
6 Also exhort the young people to be moderate in everything,
7 giving them yourself an example of good conduct, in regard to purity of doctrine, dignity,
8 to correct and unobjectionable teaching. In this way, the adversary will be confused, because he will have nothing to reproach us for.
9 Let the slaves obey their owners in everything and try to please them, trying not to contradict them. Don't let them down,
10 but that they demonstrate absolute fidelity to them, to do honor in everything to the doctrine of God, our Savior.
11 For the grace of God, which is the source of salvation for all men, has appeared.
12 She teaches us to reject ungodliness and the lusts of the world, to live in the present life with sobriety, justice and godliness,
13 as we wait for the happy hope and the Manifestation of the glory of our great God and Savior, Christ Jesus.
14 He gave himself for us, in order to free us from all iniquity, to purify us and to create for himself a People chosen and filled with the practice of good.
15 Thus you must speak, exhort and rebuke with all authority. Don't give anyone a chance to despise you.
1 Remind everyone to respect rulers and authorities, to obey them and always be ready for any good work.
2 Let them not insult anyone and be lovers of peace, be benevolent and show great humility towards all men.

3 For we too were previously foolish, rebellious, gone astray, slaves to evil desires and all kinds of lust, and lived in wickedness and envy, being
object of hate and hating each other.
4 But when the goodness of God our Savior and his love for men was revealed,
5 Not because of the works of righteousness that we had done, but only because of his mercy, he saved us, causing us to be reborn through baptism and renewing us through the Holy Spirit.
6 And he poured out that Spirit on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
7 so that, justified by his grace, we may be heirs of eternal Life in hope.

8 This is a doctrine worthy of faith, and I want you to be categorical on this point, so that those who have put their faith in God may try to stand out for their good works. This is indeed
good and profitable for men.
9 Avoid, however, senseless investigations, genealogies, polemics and controversies about the Law: all this is useless and vain.
10 As for those who create factions, after a first and second warning, depart from them:
11 you know that they are strays and sinners who condemn themselves.
12 When I send you Artemas or Tychicus, try to meet me in Nicopolis, because that is where I have decided to spend the winter.
13 Take all the necessary measures for the trip of the lawyer Zenas and Apollo, so that they do not lack anything.
14 Ours must learn to stand out for their good works, also with regard to the needs of this world: in this way, their lives will not be barren.
15 Receive greetings from all who are with me. Greet those who love us in faith. The grace of the Lord be with you all.
1 Paul, prisoner of Christ Jesus and brother Timothy, we greet you, Philemon, our dear friend and collaborator,
2 and to the church that meets in your house, as well as to sister Appia and our fellow fighter Archippus.
3 May grace and peace come to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
4 I never stop thanking God whenever I remember you in my prayers,
5 because I have heard about the love and faith that you show towards the Lord Jesus and in favor of all the saints.
6 May your participation in our common faith lead you to the perfect knowledge of all the good that you possess through union with Christ.
7 For my part, I have experienced great joy and have felt comforted by your love, seeing how you, dear brother, alleviated the needs of the saints
8 Therefore, although I have absolute freedom in Christ to command you what you must do,
9 I prefer to plead with you in the name of love, I, Paul, already old and now a prisoner for Christ Jesus,
10 I beseech you on behalf of my son Onesimus, whom I fathered in prison.
11 Before, he was of no use to you, but now he will be very useful to you, as he is to me.
12 I send him to you as if he were myself.
13 I would gladly have kept him at my side, to serve me in your name while I am a prisoner for the gospel.
14 But I have not wanted to do anything without your consent, so that the benefit you do me may not be forced, but voluntary.
15 Perhaps he departed from you for a moment, so that you might recover him forever,
16 no longer as a slave, but as something much better, like a dear brother. If he is so dear to me, how much more will he be to you, who are united to him by human ties and in the Lord.
17 Therefore, if you consider me a friend, welcome him as myself.
18 And if he has wronged you or owes you anything, write it down to my account.
19 I will pay it, Paul, who signs this letter with my own handwriting. I don't want to remind you that you are also my debtor, and the debt is yourself.
20 Yes, brother, render me this service for the love of the Lord and calm my heart in Christ.
21 I write to you fully trusting in your docility and knowing that you will do even more than what I ask of you.
22 Also prepare a place for me to stay, because I hope that through your prayers, you will be granted the grace that I come to see you.
23 Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you,
24 as well as Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke, my collaborators.
25 The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ remain with your spirit.
1 After having spoken to our fathers through the Prophets on many occasions and in various ways,
2 Now, in this end time, God spoke to us through his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things and through whom he made the world.

3 He is the brightness of his glory and the imprint of his being. He sustains the universe with his powerful Word, and after performing the purification of sins, he sat down at the
right of the throne of God in the highest heaven.
4 Thus he became so superior to the angels, as the Name which he received as an inheritance is incomparably greater than theirs.
5 Did God ever say to an angel: "You are my Son, today I have begotten you"? And of what angel did he say: "I will be a father to him and he will be a son to me"?
6 And in introducing his Firstborn into the world, God tells us: "May all the angels of God worship him."
7 Speaking of angels, he states: "He makes his angels like gusts of wind, and his servants like flames of fire."
8 Instead, he says to his Son: "Your throne, God, endures forever. The scepter of your kingship is a scepter of justice.
9 You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity. Therefore God, your God, anointed you with the oil of joy, preferring you over your companions."
10 And he also said to him: "You, Lord, in the beginning founded the earth, and the heaven is the work of your hands.
11 They will disappear, but you remain. They will all wear out like a dress
12 and you will roll them up like a cloak: they will be like a garment that is changed. But you are always the same, and your years will have no end."
13 And to which of the angels did he ever say, "Sit at my right, until I put your enemies under your feet"?
14 Are they not all spirits at the service of God, sent to help those who are going to inherit salvation?
1 Therefore, we must pay more attention to what we have heard, lest we drift.
2 For if the Word promulgated through the angels was fully effective, to the point that every transgression and disobedience received its just retribution,
3 How shall we be delivered, if we refuse such salvation? This salvation, first announced by the Lord, was later confirmed to us by all those who had heard it announced,
4 while God added his testimony with signs and wonders, with all kinds of miracles and with the gifts of the Holy Spirit, distributed according to his will.
5 For God has not subjected the world to come, of which we speak, to the angels.
6 About this, there is a testimony that says: "What is man that you remember him, the human being that you care for him?
7 For a short time you placed him below the angels and crowned him with glory and splendor.
8 You put everything under his feet." If God has put all things under him, nothing has been left outside his control. In fact, we still do not see that everything is under him.

9 But we now see him who was placed under the angels for a short time, Jesus, crowned with glory and splendor because of the death he suffered. Thus, by the grace of God, he
He experienced death for everyone.

10 Indeed, it was fitting that He, through whom and for whom all things exist, in order to bring a great number of sons to glory, should perfect, through suffering, the
leader who would lead them to salvation.
11 For he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified all have one origin. Therefore, he is not ashamed to call them brothers,
12 when he says: "I will announce your Name to my brothers, I will praise you in the midst of the assembly."
13 And also: "I will put my trust in him." And furthermore: "Here we are, me and the children that God has given me."

14 And since children have the same blood and the same flesh, he also had to participate in that condition, to reduce to impotence, through his death, the one who had the dominion of death,
that is, to the devil,
15 and thus free all those who were completely enslaved by the fear of death.
16 For he did not come to help the angels, but to the descendants of Abraham.
17 Consequently, he had to become like his brothers in everything, to become a merciful and faithful High Priest in the service of God, in order to atone for the sins of the people.
18 And because he has personally experienced trial and suffering, he can help those who are under trial.
1 Therefore, brothers, you who have been sanctified and share in the same heavenly calling, think of Jesus, the Apostle and High Priest of the faith we profess.
2 He is faithful to God, who established him as such, just as Moses was faithful to all the house of God.
3 For he was considered worthy of a glory greater than that of Moses, in the same measure as the dignity of the builder is greater than that of the house.
4 For every house has its builder, and the builder of all things is God.
5 Moses was faithful throughout his house, as a servant, to bear witness to what was to be announced,

6 while Christ was faithful as a Son, as head of the house of God. And that house is us, as long as we preserve the security and hope of which we
we glory.
7 Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: "If you listen to his voice today,
8 Do not harden your hearts as in the time of the Rebellion, the day of Temptation in the wilderness,
9 when his parents tempted me by testing me, even though they had seen my works
10 for forty years. Therefore I was angry with that generation, and said, Their heart is always gone astray, and they have not known my ways.
11 Then you will enter my Rest."
12 Be careful, brothers, lest any of you have such an evil heart that he turns away from the living God through unbelief.
13 But encourage each other every day while this day lasts, so that no one becomes hardened and seduced by sin.
14 For we have become partakers of Christ, provided we maintain our initial attitude firmly to the end.
15 When the Scripture says, "If you hear his voice today, do not harden your hearts as in the time of the Rebellion,"
16 Who are those who rebelled after hearing it? Aren't they all those who left Egypt led by Moses?
17 And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not against those who had sinned and whose corpses were left lying in the desert?
18 And to whom did God swear that they would not enter his Rest, except those who had disobeyed him?
19 Thus we see that those could not enter because of their lack of faith.
1 Let us fear, then, while the promise of entering the Rest of God remains in force, lest any of you be excluded.
2 For we also, like them, have received good news; but the Word that they heard was of no use to them, because they were not united by faith to those who accepted it.

3 We, however, who have believed, are going towards that Rest of which it was said: "Then I swore in my indignation: They will never enter my Rest." In fact, the works of
Dio were completed since the creation of the world,
4 since in a certain passage it is said about the seventh day of creation: And God rested from all his works on the seventh day;
5 and in this, in turn, it is said: They will never enter my Rest.
6 Now, we know that the entrance to that Rest is reserved for some, and that the first who received the good news did not enter it, because of their disobedience.
7 For this reason, God again sets a day – today – when many years later, he says through the mouth of David the words already quoted: "If you hear his voice today, do not harden your hearts."
8 For if Joshua had brought the Israelites into that Rest, God would not have spoken afterwards about another day.
9 Therefore, a Rest is reserved, that of the seventh day, for the People of God.
10 And he who enters the Rest of God rests from his labors, as God rested from his.
11 Let us strive, then, to enter that Rest, so that no one falls imitating that example of disobedience.

12 For the Word of God is living and active, and sharper than any double-edged sword: it penetrates to the root of the soul and of the spirit, of the joints and of the marrow, and
discerns the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
13 No created thing escapes his sight, but everything is naked and revealed to the eyes of him to whom we must give an account.
14 And since we have in Jesus, the Son of God, a distinguished High Priest who entered heaven, let us remain firm in the confession of our faith.
15 For we do not have a High Priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses; On the contrary, he was subjected to the same tests as us, except for sin.
16 Let us go, then, boldly to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and obtain the grace of timely help.

1 Every High Priest is taken from among men and appointed to intervene on behalf of men in everything that concerns the service of God, in order to offer gifts and
sacrifices for sins.
2 He can show leniency to those who sin through ignorance and to those who go astray, because he himself is subject to human weakness.
3 Therefore he must offer sacrifices, not only for the sins of the people, but also for his own sins.
4 And no one arrogates to himself this dignity, unless he is called by God as Aaron was.
5 Therefore, Christ did not attribute to himself the glory of being High Priest, but received it from him who said to him: "You are my Son, today I have begotten you."
6 As he also says elsewhere: "You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek."
7 During his earthly life he addressed supplications and prayers, with loud cries and tears, to the one who could save him from death, and was heard for his humble submission.
8 And although he was the Son of God, he learned through his own sufferings what it means to obey.
9 In this way he attained perfection and became the cause of eternal salvation for all who obey him,
10 because God proclaimed him High Priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
11 We would have many things to say about this, but it is difficult to explain them to you, because you are slow to understand.

12 Although it is time for you to be teachers, you need to be taught again the rudiments of the Word of God: you have once again needed milk, instead of
solid food.
13 Now he who feeds on milk cannot understand the doctrine of righteousness, because he is but a child.
14 Solid food is typical for adults, for those who through practice have the sensitivity trained to discern between good and evil.

1 Therefore, leaving aside the elementary teaching about Christ, let us go to the most perfect, without returning again to the fundamental truths, such as repentance for the works that
They lead to death and faith in God.
2 the instruction on baptisms and the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.
3 This is what we are going to do, if God allows it.
4 For those who once were enlightened and tasted the heavenly gift, those who participated in the Holy Spirit
5 and they tasted the good Word of God and the wonders of the world to come,

6 and despite everything they fell, it is impossible to renew them again by elevating them to conversion, since they on their own crucify the Son of God again and expose him to the mockery of
everyone.
7 When the land is watered by abundant rains and produces good vegetation for those who cultivate it, it receives its share of blessing from God.
8 But if it produces nothing but thorns and thistles, it has no value, its curse is near and it will end by being burned.
9 Dear brothers, although we have expressed ourselves in this way, we are convinced that you are in the best condition, the one that leads to salvation.

10 For God is not unjust to forget what you have done and the love you have for his Name, that love demonstrated in the service you have rendered and continue to render to others.
saints
11 We only wish that each one always shows the same zeal to ensure the fulfillment of his hope.
12 Thus, instead of being lazy, they will imitate the example of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
13 For when God made the promise to Abraham, since he could not swear by someone greater than himself, he swore by himself,
14 saying: Yes, I will shower you with blessings and give you numerous descendants.
15 And because of his patience, Abraham saw the fulfillment of this promise.
16 Men usually swear by something greater than themselves, and what is confirmed by an oath is beyond dispute.
17 Therefore God, wanting to give the heirs of the promise clearer proof that his decision was irrevocable, guaranteed it with an oath.

18 In this way, there are two irrevocable realities – the promise and the oath – in which God cannot deceive us. And thanks to them, we, those who turn to him, feel
powerfully stimulated to hold on to the hope offered to us.
19 This hope that we have is like an anchor of the soul, solid and firm, which penetrates beyond the veil,
20 right there where Jesus entered for us, as a forerunner, becoming a High Priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.
1 This Melchizedek, who was king of Salem, priest of God, the Most High, went out to meet Abraham when he returned from defeating the kings and blessed him;

2 and Abraham gave him a tenth of all the spoils. Melchizedek's name means, first of all, "king of justice" and he was, in addition, king of Salem, that is, "king of
peace."
3 Of him there is no mention of father or mother or ancestors, neither beginning nor end of his life: thus, like the Son of God, he is a priest forever.
4 Consider now the greatness of him to whom the patriarch Abraham himself gave the best of the spoils as a tithe.

5 To the descendants of Levi who receive the priesthood, the Law commands them to receive the tithe of the people, that is, of their own brothers, who nevertheless belong like them to the descendants of
Abraham.
6 But Melchizedek, who had no common ancestry with them, received the tithe from Abraham and blessed the depositary of the promises.
7 Now, there is no doubt that it is up to the superior to bless the inferior.

8 Furthermore, in the case of the descendants of Levi, those who receive the tithe are mortal men, while in the case of Melchizedek, it is someone who is
testifies that he lives.
9 Lastly, it can be said that Levi himself, who is responsible for collecting tithes, paid his tithes to Melchizedek in the person of Abraham,
10 because, in a sense, Levi was already in the body of his father Abraham when Melchizedek met him.

11 Therefore, if perfection could be achieved through the Levitical priesthood, on which the Law given to the people is founded, what need then was there for another priest to arise,
according to the order of Melchizedek and not according to the order of Aaron?
12 Because the change of priesthood necessarily implies a change of Law.
13 In fact, Jesus, of whom these things are said, belonged to a tribe other than Levi, none of whose members dedicated themselves to the service of the altar.
14 Because it is known that our Lord is descended from Judah, and of that tribe, Moses never spoke when referring to the priests.
15 And this becomes even more evident, if we take into account that this new priest, like Melchizedek,
16 is constituted, not according to the disposition of a merely human law, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
17 Of him it has been attested: "You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek."
18 In this way, the previous provision is repealed, due to its ineffectiveness and uselessness
19 – since the Law is incapable of leading to perfection – and a better hope is introduced, which allows us to draw closer to God.
20 Furthermore, all this has been confirmed by an oath. For, while the descendants of Levi were ordained priests without the guarantee of an oath,
21 Jesus was so with an oath, that of the one who said to him: "The Lord has sworn and will not repent: You are a priest forever."
22 Therefore, Jesus has become the guarantor of a higher Covenant.
23 The other priests had to be many, because death prevented them from remaining;
24 but Jesus, since he remains forever, has an immutable priesthood.
25 Hence he can definitively save those who approach God through him, since he lives eternally to intercede for them.
26 He is the High Priest we needed: holy, innocent, blameless, separated from sinners and elevated above heaven.

27 He has no need, like the other high priests, to offer sacrifices every day, first for his sins, and then for those of the people. This he did once and for all, offering
to himself.
28 Indeed, the Law establishes weak men as high priests; On the other hand, the word of the oath – which is after the Law – establishes a Son who became perfect forever.
1 This is the main point of what we are saying: we have a High Priest so great that he sat at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven.
2 He is the minister of the Sanctuary and of the true Dwelling, erected not by man, but by the Lord.
3 Now every High Priest is appointed to present offerings and sacrifices; hence the need for it to have something to offer.
4 If Jesus were on earth, he could not be a priest, because there are already other priests here who present offerings according to the Law.

5 But the worship that they celebrate is an image and a shadow of the heavenly realities, as God warned Moses when he was going to build the Dwelling, saying: You have to do everything
according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.
6 But now Christ has received a far superior ministry, for he is the mediator of a more excellent Covenant, founded on better promises.
7 Because if this first Covenant had been perfect, it would not have been necessary to replace it with another.
8 Instead, God reproached the people: "The days will come, says the Lord, when I will make a New Covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah,

9 not like that which I did with your parents on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt. Since they did not remain faithful to my Alliance, I neglected them
–says the Lord–:

10 And this is the Covenant that I will establish with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws on their conscience, I will engrave them on their hearts; I will be your God and
They will be my People.
11 Then no one will have to instruct his countryman or his brother, saying, "Know the Lord"; because everyone will know me, from the smallest to the greatest.
12 For I will forgive their iniquities and remember their sins no more."
13 When speaking of a New Covenant, God declares the first outdated, and what is old and outdated is about to disappear.
1 The First Alliance had a ritual for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
2 In it a first enclosure was installed, where the candlestick, the table and the loaves of the oblation were: it was the place called Holy.
3 Then behind the second veil was another room, called the Holy of Holies.

4 There were the golden altar for perfumes and the Ark of the Covenant, all overlaid with gold, in which was a golden chest of manna, Aaron's rod that had blossomed, and the tablets of
the alliance.
5 Above it were the Cherubim of Glory, covering the Mercy Seat with the shadow of their wings. But this is not the time to go into details.
6 Within this order, priests always enter the first room to celebrate worship.
7 But to the second, the High Priest only enters once a year, taking with him the blood that he offers for his faults and those of the people.
8 The Holy Spirit implies with this that the path to the Sanctuary is not accessible as long as the first enclosure remains.
9 This is a symbol for the present time: in fact, gifts and sacrifices are offered there that cannot make the one who practices the cult perfect in his conscience.
10 These are only external prescriptions regarding food, drinks and various ablutions, valid until the moment of renewal.

11 Christ, however, has come as High Priest of future goods. He, through a more excellent and perfect Dwelling than the old one - not built by human hands, that is, not of this
created world –
12 He entered the Sanctuary once and for all, not by the blood of goats and calves, but by His own blood, thus obtaining for us an eternal redemption.
13 For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a calf, with which those who are defiled by sin are sprinkled, sanctify them and obtain external purity for them,

14 How much more will the blood of Christ, which through the eternal Spirit offered himself without stain to God, purify our conscience from works that lead to death, to enable us to worship
to the living God!

15 Therefore, Christ is the mediator of a New Covenant between God and men, so that, having died for the redemption of the sins committed in the first Covenant, those who are called may receive the
eternal inheritance that has been promised.
16 Because for a will to be fulfilled, the testator must die:
17 While one is alive, the will is not valid, and only upon his death does it come into force.
18 Hence the first Covenant was not inaugurated without bloodshed either.

19 Indeed, when Moses proclaimed each of the commandments written in the Law before all the people, he took the blood of bulls and goats—along with water, scarlet wool, and
hyssop – and sprinkled the Book and also all the people,
20 saying, "This is the blood of the Covenant that God has established with you."
21 In the same way, he sprinkled blood on the Mansion and all the objects of worship.
22 Furthermore, as the Law prescribes, almost all purifications must be done with blood, since there is no remission of sins without the shedding of blood.

23 Now, if the figures of the heavenly realities had to be purified in this way, it was necessary that those same realities also be purified, but with very sacrifices.
superiors.
24 Christ, in fact, did not enter a Sanctuary built by human hands – a simple figure of the authentic Sanctuary – but into heaven, to appear before God on our behalf.
25 And he did not enter to offer himself many times, as the High Priest does who enters the Sanctuary each year with blood that is not his own.

26 Because in that case, he would have had to suffer many times since the creation of the world. But now he has appeared only once, at the end of time, to abolish the
sin through his Sacrifice.
27 And just as the destiny of men is to die once, after which comes the Judgment,

28 So Christ, after having offered himself once to take away the sins of the multitude, will appear a second time, no longer in connection with sin, but to save those who sin.
they wait.

1 The Law, in effect – having only the shadow of future goods and not the reality of things themselves – with the sacrifices repeated year after year in an uninterrupted manner, is incapable of
perfect those who draw near to God.
2 Otherwise, these sacrifices would no longer have been offered, because those who partake of them, being purified once for all, would no longer be aware of any sin.
3 But these sacrifices renew the memory of sin every year,
4 because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
5 Therefore, Christ, upon entering the world, said: "You did not want sacrifice or oblation, but you gave me a body.
6 You have not looked with favor on burnt offerings or atoning sacrifices.
7 Then I said, "Here I am, I come, as it is written about me in the book of the Law, to do your will, God."
8 He begins by saying, "You have not desired nor looked with pleasure on sacrifices, burnt offerings, or atoning sacrifices," even though they are prescribed by the Law.
9 And then he adds: "Here I am, I come to do your will." Thus he declares the first regime abolished to establish the second.
10 And by virtue of this will we are sanctified by the oblation of the body of Jesus Christ, once for all.
11 Each priest appears daily to fulfill his ministry and offer many times the same sacrifices, which are totally ineffective in removing sin.
12 But Christ, after having offered a single Sacrifice for sins, sat down forever at the right hand of God,
13 where he expects his enemies to be put under his feet.
14 And so by one oblation he has perfected forever those he sanctifies.
15 The Holy Spirit witnesses all this, because after having announced:
16 "This is the Covenant that I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their hearts and engrave them on their conscience,
17 and I will remember their sins and their iniquities no more."
18 And if sins are forgiven, there is no longer any need to offer any oblation for them.
19 Therefore, brothers, we are fully assured that we can enter the sanctuary through the blood of Jesus,
20 following the new and living path that he opened for us through the veil of the Temple, which is his flesh.
21 We also have a distinguished High Priest leading the house of God.
22 Let us approach, then, with a sincere heart and full of faith, purified internally from all bad conscience and with our bodies washed by pure water.
23 Let us hold firmly to the confession of our hope, for he who has made the promise is faithful.
24 Let us watch over each other, to encourage each other in love and good works.
25 Let us not desert our assemblies, as some are wont to do; On the contrary, let us encourage each other, all the more as we see the day approaching.
26 For if after we have received full knowledge of the truth, we sin deliberately, there is no more sacrifice for sins.
27 All that remains is to wait in terror for the judgment and the burning fire that will consume the rebels.
28 He who violates the Law of Moses is condemned to death irrevocably on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
29 Consider, then, what punishment will be deserved by him who trampled on the Son of God, who profaned the blood of the Covenant with which he was sanctified, and who insulted the Spirit of grace.
30 For we know him who said: Vengeance belongs to me and I will repay. And furthermore: The Lord will judge his people.
31 Truly it is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God!
32 Remember the early times: you had barely been enlightened and you already had to endure a rough and painful combat,
33 sometimes publicly exposed to insults and abuses, and other times, showing solidarity with those who were treated in that way.

34 You then shared the sufferings of those who were in prison and gladly accepted that they were stripped of their property, knowing that they had better wealth.
and permanent.
35 Then do not lose confidence, for which a great reward is reserved.
36 You need perseverance to fulfill the will of God and enter into possession of the promise.
37 For there is still a little time, very little time, and he who must come will come without delay.
38 The righteous will live by faith, but if he turns back, I will stop loving him.
39 We are not of those who turn back to their destruction, but we live in faith to preserve our souls.
1 Now faith is the guarantee of things hoped for, the full certainty of realities not seen.
2 Through it our ancestors were considered worthy of approval.
3 By faith, we understand that the Word of God formed the world, so that what is visible comes from what is invisible.

4 By faith, Abel offered to God a sacrifice superior to that of Cain, and for this reason he was recognized as righteous, as God himself attested by accepting his gifts. And by that same faith,
he continues to speak, even after his death.
5 By faith, Enoch was taken to heaven without passing through death. No one could find him because God took him, and the Scripture testifies of him that before he was taken he was pleasing to God.
6 Now, without faith it is impossible to please God, because he who approaches God must believe that he exists and is the just rewarder of those who seek him.

7 By faith, Noah, being warned by God about things not yet seen, moved with holy fear, built an ark to save his family. Thus, by that same faith, he condemned the world and inherited the
justice that comes from faith.
8 By faith, Abraham, obeying the call of God, set out toward the place he was going to receive as an inheritance, not knowing where he was going.
9 By faith he lived as a stranger in the Promised Land, living in tents, just as Isaac and Jacob, heirs with him of the same promise.
10 For Abraham was waiting for that city with solid foundations, whose architect and builder is God.
11 Also by faith, Sarah received the power to conceive, despite her advanced age, because she judged the one who promised her worthy of faith.
12 And therefore, from one man, and from a man already close to death, was born a descendant numerous as the stars of heaven and countless as the sand that is on the seashore.
13 All of them died in faith, without achieving the fulfillment of the promises: they saw them and greeted them from afar, recognizing that they were strangers and pilgrims on earth.
14 Those who speak thus clearly demonstrate that they are seeking a homeland;
15 and if they had thought about the one from which they had left, they would have had the opportunity to return.
16 But they aspired to a better country, nothing less than the heavenly one. Therefore, God is not ashamed to call himself “your God” and, in fact, he has prepared a City for you.
17 By faith Abraham, when he was tested, presented Isaac as an offering: he offered his only son, the heir of the promises,
18 to him of whom it was announced: From Isaac will be born descendants who will bear your name.
19 And he offered it, because he thought that God had power, even to raise the dead. That's why he got his son back, and this was like a symbol.
20 Also by faith, Isaac, seeing what was about to happen, blessed Jacob and Esau.
21 By faith, Jacob, before he died, blessed each of Joseph's sons, while he bowed down, leaning on his staff.
22 By faith, Joseph, at the end of his life, referred to the exodus of the Israelites and left instructions regarding their remains.
23 By faith, Moses, as soon as he was born, was hidden by his parents for three months, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the king's edict.
24 And by faith, Moses, when he was grown up, renounced being called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.
25 He preferred to share the sufferings of the People of God, rather than enjoy the ephemeral pleasures of sin:
26 He considered that sharing the reproach of the Messiah was a wealth greater than the treasures of Egypt, because he had his eyes set on the true reward.
27 By faith Moses fled from Egypt, not fearing the king's fury, and stood firm as if he were seeing the Invisible One.
28 By faith he celebrated the first Passover and made the first sprinkling of blood, so that the Exterminator would not harm the firstborn of Israel.
29 By faith, the Israelites crossed the Red Sea as if they were walking on dry land, while the Egyptians, who attempted to do the same, were swallowed up by the waves.
30 By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after the people had circled around them for seven days.
31 By faith, Rahab, the prostitute, did not perish with the unbelievers, since she had welcomed those who went to explore the Earth.
32 And what more can I say? I would not have time to talk about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the Prophets.
33 Through faith they conquered kingdoms, administered justice, achieved the fulfillment of promises, closed the jaws of lions,
34 they extinguished the violence of the fire, they escaped the edge of the sword. Their weakness turned into strength: they were strong in fighting and repelled the attacks of foreigners.
35 There were women who recovered their dead alive. Some allowed themselves to be tortured, refusing to be liberated, to obtain a better resurrection.
36 Others suffered insults and beatings, chains and prisons.
37 They were stoned, torn to pieces, killed by the sword. They wandered, covered in sheep and goat skins, lacking everything, oppressed and mistreated.
38 Since the world was not worthy of them, they had to wander through deserts and mountains, taking refuge in caves and caverns.
39 But although their faith earned them such a valuable testimony, none of them came into possession of the promise.
40 Because God had something better in store for us, and did not want them to reach perfection without us.

1 Therefore, since we are surrounded by a veritable cloud of witnesses, let us throw off everything that hinders us, especially sin, which always assails us, and let us run resolutely to the
combat that is presented to us.

2 Let us fix our gaze on the originator and perfecter of our faith, on Jesus, who, instead of the joy that was offered to them, endured the cross without regard to infamy, and now sits at
the right hand of the throne of God.
3 Think of him who suffered such hostility from sinners, and then you will not let yourself be discouraged.
4 After all, in the fight against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.
5 You have forgotten the exhortation that God addresses to you as his children: "My son, do not despise the Lord's correction, and when he rebukes you, do not be discouraged.
6 For the Lord corrects whom he loves and punishes everyone whom he accepts as a son."
7 If you have to suffer it is for your correction; because God treats them as sons, and is there any son who is not corrected by his father?
8 If God did not correct you, as he does with everyone, you would be bastards and not sons.

9 After all, our carnal parents corrected us, and that didn't mean we stopped respecting them. With all the more reason, then, we must submit to the Father of our spirit, to possess
Life.
10 Because our parents only correct us for a short time and according to their discretion. God, on the other hand, corrects us for our good, in order to communicate to us his holiness.

11 It is true that every correction, at the moment of receiving it, is a reason for sadness and not for joy; but later, it produces fruits of peace and justice in those who have been
trained by her.
12 Therefore, let the hands that fail and the knees that weaken be restored to strength.
13 And you, advance on a level path, so that the lame person does not fall, but is healed.
14 Seek peace with everyone and sanctification, because without it no one will see the Lord.
15 Be careful so that no one is deprived of the grace of God, and so that no poisonous root sprouts capable of disturbing and contaminating the community.
16 Let there be no impudent or defiler, like Esau, who sold his birthright for a plate of food.
17 Remember that later, when he wanted to inherit his father's blessing, he was rejected, and no matter how much he implored it with tears, he could not obtain a change of decision.
18 In fact, you have not approached anything tangible: burning fire, darkness, darkness, tempest,
19 the sound of a trumpet, and such a roar of words that those who heard it did not want to be spoken to any further.
20 Because they could not bear this prescription: Anyone who touches the mountain will be stoned, even the animals.
21 This sight was so terrible that Moses exclaimed: I am terrified and tremble.
22 But you have come to Mount Zion, to the City of the living God, to the heavenly Jerusalem, to a multitude of angels, to a solemn feast,

23 to the assembly of the firstborn whose names are written in heaven. They have approached God, who is the Judge of the universe, and the spirits of the righteous who have already arrived
to perfection,
24 to Jesus, the mediator of the New Covenant, and to the purifying blood that speaks more eloquently than that of Abel.

25 Be careful not to ignore the speaker. For if those who refused to listen to him who gave oracles on earth could not escape punishment, how can we escape if we turn the tables?
back to the one who speaks from heaven?
26 He who on that occasion made the earth shake with his voice has now made this promise to us: Once again I will shake not only the earth, but also the sky.
27 These words once again mean that the things that are moved will change – because they are created – so that those that are unshakeable remain.
28 Therefore, having received the possession of a Kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us hold fast to this grace, and with piety and fear, worship God that is pleasing to Him,
29 for our God is a devouring fire.
1 Persevere in brotherly love.
2 Do not forget to practice hospitality, since thanks to it, some, without knowing it, hosted angels.
3 Remember those who are imprisoned, as if you were with them, and those who are mistreated, as if you were in their own body.
4 Respect marriage and do not dishonor the marital bed, because God will condemn the lustful and the adulterers.
5 Do not be carried away by greed, and be content with what you have, because God Himself has said: I will not leave you nor forsake you.
6 So we can say with full confidence: The Lord is my protector: I will not fear. What can men do to me?
7 Remember those who led you, because they proclaimed the Word of God to you: consider how their life ended and imitate their faith.
8 Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today, and will be the same forever.
9 Do not be led astray by any kind of strange doctrines. It is best to strengthen the heart with grace, not with foods that are of no benefit to those who eat them.
10 We have an altar from which the ministers of the Old Covenant have no right to eat.
11 The sacrificed animals, whose blood is brought to the Sanctuary by the High Priest for the atonement of sin, are burned outside the camp.
12 Therefore Jesus, to sanctify the people with his blood, suffered outside the city gates.
13 Let us also leave the camp to go to him, bearing his disgrace.
14 For we do not have a permanent city here below, but we are looking for a future one.
15 And through him let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of the lips that confess his Name.
16 Always do good and share what you have, because these are sacrifices pleasing to God.

17 Obey with docility those who direct you, because they are vigilant for you, as one who has to give an account. Thus they will be able to fulfill their duty with joy and not with difficulty, which
which would not bring you any benefit.
18 Pray for us. In reality, we are convinced that we have a good conscience, since our intention is to proceed correctly in everything.
19 Furthermore, I insistently ask you to pray, so that I can meet you as soon as possible.
20 May the God of peace – the same one who raised from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great Shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of an eternal Covenant –

21 enable them to do his will, doing all kinds of good. May he do in us what is pleasing in his eyes, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever.
the centuries. Amen.
22 I beg you, brothers, to patiently accept these words of exhortation, considering that I have written to you briefly.
23 Know that our brother Timothy has been released; If he arrives in time, I will go to see them with him.
24 Greet all your leaders and all the brothers. The brothers from Italy send you greetings.
