1 James, servant of God and the Lord Jesus Christ, greets the twelve tribes of the Dispersion.
2 Brothers, rejoice deeply when you are subjected to any kind of trials,
3 knowing that faith, when tested, produces patience.
4 And patience must be accompanied by perfect works, so that you may reach perfection and maturity, lacking nothing.
5 If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, and he will receive it, for he gives it generously to all, requiring nothing in return.
6 But let him ask in faith, without wavering, for he who wavers is like the waves of the sea, lifted up and tossed by the wind.
7 He who is like this does not expect to receive anything from the Lord,
8 since he is a man internally divided and inconstant in his way of proceeding.
9 Let the lowly brother glory when he is exalted,
10 and the rich man rejoices when he is humiliated, for he will pass away like a flower of the field:
11 As soon as the sun rises and becomes hot, the grass dries up, its flower withers and its beauty disappears. The same will happen with the rich in their companies.
12 Happy is the man who endures the trial, because after having overcome it, he will receive the crown of Life that the Lord promised to those who love him.
13 Let no one, when tempted, say that God tempts him: God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone,
14 but each one is tempted by his own lust, which draws him and seduces him.
15 Lust is the mother of sin, and sin, once committed, engenders death.
16 Do not be deceived, dear brothers.
17 Everything that is good and perfect is a gift from above and comes down from the Father of the luminous stars, in whom there is no change or shadow of declination.
18 He wanted to beget us through his Word of truth, so that we might be like the firstfruits of his creation.
19 Keep in mind, dear brothers, that we must be willing to listen and be slow to speak and slow to get angry.
20 The wrath of man never realizes the justice of God.
21 Put aside, then, all impurity and all traces of evil, and receive with docility the Word sown in you, which is able to save you.
22 Put the Word into practice and do not be content just to hear it, so that you deceive yourselves.
23 He who hears the Word and does not practice it is like a man who looks in the mirror,
24 but immediately he leaves and forgets what he is like.

25 On the other hand, he who carefully considers the perfect Law, which makes us free, and is fond of it, not as a distracted listener, but as a true keeper of the Law, will be happy in practicing it.
26 If someone believes that he is a religious man, but does not master his language, he deceives himself and his religiosity is empty.
27 Pure and blameless religiosity before God, our Father, consists in taking care of orphans and widows when they are in need, and in not contaminating oneself with the world.
1 Brethren, you who believe in our glorified Lord Jesus Christ, do not respect persons.
2 Suppose that when they are gathered, a man enters with a gold ring and elegantly dressed, and at the same time, another poorly dressed man enters.
3 If you notice the one who is very well dressed and say to him, "Sit here, in the place of honor," and to the poor man you say, "Stay there, standing," or, "Sit at my feet,"
4 Are you not making distinctions among yourselves and acting as malicious judges?
5 Listen, dear brothers: Has not God chosen the poor of this world to enrich them in faith and make them heirs of the Kingdom that he has promised to those who love him?
6 And yet you despise the poor! Aren't the rich the ones who oppress you and make you appear in court?
7 Are they not the ones who blaspheme against the beautiful Name that has been pronounced over you?
8 Therefore, if you fulfill the Law par excellence that is in the Scripture: You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you do well.
9 But if they show partiality, they commit a sin and are condemned by the Law as transgressors.
10 In fact, even if a person keeps the whole Law, if he sins against a single precept, he breaks the whole Law.
11 For he who said, Thou shalt not commit adultery, also said, Thou shalt not kill. Therefore, if you avoid adultery, but commit murder, you become a transgressor of the Law.
12 Speak and act as those who must be judged by a Law that makes us free.
13 For he who has no mercy will be judged without mercy, but mercy laughs at judgment.
14 What good is it, my brothers, for saying that you have faith, if you do not have works? Can that faith save him?
15 What good is it if one of you, seeing a brother or sister naked or without necessary food,
16 says to them, "Go in peace, keep warm and eat," and does not give them what they need for their bodies?
17 The same thing happens with faith: if it is not accompanied by works, it is completely dead.

18 However, someone may object: "One has faith and another has works." To that one we would have to respond: «Show me, if you can, your faith without works. I, however, through works,
I will demonstrate my faith"
19 Do you believe there is only one God? You do well. The demons also believe, and yet they tremble.
20 Do you want to convince yourself, foolish man, that faith without works is sterile?
21 Was not our father Abraham justified by works, when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
22 Do you see how faith was not separated from works, and through works it reached its perfection?
23 Thus was fulfilled the Scripture which says: Abraham believed in God, and this was taken into account for his justification, and he was called the friend of God.
24 You see, a man is not justified by faith alone, but also by works.
25 Was Rahab the prostitute not justified by works when she received the messengers and made them take another path?
26 Just as a body without a soul is dead, so faith is dead without works.
1 Brethren, let there not be many among you who claim to be teachers, knowing that we who teach will be judged more severely,
2 because we are all lacking in many ways. If someone does not lack words, he is a perfect man, because he is capable of dominating his entire person.
3 When we put a bit in the mouth of horses to make them obey us, we control their entire body.
4 The same thing happens with ships: no matter how big they are and despite the violence of the winds, by means of a small rudder, they are directed where the pilot wants.
5 In the same way, the tongue is a small member, and yet it can boast of doing great things. Look how a small flame is enough to set a large forest on fire.
6 The tongue is also a fire: it is a world of evil placed in our members, which contaminates the entire body, and ignited by hell itself, it sets the entire cycle of human life on fire.
7 Wild animals and birds, reptiles and fish of all kinds, have been and are dominated by man.
8 On the contrary, no one can control the tongue, which is a scourge always active and full of deadly poison.
9 With it we bless the Lord our Father, and with it we curse men, made in the image of God.
10 From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. But it should not be like that, brothers.
11 Do sweet and bitter water spring from the same fountain?
12, brothers, can a fig tree produce olives, or a vine produce figs? Nor can the sea produce fresh water.
13 He who considers himself wise and prudent, demonstrate by his good conduct that his actions have the simplicity proper to wisdom.
14 But if you are dominated by rivalry and a spirit of discord, do not boast or falsify the truth.
15 Such wisdom does not come from above but is earthly, sensual and demonic.
16 For where there is rivalry and discord, there is also disorder and every kind of wickedness.

17 But the wisdom that comes from above is, above all, pure; and also, peaceful, benevolent and conciliatory; she is full of mercy and willing to do good; is
impartial and sincere.
18 A fruit of justice is sown peacefully for those who work for peace.
1 Where do the fights and quarrels between you come from? Is it not precisely one of the passions that fight in their very members?
2 You covet, and if you don't get what you want, you kill; They envy, and when they do not achieve what they want, they fight and wage war. You do not have, because you do not ask.
3 Or else, they ask and do not receive, because they ask badly, with the sole purpose of satisfying their passions.
4 Adulterous hearts! Don't you know that by becoming friends of the world you become enemies of God? Because he who wants to be a friend of the world becomes an enemy of God.
5 Do not think that the Scripture says in vain: The soul that God put in us is full of envious desires.
6 But he gives us even greater grace, according to the word of Scripture that says: God resists the proud and gives his grace to the humble.
7 Submit to God; Resist the devil, and he will depart from you.
8 Draw near to God and he will draw near to you. Let sinners purify their hands; May those who have a divided heart be sanctified.
9 Acknowledge your misery with pain and tears. May your joy be transformed into tears, and your joy into sadness.
10 Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.

11 Brothers, do not speak evil of one another. He who speaks against a brother or condemns him, speaks against the Law and condemns him. Now, if you condemn the Law, you are not
fulfiller of the Law, but judge of it.
12 And there is but one lawgiver and judge, the one who has the power to save or to condemn. Who are you to condemn your neighbor?
13 And you who now say, "Today or tomorrow we will go to such and such a city and stay there all year round, do business and earn money,"
14 Do you know what will happen to you tomorrow? For his life he is like smoke, which appears for a moment and then dissipates.
15 Rather say: "If God wills, we will live and do this or that."
16 You, however, boast presumptuously, and that boasting is evil.
17 He who knows how to do good and does not do it commits sin.
1 You rich people, weep and moan for the misfortunes that are going to befall you.
2 For their riches have gone to waste and their clothes have been gnawed by moths.

3 Your gold and silver have become rusty, and that rust will testify against you and devour your bodies like fire. You have accumulated riches, now that it is time
final!
4 Know that the wages you have withheld from those who worked in your fields are crying out, and the cry of the harvesters has reached the ears of the Lord of the universe.
5 You led a life of luxury and pleasure in this world, and you have fattened yourselves for the day of slaughter.
6 They have condemned and killed the righteous man, without him resisting them.

7 Be patient, brothers, until the Lord comes. See how the sower waits for the precious fruit of the earth, waiting patiently until the rains of autumn and winter fall.
spring.
8 Be patient and take courage, because the Coming of the Lord is near.
9 Brethren, do not complain about one another, lest you be condemned. Look, the Judge is already at the door.
10 Take as an example of strength and patience the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

11 For we call happy those who suffered patiently. You heard about Job's patience, and you know what the Lord did to him, because the Lord is
compassionate and merciful.
12 But first of all, brothers, do not swear by heaven or by earth or by any means: that when you say "yes," it is yes; and when they say “no,” let it be no, so as not to be condemned.
13 If anyone is afflicted, let him pray. If he is happy, let him sing psalms.
14 If he is sick, let him call the presbyters of the Church, so that they may pray for him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
15 The prayer that is born of faith will save the sick, the Lord will relieve him, and if he has sins, they will be forgiven.
16 Confess your sins to each other and pray for each other, that you may be healed. The persevering prayer of the righteous is powerful.
17 Elijah was a man like us, and yet when he prayed earnestly that it would not rain, it did not rain on the land for three years and six months.
18 Then he prayed again; then the sky gave rain, and the earth produced fruit.
19 My brothers, if one of you strays from the truth and another turns him back,
20 know that he who turns a sinner from his evil way will save his life from death and obtain forgiveness for many sins.
1 Peter, Apostle of Jesus Christ, greets those who live as foreigners, scattered in Pontus, in Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia, those who have been chosen
2 according to the foresight of God the Father, and have been sanctified by the Spirit to obey Jesus Christ and receive the sprinkling of his blood. To you, grace and peace in abundance.
3 Blessed be God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in his great mercy has caused us to be reborn, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, to a living hope,
4 to an inheritance incorruptible, undefiled and imperishable, which you have reserved in heaven.
5 Because through faith, the power of God preserves you for salvation ready to be revealed at the final moment.
6 Therefore, you rejoice despite the various trials that you must momentarily suffer:

7 So your faith, once tested, will be much more valuable than perishable gold purified by fire, and it will become a reason for praise, glory and honor.
day of the Revelation of Jesus Christ.
8 Because you love him without having seen him, and believing in him without seeing him yet, you rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory,
9 sure of reaching the end of that faith, which is salvation.

11 They sought to discover the time and circumstances marked by the Spirit of Christ, who was present in them and announced in advance the sufferings reserved for them.
Christ and the glory that would follow.

12 It was revealed to them that they were serving a message intended not for themselves, but for you. And now you have received the announcement of that message through the work of those who, under the
action of the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, they transmitted the Good
News that angels long to contemplate.
13 Therefore, keep your spirit alert, live soberly, and place all your hope in the grace that you will receive when Jesus Christ is revealed.
14 As obedient children, do not act according to the evil desires you previously had while living in ignorance.
15 Just as he who called you is holy, so be holy in all your conduct,
16 according to what is written: Be holy, for I am holy.
17 And since you call Father Him who, without respect of persons, judges each one according to his works, live in fear while you are passing through this world.
18 You know that you were rescued from the vain conduct inherited from your fathers, not with corruptible goods, such as gold and silver,
19 but with the precious blood of Christ, the Lamb without spot and without blemish,
20 predestined before the creation of the world and manifested in the last times for your good.
21 Through him you believe in God, who raised him up and glorified him, so that your faith and hope are in God.
22 By your obedience to the truth, you have purified yourselves to sincerely love one another as brothers. Constantly love one another with a pure heart,
23 as those who have been born again, not of a corruptible seed, but of an incorruptible one: the Word of God, living and eternal.
24 For all flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like a flower of the field: the grass withers and its flower fades,
25 but the Word of the Lord remains forever. This is the Word that has been announced to you, the Good News.
1 Renounce all evil and all deceit, hypocrisy, envy and all kinds of slander.
2 Like newborn babies, desire the pure milk of the Word, that I will grow you up to salvation,
3 since they have tasted how good the Lord is.
4 As he approached him, the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in the sight of God,
5 You too, like living stones, are being built as a spiritual house, to exercise a holy priesthood and offer spiritual sacrifices, pleasing to God through Jesus Christ.
6 For the Scripture says, I am laying in Zion a cornerstone, chosen and precious: whoever puts his trust in it will not be confounded.
7 Therefore, the honor belongs to you who believe. But for unbelievers, the stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone:
8 stone of stumbling and rock of scandal. They stumble because they do not believe in the Word: that is the fate that is reserved for them.

9 You, however, are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people chosen to proclaim the wonders of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous
light:
10 You, who were not a people before, are now the People of God; You who had not obtained mercy before have now obtained it.
11 My dear ones, I exhort you, as people passing through and foreigners: do not give in to those carnal desires that fight against the soul.

12 Observe good conduct among the pagans, and thus the same ones who now slander as evildoers, seeing your good works, will have to glorify God on the day of
your visit.
13 Respect all human authority as the Lord wants;
14 either the king, because he is the sovereign, or the governors, as delegated by him to punish those who do evil and reward those who do good.
15 It is God's will that you, by doing good, put a stop to the ignorance of fools.
16 Proceed as truly free men, obeying God, and not as those who make freedom an excuse for their malice.
17 Respect everyone, love your brothers, fear God, honor the king.
18 Servants, treat your masters with due respect, not only the good and understanding, but also the bad.
19 Because it is a grace to bear, with our thoughts on God, the pains that are suffered unjustly.
20 Indeed, what glory would there be in bearing the punishment for a fault that has been committed? But if despite doing good, you endure suffering, this is a grace before God.
21 To this you have been called, because Christ also suffered for you, and left you an example so that you may follow in his footsteps.
22 He committed no sin and no one could find a lie in his mouth.
23 When he was insulted, he did not return the insult, and while he suffered he did not utter threats; On the contrary, he entrusted his cause to him who judges rightly.
24 He bore our sins on the cross, carrying them in his body, so that, dead to sin, we might live for righteousness. Thanks to his wounds, you were healed.
25 For you once walked like lost sheep, but now you have returned to your Shepherd and Guardian.
1 Let wives also respect their husbands, so that if any of them refuse to believe in the Word, he may be convinced without a word by his wife's conduct,
2 seeing his chaste and respectful life.
3 Let your elegance not be the external adornment – consisting of elaborate hairstyles, gold jewelry and luxurious dresses –
4 but the inner attitude of the heart, the incorruptible adornment of a sweet and serene spirit. This is what is worth in the eyes of God.
5 This is how the holy women once adorned themselves, who had their hope in God and respected their husbands,
6 such as Sarah, who obeyed Abraham and called him her lord. Now you have become his daughters, doing good and not letting yourself be disturbed by any kind of fear.

7 Husbands, in turn, understand that they must share their lives with a weaker being, such as the woman: treat her with the respect due to co-heirs of the grace that Life gives. That way, nothing
It will be an obstacle to prayer.
8 Finally, live together, share each other's concerns, love each other as brothers, be merciful and humble.
9 Do not return evil for evil, nor injury for injury: on the contrary, repay with blessings, for you yourselves are called to inherit a blessing.
10 "He who loves life and desires to enjoy happy days, let him keep his tongue from evil and his lips from lying words;
11 depart from evil and do good; Seek peace and follow after it.
12 For the eyes of the Lord look on the righteous and his ears are attentive to his prayer, but he rejects those who do evil."
13 Who can harm you if you do good?
14 Blessed are you, if you have to suffer for justice. Do not fear or worry;
15 but glorify Christ the Lord in your hearts. Always be ready to defend yourself before anyone who asks you for the reason for the hope that you have.

16 But do it gently and respectfully, and with a clear conscience. Thus all those who defame you will be ashamed of your slander, because you behave like servants of
Christ.
17 It is better to suffer doing good, if this is the will of God, than doing evil.
18 Christ died once for our sins – being righteous, he suffered for injustice – to bring us to God. Delivered to death in his flesh, he was made alive in the Spirit.
19 And then he went to make his announcement to the spirits that were prisoners,
20 to those who refused to believe when God waited patiently, in the days when Noah was building the ark. In it, a few – eight in total – were saved through the water.

21 All this is a figure of the baptism, by which you are now saved, which does not consist in the removal of a bodily stain, but is the commitment to God of a pure conscience, for
the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
22 who is at the right hand of God, after ascending to heaven and having submitted to him the Angels, the Dominions and the Powers.

1 And since Christ suffered in his flesh, let yourselves also be filled with this conviction: he who has suffered in the flesh has broken with sin. Because he who suffers in the flesh is free
of sin,
2 to live the rest of his mortal life, not according to human desires, but according to the will of God.

3 They have lived long enough according to the standards of the pagans, indulging in all kinds of debauchery, evil desires, drunkenness, excessive eating, orgies, and worship.
illicit of idols.
4 Now the pagans are surprised that you do not rush with them into this overflow of debauchery, and they revile you.
5 For this they will have to give an account to him who will judge the living and the dead.

6 For the Good News has been announced to the dead, so that they, after having been judged in the flesh according to their human condition, might live by the Spirit with the life of
God.
7 The end of all things is approaching: therefore, have the necessary moderation and sobriety to be able to pray.
8 Above all, love one another deeply, for love covers all sins.
9 Practice hospitality, without complaining.
10 Put the gifts you have received at the service of others, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

11 He who has received the gift of the Word, let him teach it as the Word of God. He who exercises a ministry should do so as one who receives that power from God, so that God may be glorified.
in all things, through Jesus Christ. To him be glory and power, forever
of the centuries! Amen.
12 My dear ones, do not be surprised at the violence that has been unleashed against you to test you, as if something extraordinary were happening to you.
13 Rejoice to the extent that you can share in the sufferings of Christ. Thus, when his glory is manifested, you too will overflow with joy and gladness.
14 Blessed are you if you are insulted for the name of Christ, because the Spirit of glory, the Spirit of God, rests on you.
15 May no one have to suffer as a murderer, thief, evildoer or informer.
16 But if you suffer because you are a Christian, do not be ashamed and glorify God for bearing that name.

17 For the time has come when judgment will begin, beginning with the house of God. Now, if the judgment begins with us, what will be the fate of those who refuse to believe in the
Good News from God?
18 If the righteous are barely saved, what will happen to the wicked and the sinner?
19 Therefore, those who suffer according to the will of God, do good, placing themselves in the hands of their Creator, who is faithful.
1 I exhort the priests who are among you, since I am a priest like them and a witness of the sufferings of Christ and a sharer in the glory that is to be revealed.
2 Feed the Flock of God, which has been entrusted to you; watch over him, not forced, but spontaneously, as God wants; not out of petty interest, but with self-denial;
3 not seeking to dominate those entrusted to them, but being an example for the Flock from the heart.
4 And when the Chief Shepherd comes, you will receive the everlasting crown of glory.

proud and gives his help to the humble.
6 Humble yourselves under the powerful hand of God, so that he may lift you up at the opportune time.
7 Unload all your concerns on him, since he takes care of you.
8 Be sober and always be alert, because your enemy, the devil, prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
9 Resist it firm in faith, knowing that your brothers scattered throughout the world suffer the same sufferings as you.
10 The God of all grace, who has called us to his eternal glory in Christ, after you have suffered a little, will restore and establish you, make you strong and unshakable.
11 To him be glory and power forever! Amen.

12 I write these words to you through Silvanus, whom I consider a faithful brother, to exhort you and testify that this is the true grace of God: remain attached to
her.
13 The church of Babylon, which has been chosen like you, greets you, as does my son Mark.
14 Greet one another with a kiss of brotherly love. May peace descend upon all of you who are united to Christ.
1 Simon Peter, servant and Apostle of Jesus Christ, greets all those who, through the justice of our God and Savior Jesus Christ, have received a faith as precious as ours.
2 May grace and peace come to you in abundance through the knowledge of God and Jesus Christ our Lord.
3 His divine power, in fact, has freely granted us everything necessary for life and piety, making us know him who called us by the power of his own glory.

4 Thanks to her, the greatest and most valuable promises have been granted to us, so that you can participate in the divine nature, escaping the corruption that reigns in the world today.
cause of concupiscence.
5 For this same reason, make every effort to unite faith with virtue; to virtue, knowledge;
6 to knowledge, temperance; to temperance, perseverance; to perseverance, piety;
7 to piety, the brotherly spirit, and to the brotherly spirit, love.
8 For if you possess these things in abundance, you will not remain inactive or barren in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
9 He who does not possess them is blind, short-sighted, because he forgets that he has been purified from his past sins.
10 Therefore, brothers, try to strengthen more and more the call and the election of which you have been subjected: if you do this, you will never fall
11 and the doors of the eternal Kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be widely opened to you.

13 It seems only fair that I keep you awake, reminding you of this while I live in this tent
14 because I know that very soon I will have to leave her, as our Lord Jesus Christ has made known to me.
15 And I will do everything possible so that after I am gone you will always remember these things.
16 For we did not make known to you the power and Coming of our Lord Jesus Christ based on cleverly invented fables, but as eyewitnesses of his greatness.
17 In fact, he received honor and glory from God the Father, when the Glory full of majesty addressed him this word: "This is my very dear Son, in whom I have set my preference."
18 We heard this voice coming from heaven, while we were with him on the holy mountain.

19 Thus we have seen the word of the prophets confirmed, and you do well to pay attention to it, as to a lamp that shines in a dark place until the day dawns and the star appears.
of the morning in their hearts.
20 But remember first of all that no one can interpret a prophecy of Scripture on his own.
21 For no prophecy was announced by the will of man, but men spoke from God, moved by the Holy Spirit.

1 Among the people of Israel there were also false prophets. In the same way, there will be false teachers among you who will secretly introduce harmful deviations, and will deny the Lord who
He redeemed them, bringing upon themselves imminent destruction.
2 Many will imitate their debauchery, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed.
3 Driven by ambition and using deceitful words, they will take advantage of you. But judgment has long threatened them and perdition stalks them.
4 For God did not spare the angels who sinned, but cast them into hell and plunged them into the abyss of darkness, where they are reserved for Judgment.
5 Nor did he spare the ancient world, but unleashed the flood on a land populated by the wicked, sparing only eight people, among them Noah, the herald of justice.
6 He also condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to destruction and burned them to ashes, so that they would serve as an example to the wicked of the future.
7 Instead, he delivered Lot, the righteous, who was afflicted by the licentious conduct of those lawless men;
8 because having to live among them, his righteous soul felt constantly tortured by the iniquities that he saw and heard.
9 Indeed, the Lord knows how to deliver pious men from trial, and saves the guilty to be punished on the day of Judgment,

10 above all, those who, driven by their evil desires, run after carnal pleasures and despise Sovereignty. These bold and arrogant men are not afraid to
blaspheme against fallen angels.
11 while the angels superior in strength and power do not pronounce any slanderous judgment against them in the presence of the Lord.
12 But they, like irrational animals, destined by nature to be captured and destroyed, speak insultingly of what they do not know, and they will perish like those same animals,

13 thus suffering the punishment in payment for his iniquity. They delight in indulging in depravity in broad daylight; They are vicious and corrupt men, who enjoy deceiving them.
while they eat with you.
14 They are cursed beings, whose eyes cannot look at a woman without desiring her; beings insatiable with sin, who seduce weak souls and whose hearts only know greed.
15 They abandoned the straight path, wandering in the footsteps of Balaam, son of Bosor, who allowed himself to be seduced by unjust wages;
16 But he found someone who reproached him for his fault: an animal of burden spoke human words and put a stop to the prophet's folly.
17 Those who do this are fountains without water, clouds carried by the hurricane: the density of darkness is reserved for them.
18 With their high-sounding and empty words, they attract, through the unbridled desires of the flesh, those who have just freed themselves from those who live in error.
19 They promise them freedom, being themselves slaves of corruption: for one is a slave to that which dominates him.

20 In fact, if someone separates himself from the vices of the world, through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and then allows himself to be entangled and dominated by those vices again, his
final state becomes worse than the first.
21 It would have been better for him not to know the way of righteousness than after having known it, to depart from the holy commandment that was handed down to him.
22 In him is fulfilled what the proverb says: The dog ate again what he had vomited, and this other: "The freshly washed sow wallows in the mud."
1 Dear brothers, this is the second letter I write to you. In both of them I have recommended some things, so that you have an exact criterion.
2 Do not forget what has been announced by the holy prophets, nor the commandment of the Lord Savior, which the Apostles have transmitted to you.
3 Know, first of all, that in the last days there will come men mocking and full of sarcasm, who live according to their passions,
4 and they will say: “Where is the promise of His Coming? Our parents have died and everything continues as at the beginning of creation.
5 In affirming this, they do not take into account that long ago there was a heaven, and also an earth arising from water that took shape in the midst of the waters by the word of God.
6 Because of those waters, the world of that time perished submerged by the flood.
7 That same word of God has reserved heaven and earth from now on to purify them by fire on the day of Judgment and destruction of the wicked.
8 But you, dear brothers, must not ignore that, before the Lord, one day is like a thousand years and a thousand years like one day.
9 The Lord is not slow to fulfill what he has promised, as some imagine, but he is patient with you because he does not want anyone to perish, but for everyone to convert.

10 However, the Day of the Lord will come like a thief, and on that day, the heavens will disappear with a crash; the elements will be disintegrated by fire, and the earth, with everything in it
she will be consumed.
11 Since all things will be disintegrated in this way, how holy and godly your conduct must be,
12 waiting and hastening the coming of the Day of the Lord! Then the heavens will be consumed and the elements will be melted by fire.
13 But we, according to the promise of the Lord, look forward to a new heaven and a new earth where righteousness will dwell.
14 Therefore, dear brothers, while you wait for this, try to live in such a way that he finds you at peace, without stain or reproach.
15 Keep in mind that the patience of the Lord is for our salvation, as our brother Paul has written to you, according to the wisdom given to him,

16 and repeats it in all the letters where he discusses this topic. In them there are passages that are difficult to understand, which some ignorant and unstable people interpret crookedly - such as, on the other hand,
part, they do it with the rest of Scripture – to their own perdition.
17 My brothers, you are warned. Be on your guard, lest, carried away by the wanderings of those who do evil, you lose your firmness.
18 Grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be the glory, now and in eternity!

1 What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have contemplated and what we have touched with our hands concerning the Word of Life, is what
we announce.
2 For Life became visible, and we saw it and are witnesses, and we announce to you the eternal Life, which existed with the Father and which has been revealed to us.
3 What we have seen and heard, we also proclaim to you, so that you may live in communion with us. And our communion is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.
4 We write this to you so that our joy may be complete.
5 The news that we have heard about him and that we announce to you is this: God is light, and in him there is no darkness.
6 If we say that we are in communion with him and walk in darkness, we lie and do not act according to the truth.
7 But if we walk in the light, as he himself is in the light, we are in communion with one another, and the blood of his Son Jesus purifies us from all sin.
8 If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.
9 If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us and purify us from all unrighteousness.
10 If we say that we have not sinned, we make him out to be a liar, and his word is not in us.
1 My children, I have written these things to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone sins, we have a defender before the Father: Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.
2 He is the scapegoating Victim for our sins, and not only for ours, but also for those of the entire world.
3 The sign that we know him is that we keep his commandments.
4 He who says, "I know him," and does not keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
5 But in him who keeps his word, the love of God has truly reached its fullness. This is the sign that we live in it.
6 He who says that he abides in him, must act like him.
7 Beloved, I do not give you a new commandment, but an old commandment, which you learned from the beginning: this old commandment is the word that you heard.
8 However, the commandment I give you is new. And this is true both in him and in you, because the darkness is dispelled and the true light now shines.
9 He who says he is in the light and does not love his brother is still in darkness.
10 He who loves his brother abides in the light and nothing causes him to stumble.
11 But he who does not love his brother is in darkness and walks in it, not knowing where he is going, because the darkness has blinded him.
12 Children, I write to you because your sins have been forgiven in the name of Jesus.
13 Fathers, I write to you because you know him who existed from the beginning. Young people, I write to you because you have defeated the Evil One.

14 Children, I have written to you because you know the Father. Fathers, I have written to you because you know him who existed from the beginning. Young people, I have written to you because you are strong, and the
The Word of God remains in you, and you have defeated the Evil One.
15 Do not love the world or worldly things. If someone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
16 For all that is in the world is the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the display of wealth. All this does not come from the Father, but from the world;
17 But the world passes away, and with it its lust. On the other hand, he who fulfills the will of God remains eternally.
18 My children, the last hour has come. You heard it said that the Antichrist would come; In reality, many antichrists have already appeared, and that is why we know that the last hour has arrived.

19 They came out from among us, however, they were not ours. If they had been, they would have remained with us. But it had to be made clear that not all
They are ours.
20 You have received the anointing of him who is Holy, and you all have true knowledge.
21 I have written to you, not because you are ignorant of the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie comes from the truth.
22 Who is the liar, except he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? That is the Antichrist: the one who denies the Father and the Son.
23 He who denies the Son is not united to the Father; he who recognizes the Son is also united to the Father.
24 As for you, remain faithful to what you heard from the beginning: in this way you will also remain in the Son and in the Father.
25 The promise he made to us is this: eternal Life.
26 This is what I wanted to write to you about those who try to deceive you.

27 But the anointing you received from him remains in you, and you do not need anyone to teach you. And since that anointing instructs you in everything and is true and does not lie,
remain in it, as she has taught you.
28 Yes, abide in him, my children, so that when he appears we may have full confidence and not be ashamed before him on the Day of his Coming.
29 If you know that he is righteous, know also that everyone who does righteousness was born of him.
1 Look how the Father loved us! He wanted us to call ourselves children of God, and we truly are. If the world does not recognize us, it is because it has not recognized him.
2 My dear ones, from now on we are children of God, and what we will be has not yet been revealed. We know that when he appears, we will be like him, because we will see him as he is.
3 He who has this hope in him is purified, just as he is pure.
4 He who commits sin also commits iniquity, because sin is iniquity.
5 But you know that he appeared to take away sin, and that he is without sin.
6 He who abides in it does not sin, and he who sins has not seen it nor known it.
7 My children, let no one deceive you: he who does justice is righteous, just as he himself is righteous.
8 But he who sins comes from the devil, because the devil was a sinner from the beginning. And the Son of God appeared to destroy the works of the devil.
9 He who is born of God does not sin, because the seed of God remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he was born of God.
10 The children of God and the children of the devil are manifest in this: he who does not practice justice is not of God, nor is he who does not love his brother.
11 The news you heard from the beginning is this: that we love one another.
12 Let us not do like Cain, who belonged to the Evil One and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because his works were evil, and his brother's works were right.
13 Do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates you.
14 We know that we have passed from death to Life, because we love our brothers. He who does not love remains in death.
15 He who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer possesses eternal Life.
16 By this we have known love: that he laid down his life for us. Therefore, we too must give our lives for our brothers.
17 If someone lives in abundance, and seeing his brother in need, closes his heart to him, how will the love of God remain in him?
18 My little children, let us not love only with tongue and word, but with deeds and truth.
19 By this we will know that we are of the truth, and we will have peace before God
20 even if our conscience reproaches us for something, because God is greater than our conscience and knows all things.
21 My dear ones, if our hearts do not reproach us, we can approach God with complete confidence,
22 and he will grant us whatever we ask, because we keep his commandments and do what pleases him.
23 His commandment is this: that we believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and love one another as he commanded us.
24 He who keeps his commandments abides in God, and God abides in him; and we know that he abides in us, through the Spirit which he has given us.
1 My dear ones, do not believe anyone who considers himself inspired: test your inspiration to see if it comes from God, because many false prophets have appeared in the world.
2 By this you will recognize him who is inspired by God: everyone who confesses Jesus Christ manifested in the flesh comes from God.
3 And everyone who denies Jesus does not come from God, but is inspired by the Antichrist, whom you heard said would come and is already in the world.
4 My children, you are from God and you have defeated those false prophets, because he who is in you is greater than he who is in the world.
5 They are of the world, that is why they speak the language of the world and the world listens to them.
6 We, however, belong to God. He who knows God listens to us, but he who is not of God does not listen to us. And in this we will distinguish true inspiration from false inspiration.
7 My dear ones, let us love one another, for love comes from God, and he who loves is born of God and knows God.
8 He who does not love has not known God, because God is love.
9 Thus God manifested his love to us: he sent his only Son into the world, so that we might have Life through him.
10 And this love is not that we loved God, but that he first loved us, and sent his Son as a scapegoat for our sins.
11 My dear ones, if God loved us so much, we too must love one another.
12 No one has ever seen God: if we love one another, God remains in us and the love of God has reached its fullness in us.
13 The sign that we abide in him and he abides in us is that he has communicated his Spirit to us.
14 And we have seen and testified that the Father sent the Son as Savior of the world.
15 He who confesses that Jesus is the Son of God abides in God, and God abides in him.
16 We have known the love that God has for us and we have believed in him. God is love, and he who abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him.
17 The sign that love has reached its fullness in us is that we have complete confidence before the day of Judgment, because in this world we are already similar to it.
18 In love there is no place for fear: on the contrary, perfect love eliminates fear, because fear implies a punishment, and he who fears has not reached the fullness of love.
19 We love because God first loved us.
20 He who says, “I love God,” and does not love his brother, is a liar. How can he who does not love his brother, whom he sees, love God whom he does not see?
21 This is the commandment we have received from him: whoever loves God must also love his brother.
1 He who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God; and he who loves the Father also loves him who is born of him,
2 The sign that we love God's children is that we love God and keep his commandments.
3 Love for God consists in keeping his commandments, and his commandments are not a burden,
4 because he who is born of God overcomes the world. And the victory that triumphs over the world is our faith.
5 Who is he who overcomes the world, except he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
6 Jesus Christ came by water and blood; not only with water, but with water and blood. And the Spirit is the truth.
7 There are three who bear witness:
8 the Spirit, the water and the blood; and all three agree.
9 If we believe the testimony of men, with all the more reason we must accept the testimony of God. And God has borne witness to his Son.

10 He who believes in the Son of God has the testimony of God in his heart. He who does not believe God makes him appear to be a liar, because he does not believe in the testimony that God has given
about his Son.
11 And the testimony is this: God gave us eternal Life, and that Life is in his Son.
12 He who is united to the Son has Life; He who is not, does not have Life.
13 I have written these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal Life.
14 We have complete confidence that God hears us if we ask him for something according to his will.
15 And knowing that he hears us in everything we ask, we know that we already have what we asked of him.

16 He who sees his brother commit a sin that does not lead to death, let him pray and it will give him Life. I mean those who commit sins that do not lead to death, because there is a sin that leads to death.
death; For this I do not ask you to pray.
17 Although all evil is sin, not all sin leads to death.
18 We know that he who is born of God does not sin, but the Son of God protects him, and the Evil One can do nothing to him.
19 We know that we are from God, and that the whole world is under the power of the Evil One.

20 And we also know that the Son of God has come and given us understanding so that we may know Him who is True; and we abide in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal Life.
21 My little children, beware of idols...
1 I, the Priest – and not only I, but also all those who have known the truth – greet the chosen Community and its members, whom I truly love,
2 because of the truth that abides in us and will be with us forever,
3 The grace, mercy and peace of God the Father and of his Son Jesus Christ, in truth and love, will also be with us.
4 I have been very happy to find some of your children who live in the truth, according to the commandment we have received from the Father.
5 And now I pray you: let us love one another. With which I do not communicate to you a new commandment, but the one we have from the beginning.
6 Love consists of living according to God's commandments. And the commandment that you have learned from the beginning is to live in love.
7 For many seducers have invaded the world who do not confess Jesus Christ manifested in the flesh. They are the Seducer and the Antichrist!
8 Be careful not to lose the fruit of your labors, so that you may receive a perfect reward.
9 Anyone who ventures beyond the doctrine of Christ and does not abide in it is not united with God. On the other hand, he who remains in his doctrine is united to the Father and also to the Son.
10 If anyone comes before you and does not bring this same doctrine, do not welcome him into your house or greet him.
11 Because whoever greets him becomes an accomplice in his evil deeds.
12 I would have many other things to write to you, but I did not want to do it by letter, because I hope to go see you to speak with you personally, so that our joy may be complete.
13 The children of this chosen Community also greet you fraternally.
1 I, the Priest, greet my dear brother Gaius, whom I truly love.
2 Dear brother, I pray that God finds you perfectly well and that you enjoy good health in your body, as you have in your soul.
3 I was very happy when some brothers came and testified to your adherence to the truth, because you actually live according to it,
4 and my greatest joy is knowing that my children live in the truth.
5 Dear brother, you work faithfully, putting yourself at the service of your brothers, even those who are passing through,
6 and they testified to your love before the Church. You will do well to help them so that they can continue their journey in a manner worthy of God.
7 because they set out to serve Christ, accepting nothing from the pagans,
8 That is why we must welcome them, in order to collaborate with them in favor of the truth.
9 I wrote a letter to the Church, but Diotrephes, who aspires to occupy the first place in it, does not recognize our authority.

10 Therefore, when he comes, I will reproach him for the evil he does by speaking against us. And not content with this, he does not want to receive the brothers, and those who would like to receive them,
He forbids them to do so and expels them from the Church.
11 Dear brother, do not imitate the bad, but the good. He who does good belongs to God, but he who does evil has not seen God.
12 But they all testify in favor of Demetrius, and the truth confirms this testimony. We do it too, and you know that our testimony is true.
13 I would have many things to tell you, but I don't want to do it by letter.
14 I hope to see you soon to talk to you personally.
15 Peace be with you. Friends greet you. Greet ours, each one in particular.
1 Judas, servant of Jesus Christ, brother of James, greets those who have been called, those loved by God, the Father, and protected by Jesus Christ.
2 May mercy, peace and love come to you in abundance.

3 My dear ones, I had a great desire to write to you about our common salvation, but I have been forced to do so in order to exhort you to fight for the faith, which once and for all.
It has always been transmitted to the saints.

4 For certain men have crept in among you, whose condemnation was foretold a long time ago. They are impious who make the grace of God a pretext for their debauchery and
They deny our only Owner and Lord Jesus Christ.
5 I want to remind you, although you have already learned it once and for all, that the Lord, after having saved the people, bringing them out of Egypt, immediately caused the unbelievers to die.
6 As for the angels who did not know how to preserve their preeminence and abandoned their own dwelling, the Lord has them eternally chained in darkness for the Judgment of the great Day.

7 Also Sodom and Gomorrah, and the neighboring cities, which prostituted themselves in a manner similar to them, allowing themselves to be carried away by relations contrary to nature, have remained as an example, subjected
to the penalty of eternal fire.
8 The same thing happens with these wicked: in their delirium they profane the flesh, despise Sovereignty and revile the glorious angels.

9 Now the archangel Michael himself, when he confronted the demon and argued with him regarding the body of Moses, did not dare to utter any slanderous judgment against him, but
He only said: "May the Lord restrain you."
10 These wicked people, however, speak insultingly of things they do not know; and what they know by natural instinct, like irrational animals, only serves to ruin them.
11 Woe to them! Because they followed the path of Cain; For the love of money they fell into the error of Balaam and perished in the rebellion of Korah.

12 They stain brotherly meals, because they indulge in gluttony without any shame and only try to satisfy themselves. They are clouds without water carried by the wind, trees
fruitless autumn trees, doubly dead and uprooted;
13 fierce waves of the sea, which throw forth the foam of their own dishonours, wandering stars to which the density of darkness is reserved forever.
14 Enoch, the seventh patriarch after Adam, was referring to them when he prophesied: “The Lord is coming with his thousands of angels,
15 to judge all and to condemn the wicked for the wickedness they committed, and the sinners for the insolent words they uttered against him.
16 These are all gossips and malcontents who live according to the whims of their passions: their mouths are full of petulance and they flatter others out of interest.
17 As for you, my dears, remember what the Apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ foretold.
18 They said to them, "In the last times there will be people who will mock everything and live according to their ungodly passions."
19 These are the divisive ones, sensual men who do not have the Spirit.
20 But you, my dear ones, build yourselves on the foundation of your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit.
21 Remain in the love of God, waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ for eternal Life.
22 Try to convince those who have doubts,
23 and save them by delivering them from the fire. As for the rest, have mercy on them, but carefully, hating even the tunic contaminated by their body.
24 To him who is able to preserve you from every fall and make you appear blameless and with joy in the presence of his glory,

25 To the only God who is our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, honor, strength and power, from before all time, now and forever.
Amen.
1 Revelation of Jesus Christ, which was entrusted to him by God to teach his servants what must happen soon. He sent his Angel to transmit it to his servant John.
2 This one testifies that everything he saw is the Word of God and a testimony of Jesus Christ.
3 Happy is he who reads, and happy are those who hear the words of this prophecy and take into account what is written in it, because the time is near.

5 and of Jesus Christ, the faithful Witness, the First who rose from the dead, the King of the kings of the earth. He loved us and purified us from our sins, through his blood,

7 He will come among the clouds and everyone will see him, even those who had passed through him. For him all the races of the earth will beat their chests. Yes, it will be so. Amen.

of the testimony of Jesus.

11 "Write in a book what you are now going to see, and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, to Smyrna, to Pergamum, to Thyatira, to Sardis, to Philadelphia and to Laodicea."
12 I turned to see whose voice was speaking to me, and I saw seven golden lampstands,
13 and in the midst of them was someone like a Son of man, clothed in a long tunic that was girded around his chest with a golden sash.
14 His head and hair were as white as wool and snow; his eyes looked like flames of fire;
15 his feet, bronze cast in the crucible; and his voice was like the roar of great waterfalls.
16 In his right hand he had seven stars; A double-edged sword came out of his mouth; and his face was like the sun when it shines with all its strength.
17 When I saw this, I fell at his feet, as if dead, but he, touching me with his right hand, said to me: "Do not be afraid: I am the First and the Last, the Living One.
18 I was dead, but now I live forever and I have the key to Death and the Abyss.
19 Write down what you have seen, what is happening now, and what will happen in the future.

20 The mysterious meaning of the seven stars that you saw in my hand and the seven golden lampstands is this: the seven stars are the Angels of the seven Churches, and the
seven candelabra are the seven Churches.
1 Write to the Angel of the Church of Ephesus: "He who holds the seven stars in his right hand and walks among the seven golden lampstands, says:

liars

faithful until death and I will give you the crown of life.

12 Write to the Angel of the Church of Pergamon: “He who has the double-edged sword says:

who was killed in the place where Satan dwells.

eating food sacrificed to idols.

new name that no one knows except the one who receives it.
18 To the Angel of the Church of Thyatira write: “The Son of God, who has eyes like flames of fire and feet like molten bronze, says:

20 But I must reproach you for tolerating Jezebel, that woman who claims to be a prophetess, who deceives all my servants and teaches them to prostitute themselves by eating sacrificed food.
to the idols.
